news.Title: Not Apple. Not Microsoft. This "Magnificent Seven" Stock Is My Top Tech Buy for 2027.
news.Content:
Many companies are tapping into the artificial intelligence (AI) boom in their own way. Two companies in this sector are already seeing benefits, and it has helped reinforce their status among the "Magnificent Seven" -- seven mega-cap, tech-heavy companies that have driven a huge share of U.S. stock market gains in recent years.

Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) is integrating AI agents into its legacy software and renting out cloud computing capacity through its Azure services. And Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) recently launched an update to Siri AI to better answer users' questions and debuted new devices that it says are optimized to run AI. I have no doubt that these two Magnificent Seven companies will succeed in the AI era in their own way.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But if I had to pick a different Magnificent Seven stock to buy for 2027 and beyond, it would have to be Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG). Its investments in Google Cloud are already paying off, and its shares look like a bargain right now.

Here's why it's worth buying Alphabet stock right now.

Playing the long game with AI

Alphabet stock fell hard recently after the company reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion for the third quarter, which ended Sept. 30. That was the second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow, and investors were understandably concerned.

But they also may have missed two important things related to its cash flow. The first was that a substantial portion of the loss resulted from a $5.2 billion one-time fee paid to the European Commission. The second is that management has successfully built out a behemoth of an AI cloud service in Google Cloud, and it could generate significant revenue and earnings for years to come.

Google Cloud revenue surged 103% year over year in the quarter to $30.7 billion, making it Alphabet's fastest-growing segment by far. Management says it will allocate between $195 billion and $205 billion to capital expenditures, which is a lot, but with the goal of broadening its AI services even further. What's more, Google Cloud now has $561 billion in backlogs, half of which will be realized as revenue over the next 24 months, the company says.

Google Cloud's growth in the quarter is a good indicator that Alphabet's spending is paying off. But it's not just the revenue that's important; Google Cloud also has impressive operating margins of 36.2%, up from just 23.7% in the year-ago quarter. The combination of growth and higher margins led to Google Cloud operating income more than tripling in the quarter to $11.1 billion.

Story Continues

And there could be plenty more where that came from. As more companies integrate AI agents into their software, they increasingly need to tap into cloud services to run their businesses. This is creating a huge AI cloud market that Goldman Sachs estimates will be worth $2 trillion by 2030.

Alphabet stock looks like a good deal right now

Not only is Alphabet benefiting from the current AI boom and poised for more growth from its current AI investments, but its stock is also a really good deal right now. Its trailing price-to-earnings is just under 15, far less expensive than the tech sector's average price-to-earnings ratio of 32.

The stock already looked like a good deal over the past several months, but the recent AI sell-off has made it look like a bargain heading into 2027.

And while I think there are legitimate concerns about AI spending eventually slowing down, it doesn't appear to be happening anytime soon. Bank of Amerca estimates tech companies will double this spending over the next few years, reaching $2.1 trillion by 2028.

And even if Alphabet does have to pull back in the near future, the money it's spending now will likely continue to pay off in the coming years as demand for AI cloud services rises.

news.Title: Anthropic IPO to Cap Year of Record-Breaking Equity Megadeals
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- Anthropic PBC is poised to add to a blockbuster year of transactions that are orders of magnitude larger than those seen in the past decade, with the biggest initial public offering of all time joining a half dozen other jumbo equity deals.

Most Read from Bloomberg

'I'm a Piece of Sh--': Jensen Huang's Last Hours as Nvidia CEO

Microsoft Races to Fix Outlook in One of Its Longest Outages

Alice Huang, Suspected China Spy, Spent Years in Nvidia's Orbit

Nvidia Scandal Creates Risk for Entire AI Industry, Not Just CEO

Alleged Chinese Spy at Heart of Nvidia Scandal Is in Beijing

If Anthropic's first-time share sale prices at the top of its marketed range on Nov. 18, the artificial intelligence lab's IPO and private placement would together raise $90.4 billion, easily surpassing the $86.2 billion in Elon Musk's SpaceX listing in June.

Exercising the so-called over-allotment option after the trading begins, bringing it to more than $100 billion, would surpass Meta Platforms Inc.'s roughly $98 billion equity deal announced last month, also to fund its AI business.

More than $425 billion has been raised across US-listed companies when accounting for IPOs, completed at-the-market share sale programs and marketed share sales, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. That tops the 2021 total of roughly $408 billion raised, the data show.

Including Anthropic, the US's three biggest-ever IPOs landed in a matter of months of each other, a sign of how deals are being turbo-charged by AI companies' need for cash on a scale never seen before. Even adjusted for inflation, this year's biggest IPOs are far larger than previous record-holders like Saudi Aramco and Visa Inc.

While SK Hynix Inc.'s $26.5 billion US listing in July marked the largest for a company based outside of the country, its size after adjusting for inflation is actually more in line with deals from decades ago. By that measure, the South Korean company's US first-time share sale trails debuts from Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. in 2014 and SoftBank Corp. in 2018.

First Deals in Decades

The hunt for AI funding has not only broken records, it has also prompted a handful of tech giants to sell stock for the first time in decades.

Meta, led by Mark Zuckerberg, would likely hold the title for the biggest equity fundraise with its $98 billion of offerings including a marketed stock sale and preferred shares. The bulk of the total comes in the form of a planned $60 billion at-the-market share sale program, which allows companies to periodically sell shares in the open market.

Story Continues

Like IPOs, ATMs have metastasized in the AI era. Bitcoin treasury firm Strategy Inc. raised $21 billion in 2024 via an ATM and did another of the same size in 2025, data compiled by Bloomberg show.

This year, Alphabet Inc.'s roughly $85 billion funding plan includes a $40 billion ATM program. Oracle Corp. sold roughly $20 billion of shares through an ATM program, on top of raising tens of billions of dollars through the sale of additional equity and debt.

news.Title: Can SIMO's Advanced SSD Solutions Boost Its Enterprise Storage Growth?
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO is expanding its presence in the growing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market through its next-generation enterprise storage solutions. Its PCIe Gen5 and Gen6 MonTitan SSD controllers and reference platforms are designed to meet the increasing storage needs of AI factories, Agentic AI applications and large-scale inference workloads.

Silicon Motion's SM8366 PCIe Gen5 controller supports enterprise SSD capacities of up to 256TB using QLC NAND and multiple storage form factors. Powered by its PerformaShape QoS Engine, the platform aims to provide low latency and consistent performance for AI applications, including KV cache offload. Meanwhile, the SM8466 PCIe Gen6 controller delivers up to 28 GB/s sequential throughput and seven million random IOPS, while the SM8388 controller focuses on power-efficient, high-capacity storage for data centers.

The company also offers enterprise PCIe NVMe boot SSD solutions with DRAM-less and DRAM-equipped options for AI servers, networking systems and data processing units, with the latter delivering sequential read speeds of up to 14 GB/s. Silicon Motion's boot SSD technology supports NVIDIA Corporation 's NVDA DPU platform, while its Ferri-eMMC storage solution is paired with ASPEED's AST2600 BMC.

These developments reflect Silicon Motion's efforts to capitalize on rising storage demand in the AI infrastructure market. As AI applications require faster data access, greater storage capacity and reliable performance, the company's advanced SSD controllers and enterprise storage solutions could strengthen its position in the growing data center market.

How Are Competitors Advancing in the Enterprise Storage Market?

Silicon Motion faces competition from Seagate Technology Holdings plc STX and Micron Technology, Inc. MU. Seagate is strengthening its enterprise storage business to meet rising demand from AI and cloud data centers. The company is advancing its Mozaic platform to increase hard drive capacity, improve storage efficiency and lower operating costs. Seagate's HAMR-based Exos hard drives enable enterprise customers to store more data within the same data center space.

Micron is developing its enterprise SSD portfolio to address the growing storage requirements of AI and cloud applications. The company is focusing on high-capacity drives powered by advanced NAND technology to deliver faster data access and better power efficiency. Micron is advancing its PCIe Gen6 SSD technology to deliver higher data transfer speeds and support demanding workloads across AI and enterprise data centers.

Story Continues

SIMO's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Silicon Motion shares have rallied 107.3% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 94.3%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 8.95 forward earnings, lower than 9.06 for the industry.

Earnings estimates for 2026 have increased 20.5% to $13.45 over the past 60 days, while those for 2027 have increased 28.8% to $21.05.

news.Title: Cisco's Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates, Strong Networking Aids Revenues
news.Content:
Cisco Systems CSCO reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $1.40 per share, up 40% year over year and beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 5.26%. Strong networking demand, AI infrastructure growth and operating leverage supported the year-over-year improvement.

Revenues increased 24% year over year to $18.517 billion, surpassing the consensus mark by 2.14%. Product revenues increased 32%, while services revenues rose 1%. Total product orders grew 21% year over year, reflecting broad-based demand across geographies and customer markets.

Cisco Systems, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Cisco Systems, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Cisco Systems, Inc. Quote

CSCO's Networking Growth Accelerates

Networking revenues surged 43% year over year to $11.132 billion. Growth reflected triple-digit increases in AI infrastructure, double-digit expansion in data center switching and continued strength in campus networking.

Networking product orders increased 28%, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Campus networking orders advanced 14%, while industrial IoT orders jumped approximately 50%. The next-generation campus portfolio continued to ramp faster than previous product launches.

Wireless orders increased more than 20%, with Wi-Fi 7 accounting for more than 60% of access point orders. New products represented less than 10% of campus switching orders, highlighting the early stages of Cisco's multiyear network refresh opportunity.

Cisco's AI Infrastructure Momentum Strengthens

Cisco raised its fiscal 2027 hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue expectation to $9 billion from $7.5 billion, representing more than double the fiscal 2026 level. The company attributed the increase to sustained customer demand and improved visibility into deployments.

Cisco secured three new AI infrastructure design wins during the reported quarter, bringing the total to 18 over the past five quarters. Two involved Silicon One P200-powered systems for data center interconnect and scale-across applications, while another involved 1.6-terabit optics.

Demand also broadened beyond hyperscalers. Orders for Nexus data center switches associated with AI deployments increased 47% year over year, supported by neocloud, sovereign cloud and enterprise customers.

CSCO's Security and Software Trends Improve

Security revenues increased 7% year over year to $2.120 billion, supported by Splunk, network security and secure access service edge offerings. Security orders excluding Splunk increased approximately 15%, while firewall orders grew more than 30% for the third consecutive quarter.

Cisco's Zero Trust Secure Access platform reached 5,400 customers, adding nearly 800 during the quarter. AI Defense approached 500 customers and protected more than 2 trillion tokens monthly, reflecting growing adoption of AI security solutions.

Collaboration revenues increased 8% to $1.136 billion, while Observability revenues rose 2% to $279 million.

Total software revenues increased 8% to $6.132 billion. Subscription revenues represented 44% of total revenues, while annualized recurring revenue reached $32.7 billion, up 4% year over year.

Story Continues

Cisco Balances Margin Pressure With Operating Leverage

Non-GAAP gross margin contracted 250 basis points (bps) year over year to 65.6%. Product gross margin declined 350 bps to 63.7%, primarily reflecting a higher hardware mix and elevated memory costs. Productivity improvements and price increases partially offset these pressures.

Services gross margin expanded 220 bps to 72.9%.

Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 2% to $5.140 billion but declined to 27.8% of revenues from 33.7% a year earlier.

Consequently, non-GAAP operating margin expanded 340 bps to a record 37.8%, demonstrating operating leverage despite gross-margin headwinds.

CSCO's Cash Flow and Recurring Metrics Remain Solid

Cash, cash equivalents and investments totaled $15.845 billion at the end of the fiscal first quarter. Operating cash flow increased 36% year over year to $4.357 billion.

Remaining performance obligations reached $46.2 billion, up 8% year over year. Product obligations increased 7%, while services obligations advanced 9%. Deferred revenues grew 7% to $30.058 billion.

Cisco returned $3.656 billion to shareholders through $2.002 billion in share repurchases and $1.654 billion in dividends. Approximately $6.1 billion remained under its repurchase authorization.

Cisco Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Cisco expects revenues between $18 billion and $18.2 billion. Non-GAAP earnings are projected at $1.34-$1.36 per share, with a non-GAAP gross margin of 65-66% and an operating margin of 36-37%.

For fiscal 2027, Cisco now projects revenues of $74.8-$75.8 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $5.47-$5.53 per share.

The revised outlook reflects stronger hyperscaler demand and broad-based growth in Cisco's core business. The company expects fiscal 2027 non-GAAP operating margin to reach approximately 36%, supported by revenue growth and disciplined expense management.

Zacks Rank & Other Stocks to Consider

Cisco currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Some better-ranked stocks in the broader sector include Vertiv VRT, Teradyne TER, and Unity Software U. Each of the three stocks sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Vertiv, Teradyne and Unity Software shares have jumped 29.4%, 37% and 13.6% year to date, respectively. Long-term earnings growth rate for Vertiv, Teradyne and Unity Software is currently pegged at 43.81%, 54.38% and 41.63%, respectively.

news.Title: AAPL is Trading at a Premium at 36.15X P/E: Is the Stock Still a Hold?
news.Content:
Apple AAPL shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F. The AAPL stock is trading at a forward 12-month price/earnings (P/E) of 36.15X compared with the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's 17.48X. Apple shares are trading at a premium compared with peers, including Alphabet GOOGL, Microsoft MSFT and Amazon AMZN. Shares of Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon are trading at a P/E multiple of 19.17, 24.49 and 24.22, respectively.

AAPL Stock's Valuation

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Is Apple worth buying at current prices? Let's dig deep to find out.

Strong iPhone Sales & Services to Boost Apple's Prospects

Apple shares have appreciated 30.6% year to date (YTD), outperforming the broader sector's return of 8.9%. The stock has outperformed Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon over the same time frame. Shares of Amazon and Microsoft have returned 15.9% and 8.2%, respectively, YTD, while Alphabet drops 4.2%.

Apple Stock's YTD Price Performance

The outperformance reflects investor optimism surrounding robust iPhone demand, accelerating hardware innovation, expanding artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and continued growth in the high-margin Services business. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, iPhone revenues jumped 17% year over year to $57.6 billion, driven by strong customer demand despite supply constraints. The company achieved September-quarter revenue records for iPhone and registered record upgrades worldwide, including in the United States, Mainland China and India. The launch of iPhone Duo, alongside iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, has strengthened Apple's product portfolio and created additional upgrade opportunities.

Apple's growing investments in AI are expected to support its long-term prospects. Siri AI, which integrates personalized assistance, contextual awareness and privacy-focused processing, could encourage customers to upgrade to newer devices. The company also plans to monetize advanced server-based AI capabilities by offering expanded access to users requiring greater processing capacity. Increasing adoption of Apple Intelligence across iPhone, Mac and iPad could create incremental subscription revenues and strengthen customer engagement.

Apple's expanding Services business remains a significant long-term catalyst. The company's installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices provides a substantial opportunity to increase adoption of Apple Pay, iCloud+, Apple Music, Apple TV and advertising services. The expansion of iCloud+ packages to include Apple TV and Apple Arcade in more than 100 countries and regions could attract additional subscribers. Apple's introduction of Apple Pay in India and advertising on Apple Maps also creates new monetization opportunities.

Story Continues

AAPL Suffers From High Memory Cost & Supply Chain Constraints

Increasing component costs represent a significant challenge for Apple's prospects. The company expects gross margin to decline to 45-46% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 from 47.9% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, primarily due to rising memory prices and Siri AI-related expenses. Apple expects memory costs to increase further beyond the December quarter, potentially pressuring profitability.

Apple continues to face supply constraints across its product portfolio. In the fiscal fourth quarter, limited availability of advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity affected iPhone, Mac and iPad shipments. Although advanced-node constraints are easing, memory shortages are expected to affect Mac and iPad availability in the December quarter.

Increasing regulatory scrutiny of Apple's App Store business model and third-party licensing arrangements presents long-term risks. Apple expects Services revenue growth to moderate to 8-9% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 from 10% in the preceding quarter, reflecting licensing-related and foreign-exchange headwinds. Persistent regulatory pressures and evolving competition are expected to challenge the sustainability of Services growth.

AAPL's FY27 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Declining Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Apple's fiscal 2027 earnings has decreased by 8 cents to $9.45 per share over the past 30 days, indicating 7.1% growth from the figure reported in fiscal 2026.

Apple Inc. Price and Consensus

Apple Inc. price-consensus-chart | Apple Inc. Quote

The consensus mark for Apple's fiscal 2027 revenues is pegged at $526.45 billion, indicating 10% growth over the figure reported in fiscal 2026.

Conclusion

Strong iPhone demand, expanding Services business and growing AI capabilities are expected to support Apple's long-term growth prospects. The company's extensive installed base and continued product innovation provide opportunities for sustained revenue growth. However, rising memory costs, supply chain constraints, regulatory uncertainties and moderating Services growth remain concerns. Moreover, downward earnings estimate revisions and a premium valuation compared with the broader sector and peers limit the stock's near-term upside potential. Although Apple's solid fundamentals and AI-driven opportunities remain encouraging, its elevated valuation warrants caution. Investors may prefer to wait for a more attractive entry point before accumulating AAPL shares.

Apple currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Content:

Sandisk ( NASDAQ:SNDK ) has lost about 37% in a month , but Evercore ISI is sticking with its Outperform rating and $2,500 price target.

Analyst Amit Daryanani's case hinges on multiyear supply deals that could protect profits when flash memory prices cool. The target implies roughly 167% upside from Thursday's $937.46 close, with both figures on a pre-split basis.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with SNDK.

Sandisk makes NAND flash memory, the technology behind solid-state drives and other storage devices. It sells enterprise drives to data center customers and storage products for computers, cars and consumer electronics.

After meeting with management, Evercore told clients that Sandisk had contracted about half of its fiscal 2027 bit volume and 67% of fiscal 2028 volume, according to TipRanks. The deals include purchase commitments, price floors and ceilings, and nearly $16.5 billion in financial guarantees.

Price floors can cushion a downturn, while ceilings can limit how much Sandisk gains if shortages drive prices higher.

The latest results show how much is at stake. Fiscal first-quarter data center revenue rose 61% from the prior quarter to $4.8 billion, helping lift total revenue to $11 billion. Adjusted gross margin reached 85.1%. Evercore says customers are still asking for more storage for AI systems already being deployed.

The bigger test comes with fiscal second-quarter results. Sandisk projects $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion in sales and an adjusted gross margin of 84.5% to 85.5%.

Watch how much fiscal 2028 volume Sandisk locks in and whether enterprise SSD sales keep climbing. If margins hold as spot prices soften, that would support Evercore's case. If suppliers ramp production or customers delay AI deployments, sales outside those contracts could come under pressure.

news.Title: Cisco Q1 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Higher Outlook
news.Content:
Cisco Systems, Inc. CSCO highlighted accelerating artificial intelligence infrastructure demand, broad-based networking momentum and improving operating efficiency during its first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call.

Management raised its annual outlook, citing stronger hyperscaler spending and enterprise networking investments. However, an increasing hardware mix and component costs remain important considerations for profitability.

Cisco reported non-GAAP earnings of $1.40 per share, up 40% year over year, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.33. Revenues rose 24% to $18.52 billion, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $18.13 billion.

Cisco Systems, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Cisco Systems, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Cisco Systems, Inc. Quote

Cisco Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook

Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Mark Patterson projected fiscal 2027 revenues of $74.8 billion to $75.8 billion, with non-GAAP earnings of $5.47 to $5.53 per share.

For the second quarter, revenues are expected between $18 billion and $18.2 billion, while non-GAAP earnings are projected at $1.34 to $1.36 per share.

Patterson attributed the stronger outlook to accelerating demand and operating leverage. Management expects non-GAAP operating margin to reach approximately 36% for fiscal 2027.

CSCO Sees Accelerating Hyperscaler AI Spending

Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Charles Robbins raised the fiscal 2027 hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue target to $9 billion from $7.5 billion, representing more than double the prior year's level.

Cisco secured three additional AI design wins during the quarter, including two involving Silicon One P200-powered systems and another involving 1.6-terabit optics.

Responding to Evercore ISI, Robbins attributed the higher target to continued customer orders and improved visibility. He emphasized that the increase reflected stronger demand rather than a fundamental change in strategy.

Cisco Highlights a Multiyear Networking Opportunity

Robbins characterized networking demand as an early-stage, multiyear expansion opportunity. Product orders increased 21%, while networking orders advanced 28%, marking nine consecutive quarters of double-digit growth.

Enterprise orders rose 15%, while public-sector orders increased 13%. Campus networking orders advanced 14%, reflecting continued infrastructure modernization.

Addressing Bank of America, Robbins identified hyperscaler investment, campus upgrades, security modernization, sovereign infrastructure and hybrid data centers as five important growth drivers.

Story Continues

CSCO Expands Security and AI Capabilities

Robbins highlighted improving security momentum, with orders excluding Splunk growing approximately 15%. Firewall orders increased more than 30% for the third consecutive quarter.

Cisco AI Defense now protects more than 2 trillion tokens monthly. The company also expanded its security capabilities through integrations involving Anthropic's Claude Mythos cybersecurity model.

During Morgan Stanley's questioning, Patterson noted that security revenues increased 7%, exceeding earlier expectations. Management anticipates further improvement in Splunk and broader security growth throughout fiscal 2027.

Cisco Balances Growth With Margin Pressures

Patterson reported a non-GAAP operating margin of 37.8%, supported by revenue growth and expense discipline. However, non-GAAP gross margin declined 250 basis points to 65.6%.

He attributed the pressure primarily to higher hardware exposure and memory costs, partially offset by pricing actions and productivity improvements.

Responding to JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs, Patterson highlighted strategic supply agreements and operational efficiencies. He maintained expectations for full-year gross margin slightly below 65%.

CSCO Addresses Demand Sustainability

During questioning from Melius Research, Robbins described neocloud exposure as relatively immaterial and emphasized conservative credit practices. He clarified that the company's hyperscaler AI revenue forecast excludes neocloud customers.

Responding to UBS, Robbins acknowledged uneven quarterly AI ordering patterns and emphasized revenue as a clearer measure of business progress.

Patterson added that the increased annual revenue outlook reflects contributions from both hyperscalers and the broader core business, demonstrating demand beyond AI infrastructure.

Cisco Maintains an Execution-Focused Approach

Management's commentary reflected confidence in sustained networking demand, supported by AI infrastructure expansion and enterprise modernization.

Robbins emphasized continued investment in innovation, while Patterson highlighted expense discipline, cash generation and shareholder returns as priorities supporting profitable growth.

news.Title: Microsoft updates on outage disrupting Outlook email, Teams, and Copilot for users
news.Content:
Microsoft ( MSFT) was working into Friday to restore user access to its workplace software tools, including email, after an outage that spanned multiple regions. The connectivity issues, which began Thursday, were being worked on for hours with the company at one point Thursday evening indicating that servers that had been brought back online became unresponsive again.

By Friday morning, Microsoft said it was seeing continued recovery progress across affected regions, with broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia Pacific.

"Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as mitigation continues across remaining affected infrastructure," said the update on X.

On Thursday afternoon, Microsoft said users of Exchange Online, which powers Outlook email, as well as the company's Teams videoconferencing app and Copilot AI chatbot, may experience disruptions. In a separate post on X, the company said users "in any region" could be affected.

Microsoft said it was rerouting connection traffic across its global infrastructure and restarting affected servers. Around 7:05 p.m. ET, Microsoft said some servers were becoming unresponsive again as traffic returned, underscoring that the company had not yet fully stabilized the outage.

A while later, the company said it was adding capacity to handle increased traffic as more regions came back online.

Friday morning, Microsoft said, "Our focus remains on stabilizing recovered infrastructure, completing mitigation in remaining impacted areas, and reducing delayed email queues and backlogs while we validate service consistency across connection methods."

news.Title: Is Tesla Stock Worth Buying Now on Robotaxi & FSD Progress?
news.Content:
Electric vehicle (EV) and tech giant Tesla TSLA is gaining the spotlight for the right reasons. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has pinned the company's next growth chapter on artificial intelligence, autonomous vehicles, robotaxis and robotics, and the recent developments show progress on the self-driving technology and robotaxi fronts.

Tesla has edged past Alphabet 's GOOGL Waymo on robotaxi fleet size in Texas. According to Teslarati, Texas Department of Motor Vehicles records as of Nov. 10 show 1,302 vehicles registered under Tesla Robotaxi, LLC, narrowly ahead of Waymo's 1,297. When Texas' autonomous vehicle registry became publicly available in late May 2026, Tesla had just 42 vehicles listed, compared with several hundred for Waymo. Its authorized fleet has since grown more than 30-fold, reflecting substantial Model Y additions and a growing Cybercab presence.

In another development, Tesla won Finland's nod for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology. With that, Finland has become the 11th European Union (EU) country to grant provisional approval for the system, adding momentum ahead of an EU-wide vote expected next month.

Amid all this, merger talks between SpaceX SPCX and Tesla are actively progressing, with many reports expecting the announcement to be made next month only. Both companies are pivoting toward AI, and consolidation promises meaningful synergies.Terafab, a joint project between Tesla and SpaceX, aims to produce the advanced AI chips Tesla needs for Optimus and its wider AI ambitions.

Over the past five trading sessions, the stock has jumped more than 15%. But year to date, Tesla shares are down roughly 12%. Given the recent progress on robotaxi and FSD domains, should you consider buying Tesla stock? Or does the stock still have enough to prove before jumping to invest in it? Let's discuss.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Beneath the Headline Progress in Robotaxis

Tesla began deploying Cybercabs in Austin in September 2026. On the third-quarter earnings call, the company highlighted that the cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles (including Model Y and Cybercab) rose eightfold sequentially to nearly 2 million. Management expects robotaxi operations to contribute more meaningfully to revenues from next year.

Image Source: Tesla, Inc.

The Cybercab is a significant milestone for Tesla and the fact that it has surpassed Waymo's fleet in Texas is also encouraging. However, registered vehicles are not necessarily active robotaxis carrying paying passengers. A larger fleet does not automatically translate into more rides, higher utilization or better economics. Also, Alphabet's Waymo operates beyond Texas, making this comparison particularly narrow. Tesla still needs to demonstrate strong vehicle utilization, sustainable operating economics and successful expansion into additional markets.

Story Continues

FSD Adoption Aiding TSLA But Bigger Test Ahead

The regulatory push matters to Tesla's effort to build recurring software revenues beyond vehicle sales. Tesla's paid FSD customer base rose 67% year over year to 1.74 million in the third quarter of 2026. More than 75% of new vehicle deliveries in North America included paid FSD subscriptions at delivery. Increasing subscription adoption should strengthen Tesla's software revenues.Tesla now has approvals in 11 EU countries and 19 countries worldwide.

Tesla still needs support at the EU level. An approval requires a qualified majority— at least 15 member states representing 65% of the bloc's population.

The EU's Technical Committee for Motor Vehicles is expected to decide in December. If approved, the decision could apply across the bloc in about three weeks. A rejection would invalidate the national approvals already granted, making the vote critical to Tesla's European plans.

TSLA Narrative is Improving But Not a Buy Yet

Tesla's vehicle demand and margins are moving in the right direction. The company delivered 486,532 vehicles in the last reported quarter, its second straight quarter above 480,000 units. It also posted its highest passenger vehicle order backlog in four years. Automotive gross margin improved to 18.5% from 17% a year earlier. The energy business is also performing well. Musk said Megapack supply for 2027 is almost sold out.

Free cash flow swung to positive $1.53 billion in the third quarter from negative $1.09 billion in the second quarter of 2026. Management also trimmed 2026 capex guidance to $20 billion from $25 billion and secured up to $30 billion in borrowing capacity, with no draws planned this year. And the AI roadmap now has tangible milestones behind it.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Tesla's EPS has moved north over the past 30 days.

None of this makes Tesla a risk-free story. Operating expenses remain high, supply chain challenges persist, and operating profits are expected to decline year over year in the coming quarters as costs rise to fund the next growth cycle. Robotaxi and Optimus revenues still depend on execution and regulatory approvals.

While this might not be the time to buy TSLA stock outright, the stock should be on your watchlist. For investors with a long horizon, any dips from here could look more like opportunities. Tesla stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Jensen Huang was 'broken and shattered' in final hours as Nvidia CEO
news.Content: Jensen Huang spent more than three decades building Nvidia. By the time he left, he appeared to have little fight left. Bloomberg reported that Huang looked "broken and shattered" in his final hours as chief executive. His usual insistence on controlling the details had gone. According to a person familiar with the situation, he had begun saying "whatever" and "I don't care." Nvidia announced his resignation on Nov. 12 and named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. Huang also left the board, ending his formal leadership of the company he co-founded in 1993. For those who are hoping Huang might eventually return, Steve Jobs offers a precedent. Jobs left Apple in 1985 after losing a power struggle with CEO John Sculley. The board sided with Sculley, stripping Jobs of operating authority. He later returned through Apple's acquisition of NeXT and became interim CEO in 1997. But the reasons for their departures are very different. Jobs lost a fight over how Apple should be run. Huang's resignation followed disclosures of extramarital relationships and questions about his involvement with a woman who's a suspected spy for China. Days later, it was reported that he also had affairs with Nvidia employees, which led to his ouster. Jobs was also just 30 when he left Apple. Huang is now 63. A return on Jobs' roughly 12-year timetable would put him in his mid-70s. Also read: CoreWeave stock sinks nearly 7% after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns Age alone would not prevent a comeback. But the personal strain described in Bloomberg's account gives little reason to assume Huang would want to repeat the struggle. People who had spoken with him said his attention had turned toward his wife and the damage to the women publicly linked to him. Still, that describes his current state of mind rather than a decision about the rest of his career. What's next for Jensen Huang Leaving Nvidia will not end the questioning. Three House committee chairs have requested that Huang appear for a closed-door, transcribed interview on Dec. 1, threatening a subpoena if he does not comply. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has separately asked him to testify. The requests concern national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology. Related: Cathie Wood buys $15.3 million of tumbling semiconductor stock Huang has spent years cultivating access in both Washington and Beijing while arguing that American chipmakers needed to compete in China. He repeatedly challenged U.S. export controls, the rules restricting sales of advanced chips overseas. In 2025, he called the restrictions a "failure," arguing that they cost American companies business while encouraging Chinese customers to turn to domestic suppliers such as Huawei. Story Continues Those relationships gave Huang unusual access on both sides of an increasingly bitter technology rivalry. They now leave lawmakers with questions about his contacts and Nvidia's safeguards. An earlier congressional exchange shows how questioning about a company's Chinese ties can turn toward an executive's citizenship and personal loyalties. At a 2024 Senate hearing, Sen. Tom Cotton (R-Ark.), repeatedly questioned TikTok CEO Shou Zi Chew about his nationality, passports, and connections to China. "Have you ever been a member of the Chinese Communist Party?" Cotton asked. "Senator, I'm Singaporean," Chew replied. Huang faces different allegations, and there is no basis to predict the same exchange. But his departure from Nvidia has done little to reduce Congress's interest in hearing from him. The espionage allegations have not been established, either. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy, and Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Nov. 12 that the Justice Department had not reached a conclusion on that question, Reuters reported. Yorkville Ives managing partner Dan Ives maintained his Outperform rating on Nvidia, saying he was "not throwing in the white towel" on the stock at its current price. Ives called Huang's expected departure "a dark day for Nvidia and the U.S. tech industry," but said the U.S. still leads China in AI and other tech leaders will have to step up. "Other U.S. tech leaders are now going to have step in up even more as visionaries with Jensen gone, including Nadella, Sundar, Cook, Dario, Zuckerberg, Altman, Karp, Jassey, Su, Nikesh, Kurtz, and many others," Ives wrote. Nvidia is set to report its fiscal third-quarter earnings on Nov. 17. The stock fell 4.34% to close at $166.19 on Nov. 12, bringing its year-to-date loss to over 10%. Related: Billionaire Bill Ackman's market warning resurfaces as stocks plunge This story was originally published by TheStreet on Nov 13, 2026, where it first appeared in the Investing section. news.Title: MKS (MKSI) Reliance on International Sales: What Investors Need to Know
news.Content:
Have you assessed how the international operations of MKS (MKSI) performed in the quarter ended September 2026? For this maker of analysis and processing equipment for semiconductor companies, possessing an expansive global footprint, parsing the trends of international revenues could be critical to gauge its financial resilience and growth prospects.

In the modern, closely-knit global economic landscape, the capacity of a business to access foreign markets is often a key determinant of its financial well-being and growth path. Investors now place great importance on grasping the extent of a company's dependence on international markets, as it sheds light on the firm's earnings stability, its skill in leveraging various economic cycles and its broad growth potential.

Being present in foreign markets serves as protection against local economic declines and helps benefit from more rapidly expanding economies. Yet, such expansion also introduces challenges related to currency fluctuations, geopolitical uncertainties and varied market behaviors.

While delving into MKSI's performance for the past quarter, we observed some fascinating trends in the revenue from its foreign segments that are commonly modeled and observed by analysts on Wall Street.

The company's total revenue for the quarter amounted to $1.41 billion, marking an increase of 43% from the year-ago quarter. We will next turn our attention to dissecting MKSI's international revenue to get a clearer picture of how significant its operations are outside its main base.

Decoding MKSI's International Revenue Trends

Japan generated $91 million in revenues for the company in the last quarter, constituting 6.4% of the total. This represented a surprise of +40.63% compared to the $64.71 million projected by Wall Street analysts. Comparatively, in the previous quarter, Japan accounted for $78 million (6.3%), and in the year-ago quarter, it contributed $56 million (5.7%) to the total revenue.

Other International accounted for 17.9% of the company's total revenue during the quarter, translating to $253 million. Revenues from this region represented a surprise of -10.88%, with Wall Street analysts collectively expecting $283.88 million. When compared to the preceding quarter and the same quarter in the previous year, Other International contributed $238 million (19.1%) and $264 million (26.7%) to the total revenue, respectively.

Of the total revenue, $90 million came from Singapore during the last fiscal quarter, accounting for 6.4%. This represented a surprise of -1.72% as analysts had expected the region to contribute $91.57 million to the total revenue. In comparison, the region contributed $78 million, or 6.3%, and $60 million, or 6.1%, to total revenue in the previous and year-ago quarters, respectively.

Story Continues

During the quarter, China contributed $334 million in revenue, making up 23.6% of the total revenue. When compared to the consensus estimate of $322.47 million, this meant a surprise of +3.58%. Looking back, China contributed $292 million, or 23.4%, in the previous quarter, and $236 million, or 23.9%, in the same quarter of the previous year.

Of the total revenue, $82 million came from Taiwan during the last fiscal quarter, accounting for 5.8%. This represented a surprise of -6.57% as analysts had expected the region to contribute $87.77 million to the total revenue. In comparison, the region contributed $87 million, or 7%, and $70 million, or 7.1%, to total revenue in the previous and year-ago quarters, respectively.

International Market Revenue Projections

Wall Street analysts expect MKS to report $1.49 billion in total revenue for the current fiscal quarter, indicating an increase of 44.3% from the year-ago quarter. Japan, Other International, Singapore, China and Taiwan are expected to contribute 4.9% (translating to $72.94 million), 18.1% ($270.38 million), 5.9% ($88.21 million), 20.9% ($311.6 million), and 5.7% ($84.3 million) to the total revenue, respectively.

For the full year, a total revenue of $5.16 billion is expected for the company, reflecting an increase of 31.3% from the year before. The revenues from Japan, Other International, Singapore, China and Taiwan are expected to make up 5.3%, 19.7%, 6.4%, 22.7%, and 6.2% of this total, corresponding to $272.08 million, $1.02 billion, $331.63 million, $1.17 billion, and $318.09 million, respectively.

Wrapping Up

MKS' reliance on international markets for revenues offers both opportunities and risks. Hence, keeping an eye on its international revenue trends could significantly help forecast the company's prospects.

With the increasing intricacies of global interdependence and geopolitical strife, Wall Street analysts meticulously observe these patterns, especially for companies with an international footprint, to tweak their forecasts of earnings. Importantly, several additional factors, such as a company's domestic market status, also impact these earnings forecasts.

Emphasizing a company's shifting earnings prospects is a key aspect of our approach at Zacks, especially since research has proven its substantial influence on a stock's price in the short run. This correlation is positively aligned, meaning that improved earnings projections tend to boost the stock's price.

The Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating mechanism, demonstrates a notable performance history confirmed through external audits. It effectively utilizes the power of earnings estimate revisions to act as a predictor of a stock's price performance in the near term.

At the moment, MKS has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), signifying that it may outperform the overall market trend in the upcoming period. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Exploring Recent Trends in Stock Price

The stock has witnessed a decline of 3.1% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's a decrease of 2.6%. In the same interval, the Zacks Computer and Technology sector, to which MKS belongs, has registered a decrease of 11.5%. Over the past three months, the company's shares saw a decrease of 21.4%, while the S&P 500 declined by 1.7%. In comparison, the sector experienced a decline of 8.2% during this timeframe.

news.Title: CRWV Q3 Earnings Impress, Outlook Raised: How to Play the Stock Now?
news.Content:
CoreWeave, Inc. CRWV described the third quarter as a breakout quarter, with revenue increasing by more than $1 billion sequentially, improved adjusted operating margins, expanding infrastructure capacity and stronger customer commitments. It reported revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% year over year, highlighting the company's ability to convert AI infrastructure demand into business growth rapidly.

CoreWeave's adjusted operating income rose to $379 million, achieving a 10% margin versus 5% in the previous quarter. Adjusted EBITDA surged 169% year over year to $2.3 billion, with a 62% margin. However, the company reported a $709 million GAAP net loss, while net interest expense climbed to $846 million, highlighting the high financing costs of its aggressive expansion. Overall, improving margins signal stronger operating leverage, but GAAP profitability remains elusive.

In the past month, CRWV shares have plunged 14% compared with the Zacks Internet-Software Market's fall of 9.5%. The stock has underperformed the Zacks Computer & Technology sector and the S&P 500 Composite, which dipped 9% and 2.3%, respectively, over the same period. Its key competitors include Nebius Group N.V . NBIS and Microsoft MSFT. MSFT and NBIS have lost 2% and 30.9%, respectively, in the past month.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

CRWV's expanding relationships with leading AI companies, investments in next-generation NVIDIA NVDA infrastructure and international expansion further strengthen its position in the rapidly evolving AI cloud market. For investors, the key question is now whether CoreWeave's accelerating growth justifies its valuation and whether the stock remains an attractive buying opportunity after its strong performance.

Infrastructure Expansion Strengthens CRWV's Competitive Position

CoreWeave added more than 200 MW of active power capacity, bringing its total active power to over 1.7 GW. This represents a doubling of its active infrastructure footprint since the beginning of 2026. Total contracted power increased by more than 900 MW to over 4.6 GW. Active power represents infrastructure capacity already available for operations, while contracted power reflects secured future capacity that may require additional development before becoming operational.

CoreWeave also expanded its international presence, with more than 1.3 GW of contracted power across international markets, including India, Indonesia and Spain. This international expansion creates opportunities to serve customers seeking geographically distributed computing capacity, lower-latency infrastructure and greater control over data residency. Management expects active power to exceed 1.85 GW by the end of 2026, indicating that infrastructure deployment remains a major operational priority.

Story Continues

Another encouraging development involved the deployment of NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin NVL72 infrastructure, with initial production workloads for Cognition delivering 4.8 times higher token throughput than GB200 NVL72. The company also announced support for NVIDIA Vera CPUs, designed for AI agent workloads. These developments could strengthen CoreWeave's competitive edge as demand for AI inference, agentic AI and advanced computing infrastructure grows.

CoreWeave is also strengthening its enterprise ecosystem. In September, it introduced Physical AI Field Engineering, an initiative that places its engineers alongside customer teams to help transform proprietary data into production-ready AI applications. It also established the CoreWeave Partner Network, bringing together technology providers across observability, security and data infrastructure. Initial partners include Grafana Labs, CrowdStrike and VAST Data. These partnerships could make CoreWeave Cloud more attractive to enterprises looking for integrated AI infrastructure rather than standalone GPU computing capacity.

CRWV's Raised View Signals Stronger AI Infrastructure Demand

A key factor for CRWV stock has been management's decision to raise its full-year 2026 outlook. CoreWeave now expects 2026 revenue of $13 billion to $13.3 billion compared with its previous range of $12.4-$13.2 billion. Adjusted operating income guidance increased to $1.28 billion-$1.38 billion from $960 million-$1.15 billion. It also raised its year-end annualized revenue run-rate target to $20-$21 billion, up from $18.5-$19.5 billion.

The company raised its adjusted operating income guidance by 26% at the midpoint compared with its previous outlook. This suggests that the business is achieving better operating efficiency as its infrastructure footprint expands. Another key metric is its $132.5 billion revenue backlog, which increased 138% year over year. This provides substantial visibility into future contracted revenue, although conversion depends on infrastructure delivery, service availability and contract execution.

CoreWeave Inc. Price and Consensus

CoreWeave Inc. price-consensus-chart | CoreWeave Inc. Quote

CRWV also expects approximately $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months. These payments can help finance infrastructure expansion and improve liquidity, although they should not be confused with recognized revenue or operating profit.

Elevated Debt & Capex Pose Bigger Risk for CRWV

Despite its strong growth outlook, CoreWeave's financial structure deserves careful consideration. The company's infrastructure expansion requires enormous capital investment. Management now expects 2026 capital expenditure of $37 billion to $39 billion, reflecting plans to deploy infrastructure and deliver capacity to customers sooner than expected. Its debt was approximately $47 billion at the end of September 2026.

Heavy reliance on debt and capital markets also exposes the company to rising interest rates and tighter financing conditions. Quarterly net interest expense totaled $846 million, and management expects fourth-quarter interest expense of $1.05-$1.15 billion. These figures explain why strong revenue growth has not yet translated into positive GAAP earnings. Additional concerns include macroeconomic and regulatory uncertainty, potential industry oversupply, rising operating expenses, customer and infrastructure concentration and limited visibility beyond 2027. These factors could pressure margins, cash flow and long-term profitability.

CoreWeave's long-term success will depend not only on securing customer contracts but also on converting infrastructure investments into sustainable operating cash flow.

CRWV's Estimate Revision Trend

CRWV's estimates are being revised downward. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for its earnings for 2026 has been revised south 2.4% over the past 60 days.

Valuation Expectations

CRWV stock seems attractive, as suggested by the Value Style Score of B. In terms of Price/Book, CRWV shares are trading at 5.17X, slightly higher than the Internet Software industry's 4.9X, but it could mean more risk than opportunity.

NBIS and MSFT shares are trading at multiples of 3.15X and 8.26X, respectively.

How to Play CRWV Stock After Q3 Results

CRWV currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

CoreWeave's third-quarter results highlight robust demand for specialized AI cloud infrastructure. Revenue increased 168% year over year, adjusted operating income reached $379 million, and the company raised its full-year revenue and profitability outlook. Its $132.5 billion backlog and expanding infrastructure footprint also provide long-term growth opportunities. However, the investment case is not without risks. Approximately $47 billion in debt, rising interest expenses, substantial capital expenditure and potential equity dilution make CRWV a relatively high-risk investment.

CoreWeave remains an attractive long-term AI infrastructure growth opportunity, but shareholders can consider holding the stock now while monitoring backlog conversion and cash flow generation.

news.Title: 5 Best Stocks to Buy for a Rising Interest Rate Environment

Back in September, the Federal Reserve increased rates by 25 basis points, and economists are now anticipating another rate hike in December, according to a recent Reuters poll. Bond markets have already reacted to yield curve changes, as the 10-year Treasury yield jumped from 3.97% in February 2026 to 5.31% during the first week of October. It came down to 4.98% by the end of October. Fed's preferred inflation metric, Core PCE, went up by 0.3% during September to its highest reading in a year. Some segments benefit as rates climb, while others carry strong pricing power and balance sheet strength to navigate through them. Insurance players can reinvest their float at relatively higher yields, as indicated by Chubb's CEO in October, who highlighted a direct correlation between operating income and rising rates.

Similarly, Banks have the opportunity to widen the gap between what they earn on loans and what they pay on deposits. With that backdrop, let's explore our 10 Best Stocks to Buy for a Rising Interest Rate Environment.

ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. (NYSE:XOM) is one of the standout names across the energy sector, which tends to outperform the market following an interest rate rise. The underlying inflation-hedging traits and commodity price dynamics would enable the company to overcome demand weakness that accompanies rate hikes. Additionally, its conservative balance sheet insulates its operations from interest rate vulnerabilities. It ranked #2 in Insider Monkey's recent list of 10 Most Undervalued Dividend Growth Stocks According to Hedge Funds .

The company's cash flow generation capacity remains notable, as it generated $28.3 billion in levered free cash flow over the last twelve months. A jump in benchmark rates enables the bank to reprice its new loans and floating-rate assets more rapidly compared to adjustments in deposit costs. This expands the bank's net interest margins.

Citigroup's cash management and institutional functions, including its Services and Treasury operations, benefit from rate hikes. This is due to elevated yields on its float income and cash, along with a higher level of client activity across corporate liquidity management. It was amongst the top banking names according to billionaires , ranking #5 in the list.

Apart from the loan hedges, overall corporate lending revenues have faced compression, exhibiting sequential and annual decline. Microsoft has been allocating a substantial amount of capital toward AI capabilities. So how does that make its Azure platform integral to the broader growth narrative?

There are some concerns around the company's soaring AI capital expenditure, which has taken a notable hit on underlying free cash flows. The Q1 fiscal 2027 free cash flows went down 27% compared to the corresponding period last year, as cash capex saw more than a twofold jump.

news.Title: 3 signs AI stocks may be a great trade again
news.Content:
Many AI stock bulls may be mourning the loss of Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia ( NVDA ), but they shouldn't sulk for too long.

The AI trade may be back, for now, after an early fall slumber. Here are several under-the-radar moves in the AI sector this week that investors may have overlooked amid the outsized focus on the Huang scandals.

Cisco's strong guidance

If AI demand is beginning to slow, you didn't see it in the quarter or outlook from networking giant Cisco ( CSCO ) late Thursday.

The company beat on the top and bottom lines for the most recent quarter. Guidance for the current quarter was also above estimates.

Cisco raised its expectation for AI infrastructure sales from hyperscalers to $9 billion this fiscal year. That would be more than double the results from the previous fiscal year.

"We're executing against our strategy and seeing growing demand as customers invest in the infrastructure they need for the AI or SI era," Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins said.

KeyBanc analyst Brandon Nispel said the stock looks "attractively" valued in the wake of earnings.

Cerebras mirrors Cisco

The AI infrastructure play, similar to Cisco, beat on sales and earnings in the most recent quarter late Thursday.

Cerebras ( CBRS ) said it sees a core gross margin of 47% to 49% and sales of $310 million to $330 million for the current quarter. Analysts had estimated a 42.1% gross margin and $271 million in sales.

"Net-net, key customers remain intact, CBRS is adding new hyperscalers, but the industry is experiencing LPS delays across many providers, which is causing slowness in the OAI ramp and could push timing of revenue," Barclays analyst Tom O'Malley said. "With the level of pressure the company saw over the last month (-33% vs. SOX -14%), we think the clearing of the bear case and new customers should more than offset industry-wide concerns on LPS delays in the near term. The new focus should be on execution of OAI and the new customer set."

Shares surged 13% in premarket trading on Friday.

CoreWeave calms the bears

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) left nothing for the bears to chew on when it reported earnings earlier this week.

The company beat on the top and bottom lines. It signaled strong demand trends. And it fought back against the view that it would need to tap high-yield debt markets to fuel its growth.

"We already have a robust pipeline of customers competing for this capacity. At current pricing levels, 2027 renewals would generate approaching $4 billion of incremental annualized revenue with no additional capex required," CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said. "This grows to nearly $10 billion of annualized incremental revenue when including 2028 renewals. Furthermore, if data center construction across the sector were to slow, installed compute becomes scarcer, and the knock-on effect is that GPU pricing may stay higher for longer."

Shares of CoreWeave are up 22% this week.

news.Title: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.Content:
Alphabet (GOOGL) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this internet search leader have returned -14.5%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -2.6% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Services industry, which Alphabet falls in, has lost 15%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Alphabet is expected to post earnings of $3.14 per share, indicating a change of +11.4% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -3.4% over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $19.81 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +83.3%. This estimate has changed -3.2% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $14.92 indicates a change of -24.7% from what Alphabet is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -0.1%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Alphabet.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Projected Revenue Growth

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Alphabet, the consensus sales estimate of $124.93 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +28.5%. The $434.49 billion and $574.27 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +26.7% and +32.2%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Alphabet reported revenues of $111.21 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +27.1%. EPS of $2.12 for the same period compares with $2.87 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $111.8 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of -0.53%. The EPS surprise was -27.89%.

Over the last four quarters, Alphabet surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates three times over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

As part of the Zacks Style Scores system, the Zacks Value Style Score (which evaluates both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics) organizes stocks into five groups ranging from A to F (A is better than B; B is better than C; and so on), making it helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Alphabet is graded B on this front, indicating that it is trading at a discount to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Bottom Line

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Alphabet. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: NVIDIA Leadership Crisis Opens Door for Chip Rivals? ETFs in Focus
news.Content:
NVIDIA 's NVDA leadership turmoil is creating an opportunity for rival semiconductor companies to gain ground in the artificial intelligence (AI) chip market. Following Jensen Huang's resignation, investors are shifting toward competitors such as Advanced Micro Devices AMD, Broadcom AVGO and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM, betting that the disruption could weaken NVIDIA's dominance. NVDA shares lost 4.3% yesterday, while AMD added 5.9% and AVGO added 5.5%.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and led it for 33 years, resigned on Thursday after two separate extramarital affairs — one with an alleged Chinese spy and the other with an employee — were made public.

Mark Franklin, head of multi-asset solutions for Asia at Manulife Investment Management, said investors are rotating into other advanced chipmakers on expectations that they could narrow the technological gap with NVDA, as quoted on CNBC.

Chipmakers Stand to Benefit

Investors see TSMC, Broadcom and AMD as potential beneficiaries because they face less direct exposure to Nvidia's management uncertainty. TSMC, in particular, could benefit regardless of which chip designer eventually gains market share, as it manufactures NVIDIA's advanced processors.

The rotation has also spread to more defensive areas of the semiconductor industry. Analog chipmakers Texas Instruments, Analog Devices and Germany's Infineon have gained 13%, 12% and 14%, respectively, this week as investors diversify their exposure.

AI Spending Remains Strong

Despite the reshuffling within the semiconductor industry, the broader AI investment cycle remains intact. Franklin pointed to major technology companies' plans for higher AI spending in 2027, with further increases possible in 2028.

However, growing competition and the spread of open-source technologies could eventually make AI capabilities more commoditized, putting pressure on chip prices and investment returns.

What Lies Ahead of NVIDIA Now?

Most analysts flagged uncertainty over NVIDIA's medium- to long-term product strategy, including how its new leadership would coordinate with partners across the AI ecosystem. According to Dylan Patel, CEO of semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis, Huang personally built relationships with manufacturers and component suppliers, helping NVIDIA secure scarce production capacity ahead of competitors, per the same CNBC article.

The Huang saga comes at a challenging time for NVIDIA, as Google and Amazon expand their proprietary AI chip businesses and compete for limited supply-chain capacity. Meanwhile, AMD and other chipmakers are stepping up efforts to capture a larger share of the growing AI market.

Story Continues

Investors will closely monitor management's strategy for navigating the leadership crisis. However, some may view the recent selloff as a buy-the-dip opportunity. Reflecting this interest, NVDA shares rose about 2% in premarket trading on Nov. 13, 2026, at the time of writing.

Opportunities for ETF Investors

Against this backdrop, investors can play the AMD-heavy or AVGO-heavy ETFs for the near term. Some of these ETFs also host NVDA, which is good for the investors looking to explore buy-the dip opportunity.

Examples of such ETFs are AOT Growth and Innovation ETF AOTG, iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX, Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF IGPT, Amplify Video Game Leaders ETF GAMR, VanEck Fabless Semiconductor ETF SMHX, Strive U.S. Semiconductor ETF SHOC, Invesco PHLX Semiconductor ETF SOXQ and SP Funds S&P World (ex-US) ETF SPWO.

news.Title: What's Wrong With Amazon.com (AMZN) Stock, and Is It a Buy in November?
news.Content:
Shares of Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) have averaged annual gains of 4% over the past 15 years and 22% over the past decade. But over the past year, they're up only 9%. So what's wrong with Amazon? I would argue not much, but let's take a look.

First off, know that the long-term average annual gain for the stock market is close to 10%, and a 9% gain is quite respectable. Also, it can be hard for any company to sustain an average annual gain of more than 20% -- especially once it has become a huge company, and Amazon's recent market value is nearly $3 trillion .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Furthermore, stocks of healthy and growing companies will tend to rise in value over time, but they won't do so in a straight line. The lines are always jagged, reflecting jumps and drops. Another factor is that when a company's stock rises too far, too fast, it becomes overvalued and more likely to pull back at least a bit, toward a more intrinsic value.

How is Amazon doing?

All those things are true, but sometimes the company in question is struggling. Amazon doesn't seem to be on very rocky ground. For example, its third quarter featured revenue up 12% year over year and its highest operating profit margin ever, 13.9%. And its cloud computing platform, Amazon Web Services (AWS), is dominant , with CEO Andy Jassy predicting it will be worth $1 trillion.

Still, there are some issues: The company's e-commerce growth is slowing a bit, and it's spending heavily on capital expenditures, such as its artificial intelligence (AI) build-out. Shrinking free cash flow, along with meaningful debt (recently $173 billion), is causing concern among some investors.

Still, I think Amazon is a buy this month for long-term investors -- because it's posting some heady numbers -- such as AWS revenue growing by 39% year over year -- and its valuation still seems reasonable. Its recent forward-looking price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 25, for example, is below its five-year average of 38.

Investing.com — The early November data-center permitting panic has hammered the companies that wire AI servers together. Astera Labs (NASDAQ:ALAB) has lost 28.8% over the past month and Rambus (NASDAQ:RMBS) has slipped 15.5%. Yet Credo Technology Group (NASDAQ:CRDO)—the high-speed connectivity specialist that just posted its seventh consecutive quarter of triple-digit revenue growth—has taken the steepest fall of the three, tumbling 29.6% over the same stretch even after snapping back 25.9% in the past week to trade near $139.80.

The sell-off prices Credo like a single-product cable vendor about to lose its monopoly. MaxLinear's CEO has put Credo's share of the active electrical cable (AEC) market at 93% to 99%, and October reports that Cisco is seeking quotes for a proprietary 1.6T cable program sent the stock sharply lower. But Credo is already building a second franchise in optics, where management expects more than $600 million in revenue this fiscal year. The real obstacle is volatility: with a five-year beta of 3.29, Credo swings on every rival's headline.

Owning the Link Between AI Servers

Credo's moat is its grip on the physical connections inside AI clusters: it designs the SerDes, DSP, and silicon photonics chips that move data between servers and racks, then sells them as fully qualified cables and transceivers. That vertical integration delivers real pricing power, with non-GAAP gross margin holding at 68%. Qualification with five major hyperscalers keeps Credo designed into each new generation of their AI platforms.

First-quarter fiscal 2027 results proved that the franchise is widening, not shrinking. Revenue climbed 115% year-over-year and 10% sequentially to a record $479 million, topping the $470.38 million consensus. That growth converts into cash. Operating cash flow reached $500.4 million over the last twelve months, and Credo paid roughly $679 million in cash for DustPhotonics while still holding $764.3 million in cash against just $26.2 million in total debt.

Wall Street Sees a Double, Fair Value Sees Far Less

Wall Street has stayed firmly behind the stock through the rout. Stifel rates Credo a Buy with a $310 target and Mizuho holds a Buy at $245 after naming it a top pick during September's semiconductor pullback, while Rosenblatt is the lone Hold among the latest ratings at $235. Analysts maintain an average price target of $284.05, with a high of $315, implying 103.2% upside. Earnings estimates keep climbing too: 12 upward EPS revisions against three downward over the past 90 days put consensus at $6.73 for fiscal 2027 and $10.32 for fiscal 2028.

Those estimates leave the stock at just 21 times fiscal 2027 earnings, against 49.4 times trailing earnings, and a PEG ratio of 0.15 shows how little the market is paying for that growth—well below 0.71 for Astera Labs and 2.26 for Rambus. Edgewater Research found limited evidence of near-term 1.6T AEC deployments among the largest AI programs, and inventory rose $62.2 million sequentially to $313.1 million. Nu Holdings shares climbed 3.1% in premarket trading to $12.20 after the Latin American digital banking group reported record third-quarter earnings. Net income reached $1.1 billion, up 31% year-over-year on a currency-neutral basis, while gross revenue rose 37% to $6.3 billion. Adjusted earnings of $0.22 per share and net revenue of $5.82 billion narrowly missed analyst expectations of $0.23 and $5.91 billion, respectively. Investors appeared to focus instead on the company's operating performance: return on equity reached 32%, its customer base expanded to 143 million globally, and management tightened its full-year 2026 efficiency ratio outlook to 19%–19.5%, from a previous expectation of around 20%.

Cisco shares slipped nearly 2% in premarket trading despite reporting record fiscal first-quarter results, as investors focused on pressure on profit margins. However, non-GAAP gross margin narrowed to 65.6% from 68.1% a year earlier, while product gross margin fell to 63.7% from 67.2%, reflecting a greater mix of lower-margin AI networking hardware and higher memory component costs.

Modine Manufacturing shares surged 31% after Bloomberg reported that Samsung Electronics was in discussions to acquire the data center cooling systems maker, with a potential transaction possibly coming together within weeks. The report comes as Modine sharpens its focus on climate solutions following the recent spin-off of its Performance Technologies segment, which was merged with Gentherm. Its data center business has been a major growth driver, with revenue rising 95% year-over-year in its latest quarter and quarterly orders reaching a record of more than $1 billion.
