news.Title: What Cerebras Systems (CBRS) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Cerebras Systems Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record Q3 performance lifted Cerebras' outlook: Core revenue rose 70% year over year to $231 million, and the company reported its first positive non-GAAP net income as a public company. It raised full-year 2026 core revenue guidance to $940 million–$960 million.

Data center delays are holding back OpenAI deliveries: Cerebras said it fell behind on initial capacity commitments because of land, power and construction constraints, not chip supply. Less than 5% of the 750-megawatt commitment could face cancellation this year, and none had been canceled at the time of the call.

New partnerships and capacity support future growth: A Microsoft cloud agreement brings Cerebras' hyperscaler customers to three, with revenue expected to begin in 2027. The company expects to return to its OpenAI delivery schedule in the second half of 2027 and forecasts revenue to triple in 2027.

Front-Running the AI Hardware Shift with Cerebras

Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ:CBRS) raised its 2026 financial outlook after reporting record third-quarter core revenue and announcing a cloud agreement with Microsoft, while executives said data center delays have put portions of its OpenAI contract behind schedule.

Chief Executive Officer Andrew Feldman said the Microsoft agreement, signed on the day of the earnings call, brought the company's hyperscaler customer count to three, alongside Amazon Web Services and Oracle. Cerebras expects to disclose more about the Microsoft deal in the first half of 2027, when revenue from the agreement is also expected to begin.

→ D-Wave Quantum Has Long-Term Potential, But Is Now the Time to Buy?

NVIDIA's MediaTek Bet Shows How It Plans to Defend Its AI Moat

The company continues to expect revenue to triple in 2027, with improving gross margins, as it expands manufacturing and data center capacity. However, Chief Financial Officer Bob Komin said fourth-quarter cloud revenue would be roughly flat sequentially because new capacity will arrive too late to materially affect the period.

Quarterly Results and Outlook

Third-quarter core revenue rose 70% from a year earlier to $231 million, exceeding the midpoint of the company's guidance by $16 million. Core cloud and other services revenue increased 272% year over year to $145 million, while core hardware revenue was $86 million, up 5% sequentially.

→ Archer Aviation's FAA Certificate Is a Milestone, But It Isn't the Final One

Speed Sells: Cerebras Cracks the Silicon Ceiling

Story Continues

Core gross margin was 41%, up 40 basis points from the second quarter. Core hardware gross margin fell to 31%, which Komin attributed to the final shipments under an older, lower-priced customer agreement. Core cloud and other services gross margin improved to 46.9% from 41.8% in the prior quarter, helped by higher-priced new business.

Core operating loss was approximately $33 million, while core net income was positive at $30 million. Komin said the company delivered positive non-GAAP net income for the first time as a public company.

→ Fox's $22 Billion Roku Acquisition Reshapes Its Streaming Business

For the fourth quarter, Cerebras raised its guidance to core revenue of $310 million to $330 million, core gross margin of 47% to 49%, and core operating margin of negative 1% to positive 1%. For full-year 2026, it raised its core revenue forecast to $940 million to $960 million, with core gross margin of 42% to 44% and core operating margin of negative 10% to negative 8%.

Komin said hardware shipments to new customers, including Oracle, are expected to lift fourth-quarter revenue and continue through at least the first half of 2027. He said hardware could account for closer to 50% of revenue in the fourth quarter and first quarter of 2027, although shipment timing depends on customers having data centers ready.

OpenAI Delays and Capacity Constraints

Feldman said Cerebras lacked sufficient capacity for a broad rollout of OpenAI's Ultrafast offering and had fallen behind on the initial capacity deliveries under its agreement with OpenAI. He attributed the delays to land, power and data center construction, rather than chip or material availability.

OpenAI is a large customer and remains a close partner, Feldman said, adding that its business grew in the third quarter from the second. He also rejected suggestions that Cerebras systems could not technically support Astra-scale models.

Cerebras reported $26.1 billion in remaining performance obligations at Sept. 30. Komin said OpenAI represents the majority of that balance and that Cerebras deducted estimated potential delay credits from it. The figure did not include the Oracle deal, which was signed after the quarter ended.

Under the OpenAI take-or-pay agreement for 750 megawatts of capacity, delays lasting at least 90 days give either party the option to cancel the affected portion. Komin estimated that less than 5% of the total committed megawatts could become subject to cancellation this year. Feldman confirmed that no delayed capacity had been canceled at the time of the call.

Komin said Cerebras expects to return to the delivery schedule in the second half of 2027. Feldman added that OpenAI has the contractual right to purchase hardware, though he said the customer's own data centers were also behind schedule.

Expansion and Product Roadmap

Cerebras has secured approximately 700 gross megawatts of data center capacity for delivery by the end of 2027, Feldman said. More than 75% of the capacity coming online in 2027 is outside the United States, including facilities in Canada, France and Norway.

The company expects its Cerebras-powered Oracle Cloud inference service to launch in the summer of 2027. Oracle is purchasing Cerebras hardware for deployment in its U.S. data centers, Feldman said.

Cerebras has begun shipping its CS-4 system and expects it to overtake CS-3 deployments in the first quarter of 2027. Its next-generation CS-5 system is undergoing testing and is expected to enter production in early summer 2027. The company also said it has deployed an inference configuration that combines AMD graphics processors with Cerebras CS-3 systems to increase token output.

Cerebras ended the quarter with $7.8 billion in cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities, and had not drawn on its revolving credit facility of up to $850 million, Komin said.

About Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ:CBRS)

Cerebras Systems develops computing systems and software designed for artificial intelligence and other compute-intensive workloads. Its products are built around the Wafer-Scale Engine, a large processor designed to support AI model training and inference, and include the CS-3 system and related software. The company also offers cloud-based access to its AI computing infrastructure, giving customers a way to run AI workloads without deploying its systems on site. Its offerings are aimed at organizations developing and operating large AI models, including businesses, research institutions and public-sector customers.

news.Content:

news.Title: 黃仁勳下台利空出盡 台股上漲千點 聯發科成大贏家噴漲停
news.Content:
輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳因外遇風波，於台灣時間昨（12）晚宣布辭去執行長及董事職務，衝擊輝達股價一度重挫14%，但隨後跌幅收斂跌4.34%，市場以利空出盡解讀，台股今（13）日開盤上漲逾千點，回到44025.63點。

輝達陷入動盪聯發科等ASIC陣營將受惠，聯發科股價上漲飆漲停4235元。IC設計股走強創意、世芯-KY等漲停。

黃仁勳下台牽動供應鏈前景，其中，輝達約占京元電營收比重達36%，其他包括緯創占21%，台積電占19%。但市場以利空出盡解讀， 京元電漲3%，緯創及鴻海漲2%。

摩爾證券投顧林漢偉分析師表示，受到輝達執行長黃仁勳去留消息衝擊，美股AI硬體股承壓，輝達下跌4.34%，台積電ADR也回跌1.86%。

不過，超微與博通逆勢大漲，台指期夜盤更上漲548點，顯示市場並非全面看空AI，而是資金開始重新選擇受惠族群。

林漢偉指出， 台股周五挑戰週四黑K中值，觀察成交量能否放大，以及反彈買盤是否持續。外資現貨連續十天賣超，但期貨空單大幅減少，籌碼面雖然仍偏空，短線壓力已有緩和跡象。

美股道瓊工業指數下挫189.40點或0.36%，報52297.09點；那斯達克指數下跌100.10點或0.39%，報25366.09點；標普500指數跌26.98點或0.35%，報7592.40點；費城半導體指數下殺57.44點或0.54%，報10506.67點。

A : Stein said ES had essentially zero growth in the first half but expects significant double-digit growth over the next couple of quarters. Mertin added that AT&S is rebuilding most of its plants from PCB workshop to high-end technology, building clean rooms, training people and installing new equipment to enable these products. Q : With Intel EMIB-T approval now public, what is your view on yield progression given reports of low yields on such complex products? A : Mertin said more complex substrates require longer process and technology development and cannot be made in existing plants, so low early yields are normal for these "super substrates." He expects yields will not match previous generations because larger substrates mean fewer units per panel, so a single defect hits a larger share of output. AT&S targets reasonable yields balanced against the significant performance advantages of new substrate generations, and he expects industry technology narrowing with not every player able to produce everything. Q : What changed versus three months ago that makes the Kulim 3 plan more concrete, and how do you tackle resource constraints? Q : Total Kulim investment is now around $2 billion including the Marvell line. Are you scaling back investments elsewhere? A : Stein said the prior guidance was $1.5 billion to $2 billion without Marvell, depending on final line configuration. There is no change in overall scope; figures are simply becoming more specific as building and infrastructure costs are detailed. Q : How does Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum benefit AT&S, and is embedded optics a distant future topic? A : Mertin said AT&S's connection to Marvell is on the substrate and computing side, while Lumentum is a laser optics company. He stressed these are long-lasting partnerships with aligned processes, KPIs and roadmaps over five years plus, enabling AT&S to invest with confidence and customer financing. Q : How should we model growth CapEx and maintenance CapEx apart from Kulim? A : Stein said Kulim spending is fully part of long-term customer agreements with no growth CapEx on top. Normal maintenance CapEx has been a couple of hundred million per year, plus another $150 million to $200 million this year for growth CapEx at other plants, and that should continue. He advised modeling an absolute number rather than a percentage of revenue given the significant revenue growth. 根據Yahoo Finance的報價顯示，截至台北時間13日上午8點50分為止，MJC狂飆12.72%至11,385日圓，今年迄今MJC股價累計飆漲約61%。

MJC 12日於日股盤後公布財報新聞稿指出，為了因應記憶體用探針卡需求旺盛而提前擴產，帶動業績有望優於預期，今年度(2026年1-12月)合併營收目標自原先(8月)預估的1,038億日圓上修至1,100億日圓、將年增56.8%，合併營益目標自314億日圓上修至361億日圓、將年增118.2%，合併純益目標自230億日圓上修至268億日圓、將年增122.2%。MJC並將今年度每股配息金額自178日圓調高至208日圓(上年度為95日圓)。

就部門別情況來看，MJC將今年度「探針卡事業」營收目標自1,020億日圓上修至1,084億日圓、將年增58.2%；「測試設備事業」營收目標自17億日圓下修至16億日圓、將年減2.9%。

金融情報服務公司QUICK事前所作的調查顯示，市場原先預期MJC今年度營益、純益將為324億日圓、240.6億日圓。MJC上修過後的預估值優於市場預期。

MJC並同時公布上季(2026年7-9月)財報：合併營收較去年同期暴增89.4%至327.57億日圓、合併營益狂飆206.6%至114.36億日圓、合併純益狂飆248.3%至80.45億日圓。

受惠增產效應，上季MJC「探針卡事業」營收較去年同期暴增91.0%至323.04億日圓，其中記憶體用探針卡營收飆增102.9%至303.71億日圓、創下歷史新高紀錄，非記憶體用探針卡營收微減0.6%至19.33億日圓；「測試設備事業」營收大增21.2%至4.53億日圓。

news.Title: 聯發科、創意...法人曝「黃仁勳辭職」4檔受惠股 他們是受害者
news.Content:
黃仁勳離開輝達，將對旗下供應鏈產生衝擊，主要受惠者為超微AMD、博通與以Google為首的ASIC供應鏈。投顧認為，台系ODM廠將出現分化，高度依賴輝達的業者承壓，美超微與CoreWeave訂單調整風險較高，美超微重挫11.30%，CoreWeave也慘摔6.86%。

輝達供應鏈短期有壓

綜合媒體報導，台新投顧指出，承接不同平台的業者，調整的彈性較高，營邦為超微供應鏈的主要受惠者，在ASIC供應鏈方面，機構件廠與輝達重複性高，不太會因此拿到新的訂單，受惠者在晶片設計族群，包括聯發科、世芯-KY及創意等。

客製化AI晶片ASIC中，Google出現大利多，Google TPU已經在今年第二季提升至兩年來的高點，顯示超大規模雲端運算業者加速實現算力多元化，訂單提升也會帶動台灣供應鏈。

台積電受影響？法人曝真相

台新投顧認為，對於台積電的影響中性，晶圓代工不分客戶，就算AI晶片市佔率重新分配，先進製程與先進封裝的需求不會因此改變，最大風險仍在於出口管制措施。

高頻寬記憶體HBM大廠的衝擊也為中性，總需求不會因為設計廠變更而消失，只是輝達若出現決策延遲的狀況，也會拖累中下游的狀況，影響拉貨節奏。

明年檢視輝達能否克服黃仁勳衝擊

台灣供應鏈短線有壓，長線關鍵仍在於人工智慧的需求能否維持。法人認為，黃仁勳下台之後，市場會藉由明年的法說會觀察接單能力，並檢視包括資本支出在內的相關數據，確認輝達受影響的規模。

輝達短線已經跌多，過去一個月慘跌超過30%之後，黃仁勳辭職反而成為利空出盡的訊號，低接買盤湧現，昨日跌幅也一度從重挫11%縮減至下跌4.34%，股價也回到160美元之上，收在166.19美元。

news.Title: Musk gives Cybertruck a reprieve, but many will still get refunds
news.Content:
Tesla CEO Elon Musk is giving the Cybertruck a few more months of production. But he has also acknowledged that the electric vehicle company will have to refund deposits to many customers who may not get a truck.

In a post on X , Musk said production will now run through the end of summer 2027 "to work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog." He did not give an exact end date.

That's a reversal of sorts. On Nov. 6, Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory around mid-2027 to make room for its Cybercab robotaxi.

The extension could let Tesla fill more orders. It doesn't guarantee that every customer who reserved a Cybertruck will get one.

Musk acknowledged in a follow-up post that the move may not make financial sense: "This is not the smartest move from a profit-maximizing standpoint btw, but there must be some room in this world for sentimentality or what's the point?" he wrote on X.

For customers with a deposit down, the question is simple: will Tesla deliver their truck before the line shuts down, or will they get their money back?

Musk hasn't said how many deposits Tesla expects to refund or when customers could expect refunds.

Also Read: Elon Musk's Cybertruck decision could change Tesla's next chapter

Musk says Tesla must refund Cybertruck deposits

Musk has been adjusting his plans in public all week.

Days after announcing the wind-down, he said Tesla would add another production shift to try to fulfill outstanding Cybertruck orders before dismantling the line for Cybercab expansion, as TheStreet previously reported .

Then on Nov. 9, Musk said the Cybertruck order rate "far exceeds" Tesla's production rate, according to CBS News .

More Tesla:

Tesla stock sellers should pump their brakes, 5-star analyst says

Bank of America resets Tesla forecast as Robotaxi miles double

Tesla wants to sell a car with no steering wheel this year

History of Tesla & its stock: Timeline, facts & milestones

"We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people," Musk wrote on X.

The statement raised questions about how many customers are still waiting for their vehicles and how Tesla will determine which orders can be fulfilled before production ends.

Tesla doesn't report Cybertruck deliveries separately, according to Gizmodo , so the size of the backlog is unclear.

Related: How much TSLA stock does Tesla CEO Elon Musk actually own?

What Cybertruck customers should know about refunds

Story Continues

Customers who no longer want to wait have another option.

Tesla's official Cybertruck FAQ says reservation holders can cancel before delivery and receive a full refund of their pre-order payment.

To cancel, customers can sign in to their Tesla account, select their Cybertruck order and tap "Manage," followed by "Request to Cancel." They must then select a reason, submit the cancellation request and confirm it.

Tesla says the refund will be returned to the account used to place the order.

That existing cancellation policy is separate from the refunds Musk says Tesla will need to issue for orders it cannot fulfill.

Cybertruck prices rise even as sales lag

The announcement follows a turbulent sales history for the truck, which debuted in late 2023.

U.S. Cybertruck sales fell 48% to 20,237 vehicles in 2025, down from 38,965 in 2024, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates reported by TheStreet .

That's far below the 250,000 annual Cybertruck sales Musk once projected.

Tesla has also been raising prices and trimming the Cybertruck lineup.

According to Tesla's online configurator, as reported by Electric Vehicles , the company paused Dual Motor All-Wheel Drive orders on Nov. 6 and stopped taking Premium All-Wheel Drive orders on Nov. 9.

That leaves the Cyberbeast as the only Cybertruck available to order — and it now costs $10,000 more than it did before Nov. 6. The Cyberbeast's price climbed to $109,990 from $99,990, according to Not a Tesla App .

Wall Street analyst Dan Ives, senior managing director of Yorkville Ives & Co., told CBS News the "writing was on the wall" for the Cybertruck given its high price and weak demand.

Ending production would allow Musk to concentrate more on robotics and robotaxis, he said.

news.Title: 李在明宣示「信任」為核心並改革KOSDAQ，韓政府啟動資本市場保衛戰
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】韓國總統李在明週五(13日)上午親自主持資本市場政策會議，與財政部長等政府財經官員、國會議員、機構投資人以及科斯達克(KOSDAQ)上市公司代表共商市場改革措施。面對近期韓股大幅回檔，李在明直言，資本市場的核心關鍵字在於「信任」，並明確宣示韓國決心實現資產與資本市場的正常化，同時必須針對創業板KOSDAQ市場推動深層制度改革，以化解長期存在的「韓國折價(Korea Discount)」並抵禦外部金融波動衝擊。 根據韓國政府發布的聯合聲明，受外部不確定因素影響，近期金融市場波動明顯加劇，政府將以「高度警惕」的態度嚴密評估市場狀況，並加速推動相關政策以強化資本市場的根本體質。李在明指出，儘管韓股近期經歷顯著回檔，但從總體經濟基本面與企業競爭力來看仍處於嚴重低估狀態；政府將持續推進提升企業價值與擴大股東回報的改革方案，引導長期資金入市，並透過改革創投生態系，確保擁有創新技術的企業能在KOSDAQ市場順暢獲得融資。

市場人士透露，本次政策會議高度聚焦KOSDAQ市場的活化與體質重整。除了研議將上市公司舉辦企業說明會(IR)列為強制性義務、藉此拉高資訊揭露透明度外，監管當局也將針對先前因法院禁令而暫緩的「市值基準退市制度」以及引發市場爭議的「KOSDAQ分級升降制度」進行全面檢討，力求加快不良企業退場速度並重塑投資人對創業板市場的信心。

news.Title: Sandisk Stock Is Back Above the $900 Price I Set for Buying It. Here's Why I'm Holding Off.
news.Content:
Last week, I put a number on what I'd be willing to pay for Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock. My rule was that I wouldn't pay over four years' worth of earnings at the rate management guided for this quarter, which came to around $900 a share.

The stock didn't stay under that price long. Sandisk closed at about $806 on Nov. 5. Then shares soared on Wednesday, Nov. 11 -- the day after AI cloud provider CoreWeave lifted its 2026 revenue forecast.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

At roughly $990 as of this writing, the flash memory company is up about 23% since that Nov. 5 close. Under my own rule, that means I'd hold off for now, and nothing else in the last week gives me a reason to bend it.

Image source: Getty Images.

A buyer now pays for 4.4 years of profits

Sandisk's guidance for its fiscal second quarter of 2027, which is underway now, calls for non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share between $55 and $57 on a pre-split basis. The $56 midpoint comes to around $224 a share for a full year, and four years of that is where my $900 price came from.

At about $990, Sandisk trades at about 4.4 times those annualized guided earnings, so a buyer is paying for around 4.4 years of them rather than four. In other words, the stock is around 10% above my price.

The eight-for-one stock split doesn't change any of this.

Shareholders of record on Nov. 9 get seven more shares for every one they hold, issued after the close on Nov. 19. Trading on a split-adjusted basis should start the next morning, Nov. 20. After the split, my price works out to around $112 a share, while the current price comes to about $124.

Ten percent might not seem like much for a tech company whose stock has swung this hard. After all, Sandisk still trades around 58% under its late-June record close of $2,335.

But the point of setting a price beforehand is so a fast run-up doesn't talk me into paying more for the same earnings.

On paper, a price so low compared with earnings might make Sandisk look like a value stock. Still, I think four years is about as much as a memory maker's peak profits deserve. Sandisk's adjusted earnings per share hit $49.51 for its last quarter, up from $1.22 a year before. Profits that climbed that fast might drop fast, too, if flash prices turn.

Did anything change except the price?

Story Continues

Not that I can see. Sandisk hasn't updated its guidance since the Oct. 29 report, so the earnings behind my price are the same ones I used last week.

If anything, every new outlook has gone up by less than the one before. Management's fiscal Q4 2026 outlook called for adjusted profit of $30 to $33 per share, a $31.50 midpoint. The outlook for fiscal Q1 of 2027 (the quarter ended Oct. 2, 2026) lifted that midpoint around 43% to $45. And the current fiscal Q2 outlook raised it about 24% to $56.

In short, the boom is still adding profits, just at a slowing rate.

Of course, Sandisk has earned more than it guided recently. In fiscal Q4 of 2026, its adjusted earnings were $39.25 a share, beating the $30-to-$33 range, and fiscal Q1's $49.51 topped a range of $44 to $46. But the gap narrowed, from around 19% above the top of the range to about 8%.

My rule uses guidance on purpose -- so I'm not paying ahead of time for results that haven't happened yet.

Two things could change my mind

The simplest one is the price. If the stock drops back below about $900 (or about $112 once split-adjusted trading starts) before I've bought, I'd look at it again as a buyer.

The other is a higher guided pace. When Sandisk reports its fiscal Q2 results, it will probably give an outlook for fiscal Q3. A midpoint near $62 a share would raise four years of guided earnings to about $990, close to where the stock trades as I write.

That would mean a step of about 11% from the latest midpoint, which is smaller than either of the past two, so it's arguably within reach.

But I'd rather see management give that number than assume it. Until one of those two things happens, I'm holding off. The company is still earning more every quarter. I just think a buyer at this price is paying for growth that Sandisk hasn't guided to yet.

news.Title: PwC spots a major shift in retirement money
news.Content:
I would never have imagined a situation where a teacher checking a pension statement would, in some way, tie into headlines celebrating another multibillion-dollar AI data center.

Those two stories seem poles apart. Increasingly, they aren't.

The money that's being pumped into building AI's physical backbone isn't just coming from Microsoft, Amazon, or Nvidia. An eyebrow-raising sum is coming from investment pools backing public pensions, as well as sovereign wealth funds investing on behalf of governments.

Those institutions are doing more than just scooping up shares. They're helping to own the data centers, power systems, and companies that make the technology work.

A PwC study puts the gigantic scale in perspective, and for investors, it might look like an opportunity to participate in an infrastructure buildout.

On top of that, it raises the possibility that different parts of your retirement portfolio might be riding the same AI bet, leaving your savings exposed to the technology's fortunes more than one might realize.

Pension funds are taking a bigger role in building AI

PwC's Nov. 12 report shows how the investment business is changing.

It underscores how the largest public investors are organizing deals and owning physical infrastructure, instead of simply giving money to outside fund managers. That report also puts that scale in perspective.

More Social Security:

Social Security just changed for anyone nearing retirement

Social Security rewards waiting till one age with a bigger safety net

Social Security loses billions to OBBBA tax breaks

PwC projects $36.3 trillion in global public pension assets and $22.4 trillion in sovereign wealth assets by 2030. Collectively, they total a whopping $58.7 trillion.

PwC's Eric Janson says they're "originating transactions themselves and taking controlling positions with operational roles."

That said, the evidence backing it up is much closer to home than a futuristic AI forecast.

In July 2026, CPP Investments committed $1.75 billion alongside investment firm EQT to support EdgeConneX's development and operation of AI-ready data centers. That's capital from the investment manager of Canada's national pension plan going into facilities built to develop cloud computing and grow AI demand.

The U.S. is also a major destination for this capital.

PwC found that $66 billion in global state-investor money flowed into AI and digitization in 2025, with the United States attracting the largest share.

That also includes sovereign investors along with pension funds. Additionally, retirement funds are increasingly positioned to earn strong returns from the infrastructure that supports AI, as well as from traditional investments in tech stocks.

Story Continues

Americans already have substantial exposure to AI through retirement savings

A new U.S. analysis makes that connection concrete.

On Nov. 4, the Equable Institute estimated that state and local public pensions held between $578.1 billion and $706.6 billion in AI-related businesses as of June 30.

That's nearly 9% to 11% of their $6.42 trillion in assets.

Among the public stockholdings reported by those funds, a basket of 51 AI-related companies accounted for 35.1%. The Magnificent 7 accounted for around two-thirds of the reported AI-related stock holdings.

And it's already influencing oversight.

On Nov. 9, CalPERS, which serves 2.4 million members, announced plans to present a responsible-AI investment framework to its board. The nation's largest public pension said AI featured in more than 100 company engagements during the 2026 proxy season, with concerns centering on the energy, water, and community impacts of AI projects.

For someone like a retired teacher, a defined-benefit pension generally provides payments under plan rules, so day-to-day swings in AI stocks might not directly affect that monthly check.

However, investment performance impacts a plan's funding over time, and contributions from public employers ultimately matter to taxpayers.

For a 401(k) saver, changes in stock prices are likely to reach the account balance more directly.

The same AI bet can hide in several investments

Vanguard's 2026 research found that 84% of participants in its defined-contribution plans invest in target-date funds, which typically hold broad stock indexes.

Those funds spread investments across many securities, but market-cap weighting means the largest companies receive the largest allocations.

At the end of September, the 10 largest S&P 500 holdings accounted for 37.3% of the index, S&P Dow Jones Indices indicated. Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft were among the leading names.

I see a genuine two-sided opportunity.

AI growth could potentially lift tech stocks while pension-backed data centers generate income from the infrastructure those companies need. More long-term institutional capital might also help finance expansion, benefiting developers, equipment suppliers, and other businesses serving AI customers.

Yet an investor holding both may be exposed to the same spending cycle in two different ways.

If AI customers expand quickly, chipmakers, data-center owners, and power providers can all benefit. If customers scale back their plans, the earnings expectations supporting several investments could change together.

This concern is strong enough that Britain's Pensions Regulator issued guidance on Oct. 22 , asking pension trustees to examine AI exposure across technology, infrastructure, energy, and other holdings, rather than treating each asset class separately.

news.Title: Cisco Systems Delivers Record Q1 Results, Raises FY27 Outlook
news.Content:
Cisco Systems CSCO) delivered record fiscal first-quarter results after the closing bell on Thursday, fueled by accelerating demand for AI infrastructure and networking solutions.

The technology giant also raised its full-year guidance, reinforcing confidence in its growth trajectory as the AI infrastructure buildout accelerates.

Shares rose 1% in today's trading session and are up another 1% in after-hours trading, extending a +30% year-to-date gain.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Cisco's Record Q1 Results

Cisco reported record quarterly adjusted earnings of $1.40 per share, soaring 40% year over year and topping the Zacks EPS Consensus of $1.33 by 5%.

Revenue surged 24% to an all-time quarterly high of $18.52 billion, exceeding expectations of $18.13 billion by 2%.

Most exhilarating was that this marked Cisco's strongest revenue and adjusted earnings growth in more than 15 years .

Notably, Networking revenue jumped 43% to $11.13 billion, reflecting robust AI infrastructure demand. Adjusted operating margin also reached a record 37.8%, highlighting improved operational efficiency.

Cisco Raises FY27 Guidance on AI Demand

Looking ahead, Cisco raised its current fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $74.8-$75.8 billion, up from its previous forecast of $72.2-$73.4 billion and ahead of Wall Street's expectations of $73.34 billion or roughly 16% growth.

Adjusted EPS guidance was also increased to $5.47-$5.53, compared with $5.05-$5.11 previously and ahead of consensus forecast of $5.17 or 19% growth.

Most encouragingly, Cisco raised its FY27 hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue outlook to $9 billion, more than double FY26 levels.

For Q2, management projects revenue of $18-$18.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.34-$1.36, also ahead of the Street's forecast and signaling sustained momentum.

Cisco's Dividend & Shareholder Returns

Cisco maintained its generous quarterly dividend at $0.42 per share, or $1.68 annually, returning $3.7 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases during Q1.

Bottom Line

Sporting a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) , Cisco Systems remains an attractive way to capitalize on the AI infrastructure buildout while benefiting from steady dividend income.

Record quarterly results, expanding operating margins, and higher full-year guidance reinforce Cisco's improving growth prospects, while its reasonable 19X forward earnings multiple adds to the stock's investment appeal.

news.Title: Apple rises 26 places on the Roundtable 100
news.Content:

Apple jumps to No. 39

The Blue Ribbon Committee committee's analysts rank a company on the basis of its potential to grow in the future, not its current dominance.

Wells Fargo is no longer telling investors to stay away from the AI infrastructure trade. In a new note, analysts led by Ohsung Kwon raised the firm's view on US AI infrastructure to neutral from negative. The change follows a deep selloff. Semiconductor shares trade about 38% below their June highs, and the multiples investors pay for them have compressed. At current prices, the analysts said, valuations imply earnings growth of only about 8% a year. A compressed multiple means investors now pay less for each dollar of expected profit. That can happen even while earnings keep rising, which is why a stock can fall while its business improves. Photo by osamu nakazawa on Unsplash Politics Adds a New Worry to the AI Spending Debate Democratic wins in the midterm elections, including in states that oppose new data centers, fueled concerns about regulation. A stricter permitting climate could slow construction and raise its cost, which would cut into the spending that has fed AI company revenue. The selloff has erased about $3 trillion from the S&P 500. Readers following the pullback can find the names analysts like most in our list of oversold AI stocks with 50%-plus upside . Kwon and his team said the risk-reward is now reasonable after the drop. Why 2028 Worries Analysts More Than 2027 AI spending added about 8 percentage points to S&P 500 earnings growth over the past year. The Wells Fargo analysts wrote that "The tailwind is expected to continue in 2027," and that it largely disappears in 2028 as spending growth slows and depreciation costs rise. Depreciation explains much of the concern. Companies spread the cost of data centers and chips over several years, so those charges keep landing on income statements even after the buying slows. Those charges are real expenses even though the cash left the company earlier. Profit growth then shrinks, just as the spending that lifted it fades. Analysts build their forecasts from spending levels, so a plateau in budgets changes the math quickly. The bigger risk, the analysts said, is a downturn in earnings per share once capital spending peaks. They also pointed to extra supply arriving in 2028 that prices do not yet reflect. For investors, the question is how much of that is already in share prices after the drop. Companies still growing quickly through the selloff are the subject of our roundup of the fastest-growing AI stocks . Story Continues Lam Research made it to our list because it has an average upside potential of 55%. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon kept a Buy rating and a $350 target on Lam Research on November 2, after the stock lost about 34% in a month. Lam makes the machines that chipmakers use to etch and deposit the thin layers inside a chip, and memory makers are among its largest customers. As chips stack more layers, each factory needs more of those steps. The selloff came after a record September quarter. Guidance for the December quarter only matched expectations, and worries about AI spending pulled down the whole chip equipment group. China made up 35% of September-quarter revenue and is expected to fall sharply in December, which is the main near-term drag. Other firms trimmed their targets after the drop, and the Street's average target slipped from its October peak, though it still sits above Bernstein's. Part of Lam's cushion comes from service work on machines already installed, which we examined in our look at its fast-growing support revenue . Memory makers' spending plans decide how quickly orders come back. The next test comes when the company reports December-quarter results in late January. While we acknowledge the risk and potential of LRCX as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Rosenblatt’s Kevin Cassidy Upgraded Monolithic Power Systems (MPWR). Here’s the Quarter That Won Him Over
news.Content:
We just published a list of the 10 Best Growth Stocks for the Next 5 Years and Monolithic Power Systems (NASDAQ:MPWR) ranked 8th on this list.

Technology stocks went from celebration to rout within two sessions this month. On Wednesday, November 4, equities rallied after Democrats swept Congress in the midterm elections. By Thursday, the S&P 500 had fallen 4.36% and the Dow had lost 3.44%, while the Nasdaq Composite closed 5.52% lower, its worst day since April 2025. The drop pushed the tech-heavy index into correction territory, at least 10% below its October 6 record close.

The selling did not stop there, and the S&P 500 went on to post its worst week since June. Truist chief markets strategist Keith Lerner called the action "something of a buyers' strike" in technology. Breadth was thin, with only about one in seven S&P 500 stocks rising on the day of the steepest decline.

Charts

A Midterm Shock Rattles the Market's Growth Engine

The election result mattered for reasons that go beyond party control. eToro market analyst Jakub Rochlitz said rising electricity prices turned data-center construction into a political issue during the campaign. In his view, markets now assume that the artificial intelligence buildout will be slower and more expensive, which rewrites growth expectations for every company along the supply chain.

The damage was sharpest in semiconductors. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12% and the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.4%, the biggest one-day declines for both gauges since March 2020. Readers following the group can find more names in our list of the most promising technology stocks to buy right now .

Rising Rates and Heavy Debt Put Growth Valuations to the Test

Anxiety about AI spending had been building well before the vote. Bloomberg reported that interest rates were climbing, borrowing to fund the buildout was growing, and public backlash against data centers was spreading. Investors are now demanding higher yields from heavily indebted data-center builders, which raises the cost of every new project.

The numbers show how quickly sentiment turned. An October 30 sell-off erased more than $1 trillion of tech market value, and chipmakers surrendered more than $1.5 trillion on November 5 alone. Analyst-driven picks from the same corner of the market are collected in our list of the best aggressive growth stocks to buy according to Wall Street analysts .

Not everyone read the move as a break in the trend. Argent Capital Management portfolio manager Jed Ellerbroek told Reuters that the selling felt like capitulation among the beneficiaries of data-center spending, though the size of the move looked outsized to him. His comment shows that even investors who saw capitulation in data-center names questioned the scale of the decline.

Story Continues

Monolithic Power Systems made it to our list because it has a five-year EPS growth rate of 29.77% and an average upside potential of 22%.

Rosenblatt analyst Kevin Cassidy upgraded Monolithic Power Systems to Buy from Neutral on October 30 and raised his price target to $1,700 from $1,575, pointing to a third quarter that beat expectations and lifted guidance in enterprise data and communications. The quarter gave him plenty to work with. Revenue passed $1 billion for the first time, and enterprise data sales grew 164.6% as customers building AI servers bought more of the company's power chips.

Monolithic Power Systems designs the power chips that sit beside the processors in those servers. Management said capacity is expanding toward $8 billion of annual revenue by the second half of 2027, and a first large data converter design win is set to ramp that year. Consumer sales fell, a reminder that the growth is concentrated in data-center markets, and the company also bought back stock during the quarter.

Investors have started to ask how much of the profit jump reflects lasting pricing power. That margin question is the subject of our look at Monolithic Power's margin jump and why it matters for the next downturn .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MPWR as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Alphabet Draws $5 Billion in Orders as AI Frenzy Builds
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOGL ) has attracted approximately $5 billion in early orders for its first Hong Kong- and Singapore-dollar bond offerings, demonstrating strong institutional appetite for the Google parent's debt despite mounting concerns about artificial intelligence spending. The demand could allow Alphabet to expand its borrowing as it finances an increasingly expensive global AI infrastructure push. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with CDRO. Is GOOGL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. According to Reuters, the three-tranche Hong Kong-dollar offering attracted more than HK$24 billion ($3.1 billion) in orders, while the four-tranche Singapore-dollar sale received over S$2.5 billion ($1.9 billion). However, those figures represent investor orders, not the amount Alphabet has actually borrowed. The company initially considered issuing at least HK$8 billion and S$1.5 billion, equivalent to approximately $2.2 billion combined. The offerings carry maturities ranging from 2028 to 2056, with initial yields between 2.75% and 5.50%, depending on currency and maturity. HSBC and JPMorgan are coordinating the transactions, which are expected to receive Aa2 and AA+ credit ratings from Moody's and S&P, respectively. The move follows an aggressive borrowing campaign. Alphabet issued $80.8 billion in U.S.-dollar and foreign-currency notes during the first nine months of 2026, according to its latest quarterly filing. It also recently raised 6 billion through European bond markets. The financing reflects extraordinary infrastructure requirements. Alphabet spent $132 billion on capital expenditures through September, more than double the $63.6 billion spent during the comparable 2025 period. Importantly, strong bond demand suggests institutional lenders remain comfortable financing established technology giants despite growing scrutiny of AI investment returns. Investors Takeaway The final offering size, interest rates and repayment terms will determine Alphabet's actual financing costs. Investors should monitor debt balances, free cash flow, capital expenditures and Google Cloud profitability. Alphabet's $125.1 billion in outstanding long-term debt at September's end makes balance-sheet discipline increasingly important. The company also faces $130.5 billion in future payments under leases that had not yet commenced. Stronger cloud revenue and AI monetization could justify additional borrowing. However, escalating infrastructure costs, weaker cash generation or disappointing AI returns could pressure shareholder value. The crucial test is whether Alphabet's enormous investment translates into sustainable earnings growth rather than simply larger financing obligations. news.Title: Microsoft Makes Bold Pledge on America's Power Bills
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) is promising to cover the electricity costs of its expanding data center empire without passing the burden onto American households, addressing growing political opposition to artificial intelligence infrastructure. The commitment could help protect Microsoft's ambitious $117 billion computing expansion from regulatory delays, although paying more for power could pressure profitability as AI spending accelerates. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Sign with MSFT. Is MSFT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Speaking at a BloombergNEF conference in Houston, Microsoft's President of Cloud Operations and Innovation, Noelle Walsh, emphasized the company's responsibility to local communities. We don't want other customers to be paying for our growth, Walsh said. We will pay our own way. The pledge reinforces Microsoft's Community-First AI Infrastructure Initiative, introduced in January, which commits the company to covering its electricity consumption and associated infrastructure expenses. That includes paying utility rates sufficient to fund new generation capacity, transmission upgrades and other investments necessary to support its facilities. The announcement comes as rising electricity bills and concerns about grid reliability fuel resistance to data center construction across the United States. Microsoft is already confronting those challenges in Texas. The company is working with Chevron ( NYSE:CVX ) and investment firm Engine No. 1 on Project Kilby, a massive data center and power-generation development in West Texas. However, the project has encountered permitting delays following restrictions introduced by outgoing Texas Governor Greg Abbott. Chevron still expects initial operations in 2028, with full development targeted for 2031. The stakes extend beyond Microsoft. The International Energy Agency estimates U.S. data center electricity consumption could more than triple by 2035, intensifying competition for power infrastructure. Investors Takeaway For Microsoft shareholders, the critical question is whether greater electricity spending can secure faster infrastructure approvals without materially reducing cloud profitability. Investors should monitor Azure revenue growth, capital expenditures, operating margins and progress on major projects such as Kilby. Utility agreements and regulatory approvals will also determine how quickly Microsoft can bring additional computing capacity online. Story Continues The strategy could benefit energy suppliers such as Chevron while reducing political resistance to new facilities. However, higher electricity tariffs, construction delays and escalating infrastructure costs could pressure returns. news.Title: Google's Next Big AI Push Has Apple in the Picture
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOGL ) is bringing its Gemini artificial intelligence assistant directly to Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) CarPlay, expanding Google's reach into millions of connected vehicles as competition for AI users intensifies. The November 11 launch gives iPhone owners another way to access Google's technology, potentially strengthening user engagement even as investors question the company's enormous AI spending and weakening cash flow. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Sign with MSFT. Is GOOGL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Google's new Gemini Live integration allows drivers to hold hands-free conversations through their vehicle's dashboard, going beyond traditional voice commands. Users can ask Gemini to summarize emails, review Google Calendar appointments, prepare for meetings and recommend nearby destinations. The system also supports natural conversations, allowing drivers to interrupt responses, ask follow-up questions and resume discussions later on their iPhones. The rollout is available globally across supported Gemini Live languages, although users must update their iPhone apps and enable microphone permissions. Importantly, Google previously integrated Gemini into Google Maps on CarPlay. The latest launch introduces a dedicated assistant that can perform broader productivity tasks. That distinction matters as Apple increasingly opens its automotive platform to competing AI providers, including OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. For Alphabet, the expansion represents another opportunity to deepen connections with users across devices without requiring them to abandon Apple's ecosystem. However, the development comes during a difficult stretch for shareholders. Alphabet shares have declined approximately 16% over the past month, closing November 11 at $293.45. Meanwhile, third-quarter capital expenditures reached $51.4 billion, contributing to negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion. Investors Takeaway The biggest question is whether broader Gemini adoption can eventually justify Alphabet's rapidly increasing infrastructure investments. Management expects 2026 capital expenditures of $195 billion to $205 billion, making AI monetization increasingly important. Investors should monitor Gemini engagement, subscription growth, Google Cloud revenue and free cash flow recovery. The CarPlay integration could strengthen Google's AI ecosystem, but no direct revenue contribution has been disclosed. Competition from Apple, OpenAI and other assistants also remains intense. Ultimately, stronger user adoption combined with improving cash generation would provide more convincing evidence that Alphabet's expanding AI strategy can deliver sustainable shareholder returns. news.Title: Bill Ackman says Microsoft's position is 'really, really strong' as Anthropic pushes into enterprise software
news.Content:
Billionaire investor Bill Ackman remains bullish on Microsoft ( MSFT ) despite Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) becoming more aggressive in the enterprise software tools front.

"We think they're doing a very good job staying current in terms of enabling a new AI generation of workers," the famed value investor and CEO of Pershing Square Capital Management said at Yahoo Finance Invest.

"We think Microsoft's position is really, really strong," Ackman added. "I think Microsoft's position really remains a powerful one."

Ackman began buying Microsoft earlier this year, and has said he views it as a core holding.

Anthropic, meanwhile, just sent a message to the software space led by Microsoft and its Office suite. The AI company targeted a large piece of Microsoft's business in part to justify its exorbitant valuation.

Coinciding with its roadshow launch, Anthropic released several new features late Tuesday, including Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets in beta. It also pushed Claude Dashboards to general availability as Claude Data.

Why a Wide Moat Matters When Sentiment Turns

A rout like that tests which businesses can protect their profits when investors lose their nerve. An economic moat is a company's lasting edge over its rivals, the kind that guards its market share and earnings.

Moats come in several forms. A company can be the low-cost producer, own a brand that lets it charge more, or hold patents and licenses that keep copycats out. Scale helps, because large producers spread their costs over more units. High switching costs make customers think twice before moving to a rival. What matters most is how long the advantage lasts and how much it depends on the people running the company.

Agent-style AI workloads are speeding up CPU demand, he argues, even as PC and low-end smartphone demand has come in softer.

TSMC builds chips for other companies, and its moat is manufacturing know-how that no competitor has matched at scale. Chips at 7-nanometer and smaller sizes made up 79% of wafer revenue last quarter. Revenue grew 41.2% and landed above the top of the company's guidance, and management is spending $60 billion to $64 billion this year to keep the lead.

The risks are structural. Nearly all of the most advanced production sits in Taiwan, and a handful of large customers account for much of the demand. Our look at whether the valuation can absorb that is in TSMC's Profit Soars 69%, but Can its Next Chip Breakthrough Justify the Valuation?

Google Cloud revenue more than doubled last quarter, rising 103% to $30.7 billion, and the unit earned $11.1 billion in operating income. news.Title: Why Alphabet Stock Was Moving Higher Today
news.Content:
On a day where Nvidia rocked the business world by announcing the resignation of Jensen Huang, Alphbaet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) was bucking the broader trend in the tech sector, finishing the session up 1.8%, while the Nasdaq Composite was down 0.4%.

Image source: Getty Images.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Is Nvidia's pain Google's gain?

The consequences of Huang's departure aren't fully clear, but he was seen as the face of the AI boom and had made Nvidia the dominant AI chip company.

With him out, that could leave an opening for a company like Alphabet, which has aggressively built out its own chips business in recent years.

In fact, earlier this week, the company announced an expansion of its chip lineup in a bid to challenge Nvidia, launching the 8tx and 8i max, specialized versions of its trademark tensor processing units (TPUs) and improvements on the 8t and 8i chips it introduced this spring. The TPU 8tx is optimized for secure and confidential inference, while the 8i Max is designed to overcome the memory wall, or using memory efficiently as compute scales.

With the recent news out on Nvidia, investors seem to be hedging that those chips have greater chance of gaining market share.

What's next for Alphabet

Chip stocks were mostly down on the Nvidia news, as the chipmaker underpins much for the AI boom. However, there were a handful of winners, including Alphabet. One of them was Broadcom , Alphabet's design partner for TPUs, which was up 5.5% on the day.

Time will tell if Huang's exit disrupts Nvidia's execution, but Alphabet is well-positioned to gain share in a fast-growing market if it does.

news.Title: Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji warns bond market volatility could be a key 2027 risk
news.Content: The market may be overly focused on the recent sell-off in Big Tech stocks because of dwindling free cash flow at hyperscalers like Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), but don't lose sight of the other big market move of late: the convulsions in the bond market. It's a risk factor that could return to the forefront of the market in 2027, Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji warned. "I don't know if it's just one [risk for 2027], but right now there does seem to be, if you will, disagreement between the equity markets, which are very optimistic by any historic P/E-adjusted ratio, and the bond markets, which are more volatile and more pessimistic about whether it's deficits or inflation or just capacity in the system. I think you see that argument playing out between the bond market and the equity market," Ramji said at Yahoo Finance Invest. The 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ) has climbed steadily since March, touching a high of 5.34% in early October. It marked levels not seen since 2007. Yields have also risen across five-year and 30-year Treasurys. The move higher in yields comes as oil prices remain elevated due to the US war on Iran and hotter-than-expected business activity data. Taken together, they fueled concerns about further Fed rate hikes. Ballooning US deficits have only fanned the flames of yields. The effect has been a frozen US housing market and a higher cost of capital for businesses and consumers. Insights from Yahoo Finance Invest 2026 Bill Ackman says Microsoft's position is 'really, really strong' as Anthropic pushes into enterprise software Soaring fuel prices will lead to 'a reckoning' for airlines: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby United Airlines CEO is still open to buying rival American Airlines. He just needs a 'willing partner.' Ramji has been CEO of Vanguard since July 2024. He is a former senior partner at McKinsey & Company and a longtime corporate lawyer — and the first external hire ever selected to lead Vanguard since its inception. He spent a decade at archrival BlackRock ( BLK ) as global head of iShares and index investments, where he directed the massive worldwide expansion of exchange-traded funds and managed trillions in passive capital. news.Title: Prediction: $500 a Month Invested in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Will Be Worth This Much by 2030
news.Content:
For much of its existence, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM), or TSMC, has been one of the more underappreciated companies in the tech world. We don't interact with its products or services, but as the world's largest semiconductor foundry, it makes chips for virtually all the electronics we use every day.

TSMC has been around for nearly four decades, but the recent AI boom has brought it into the spotlight. Over the past three years, its stock is up 325%, and it's now the world's sixth-most-valuable public company.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

TSMC has strong momentum, up 35% this year, but what could $500 monthly investments in the stock look like over the nearly three years leading into 2030? Let's take a look.

Could your investment double?

For illustration, let's assume TSMC finishes this year flat from its current price, giving you three full years of investing from 2027 to 2030. At $500 per month, you would personally invest $18,000 over that time. Here are three scenarios based on different average annual returns in those three years:

Average Annual Returns

Projected Value

Total Gain

10% (Conservative)

$23,958

33.1%

12.5% (Historical average)

$25,629

47.9%

25% (AI boom)

$35,156

95.3%

Calculations by author. Values rounded to the nearest dollar.

The exact percentages and values will inevitably fluctuate because each $500 monthly investment compounds differently, but they roughly reflect what you can expect under various growth environments. Which is more likely?

TSMC has been trading on the market since October 1997 (on the New York Stock Exchange), but most of its all-time gains have come in the past three years, during which it has averaged nearly 60% annual returns. I don't see it continuing at that pace over the next three years, but I believe the 25% AI boom scenario is very doable, and investors could see their stake grow above $35,000.

The AI cash flow isn't stopping in the next few years

Many investors would agree that valuations have grown out of control during the current AI mania. That could cause some stock sell-offs over the next few years, but from a business standpoint, the data center and AI infrastructure build-out isn't ending for TSMC anytime soon.

TSMC's business is well positioned for the next few years because it's the go-to for virtually all advanced AI chip manufacturing needs. It doesn't matter whether AMD catches up to Nvidia 's GPU dominance, whether the hyperscalers ( Amazon , Microsoft , Alphabet , and Meta Platforms ) begin designing their own chips, or whether Broadcom has a stronghold on AI accelerators. TSMC is who'll bring their chip designs to life.

Story Continues

Being the only game in town has given TSMC unprecedented pricing power, which it has used to expand margins and drive record profits. In the past three years, its revenue has jumped 138% ($46.7 billion in the third quarter), while its net income has jumped 219%.

TSM Revenue (Quarterly) data by YCharts

TSMC's high-performance computing segment (which includes its advanced AI chips) accounted for 68% of its revenue last quarter, so there's no doubt an AI-specific slowdown would affect its growth rate.

However, TSMC's management has remained confident about sustainable demand, citing multiyear agreements and the rise of agentic AI, which requires more compute and, therefore, more advanced chips that only TSMC can manufacture at scale.

TSMC projects 2026 revenue to be 44% higher than 2025, putting it around $176 billion. At its size, revenue growth rates will eventually slow, but I don't see it dropping below 25% annually before 2030.

TSM Revenue (Annual YOY Growth) data by YCharts

Play the long game beyond 2030

One thing to always remember is that nobody can predict how a stock will perform. Even if TSMC keeps posting impressive results (which I think it will), that doesn't necessarily mean its stock will follow suit. The market can sometimes be irrational.

That said, TSMC is a great investment option well beyond the next three years. Even if the stock hits a rough patch, the company's industry dominance and expertise give it one of the largest competitive moats in the tech world.

Semiconductor manufacturing will only become more important over time. So regardless of how the current AI arms race plays out, TSMC stands to gain a lot. It's a stock you can comfortably hold for the long haul and invest in regularly.

news.Title: What ERock (EROC) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in ERock, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Q3 revenue surged to $153 million from $40 million in Q2, driven mainly by generator deliveries and installation work for Meta's El Paso data center project. ERock posted $8.9 million in net income, its first profitable quarter as a public company.

ERock said production capacity is sold out through 2027 and into early 2028. More than $300 million in post-quarter bookings lifted its contracted backlog to a record, and the planned Houston facility is expected to add up to 900 megawatts of annual capacity by the first half of 2028.

The company reaffirmed its 2026 revenue forecast of $435 million to $465 million and adjusted EBITDA outlook of $3 million to $9 million. It ended September with $549 million in unrestricted cash, no debt, and an undrawn $250 million credit facility.

ERock (NYSE:EROC) reported third-quarter revenue of $153 million, nearly four times its second-quarter total, as work accelerated on a power project supporting Meta's data center complex in El Paso, Texas. The company reaffirmed its full-year outlook and announced plans for a new Houston assembly facility to meet demand extending into 2028.

Net income was $8.9 million, which Chief Financial Officer Ian Blakely said marked ERock's first profitable quarter as a public company. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $12.6 million from a loss of $14 million in the prior quarter.

→ D-Wave Quantum Has Long-Term Potential, But Is Now the Time to Buy?

Chief Executive Officer John Carrington said demand remained strong across the company's customer segments, despite volatility in AI infrastructure. He said ERock's production capacity is sold out through 2027 and into early 2028, and that the company is now pursuing orders for later deliveries.

El Paso project drives revenue growth

Third-quarter revenue increased from $40 million in the second quarter. Power system sales rose to $136 million from $27 million, primarily reflecting generator deliveries and installation work on the El Paso project, Blakely said.

→ Archer Aviation's FAA Certificate Is a Milestone, But It Isn't the Final One

Ongoing services revenue, excluding pass-through reimbursable variable revenue, rose 23% sequentially to $8.6 million, helped by seasonal activity. Blakely said service revenue from large projects is expected to begin contributing late next year and in 2028.

Gross profit was $34.9 million, while adjusted gross margin rose to 24.1% from 22.2% in the second quarter. Blakely attributed the improvement to higher product margins, partly offset by lower installation and services margins.

Story Continues

→ Fox's $22 Billion Roku Acquisition Reshapes Its Streaming Business

ERock is working with El Paso Electric to provide 366 megawatts of power for Meta's data center complex while the site awaits grid interconnection. Carrington said most civil work was complete, generators had begun arriving at the site and installation was expected to finish by mid-2027.

Asked about regulatory risks, President Corey Amthor said the company did not see a delay in the project's certificate process. He also said a site for an Anthropic project had not yet been named and that ERock did not currently see permitting issues that would prevent projects from moving forward on time.

Houston facility to add capacity

ERock expects its existing Hyperion facility to exit 2026 at an annual production capacity of approximately 1.2 gigawatts. Its planned Atlas facility in northeast Houston is expected to begin ramping production in late 2027 and reach about 900 megawatts of annual capacity by the first half of 2028.

Atlas could expand to 1.2 gigawatts over time, bringing combined capacity with Hyperion to as much as 2.4 gigawatts annually. The company expects to spend $20 million to $30 million on Atlas and plans to fund the expansion with existing liquidity.

Blakely said ERock would commit to capacity beyond the initial 900 megawatts as additional contracts are signed. He also said the facility's final cost will depend in part on whether the company invests in more tooling and automation to lower costs over time.

To support production, ERock signed a fixed-price agreement with Hyundai for engine long blocks covering 2027 and 2028. Carrington said the agreement secures supply for existing backlog commitments and provides visibility into generator costs. The companies are also discussing supply for 2029 and later.

Backlog and margin outlook

Contracted power system sales backlog stood at approximately $1.6 billion on Sept. 30, down from $1.7 billion at the end of June as projects converted into revenue. Carrington said more than $300 million in bookings after quarter-end brought backlog to a record; those bookings will be reflected in fourth-quarter reporting.

Blakely said the post-quarter bookings included a mix of commercial and industrial and data center business. Some customers made financial commitments to preserve project schedules while certain contract details were still being finalized.

Margins on projects delivered in 2026 and 2027 generally range from the high teens to the low 20s, Blakely said. More recently priced deals have margins in the mid-20s or higher, but he said the benefit is largely a 2028-and-beyond development because near-term production is already contracted.

Carrington said customers are also facing longer waits for grid connections. Bridge-power periods that previously started at around three years are increasingly extending to five to seven years, he said. ERock generates roughly three times as much ongoing services revenue during bridge periods as it does when systems operate in backup and dispatchable modes, according to the CEO.

Full-year guidance reaffirmed

ERock maintained its 2026 forecast for revenue of $435 million to $465 million and adjusted EBITDA of $3 million to $9 million. Blakely said the outlook implies fourth-quarter revenue of $211 million to $240 million and adjusted EBITDA of $17 million to $23 million.

The company ended September with $549 million in unrestricted cash, no outstanding debt and an undrawn $250 million credit facility. Blakely said fourth-quarter growth is expected to be driven largely by continued product and installation work on the El Paso project.

About ERock (NYSE:EROC)

ERock, formally Eagle Rock Energy Partners, L.P., was a Houston-based master limited partnership focused on natural gas and oil. Its businesses included midstream services such as gathering, processing and treating natural gas, as well as exploration and production activities. The partnership operated assets in several U.S. regions, including the Permian Basin and Gulf Coast. In 2014, it sold its upstream business to Vanguard Natural Resources and its remaining midstream operations to Regency Energy Partners, ending its operations as an independent company.

news.Title: What X-Energy (XE) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in X-Energy, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Third-quarter revenue and grant income rose 118% to $66.3 million , but operating expenses climbed 139% to $169.9 million and operating cash use increased to $51.2 million. X-Energy ended September with about $1.8 billion in cash and investments and no debt.

The NRC issued a construction permit for the proposed Dow project in Texas more than a month ahead of schedule. The permit does not commit Dow to build ; the company is expected to consider a preliminary investment decision in 2027.

X-Energy is expanding its project pipeline, including a proposed 960-megawatt, 12-reactor development with AEP and Amazon, while advancing projects with Energy Northwest and others. Construction of its first commercial-scale fuel facility reached the vertical-construction milestone.

The Ugliest Stocks in the Market Just Got a Very Expensive Vote of Confidence

X-Energy (NASDAQ:XE) reported a 118% increase in third-quarter revenue and grant income as engineering activity expanded, while executives highlighted a construction permit for a proposed advanced nuclear project at Dow's manufacturing site in Texas.

The permit, issued by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to Dow subsidiary Long Mott Energy, allows construction of the project at Seadrift but does not represent a decision to build it. CEO Clay Sell said Dow is expected to consider a preliminary investment decision in 2027, with full-scale nuclear construction following a final investment decision.

→ D-Wave Quantum Has Long-Term Potential, But Is Now the Time to Buy?

MarketBeat Week in Review – 06/29 - 07/03

X-Energy reported $66.3 million in total revenue and grant income for the third quarter of 2026, consisting of $51.5 million in services revenue and $14.8 million in grant income tied to the Dow demonstration reactor. Operating expenses rose 139% from a year earlier to $169.9 million.

Dow project moves through regulatory review

Sell said the NRC issued the construction permit more than a month ahead of schedule. He described it as the first NRC construction permit for a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor in nearly 60 years and the first approval for a pebble bed gas reactor.

→ Archer Aviation's FAA Certificate Is a Milestone, But It Isn't the Final One

Xcel Energy Stock Offers Stability as Electricity Demand Builds

Although Long Mott Energy was the permit applicant and recipient, X-Energy led the reactor licensing work on its behalf, Sell said. The company is continuing engineering, procurement and development work while preparing an operating license application.

Story Continues

Sell said Dow's preliminary decision will depend on its own formal review process, including assessments of engineering, cost targets and operating and maintenance assumptions. X-Energy's reactor design will not be complete before that preliminary decision, he said, but the company intends to finish it before construction begins.

→ Fox's $22 Billion Roku Acquisition Reshapes Its Streaming Business

The CEO said the first project is expected to come online in the early 2030s. X-Energy anticipates an operating license review of about 18 months and may file the application roughly two years before commissioning.

Sell said the company expects to reuse engineering and safety analysis from the Dow project in subsequent applications. The Dow permit took 17 months from docketing to issuance; Sell said unofficial guidance from the NRC indicated an objective of bringing subsequent reviews into a range of six to 12 months. He identified supply-chain readiness, rather than regulatory approval, as a major opportunity to shorten future project schedules.

AEP partnership expands project pipeline

In October, X-Energy announced a joint development agreement with American Electric Power and Amazon for a proposed 12-unit Xe-100 project in Sullivan County, Indiana. The project would provide approximately 960 megawatts of generating capacity and would redevelop a former coal-fueled generation site, using existing infrastructure and its PJM grid connection.

The early work includes site characterization, feasibility studies and preparation for a future construction permit application. Sell said the parties are defining the information needed to make decisions about the project's next stages.

X-Energy is also advancing the initial phase of front-end engineering for its project with Energy Northwest in Washington state, another deployment opportunity supported by Amazon. Fluor and the Cascade Nuclear Partners consortium are working on elements of the plant design, Sell said.

Across a pipeline of 144 reactors, the company has up to 40 Xe-100 reactors associated with identified project plans and development partnerships involving Dow, Energy Northwest, AEP and Centrica, according to Sell. In the United Kingdom, the Xe-100 design was accepted into the Generic Design Assessment process in September, beginning a regulatory evaluation ahead of any site-specific approvals.

Fuel manufacturing and testing advance

Vertical construction of TX-1, X-Energy's first commercial-scale fuel facility at its Oak Ridge, Tennessee, campus, was completed on schedule, Sell said. Interior construction and equipment installation are next, alongside work on a graphite matrix powder facility that will support fuel pebble production.

The company is also advancing designs for a second planned fuel facility, TX-2, and a dedicated research and development center. Sell said X-Energy's TRISO-X business intends to pursue fuel customers beyond the company's own reactor fleet.

At the X-Energy Technology Advancement Center in Frederick, Maryland, the company is expanding capabilities to test and manufacture reactor components. Sell said initial testing is underway on graphite and other components, while a planned helium test loop will be used to validate mechanical systems over the next couple of years. He said the facility's work is not a significant input to Dow's next investment decision.

Expenses and cash use increase

CFO Daniel Gross said third-quarter operating expenses included $93.6 million in direct costs and $76 million in selling, general and administrative expenses. The latter included $22 million in noncash equity-based compensation and costs associated with design and site preparation for TX-2.

Net cash used in operating activities increased to $51.2 million from $30.8 million a year earlier. Capital expenditures totaled $71.8 million, including spending on construction projects such as TX-1; the Department of Energy reimbursed $27.8 million in cash during the quarter, Gross said.

X-Energy ended September with approximately $1.8 billion in cash and investments and no outstanding debt. Gross said the Department of Energy had reimbursed the company $618 million under the Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program as of Sept. 30.

Sell also said TRISO-X President Joel Duling plans to retire from his full-time role but will remain a part-time senior adviser. The company is searching for a successor and expects to provide an update in the coming months.

About X-Energy (NASDAQ:XE)

X-energy is an advanced nuclear technology company developing small modular reactors and nuclear fuel. Its flagship design, the Xe-100, is a high-temperature, gas-cooled reactor intended to provide electricity and industrial process heat. The company's reactor design uses pebble-shaped fuel containing TRISO-X particles, which are engineered to retain radioactive materials at high temperatures. Founded in 2009, X-energy has worked with government and commercial partners to advance its reactor and fuel technologies.

news.Title: 2 No-Brainer Warren Buffett Stocks to Buy in the Post-Election Market Sell-Off and Hold Forever
news.Content:
Is it best to stay away from equity markets right now, given the significant uncertainty created by the recent U.S. midterm elections? Some might think so. After all, stocks fell significantly following the elections. However, it's important for investors not to focus too much on short-term volatility. That's a core investing principle that Warren Buffett, arguably the greatest investor of all time, has stressed time and time again.

In times like this, it's important to stay the course and look for stocks to buy that are worth holding onto forever. Let's consider two stocks Warren Buffett loves that fit the bill: Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

1. Alphabet

While Warren Buffett has historically avoided tech stocks , he made an exception last year when he engineered Berkshire Hathaway 's (NYSE:BRKA) (NYSE:BRKB) investment in Alphabet. Since that initial investment, the conglomerate has bought additional shares. Clearly, Buffett and other leaders at Berkshire Hathaway are bullish on Alphabet's prospects, and with good reason. The tech leader has many qualities that Buffett loves.

One of the most important is its wide moat -- something every company that performs well over long periods tends to have. Alphabet's moat stems from its data flywheel. The company's leading search engine, Google, enables it to collect massive amounts of data on search preferences, which helps it improve results and boost search volume.

Alphabet's advertising business still generates most of its revenue, but the company's cloud computing segment, Google Cloud, has been growing much faster in recent quarters. In the third quarter, Alphabet's total revenue increased by 25% year over year to $127.6 billion.

Cloud revenue jumped 103% year over year to $30.7 billion. The company's earnings per share dropped 26% year over year to $2.12, while its free cash flow was a negative $9.1 billion, versus a positive $24.5 billion in the year-ago period. Alphabet is doubling down on its artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments, which partly explains the significant decline in free cash flow.

Some investors are worried that these investments might not pay off. But considering Alphabet's strength in the cloud industry -- particularly in offering AI-related services -- my view is that the tech giant's investments are justified. Further, the cloud industry remains underpenetrated, providing the company with a massive long-term tailwind.

Story Continues

Lastly, Alphabet has other attractive opportunities, including in the streaming and self-driving vehicle industries. The stock is currently down 9% year-to-date, but investors who purchase Alphabet's shares now and hold them over the long term could be handsomely rewarded.

2. Coca-Cola

Coca-Cola has been in Berkshire Hathaway's public equity portfolio for decades, and it will likely remain there for much longer. The beverage leader checks a lot of the boxes on Buffett's list. First, it is a fairly easy business to understand. Coca-Cola manufactures and markets beverages across several categories.

Simple. Second, Coca-Cola boasts a wide moat that stems from its brand name. The Coca-Cola brand and logo are arguably among the most recognizable in the world. This grants the company several advantages. Not only can it command valuable shelf space in grocery stores -- something that's difficult for newcomers to pull off -- but the brand also practically sells itself at this point.

Third, Coca-Cola generates consistent earnings and cash flow. Even when the economy isn't doing particularly well, this is a highly defensive business that tends to outperform most. Last but not least, Coca-Cola is a fantastic dividend stock. It has raised its payouts for 64 consecutive years, making it a Dividend King, a company with 50 or more consecutive annual dividend increases.

Coca-Cola has crushed broader equities this year, and even though it fell sharply shortly after the elections, it has mostly recovered. Still, even at current levels, the stock is worth buying and holding onto forever.

news.Title: Cisco Systems (CSCO) Q1 Earnings and Revenues Beat Estimates
news.Content:
Cisco Systems (CSCO) came out with quarterly earnings of $1.4 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.33 per share. This compares to earnings of $1 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +5.26%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this seller of routers, switches, software and services would post earnings of $1.17 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.22, delivering a surprise of +4.27%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

Cisco, which belongs to the Zacks Computer - Networking industry, posted revenues of $18.52 billion for the quarter ended October 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.14%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $14.88 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Cisco shares have added about 30.8% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 11.3%.

What's Next for Cisco?

While Cisco has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions.
