news.Title: Apple (AAPL): A CIBC Pick Riding Record Results and a New iPhone Lineup
news.Content:
We just published the list of the 10 Best Stocks to Buy After Democrats' Election Sweep, According to CIBC and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) ranks 6th on this list.

CIBC Capital Markets recommended a list of top stock picks after the Democratic sweep of Congress, according to CNBC , citing a potentially tougher regulatory environment for corporate America. In a report published the day after the midterm vote, the Canadian bank said its Democratic basket was designed to hold up in a more defensive market, driven by a less business-friendly environment. It had built two baskets before the election: one for a Democratic-controlled Congress and one for a Republican-controlled Congress.

The Democratic list holds 36 stocks. The bank leaned toward major technology platforms and multinational companies over domestic ones, and it tilted toward lower-volatility names wherever it could, expecting investors to grow more cautious. The basket also stretches across consumer staples, real estate, health care, financials and utilities, so it is not only a technology bet. Beyond the largest technology companies, it also picked businesses in cybersecurity, consulting, payments, health insurance, waste services and utilities.

How CIBC Reads a Regulation-Driven Market

Christopher Harvey, CIBC's head of equity and portfolio strategy, wrote that in a more regulation-driven scenario, the bank would trim its exposure to the suppliers that build out AI infrastructure and lean toward the large cloud platforms and software companies.

The Republican basket is the mirror image. Its 45 names favor AI exposure, based on expectations of limited regulation and less resistance to data-center construction under a Republican-led Senate. Together, the two lists work as opposing bets on how much Washington will push back on corporate America. Readers following the group can find more names in our list of tech stocks investors are talking about .

Why Data Centers May Still Get Built

Harvey also cautioned against writing off the data center boom. Campaign promises should be respected, he wrote, but data centers bring jobs, economic growth and a larger tax base that most politicians want, and few of them want the blame for losing the AI race to China. CNBC separately reported that some economists see political pushback as a way to let some air out of an AI bubble without popping it. For another set of names, see our ranking of the most promising technology stocks to buy right now .

Not every group rallied on the news. Defense stocks slid more than 2% on Wednesday on fears that Democrats will curb spending, although Wolfe Research analyst Myles Walton told clients the knee-jerk reaction could fade quickly, pointing to past cases in which defense contractors recovered from election-driven sell-offs. Overall, the Dow had soared 1,500 points that day, its best session since April 2025.

Story Continues

Apple was among the CIBC-favored names with the most hedge fund holders, 169 in Q2 2026, and it carries a market cap of $5.03 trillion.

Apple's latest results set records. The iPhone maker posted record September-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12%, and earnings of $2.10 a share, up 14%, capping a fiscal year in which revenue hit an all-time high of $479 billion and earnings growth in the double digits.

A bigger base of devices feeds everything else the company sells. Apple said its installed base of active devices reached a new high across every major product category and geography, and Services revenue set an all-time record. Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh said the quarter produced $28 billion in operating cash flow, and the company returned the same amount to shareholders.

The next catalyst is the product lineup. Chief Executive John Ternus described the new iPhone Duo as the most transformational iPhone since the original, and it arrives alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, which he called the company's most powerful iPhones yet. The iPhone line set its own September-quarter record, and gross margin was 47.9%, including a benefit of about 1 percentage point from tariff refunds. We recently asked whether longer iPhone ownership can still lift profit per customer .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of AAPL as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. If you're looking for an extremely undervalued AI stock that also stands to benefit significantly from Trump-era tariffs and the onshoring trend, see our free report on the best short-term AI stock .

CIBC has favored large technology platforms, multinationals, and lower-volatility names amid expectations of regulatory scrutiny. From these, we selected the 10 with the most hedge fund holders in Insider Monkey's Q2 2026 database of hedge funds, and counted the list down from there.

Note: All data was sourced on November 11, 2026.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? 5 Best Stocks to Buy After Democrats' Election Sweep, According to CIBC

5. Visa (NYSE: V )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 194

Market Cap: $780.73 billion

Visa is growing faster than a company of its size normally can. Fiscal 2026 net revenue rose 15% to $45.9 billion, which Visa described as its strongest growth in more than 15 years once the pandemic rebound and acquisitions are set aside. Net revenue in the fiscal fourth quarter rose 13% to $12.1 billion, and payments volume, cross-border volume and processed transactions all stayed strong.

Spending across borders is a big part of it. Cross-border volume, excluding transactions within Europe, grew 14% in the quarter, a key driver of its international transaction revenue. Other revenue grew even faster, up 40%, and earnings per share on a GAAP basis rose faster than revenue.

The board backed the numbers with cash. It raised the quarterly dividend 16% to $0.780 a share, and the company returned $25.6 billion to shareholders over the year. Visa also says it moves with whatever changes commerce, and it has been rolling out tools for supplier-spend analytics and virtual-card fraud prevention aimed at business payments. Whether larger client rebates are worth the price is a question we explored for Visa .

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 254

Market Cap: $1.66 trillion

Meta's advertising business kept growing quickly while the company spends on artificial intelligence. Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, driven by a 14% jump in the average price of an ad and a 10% increase in ads delivered.

Meta guided fourth-quarter revenue to $73 billion to $76 billion, which would extend the run. Capital expenditures were $34.91 billion in the quarter. Cash flow from operations was $32.79 billion in the third quarter, and the company ended it with $82.45 billion in cash and marketable securities. Revenue in the United States and Canada grew especially fast, and the company said it expects to spend heavily on data centers to keep up with demand for its AI products. It also expects losses at Reality Labs, its virtual and augmented reality segment, to decline compared with 2025.

The spending has a goal. Founder Mark Zuckerberg said the quarter delivered major milestones toward "personal superintelligence for everyone," including the launch of Muse and Muse Wonder, the company's first frontier model. The best evidence is the order book. Commercial remaining performance obligation, the value of signed contracts not yet recognized as revenue, rose 73% to $677 billion. Management guided Azure growth of 49% to 50% in constant currency for the fiscal second quarter.

Other parts of the business are helping. Stronger GitHub Copilot adoption lifted the commercial Microsoft 365 cloud business, and revenue at Foundry, the service for building AI applications, more than tripled from a year earlier as the company found more capacity in its existing servers and chips. Operating margin increased slightly to 50%, and cash flow from operations rose 29% to $58 billion. You might also be interested in reading our piece on whether security bundles can lift Microsoft's profit per customer .

Google Cloud was the standout of Alphabet's third quarter. Consolidated revenue was $127.6 billion, up 25%. Amazon Web Services is speeding up at a size where most businesses slow down. AWS sales grew 39.3% to $46.0 billion in the third quarter, its fastest growth in nearly five years and its sixth straight quarter of faster growth.

Chief Executive Andy Jassy backed it with a forecast of AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. The support is a $578 billion backlog of signed commitments that is growing at triple-digit rates and spread across many customers, according to Jassy. news.Title: The king is dead, long live the king
news.Content:
Investing.com -- There is an old saying associated with the British monarchy: "The king is dead, long live the king." It captures a powerful idea: the departure of a leader does not mean the end of an institution. Quite the opposite. It is an opportunity for renewal, reinvention and a new generation of leadership.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

That idea has rarely been more relevant than today at Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA).

Jensen Huang's departure as CEO marks the end of an extraordinary chapter in corporate history. He co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and transformed it from a graphics chip manufacturer into arguably the most strategically important technology company in the world. Under his leadership, Nvidia became the engine powering the artificial intelligence revolution.

Huang was more than a CEO. He was Nvidia's public face, chief evangelist and visionary. His leather jacket became as recognizable as the company's logo. Investors, customers and employees often viewed him as synonymous with Nvidia itself.

But that is precisely why this moment matters.

Former Goldman Sachs CEO Lloyd Blankfein offered a memorable perspective on Huang's departure, invoking Charles de Gaulle: "The graveyards are filled with indispensable men."

It is a blunt observation, but an important one. No individual, however talented or successful, should be bigger than the institution they help build. Great companies must be capable of surviving their founders and, ultimately, becoming even greater under new leadership.

Steve Jobs and the Tim Cook lesson

Consider Apple.

When Steve Jobs died in October 2011 at just 56, the company faced an enormous challenge. Jobs was not simply its CEO. He was its creative genius, product visionary and cultural architect. Many investors questioned whether Apple could maintain its extraordinary momentum without him.

Tim Cook had already taken over as CEO shortly before Jobs' death. While Cook lacked Jobs' theatrical personality and product-driven mystique, he brought a different set of strengths: operational discipline, financial sophistication and an ability to scale an already remarkable business.

The skeptics were wrong.

Under Cook, Apple became one of the most valuable companies in history. Its ecosystem expanded, its services business flourished, its global reach increased and shareholder value multiplied.

Story Continues

Cook did not try to become Steve Jobs. He became Tim Cook. That distinction made all the difference.

Nvidia's next CEO has a similar opportunity.

Who will be Nvidia's next king?

The immediate challenge belongs to Colette Kress, Nvidia's CFO since 2013, who has been appointed interim CEO while the board conducts its search.

Other names being discussed as potential candidates include Rene Haas, CEO of Arm, and Ian Buck, a senior Nvidia executive with deep experience in accelerated computing and AI.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

Each represents a different leadership profile. Kress brings financial discipline, institutional knowledge and a deep understanding of Nvidia's business. Buck offers extensive technical expertise and familiarity with the company's technology roadmap. Haas brings experience leading a major semiconductor business and a broader industry perspective.

The board has an important decision to make, but it should resist the temptation to find another Jensen Huang.

There is only one Jensen Huang.

Instead, Nvidia needs a leader who can build on the foundation he created while bringing fresh thinking to the company's next phase.

The opportunity ahead

Nvidia's competitive advantage is not built on one person's personality. It rests on an extraordinary combination of semiconductor engineering, software, developer relationships, networking technology and an ecosystem that has become deeply embedded in the global technology industry.

Its CUDA software platform, GPU architecture and relationships with the world's largest technology companies represent substantial competitive strengths.

The next CEO must protect those advantages while identifying the next growth opportunities. That means navigating increasingly intense competition, managing the enormous capital demands of AI infrastructure, expanding into new markets and ensuring Nvidia remains innovative as the industry evolves.

It also means building a leadership team and corporate culture capable of making decisions without relying on a single individual.

For shareholders, this should be a moment to look beyond the immediate uncertainty. Leadership transitions inevitably create questions, particularly when a founder has been so central to a company's identity. But uncertainty is not necessarily a reason for pessimism.

Indeed, the best companies continually reinvent themselves.

Long live Nvidia

Jensen Huang deserves enormous credit for building Nvidia into a technology powerhouse. His contribution to the company and the broader computing industry will be remembered for decades.

But his departure should not become a referendum on whether Nvidia can succeed without him.

It should become a test of whether the company he built is strong enough to enter an even more ambitious chapter.

Apple proved that a company can thrive after Steve Jobs. Microsoft reinvented itself after Bill Gates stepped away from day-to-day leadership. Other great businesses have demonstrated that institutional strength, rather than founder dependence, is the ultimate measure of corporate success.

Nvidia shareholders should embrace that possibility.

The next CEO will inherit an extraordinary platform, an enviable market position and an opportunity to shape the future of computing. The task is not to preserve Jensen Huang's legacy by imitation. It is to extend that legacy through new ideas, new leadership and new ambition.

The king may be gone, but the kingdom remains.

And perhaps the most exciting possibility is that Nvidia's best days are still ahead.

The king is gone. Long live Nvidia.

news.Title: Musk’s SpaceX-Tesla empire moves closer, but China and Washington loom large
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Elon Musk's ambition to bring SpaceX and Tesla under one corporate umbrella appears to be moving closer to reality, but turning the vision into a workable deal could prove considerably harder than selling investors on the strategic rationale.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

The companies are advancing merger negotiations and could announce a combination as soon as December, Bloomberg reported Thursday, although early 2027 remains an alternative. Their boards and advisers are now working through transaction terms and the governance structure of the combined entity.

The prospect of a merger is hardly new. Musk has publicly discussed the possibility, while the companies have already established closer ties, including their joint Terafab semiconductor project in Texas. But the reported acceleration in negotiations suggests the idea is moving beyond a strategic ambition toward a potentially concrete transaction.

The bigger question is whether the two businesses can be combined without creating significant regulatory and geopolitical complications.

SpaceX's US government and defense contracts carry national security sensitivities, while Tesla maintains a substantial and profitable manufacturing presence in China. Finding a way to ring-fence Tesla's Chinese operations is among the issues under discussion, Bloomberg reported.

That tension could become particularly difficult to navigate as Washington's political environment shifts. Democrats, who took control of Congress following the midterm elections, have pledged to investigate Musk's business and political dealings, potentially bringing additional scrutiny to a transaction involving one of the country's most important defense contractors.

There is also the question of how the deal would be structured. The companies are discussing how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors would receive, alongside the governance arrangements of the combined business.

Strategically, the appeal is clear. A merger would consolidate Tesla's electric vehicles, energy storage and robotics ambitions with SpaceX's rockets, Starlink satellite network and expanding AI infrastructure business. The companies have increasingly overlapping ambitions in computing, chips and autonomous technologies.

Story Continues

But combining those operations would also bring together very different regulatory environments, business models and shareholder interests.

SpaceX, which went public in June, has a market value exceeding $1.9 trillion, compared with approximately $1.5 trillion for Tesla. The resulting combination would be worth more than $3.4 trillion based on those valuations.

No final agreement has been reached, and the December timetable remains tentative.

Elon Musk's two largest companies could announce what would be the biggest-ever deal as soon as in December, according to people familiar with the matter. That aggressive timeline reflects Musk's tendency to move quickly when it comes to corporate maneuvers.

The companies have also discussed a scenario in which an announcement slips into early 2027, said the people, who asked to not be identified because the discussions are private. Their boards and advisers are hammering out the terms of the tie-up and governance structure of the combined entity, among other matters, the people said.

Representatives for Tesla and SpaceX didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

Tesla shares jumped to a session high, rising as much as 1.9%, while SpaceX stock gained 0.5% as of 3:20 p.m. Thursday in New York.

The merger would be a blockbuster for Wall Street's dealmakers, creating a conglomerate housing electric vehicles, energy storage batteries, rockets and satellites. The rationale for bringing all those assets under one roof lies in a shared ambition to leverage artificial intelligence across space, driverless cars and humanoid robots.

But both companies will have to grapple with obstacles before they can close a transaction, including how to ring-fence Tesla's operations in China, according to the people.

National security sensitivities around SpaceX's US government and defense contracts, and Tesla's large, profitable China manufacturing footprint, loom as "key dynamics that are at odds with each other" when it comes to getting regulatory and shareholder approvals for a deal, JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta told clients in a research note last month.

The merger would be a major test case for political sentiment following the US midterm elections. Democrats, which took control of Congress, have pledged to probe Musk's business and political dealings.

Musk in October said the boards of the companies had formed special committees of independent board directors to consider combining.

Story Continues

SpaceX has a market value of more than $1.9 trillion following its initial public offering, while Tesla is worth about $1.5 trillion. Tesla is slated to host its annual shareholder meeting on Dec. 3.

Bloomberg News had reported that SpaceX and Tesla were pushing to announce a deal by the first half of next year, with the aim of closing the merger before the end of President Donald Trump's term. One of the factors being discussed is the number of shares SpaceX will have to offer Tesla investors in the transaction.

SpaceX and Tesla already have business ties, including a joint effort to build a semiconductor plant in Texas called Terafab. The companies also increasingly have been laying the groundwork for joint operations.

SpaceX, formally known as Space Exploration Technologies Corp. and based in Starbase, Texas, went public in June in a landmark listing in New York that made Musk the world's first trillionaire.

The company has transformed in recent years from a leading rocket manufacturer and launch provider into a crucial supplier of AI infrastructure to companies including Anthropic PBC as well as a top provider of internet beamed down from space.

--With assistance from Loren Grush and Kara Carlson.

news.Title: Duolingo CEO on owl's guilt-trip reminders: 'Passive-aggressive works'
news.Content:
Sometimes the face of a company is a CEO in a leather jacket. Sometimes it's a giant green owl with a grudge.

At Yahoo Finance Invest , Duolingo ( DUOL ) co-founder and CEO Luis von Ahn said he never expected the language learning app's mascot, Duo the owl, to become so popular.

For several years, the owl has been memed online. Duo recently crashed Apple's ( AAPL ) foldable iPhone Duo launch, giving away free apples. But more often, he can be found guilt-tripping you with phone notifications.

"Some of our notifications … are passive-aggressive because we have found that passive-aggressive works," von Ahn told Yahoo Finance on Thursday. "You know, parents all over the place have found this too."

Business Insider once called Duolingo "the world's meanest app," but in 2026, Duolingo pledged to dial back the "unhinged" marketing — if only slightly.

"The owl is beloved all over the world," von Ahn said. "I think that's one of the reasons why people keep coming back to Duolingo."

The language learning platform's stock is down roughly 8% year to date.

Von Ahn told Yahoo Finance the company has also been able to cut back on costly AI spending mainly by switching from frontier models to open-weight models, reducing the cost of its AI video-call feature from about $0.30 per call to less than $0.01.

He added that Duolingo is shifting much of its other AI use, such as generating learning content, stories, and cartoons, to open-weight models as well.

"We're very happy with the cost reduction," von Ahn said. "We don't think we lost any kind of quality here. … The open-weight models are excellent."

news.Title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan on turnaround efforts amid stock slump: 'I feel called to do this'
news.Content:
Intel ( INTC ) CEO Lip-Bu Tan has been charging hard all year long to bring America's iconic chipmaker back to top-tier status in tech land and among investors.

And for much of 2026, the successes had been quite evident — especially on the sales and profit lines — as tech veteran Tan used his vast network of contacts to secure new business, reinvigorated Intel's engineering culture, and benefited from sweeping cost cuts.

Sales for the nine months ended Sept. 30 increased 18% to $46.2 billion. Operating profits clocked in at $1.2 billion, compared to a year-ago loss of $2.8 billion. Intel's stock price hit a record high in mid-June of $135.

For Tan (armed with a wealth of chip industry knowledge and deep relationships to match), 66, the early wins were validation of his decision to take the turnaround CEO role at Intel in March 2025. He took the role after leading Cadence Design Systems ( CDNS ) for 12 years and working as a venture capital investor, and after he left Intel's board of directors in August 2024, reportedly amid disagreements with then CEO Pat Gelsinger.

"I think you know this is a difficult decision I made, and with my family support to do this," Tan told Yahoo Finance at Intel's headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif. "I thought that after I turned around Cadence, I'm done, and I go back to my venture capital investments. But I just felt that this is an iconic company, and it's so important for the industry, and also very important for United States, and a lot of my friends, even my competitors, they are cheering for me to be successful. Somehow, you find the motivation to do something, and it's not easy. It's a multiyear turnaround, and I'm in the middle of it. But I think I feel called to do this."

But as is often the case with corporate turnarounds at legacy giants, a few bumps in the road tend to spring up along the path back to greatness. Intel is no exception, as investors have been reminded of in recent weeks.

Yahoo Finance Invest 2026: What top CEOs are saying about AI and markets today

Six months vs. one quarter

We sat down with Tan at Intel's HQ — outfitted with a museum as soon as you walk through the doors, showing the company's immense history of innovation — on Oct. 21, ahead of the company's Oct. 29 third quarter earnings report.

Under Tan's leadership, Intel has won deserved praise on Wall Street. The company's execution and competitiveness in its core client and data center compute markets have improved. Next-generation manufacturing execution has steadied, notably yields, manufacturability, foundry process, and advanced packaging.

Story Continues

These are all metrics foundational to the Intel comeback story, and the Street tracks them like a hawk.

One couldn't be blamed for finally becoming a believer in Intel as a viable foundry in the US and a strong competitor to behemoth Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) after several years of losing a lot of money building the infrastructure to pull this off.

But then came third quarter earnings of this year. In recent weeks, Intel's stock has been hammered — suffering its worst single-day drop since 1974 after reporting its results.

The stock collapsed after Intel's forecast for fourth quarter sales fell well shy of expectations due to a worse-than-expected decline in PC sales. At the center of the PC weakness is a shortage of memory chips, which are being snapped up by AI hyperscalers, pushing prices up and causing consumers to delay purchases.

At the same time, an explosion at Intel's Kiryat Gat chip fabrication facility in Israel in early October will cost the company about $600 million in lost sales across two quarters, the company said. The lost sales include 10-nanometer server shipments.

Intel stock is down 38% over the past month.

"We continue to expect Intel to be a beneficiary of rising server demand (driven by agentic AI), and we see upside optionality from Intel's role as a US champion with its foundry business — with near-term traction in advanced packaging, and longer-term potential in wafer outsourcing. However, we are Neutral rated as we believe the stock is likely to remain under pressure until visibility stabilizes and execution improves — and we believe Intel's closest peers AMD, Nvidia and Broadcom offer more favorable risk/reward at current levels," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider wrote in a note.

Yahoo Finance caught back up with Tan via email ahead of this publication.

He highlighted several specific signposts that Intel investors should look for as evidence of progress over the next couple of quarters.

"Intel is executing a multi-year turnaround story driven by unprecedented demand for x86 processors and AI," Tan said. "While certain market segments are subject to cyclical, industry-wide headwinds, like higher memory prices and substrate constraints, we are taking concrete measures to address this by increasing Intel 3 output, improving yields and cycle times, reallocating capacity where appropriate, and working with suppliers to expand substrate capacity."

Insights from Yahoo Finance Invest 2026

Bill Ackman says Microsoft's position is 'really, really strong' as Anthropic pushes into enterprise software

Soaring fuel prices will lead to 'a reckoning' for airlines: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby

United Airlines CEO is still open to buying rival American Airlines. He just needs a 'willing partner.'

When we originally talked with Tan, we asked him how long he plans to stay in the Intel CEO job. He doesn't sound like someone who will be going anywhere anytime soon or, frankly, like someone who will let one unexpectedly poor outlook unsettle his mission.

And to be clear, that's how Tan sees what he is doing at Intel: It's a mission to put Intel back on the map in the US for the next generation. That's why Tan still has all of Intel's engineers report directly to him, so he stays in the trenches to drive the product outcomes he believes are required to win. That's why he says he is up until 1:00 a.m. working, only to wake at 5:30 a.m. for a swim and a meditation session. His only true "me" time is Sunday morning, he told us.

The climb back up the hill after the stock sell-off won't be easy.

Tan is the guy to lead it, though.

"One of the main reasons I stay on to be the CEO of Intel is because foundry has become very important," Tan said. "All these chips that we all enjoy: your cell phone, your PC, your laptop, your Apple iPhone, and iPad. They all need semiconductors, and then semiconductors need to manufacturing in the US. I'm glad TSMC, Samsung, they all move to the US, and meanwhile we are the only one that do the R&D development in the US and so with that, I think there's a role we can play to support."

news.Title: Google Expands Its AI Chip Lineup as Nvidia CEO Resigns. What It Means for the AI Trade.
news.Content:
The artificial intelligence (AI) boom has turned Nvidia (NVDA) into one of the biggest winners on Wall Street, with its powerful graphics processing units (GPUs) becoming the backbone of the global AI infrastructure buildout. But as demand for AI computing continues to surge, competition for a share of this lucrative market is intensifying. Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Google is among the companies stepping up efforts to challenge Nvidia's dominance, and the latest expansion of its custom AI chip lineup suggests the battle for AI computing supremacy is entering a new phase.

Google's announcement came at a particularly sensitive moment for Nvidia. Just as the search giant unveiled its latest AI hardware, Nvidia was grappling with a controversy surrounding then-CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affairs. The revelations triggered a sharp selloff in NVDA shares, and the turmoil culminated in Huang's resignation on Thursday.

More News from Barchart

Dear SpaceX Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 13

Oracle Stock Just Scored a New $325 Price Target

Nvidia Stock Plunges After Hours as Reports of a Second Jensen Huang Relationship Could Force the CEO Out

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

But the implications extend well beyond Nvidia. Google's latest move and Huang's sudden resignation come as investors reassess the AI trade following a period of heightened volatility. Could intensifying competition and the loss of Nvidia's longtime leader undermine the chipmaker's investment case, or might these developments ultimately create new opportunities across the broader AI ecosystem? Let's take a closer look.

Google's New TPU Systems Signal a Bigger Push Into the AI Chip Market

On Monday, Alphabet's Google unveiled two new versions of its tensor processing units (TPUs), custom-designed chips used to develop and run AI software. The announcement came as market leader Nvidia was grappling with a leadership crisis that ultimately led to the immediate resignation of CEO Jensen Huang.

Google said it expanded its eighth-generation TPU lineup with two new systems, the TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max:

The TPU 8tx was developed for government agencies and regulated industries that need to process sensitive information securely. It features hardware-level data protection and AMD's (AMD) EPYC processors, making it suitable for applications with strict security requirements. The system also allows developers to fine-tune models and train AI agents without having to transfer data between separate computing clusters.

The TPU 8i Max combines two TPU 8i chips into a single package to deliver greater computing power and memory capacity. It is designed for workloads such as advanced coding assistants, complex reasoning tasks, and AI agents that process vast amounts of information. The chip also aims to address the so-called "memory wall," a bottleneck that can limit the performance of large AI models.

Story Continues

Importantly, these are new system configurations based on existing TPU silicon rather than entirely new chip architectures. The TPU 8tx uses the same silicon as the training-focused TPU 8t, combines it with custom fifth-generation AMD EPYC CPU hosts, and incorporates the Boardfly network originally developed for the TPU 8i. Meanwhile, the TPU 8i Max combines two standard TPU 8i chips into a single package, as noted earlier. Google chip chief Amin Vahdat told Bloomberg in an interview that the company reconfigured the chips to handle workloads customers had been requesting. That means Google can respond more quickly to evolving customer needs by adjusting the systems built around its current line of processors rather than developing new chips from scratch.

The company introduced its original TPU 8 chips, developed in partnership with Broadcom (AVGO), earlier this year. The latest additions bring the number of TPU systems unveiled this year to four, highlighting a faster pace of product development at Google's chip division. Previously, the division introduced a new AI processor every two years.

The expanded lineup comes just as Google ramps up efforts to market its AI hardware. The company recently announced that its TPUs would become available on Oracle's cloud infrastructure platform beginning in 2027.

All of this tells us that Google wants a bigger slice of the pie in the lucrative AI chip market. And for good reason. According to Bloomberg Intelligence, Google's TPU sales, including related software and hardware, are projected to exceed $135 billion by 2028, up from an estimated $12 billion this year. And that forecast doesn't even include revenue from customers accessing the chips through Google Cloud.

Nvidia's Woes Complicate the Picture

As Google intensifies its challenge to Nvidia's dominance in the AI chip market, the chip giant has endured a rough few days, and the worst may still be ahead. NVDA shares plunged a combined 9.7% on Monday and Tuesday following revelations that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of spying for China. The stock staged a modest rebound on Wednesday, but the controversy surrounding Huang deepened shortly after the closing bell. The New York Times reported that Huang had also disclosed a second relationship with an Nvidia executive. That appears to have been the final straw, as the chipmaker's board announced Huang's immediate resignation as president and CEO on Thursday, sending the stock down more than 4% at the time of writing.

On Sunday, Nvidia's board launched an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang following his admission of an affair with a woman described in multiple reports as a suspected Chinese spy. The Wall Street Journal earlier reported that U.S. officials determined last year that Chinese national Alice Huang had been passing information to the Chinese government while working with Nvidia on data center development in Asia. Authorities in Singapore and Taiwan suspected that she had been recruited by Chinese intelligence services after discovering what they believed was a close relationship between her and Nvidia's CEO. Nvidia's board hired Joon H. Kim, a partner at Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to investigate whether Jensen Huang shared sensitive national-security information or confidential company information with Alice Huang. Separately, U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was also looking into the relationship.

On Wednesday, The New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee in addition to one with the suspected Chinese spy. The employee was identified in the report as Kimberly Powell, a senior executive who heads the company's healthcare business. Shortly afterward, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to oust Huang as CEO. And what seemed unthinkable just a week ago became a reality on Thursday: Jensen Huang, the face of the AI boom, was out at Nvidia.

Google's New TPUs Could Threaten Nvidia's AI Chip Pricing Power

But let's set aside the drama surrounding Huang and look at what Google's latest TPU move means for the chip giant, all else being equal.

Nvidia's GPUs have become the default choice for many AI developers thanks to their processing power, well-established CUDA software ecosystem, and widespread adoption. However, not every AI workload requires the same type of processor. Training a massive foundation model, running an AI chatbot, processing sensitive medical data, and powering an autonomous coding agent can each place very different demands on hardware.

And that opens the door for specialized chips. For example, Google's TPU 8i Max is designed for workloads requiring massive context windows, while the TPU 8tx targets applications that demand strong security safeguards. If these systems deliver better performance per dollar or per watt for their intended workloads, customers could have a compelling reason to choose them over Nvidia's GPUs.

With that, the key takeaway for NVDA investors is that intensifying competition could gradually erode the company's pricing power in the AI computing market. Even as Nvidia continues to sell more chips, its gross margins could come under pressure if customers gain access to credible, lower-cost alternatives. Still, the chipmaker's most pressing challenge now is finding a successor capable of executing as effectively as Huang did. Despite hitting NVDA stock with a downgrade, StoneX analysts expect no impact on Nvidia's revenue or EPS estimates through 2028 from Huang's resignation but warn that longer-term visibility has diminished. Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.

What Google's TPU Push and Huang's Exit Mean for the AI Trade

Beyond the implications for Nvidia, Google's latest TPU expansion highlights an important shift in the broader AI investment landscape. As AI workloads become more diverse, demand for specialized processors and supporting hardware could pick up. Google's decision to incorporate AMD EPYC CPUs into its TPU 8tx system is a good example, showing how the rise of custom AI accelerators could create new opportunities for other chipmakers.

But an even bigger question is what Huang's resignation means for the broader AI trade. For starters, AI demand shows no signs of slowing and will likely strengthen further regardless of who takes the helm at Nvidia. CoreWeave's (CRWV) earnings report on Tuesday, along with a Bloomberg report that OpenAI's quarterly revenue topped $10 billion for the first time, provided the latest evidence that AI demand remains strong. Nvidia's rivals, meanwhile, could seize the opportunity to gain market share while the chip giant grapples with leadership turmoil. That helps explain why shares of Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom are trading higher at the time of writing.

Finally, smaller AI cloud companies that have relied on Nvidia's financial backing may face the greatest risk, as it remains to be seen whether a new CEO will continue Huang's investment strategy, which has become known on Wall Street as "circular financing."

news.Title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has Nearly $110 Billion Invested in These 2 Tech Stocks
news.Content:
Since Greg Abel took over the reins at Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA)(NYSE: BRKB) after longtime CEO Warren Buffett retired at the end of last year, the company has made notable portfolio changes. It got rid of stakes in blue chips like Amazon and UnitedHealth Group , but kept Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) as its top holding and turned its stake in Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) up a notch.

As of June 30, Berkshire owns 227,917,808 Apple shares, worth around $79.4 billion at its Nov. 10 share price. It also owns 105,979,600 shares of Alphabet (both share classes), worth around $30.4 billion. Together, they make up over 30% of Berkshire's stock portfolio.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Given Berkshire's investing record and its bullish stance on both companies, should investors follow suit? I believe so.

Apple is picking up steam again

Berkshire started selling a lot of its Apple shares in 2024 and 2025, dropping from around 915 million shares at its mid-2023 peak to nearly 228 million today. Berkshire hasn't bought or sold Apple shares since Abel took over, so it seems Abel is comfortable holding steady.

So far this year, not selling definitely seems like the smart route because Apple's stock is thriving. Through Nov. 10, it's up over 28%, leading all " Magnificent Seven " stocks by a nice margin. It's also up 7% since John Ternus replaced longtime CEO Tim Cook on Sept. 1.

Part of the reason Apple's stock has been thriving is that investors are shying away from some major tech stocks that are spending aggressively on AI and are embracing the stability and predictability that come with Apple. During the earlier phases of the current AI boom, Apple got a lot of flak for seemingly lagging in the arms race. Now, its discipline is paying off.

Apple's revenue growth has been unimpressive leading up to this year, but it has accelerated a bit. In its fiscal 2026 (ended Sept. 26), the company generated $478.8 billion in revenue, up 15% year over year, and increased its earnings per share (EPS) by 20% to $8.98.

AAPL Revenue (Annual YoY Growth) data by YCharts

Apple noted that it sold the most iPhones in company history in its September-ended quarter, an encouraging sign that the company still has momentum with its main moneymaker.

Its stronghold on consumer hardware should remain strong. It won't have the revenue and earnings growth you're seeing from companies like Nvidia and other AI standouts. Still, I expect it to continue delivering good long-term returns.

Story Continues

Buy the Alphabet dip?

Berkshire first began investing in Alphabet when Buffett was still in charge, but it has doubled down since Abel took over. After adding over 60 million shares this year, it's now Berkshire's fourth-largest holding behind Apple, American Express , and Coca-Cola .

Unfortunately, Alphabet's stock has been on the opposite trajectory of Apple's. It's down over 8% this year, including an 18% drop over the past month. Regardless, now seems like the time to buy the dip rather than take it as a warning sign to jump ship.

Much of Alphabet's stock struggles can be tied to its huge spending on building out data centers and other AI infrastructure, and to investors worrying whether Alphabet will get a good enough return on those investments. An earnings miss doesn't help, either.

In the third quarter, Alphabet missed both revenue and earnings estimates for the first time in years, though revenue was up 25%. It also spent $51.4 billion in capital expenditures, with a full-year projection between $195 billion and $205 billion. That would be well over double the $91.5 billion it spent in 2025.

GOOGL Capital Expenditures (Annual) data by YCharts

Alphabet's spending might not be ideal, but its cloud growth is a sign that it has at least something to show for it. Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.7 billion, far outpacing the growth of both Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure.

Search remains Alphabet's bread and butter, accounting for half of its revenue. It's the engine that keeps money flowing in, but Google Cloud will be Alphabet's main growth driver for the foreseeable future. As long as it continues to deliver strong growth, investors can afford to be more forgiving of Alphabet's spending, especially for a company with $265.1 billion in cash and short-term investments.

Alphabet's competitive moat and value (the cheapest of the Magnificent Seven by price-to-earnings ratio) make it a no-brainer for long-term investors.

news.Title: Nvidia succession uncertainty opens door for Google TPU and Broadcom, analyst says
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Alphabet's tensor processing units, alongside key development partners Broadcom and MediaTek, stand to emerge as the primary beneficiaries of the sudden leadership shakeup at Nvidia, according to TF International Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo. NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) shares dropped 4.9% on Thursday after Chief Executive Jensen Huang resigned with immediate effect, ending his 33-year tenure amid a governance crisis stemming from reports of two extramarital relationships and potential national-security scrutiny.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

Kuo noted that succession uncertainty at the artificial intelligence leader creates an immediate opening for Google's custom silicon ecosystem to "win more trust from customers and the supply chain." Consequently, he indicated that Alphabet's key design and manufacturing partners, Broadcom and MediaTek, "could be the market's near-term focus" as hyperscalers weigh alternative compute options.

Market trading reflected this rotation, with Broadcom Inc (NASDAQ:AVGO) gaining 5.8%, Alphabet Inc Class A (NASDAQ:GOOGL) shares advancing 2.8%, and rival chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices Inc (NASDAQ:AMD) climbing 5.4%. By contrast, MediaTek Inc (TW:2454) closed 3.5% lower in earlier Taiwan trading prior to the broader U.S. session reaction.

Turning to Nvidia's own trajectory, Kuo suggested that Huang's exit represents "a one-time clearing event" for the stock, meaning near-term negative catalysts are largely priced in. Because the co-founder has formally severed ties with the company, the analyst noted that "Congress summoning him and any follow-up investigations should have less impact on Nvidia's stock from here."

Inside the chipmaker, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has assumed the role of interim chief executive as the board evaluates a permanent successor. Kuo projected that any organizational restructuring stemming from the formal transition "will likely start affecting Nvidia's product development and competitiveness in 2028 at the earliest."

Story Continues

In the meantime, supply chain checks will center on whether component makers alter their aggressive "capacity pre-booking and spec upgrades," which Huang utilized to maintain rapid commercial iteration. Kuo emphasized that monitoring shifts in capacity expansion and new technology development is critical, as these commitments remain "among the core reasons Nvidia's supply chain trades at high P/E multiples."

Addressing geopolitical headwinds, Kuo observed that the proportion of AI chip revenue reaching Chinese buyers may exceed official disclosures, though tightening U.S. restrictions are unlikely to erase underlying demand. Even under stricter rules, he noted that "Chinese buyers may still pay the premium, even at several times the price, and get Nvidia chips/racks through indirect routes" so long as overseas resale channels persist.

The leadership vacuum also prompted U.S. President Donald Trump to suggest on social media that former Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook would be a worthwhile replacement to helm Nvidia. While Kuo acknowledged that Cook's operational discipline would shine in "cost management" given Nvidia's "clear room for improvement in supply chain and cost management," he maintained that Huang remains uniquely proven in bringing cutting-edge technologies into AI chips while sustaining a "fast pace of commercial iteration."

news.Title: Prediction: This Will Be Intel’s Stock Price After 1 Year (Hint: It Implies a Nice Jump)
news.Content:
Shares of Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) delivered incredible gains to investors in the first half of 2026, but have seen significant volatility in recent months.

As it turns out, Intel stock has retreated 51% since the beginning of July. The past few days have been even more brutal for Intel investors, with the stock plunging big time following the release of its third-quarter results on Oct. 29. However, Intel's pullback could be an opportunity for savvy investors to buy a top semiconductor stock at an attractive valuation, especially given its solid upside potential.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's take a closer look at Intel's prospects and valuation to check how much upside it could deliver over the coming year.

Image source: Getty Images.

Intel's data center business will drive stronger growth in 2027

When Intel released its Q3 results, the company reported a solid 21% increase in revenue from the year-ago period to $16.5 billion. The company's non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) jumped by an incredible 126% from the year-ago period to $0.52.

Intel delivered such impressive growth despite a 5% decline in revenue from its client computing and physical artificial intelligence (AI) business segment. It is worth noting that this business is a key source of revenue for Intel, accounting for nearly half its top line in Q3. The ongoing weakness in the PC market, along with Intel's market share losses to Advanced Micro Devices , explains why Chipzilla's sales in this segment dropped last quarter.

The bad news for Intel investors is that the PC market's decline is here to stay. Counterpoint Research notes that PC sales dropped by 21% last quarter, and the Q4 decline is likely to be steeper at 27%. Higher costs of memory and other components are taking a toll on this market. The positive news is that Intel expects the PC decline to ease in 2027, with unit shipments predicted to drop by 10%.

However, the biggest takeaway from Intel's quarterly report is the impressive growth in the company's data center business. Its data center and AI revenue increased by an incredible 78% from the year-ago period to $7.3 billion, helping lift the company's top and bottom lines. Looking ahead, Intel expects the data center business to sustain its solid momentum in 2027, driven primarily by the healthy demand for server central processing units (CPUs).

Story Continues

Intel noted on the latest earnings call that its Granite Rapids server CPUs have "become one of the fastest ramping server products." Meanwhile, the company is already witnessing strong demand for its first Intel 18A server CPU codenamed Clearwater Forest, which will start shipping next year. Overall, Intel's server CPU business seems poised for healthy growth in 2027, driven by partnerships with major AI infrastructure players such as Oracle .

Intel points out that the total addressable market (TAM) for server CPUs could increase from the current $40 billion to more than $200 billion over the next five years, as these chips are used to handle agentic AI and inference workloads. As such, I won't be surprised to see Intel's DCAI business sustain solid growth in 2027 and beyond, boosting the company's overall growth as it starts accounting for a larger share of its business.

An attractive valuation and solid earnings growth make the stock a no-brainer buy

Intel trades at 37 times forward earnings, which is quite attractive for a company that delivered triple-digit earnings growth last quarter. What's more, even though Intel's Q4 guidance turned out to be weaker than expected, investors will do well to note that the company will still deliver respectable earnings growth.

Intel's Q4 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $0.25 is significantly lower than the consensus estimate of $0.43, but it implies a 66% increase from the year-ago period. For the full year, analysts are expecting Intel's EPS to increase by a whopping 254% to $1.49. Analysts expect Intel's EPS growth to slow down to 20% in 2027, but that may not be the case due to potential price hikes in server CPUs.

As a result, Intel could step on the gas over the coming year. Even Wall Street is bullish about the stock's trajectory, with Intel's 12-month median price target of $88 implying 41% upside. This AI stock could indeed deliver solid gains by outpacing Wall Street's growth expectations, thereby encouraging the market to reward it with a premium valuation.

After all, Intel trades in line with the iShares Semiconductor ETF , an exchange-traded fund that tracks the semiconductor industry and has a price-to-earnings ratio of 37. So, it seems like a good idea to accumulate Intel while it remains beaten down, as its improving data center prospects could supercharge the stock in 2027.

news.Title: 3 Unstoppable Dow Stocks to Buy in November and Hold for the Next Decade
news.Content:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) is up about 9% this year through Nov. 9. The index tracks 30 of the largest U.S. companies, picked by a committee that typically adds a stock only if the company has an excellent reputation and sustained growth. That makes the Dow a great place to hunt for truly unstoppable stocks that have the financial strength and business durability to keep growing over the long term.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)(NASDAQ:GOOG), and Home Depot (NYSE:HD) fit that description. Here's why these Dow stocks are worth buying in November and holding for the next decade.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Amazon

Amazon shares are up about 17% year to date through Nov. 9, beating the Dow. Its cloud computing arm, Amazon Web Services (AWS), grew sales 39% year over year to $46 billion last quarter, and CEO Andy Jassy believes AWS can become "a trillion-dollar revenue business in the next five to 10 years."

AWS alone could justify holding the stock, but Amazon still has significant growth in its online retail business. Nearly 80% of retail still happens in physical stores. That provides a long runway of growth for Amazon's online store.

Its artificial intelligence (AI) expertise from AWS can help it unlock that opportunity. U.S. shoppers who use Alexa for Shopping, Amazon's AI assistant, spend 50% more per order than non-users. And it's still seeing growing usage, with customer interactions up 570% year over year in Q3.

Amazon is pursuing these opportunities while becoming more profitable. Trailing-12-month operating cash flow rose 29% to $168 billion. Amazon also holds about $114 billion in cash and marketable securities, providing ample resources to invest in AI and expand its e-commerce business.

At 28 times forward earnings, Amazon trades at a premium to the S&P 500 's (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) 19x forward P/E, but that is supported by surging profitability and market dominance across cloud and e-commerce. Jassy sees a path to reaching $2 trillion in annual revenue over time across the AWS and retail businesses, making Amazon a quality growth stock to buy and hold.

2. Alphabet (Google)

Shares of Alphabet, the owner of Google and YouTube, are down about 7% year to date. The recent dip followed third-quarter results showing search ad revenue came in below Wall Street's expectations. However, total revenue grew a solid 25% year over year, with AI serving as the main catalyst. The dip is a chance to buy a dominant tech company at a lower price.

Story Continues

AI is making search more useful. Search query growth hit a five-year high last quarter, while the Gemini app has reached 1 billion users.

Meanwhile, Google Cloud may become the company's biggest growth engine over the next 10 years. Cloud revenue soared 103% over the year-ago quarter to nearly $31 billion, now making up 24% of total revenue.

Alphabet ended the September quarter with $265 billion in cash and marketable securities against $125 billion of long-term debt. Year to date, it also generated $127 billion of operating cash flow. These resources are funding infrastructure investments that can fuel more AI innovations, making its services more useful to billions of users.

At 22 times forward earnings, Alphabet stock offers a reasonable valuation that can support excellent returns as the business grows over the next 10 years.

3. Home Depot

Home Depot shares are up about 1% year to date, as of Nov. 9, trailing the Dow, as customers worried about inflation and interest rates put off large projects. But this is the best time to buy shares of the world's largest home improvement retailer, as the stock will likely trade at a higher premium when the housing market recovers.

The retail chain is going after a $1.2 trillion opportunity, including an estimated $700 billion addressable market for professional contractors. A key advantage for Home Depot is its large real estate footprint, which CFO Richard McPhail says "will never be replicated." Its large store base allows for faster delivery, helping drive second-quarter online sales up 11% -- the fifth straight quarter of double-digit growth.

Overall, second-quarter sales rose about 6% year over year to $48 billion -- solid, given the weak spending environment. Home Depot is still a very profitable business, with trailing-12-month operating income of $21 billion through the fiscal second quarter, a roughly 12.4% margin on revenue.

The risk is that the housing market could stay soft. Harvard's Joint Center for Housing Studies expects home improvement spending to remain relatively flat through late 2027. Still, at 23 times forward earnings and an attractive 2.7% dividend yield, I believe Home Depot will be a rewarding investment once the housing market rebounds.

news.Title: Apple's Market Cap Grew From $347 Billion to $4.6 Trillion During Tim Cook's 15 Years as CEO. Here's What That Growth Curve Means for Apple's Next Chapter Under John Ternus.
news.Content:
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) had a market capitalization of $347 billion when Tim Cook became CEO in August 2011. When he stepped down 15 years later, the company was worth $4.6 trillion, and it has only gotten bigger since. Today, Apple has a market cap north of $5 trillion, making it the most valuable company in the world.

Cook inherited a company with one wildly successful product: the iPhone. He left his successor, John Ternus, with something considerably bigger -- a technology giant generating nearly half a trillion dollars in annual revenue, with enormous financial resources, and an installed base exceeding 2.5 billion active devices.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

I don't expect Apple under Ternus to replicate the extraordinary growth it delivered on Cook's watch. But I believe its financial strength gives its new CEO opportunities that few competitors can match. Ternus is already putting those resources to work.

Former Apple CEO Tim Cook. Image source: Apple.

Cook built an extraordinary financial machine

Apple's annual revenue jumped from $108 billion in its fiscal 2011 to $478.8 billion in its fiscal 2026. That includes a 15% increase in the most recent fiscal year, demonstrating that Apple can still deliver impressive growth despite its enormous size.

Its fiscal fourth-quarter results reinforced that point. Revenue increased 12% to $114.5 billion, including $57.6 billion in iPhone sales, up 17%. Mac revenue jumped 24% to $10.8 billion, while services revenue reached a record $31.6 billion.

Apple's services business is particularly valuable. Its gross margin reached 76% during the quarter, providing a highly profitable revenue stream alongside the company's hardware operations.

The cash keeps coming. Apple showed $28 billion in operating cash flow in the quarter, and returned approximately the same amount to shareholders through dividends and stock repurchases. As of the end of its latest fiscal year, Apple held $137 billion in cash and marketable securities against approximately $80 billion in debt.

That's an impressive cushion for a company entering an expensive new phase of product development.

Ternus is already expanding Apple's ambitions

Ternus became CEO on Sept. 1, and his first months suggest he has little interest in simply maintaining the business Cook built.

Story Continues

Apple introduced its first foldable iPhone , the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 lineup. It also unveiled its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, expanding its premium laptop offerings with a model starting at $2,899. Then there's HomeView, a $299 smart home display built around its upgraded Siri AI assistant.

These products give Apple opportunities to generate additional revenue from existing customers while attracting new ones.

Ternus may have even bigger ambitions. Apple has reportedly explored developing AI servers using its custom processors and Nvidia 's NVLink technology. That would represent a return to the enterprise server market after a 15-year absence.

John Ternus became Apple CEO on Sept. 1 and is already making big moves. Image source: Apple.

The project remains unannounced, with no commercial launch expected before 2029. Still, it illustrates the possibilities available to a company with Apple's financial resources.

Apple is spending heavily to develop those possibilities.

Apple's next chapter won't come cheap

Apple spent $45.8 billion on research and development (R&D) during fiscal 2026, up from $34.6 billion the previous year.

During its fiscal Q4 earnings call in November, management emphasized that AI investment remains a priority. Operating expenses increased 21% in the quarter, driven largely by additional R&D spending.

However, that budget expansion is creating financial pressures. Apple reported a 47.9% gross margin in the quarter, including approximately 1 percentage point of benefit from tariff refunds. Management expects that margin to decline to between 45% and 46% in the first quarter of its fiscal 2027, primarily because of higher memory costs and expenses associated with launching Siri AI.

Ternus described the current memory pricing environment as unprecedented. That's a meaningful challenge, particularly as Apple introduces more expensive hardware and expands its AI capabilities.

Still, I believe the company's financial strength provides considerable flexibility. Apple can invest billions in new products without depending on any single initiative to succeed.

The bigger challenge is its size. Adding $100 billion in annual revenue would have nearly doubled Apple's business in 2011. Today, it would represent growth of approximately 21% from fiscal 2026 levels.

Cook's extraordinary run established Apple's financial foundation. Ternus now has the resources to expand its products, develop AI capabilities, and pursue entirely new markets. I don't expect another 13-fold increase in Apple's valuation. However, I believe the company Cook built has plenty of room to become more valuable under Ternus.

news.Title: Warren Buffett Doesn't Follow His Own S&P 500 Advice. Should You?
news.Content:
While Warren Buffett consistently recommended low-cost S&P 500 index funds, such as the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT:VOO), for individual portfolios, Berkshire Hathaway 's (NYSE:BRKA)(NYSE:BRKB) own equity holdings are significantly more concentrated.

According to the company's latest 13F filing, as of June 30, just three stocks -- Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), American Express (NYSE:AXP), and Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO) -- account for nearly 46% of Berkshire's equity portfolio.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Why has Buffett, who is now retired, advocated for broadly diversified portfolios over the years when Berkshire itself doesn't do so? More importantly, does this justify a more concentrated strategy for your own portfolio? Not really, and here's why.

Image source: Getty Images.

13F filings paint an incomplete picture

These quarterly regulatory filings track U.S. equity ownership but leave out potentially large segments of Berkshire Hathaway 's full portfolio of holdings. As of June 30, its publicly traded shares represent about $364 billion.

But this number omits two things.

The first is the company's monstrous cash pile, which is currently roughly $377 billion. The second is the value of the privately held companies that it fully owns, such as GEICO, Pilot Travel Centers, Fruit of the Loom, and Johns Manville. Berkshire Hathaway is clearly much more than just the large-cap stocks that most people think about.

Buffett was never a trader, and much of the top-heaviness in the publicly-traded segment of his portfolio is the result of long-term organic capital growth rather than deliberate favoring of a few companies. He wasn't necessarily looking to be concentrated. His long-term focus and deep research capabilities are just resulting in a few high-conviction picks.

Why Berkshire can pull off the concentrated portfolio

I think you have to look at the Warren Buffett investing style to really understand why Berkshire's high concentration in Apple, American Express, and Coca-Cola isn't necessarily the red flag that it might seem.

I think it's safe to say that Berkshire does a lot of research on its stock picks before buying a share. It's certainly more than the average retail investor does, and this helps it make informed decisions without the emotional ties.

Berkshire has a long-term buy-and-hold philosophy and doesn't sell when the S&P 500 falls by 10%. Over the years, Buffett was willing to be wrong in the short term in the pursuit of long-term gains. Plus, he actively looked for opportunities to buy the dip in order to enhance his portfolio's performance.

Berkshire has the cash sitting on the sidelines waiting to be put to work. When stock prices fall far enough, it's ready to buy if the opportunity presents itself.

Story Continues

Contrast this approach with that of a retail investor whose holding period is to often measured in months, not years, and who tends to panic when there's a correction. Buffett has the patience and mindset to make his portfolio work.

How to handle concentration in your portfolio

Buffett has suggested Vanguard's S&P 500 index fund for most investors. But it's important to remember that the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF has its own concentration issue right now. The index currently has nearly 40% of its allocation in tech stocks and nearly 40% in its top 10 holdings.

While Berkshire has a high concentration in just a few companies, broad index funds, including those targeting large caps, growth, and tech stocks, are also incredibly top-heavy at the moment. Funds like the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (NYSEMKT:RSP) do a better job of diversifying within U.S. large caps.

It's easy to look at Berkshire Hathaway's portfolio and call it undiversified. But that doesn't mean diversification doesn't work. For most investors, spreading investments across the U.S. economy is still the best way to create long-term wealth.

news.Title: ALAB Benefits From Strong PCIe Demand: Can It Beat MRVL & CRDO?
news.Content:
Astera Labs ALAB is benefiting from strong demand for PCI Express (PCIe) connectivity solutions, accelerating AI infrastructure investments and increasing adoption of high-speed interconnect technologies. The company's expanding portfolio of intelligent connectivity solutions is strengthening its competitive position against Marvell Technology MRVL and Credo Technology Group CRDO, which are also capitalizing on rising demand for advanced connectivity solutions in AI data centers.

Astera Labs' Aries PCIe retimer portfolio remains a key growth driver. In the third quarter of 2026, Aries recorded strong growth, supported by increasing adoption of PCIe Gen 6 technology across scale-up and scale-out applications. The transition toward higher-speed PCIe standards is driving demand for signal-conditioning solutions that maintain reliable connectivity between processors, accelerators and other data center components.

The company recently launched the Aries 7 portfolio, featuring PCIe Gen 7 copper and optical connectivity solutions, further strengthening its growth prospects. Higher data rates are expected to increase average selling prices, while growing adoption of active electrical cables should improve product attach rates. Astera Labs expects Aries revenues to continue growing in 2027.

Astera Labs' Scorpio AI fabric portfolio is another significant growth catalyst. Scorpio became the company's largest product family in the third quarter of 2026, exceeding $1 billion in annualized revenues. The rapid ramp of Scorpio X-Series and expanding hyperscaler deployments are strengthening ALAB's position in rack-scale AI infrastructure.

Strong PCIe demand, continued product innovation and expanding AI fabric opportunities position Astera Labs favorably for sustained growth, potentially helping it strengthen its competitive standing against Marvell Technology and Credo Technology. For the fourth quarter of 2026, revenues are expected to be between $730 million and $750 million. The midpoint implies approximately 27% sequential growth, driven by continued Scorpio X-Series and P-Series expansion, Aries PCIe 6 retimer demand and Taurus 800-gigabit deployments.

How Competitors Fare Against ALAB

ALAB is facing stiff competition from other industry players, such as Marvell Technology and Credo Technology. Both companies are making strong efforts in the connectivity space.

Marvell Technology's expanding connectivity portfolio has been noteworthy. In October, 2026, Marvell Technology launched 3.2T retimers and second-generation 1.6T AEC DSPs, featuring 224G connectivity, improved power efficiency and extended copper reach for next-generation AI infrastructure.

Credo Technology's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. In August 2026, the company announced that the Toucan Gen6x16 PCIe retimer has achieved PCI-SIG 6.x compliance at 64.0 GT/s and joined the PCI-SIG Integrators List. The certification validates Toucan's electrical performance, interoperability and PCIe 6.0 protocol capabilities, supporting reliable deployment across AI, high-performance computing, cloud and accelerated computing platforms.

The retimer combines DSP-based SerDes technology, low-power operation and advanced diagnostics through Credo Technology's PILOT software. The milestone is expected to reduce integration risks, accelerate platform deployment and strengthen Credo Technology's position in high-speed connectivity solutions for next-generation AI infrastructure.

news.Title: PayPal's Venmo Grows in Q3: Can Rising Monetization Fuel Earnings?
news.Content:
PayPal Holdings, Inc. PYPL continued to witness strong momentum in its Venmo business during the third quarter of 2026, supported by higher payment volumes, increased engagement and growing adoption of monetized services. Venmo's total payment volume (TPV) rose 14% year over year to $96.8 billion from $85.2 billion, marking its eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

Venmo accounted for 20% of PayPal's total payment volume during the quarter, up from 19% a year earlier. The platform's growth reflects increasing adoption of its debit card and Pay with Venmo offerings. Pay with Venmo TPV rose 43% year over year, highlighting growing consumer demand for using the service beyond peer-to-peer payments.

Venmo's debit card business also gained momentum, with monthly active accounts rising more than 55% year over year to 6.7 million. The platform added a record 1.6 million first-time debit card users during the third quarter. Moreover, debit card payment volume increased more than 60%, reflecting stronger spending activity and deeper customer engagement.

Monetization remains a key growth opportunity. Venmo's average revenue per active account (ARPA) increased at a double-digit rate, supported by rising adoption of financial services. Notably, debit card users generate five to six times higher ARPA than peer-to-peer-only users. With just 23% of Venmo customers using financial services, further adoption could support higher revenues and transaction margins.

For PayPal, Venmo's expansion is strengthening overall profitability. Transaction margin dollars increased 2% year over year to $3.95 billion, while non-GAAP earnings rose 8% to $1.45 per share. Management raised its full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to approximately $5.60 from $5.38, reflecting improving earnings expectations.

How Are Block & Apple Doing in the Payments Space?

Block, Inc. 's XYZ Cash App competes with PayPal's Venmo in peer-to-peer payments while offering debit spending, merchant payments and financial services. Its Neighborhoods initiative connects Cash App users with Square merchants, supporting engagement and payment adoption. In third-quarter 2026, Cash App gross profit increased 27% year over year to $2.07 billion.

Apple AAPL competes with PayPal's Venmo through Apple Cash for peer-to-peer transfers and through Apple Pay's broader digital-payments ecosystem. The September 2026 launch of Apple Pay in India further strengthened its global reach and merchant acceptance. Apple Pay now operates across more than 90 countries and regions.

Story Continues

PYPL's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Shares of PayPal have gained 30.8% in the past six months, outperforming both the broader industry and the S&P 500 Index.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

From a valuation standpoint, PayPal shares are trading cheaply, as suggested by the Value Score of A. In terms of forward 12-month P/E, PYPL stock is trading at 10.15X, which is at a significant discount to the Zacks Financial Transaction Services industry's 19.66X.

PayPal's estimate revisions reflect a positive trend. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for full-year 2026 EPS has been revised upward to $5.57 over the past month. The consensus estimate for the metric indicates a year-over-year increase of 4.9%.

PayPal currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .
