news.Title: Cisco (CSCO) vs. ANET and HPE: Can AI Networking Turn Strong Orders Into Lasting Earnings Growth?
news.Content:
Is CSCO a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Cisco Systems, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on CSCO. Cisco Systems, Inc.'s share was trading at $102 as of November 12th. CSCO's trailing and forward P/E were 31 and 19 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a networking company pitched as a great investment. CSCO shares gained 30.2% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Fortinet and Arista Networks gained 58% and 51%, respectively, during the same period. Cisco's gain may reflect accelerating AI infrastructure orders and businesses upgrading their networks, although higher component costs and pressure on hardware margins could be tempering enthusiasm. Is there still room for CSCO to rise, or has much of that growth already been priced in?

In May, we published an article about the 10 Best Stocks to Buy to Beat the S&P 500 and CSCO ranked #6 in that article. CSCO returned 17.67% since then. So, hedge funds were right about CSCO. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on CSCO. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) provides networking, security, observability, collaboration, and communications infrastructure for enterprises, governments, service providers, and hyperscale data centers. The company's growth story now centers on artificial intelligence, as businesses building AI systems need fast, reliable ways to connect thousands of GPUs and servers within massive data centers. Cisco earned its reputation making routers and switches, and the AI boom gives it a real chance to grow beyond that traditional business.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

In fiscal 2026, revenue grew 11.8% year over year to $63.3 billion, and the fourth quarter alone saw revenue jump 18% to $17.3 billion, with earnings per share of $1.22 and product orders up 35%. That's solid growth for a stock trading at about 31.9 times trailing earnings and 20.9 times forward earnings, actually cheaper than the peer median of 36.2 times trailing earnings. In simple terms, investors are paying up for Cisco's AI-driven growth, but not at a steep premium compared to other networking companies.

The bullish argument is that Cisco is turning into a real beneficiary of AI infrastructure spending, not just a mature hardware seller. AI data centers need enormous amounts of high-speed connectivity to link GPUs and servers together, and Cisco's massive existing customer base makes it easier to sell more networking, security, and software on top of what customers already use. The numbers back this up: AI infrastructure orders hit $9.3 billion in fiscal 2026, showing this demand is already real rather than just a future hope.

Story Continues

Management expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion, with earnings per share of $5.05 to $5.11, a solid step up from fiscal 2026's GAAP EPS of $3.33. If large cloud companies keep expanding their AI infrastructure and businesses keep upgrading their networks, bulls believe this growth can continue for several years rather than fade after one good year. Supporting that view, Cisco generated $14.2 billion in operating cash flow and $12.8 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2026. The company also launched its new Silicon One G300 AI networking chip, though it still needs to prove it can compete with Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) in high-performance, low-latency data centers.

Wall Street mostly agrees with the bullish case: 24 analysts have a consensus price target of $137.62, about 28% above the source article's $107.44 share price, with a median target of $135 and estimates ranging from $115 to $170. That $137.62 target implies earnings of roughly $6.58 per share at the stock's current 20.9 times forward earnings multiple, about 28% above the consensus earnings estimate and nearly double what Cisco earned over the past year. Given fiscal 2027 guidance of $5.05 to $5.11 in earnings per share, the key thing to watch is whether AI orders and enterprise network demand actually deliver enough earnings growth to justify that target, rather than the stock simply becoming more expensive.

The main risk is a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending. Even if AI demand stays strong, Cisco still has to protect its profits while growing its networking, security, and software businesses, and that's not guaranteed. Over the past year, Cisco's gross margin was 64.5%, operating margin was 25.4%, and net margin was 21.0%, but rising component and memory costs could squeeze those numbers going forward. Higher interest rates could also make it harder for companies to justify big network upgrades outside of major cloud providers. On top of that, Cisco competes with Arista Networks in high-performance data center switching and relies heavily on a supply chain based in Asia, which leaves it exposed to trade tensions and geopolitical risk. Trading at 6.7 times sales versus a peer median of 3.2 times, Cisco still needs its AI growth story to translate into real, lasting earnings.

Another risk for the stock is customers separating networking hardware from software. Large cloud providers can buy Cisco's chips or switches while using open-source software instead of its proprietary tools. Driven by demand for flexibility, this approach lets customers combine products from different suppliers. Cisco already supports SONiC, an open-source networking operating system, on its Silicon One platforms. Winning AI hardware orders therefore does not guarantee additional software subscriptions. Cisco could sell more equipment without capturing the broader customer spending that supports its growth story. In our opinion, this could pressure Cisco's price multiples if AI orders generate fewer recurring software revenues than investors expect.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 101 hedge funds held Cisco Systems at the end of the second quarter, up from 97 in the previous quarter. That's a modest increase, suggesting institutional investors remain supportive of Cisco's improving growth story but aren't rushing in aggressively. By comparison, Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) was held by 91 hedge funds, up from 85, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) was held by 85 hedge funds, up sharply from 58, and Fortinet (NASDAQ:FTNT) was held by 62 hedge funds, up from 52. The divergence suggests institutional investors showed the strongest increase in conviction toward Hewlett Packard Enterprise, while hedge fund interest also increased in Arista Networks, Fortinet, and Cisco Systems, with Cisco Systems' more modest rise coming despite accelerating AI infrastructure orders and a valuation that still requires sustained earnings growth.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for Cisco. Just 1.30% of Cisco Systems' float is sold short, slightly above Arista Networks at 1.14% and well below Fortinet at 2.06%. Hewlett Packard Enterprise stands out with much heavier bearish betting, at 4.31% of its float sold short. This suggests investors aren't especially worried about Cisco Systems' AI spending, competition, or margin risks compared with how they view Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Fortinet.

Valuation Analysis

CSCO's forward P/E is 19x. Arista Networks, Inc., Fortinet, Inc., and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company trade at forward P/Es of 39.22x, 45.05x, and 13.61x, respectively. CSCO's own forward P/E was 18.94x on January 31, 2026, putting its current valuation approximately 5% above that level. We believe the current valuation reflects improving confidence in Cisco's AI networking opportunity, tempered by competition and uncertainty about how long infrastructure spending will remain strong. However, its substantial discount to Arista and Fortinet appears attractive given its improving earnings growth, although their different business mixes mean Cisco should not automatically command similar multiples. Cisco Systems, Inc.'s adjusted earnings per share increased from $3.81 in fiscal 2025 to $4.33 in fiscal 2026, representing approximately 14% growth, while fiscal 2027 guidance implies around 17% growth at the midpoint. We believe 19.80 times expected earnings could be reasonable without further acceleration, provided growth continues beyond the forecast year, allowing rising profits to support returns without requiring a higher P/E. If Cisco can convert AI orders into sustained earnings and protect its margins, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point despite competition and the risk of slower customer spending.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Cisco Systems, Inc. (CSCO) by Kroker Equity Research in May 2025, which highlighted recurring software revenue, AI infrastructure, Splunk integration, and cybersecurity growth. CSCO's stock price has appreciated by approximately 77.78% since our coverage. We believe CSCO could be a good long-term investment, as its reasonable valuation offers an attractive entry point if AI networking demand supports sustained earnings growth.

Cisco Systems, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While CSCO could offer long-term upside if growing AI networking orders translate into stronger earnings, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than CSCO and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

news.Title: AMD is Trading at a Premium at 38.39X P/E: Is the Stock Still a Buy?
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices AMD shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F. The AMD stock is trading at a forward 12-month price/earnings (P/E) of 38.39X compared with the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's 17.48X. AMD shares are trading at a premium compared with peers, including NVIDIA NVDA, Broadcom AVGO and Intel INTC. Shares of NVIDIA, Broadcom and Intel are trading at a P/E multiple of 12.12, 17.78 and 36.16, respectively.

AMD Stock's Valuation

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Is AMD worth buying at current prices? Let's dig deep to find out.

AMD Shares Outperform Sector & Peers

AMD shares have risen 123% year to date (YTD), outperforming the broader sector's appreciation of 11.1%, Intel's rise of 74% and Broadcom's increase of 1.5%. YTD, shares of NVIDIA have dropped 7%.

AMD Stock's YTD Price Performance

The stock is expected to continue its rally due to expanding presence in the data center market. In the third quarter of 2026, Data Center revenues surged 97% year over year to $8.55 billion and accounted for approximately 64% of total revenues. Cloud and enterprise server sales more than doubled, reflecting increasing EPYC adoption across hyperscalers and enterprise customers. The launch of sixth-generation EPYC Venice processors offers additional growth opportunities, with OEM and ODM partners committing to more than 240 platforms, approximately 20% higher than Turin. AMD expects server revenues to double year over year in 2027, supported by expanding AI infrastructure investments and demand for agentic computing.

The rapid adoption of AMD's Instinct MI450 Series GPUs and Helios rack-scale systems is expected to drive significant revenue growth. In the third quarter, AMD began volume shipments of MI455X GPUs, while customers including Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle brought their first Helios racks online. The company expects Helios deployments to accelerate significantly in the fourth quarter as Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Super Micro Computer expand system availability. AMD anticipates that data center AI revenues will more than double in 2027, supported by increasing deployments across training and inference workloads.

AMD's strengthening Embedded business and expanding software capabilities provide additional growth opportunities. In the third quarter of 2026, Embedded revenues increased 29% year over year to $1.11 billion, supported by strong demand across aerospace and defense, automotive, communications and industrial markets. AMD remains on track to secure more than $18 billion in embedded design wins during 2026. Meanwhile, ROCm 10 and ROCm.AI are improving developer productivity and AI workload optimization, potentially encouraging broader Instinct GPU adoption. The proposed acquisitions of Taalas and World Labs could further strengthen the company's inference capabilities and position in emerging AI applications.

AMD's improving revenue visibility strengthens its growth prospects. The company expects fourth-quarter 2026 revenues of approximately $17 billion, representing 66% year-over-year and 27% sequential growth at the midpoint. For 2027, AMD anticipates revenue growth exceeding 80%, driven primarily by accelerating data center demand. The Data Center segment is expected to contribute more than 80% of total revenues next year. The company also expects operating expenses to grow at less than half the rate of revenue growth in 2027, potentially supporting significant operating margin expansion and profitability improvement.

These factors are expected to offset gross margin pressure from higher sales volume of low-margin data center AI products, as well as inflationary pressure from high-bandwidth memory and other components.

Story Continues

AMD's Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Positive Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fourth-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $2.90 per share, up 13.7% over the past 30 days and indicating 89.5% year-over-year growth. The consensus mark for fourth-quarter 2026 revenues is pegged at $17.06 billion, suggesting 66.1% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Price and Consensus

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Quote

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is pegged at $8.04 per share, up 7.3% over the past 30 days, suggesting 92.8% growth from 2025's reported figure. The consensus mark for 2026 revenues is pegged at $52.08 billion, suggesting 50.3% growth from 2025's reported figure.

Conclusion

AMD's strong position in the rapidly expanding AI infrastructure market, accelerating adoption of EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs, and growing demand for Helios rack-scale solutions position the company for sustained growth. The company's robust data center momentum, expanding customer base and improving revenue visibility are expected to drive significant revenue and earnings growth in 2027. Although its premium valuation and near-term gross margin pressures remain concerns, the company's strong growth trajectory and expanding AI opportunities help justify its elevated valuation.

news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Dropped on Thursday
news.Content:
Well, that was fast.

Just days after the news broke that Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang was under investigation for an alleged affair with a Chinese spy , and just hours after reports of a second affair, this time with an Nvidia executive, leaked, Huang has now resigned, and Nvidia stock is slumping.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Shares of the AI chip giant are down 4.5% through 11:05 a.m. ET Thursday, and Nvidia investors aren't the only ones suffering. Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock is down, too, losing 3.4%.

Image source: Getty Images.

What this means for Sandisk stock

Why is a leadership crisis at Nvidia impacting Sandisk stock -- a completely different company that makes completely different computer chips (specifically, NAND flash memory chips)?

Basically, the theory is this: Jensen Huang and Nvidia led the artificial intelligence revolution, inventing the GPU chips that made AI training, AI inference, and AI agents possible, and investing in Nvidia's own customers (giving them money with which to buy more Nvidia chips) to keep the AI revolution rolling. With Huang out, the revolution may derail, and the industry's future mayn't be as well planned and timed to maintain momentum for AI stocks.

If that's the case, sales could slow across the industry. Nvidia's sales would suffer, but so would Sandisk's, because one of Sandisk's biggest revenue streams is selling to data centers, where Sandisk memory chips are paired with Nvidia GPUs to enable AI functions.

What's next for Sandisk stock

Fewer GPU sales means fewer memory sales -- or so the thinking goes. But here's the thing:

While there's a risk this will happen, a risk is not a certainty. If Nvidia stumbles, other AI chip companies may pick up the slack and keep the AI industry growing.

With Sandisk trading below 5x earnings, I think it's more likely to go up than down from here.

news.Title: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman explains the 'paradox' of AI for his company
news.Content:
Reddit ( RDDT ) is one of the most frequently cited sources in AI-generated answers. Yet its most recent earnings report showed that Google's AI Overviews have undermined its search traffic.

At Yahoo Finance Invest , Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman described this dynamic as the "paradox" of AI for the company.

"AI does not exist as we know it without Reddit, " Huffman said on Thursday. "Every model you've heard of trained with or without our permission using Reddit. It's this paradox which is the more AI there is, the more the human nature of Reddit stands out."

In a quarterly letter to investors in October, Huffman noted that Reddit's search traffic "dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week" during the month. "Web search is evolving from a gateway to the web to becoming an AI-powered destination itself," Huffman said.

Huffman added in the company's third quarter earnings call that "Google is not sending [users] to Reddit the way they used to."

According to Similarweb, a web analytics platform, Reddit's traffic is down 13% year over year. Reddit's $60 million-a-year data deal with Google is up for renewal next year.

Insights from Yahoo Finance Invest 2026

AMD CEO Lisa Su on data center backlash: Tech has to sell the vision

SoFi chief market strategist on an Nvidia without Jensen Huang: 'What happens without the visionary?'

Rivian CEO says robotaxis won't end car ownership — he's betting on both

The company's Q3 report showed total daily active unique users increased 12% year over year to 130.3 million (slightly below analyst expectations of 133.7 million), while US daily active users declined 2% year over year. While the company beat earnings per share estimates, it came up short on its Q4 revenue forecast, predicting sales of $1.0 billion to $1.03 billion (slightly below some Wall Street consensus estimates near $1.05 billion).

Huffman told Yahoo Finance that Reddit will begin testing a requirement for users to log in to access content on the platform in the United States starting this quarter.

"We are not the first," Huffman said, speaking about other social media platforms. "In fact, we are quite literally the last company to go through this transition." He added that the company, however, does not want to wall itself off from the open web — whether that's humans or AI.

The ethos driving Reddit, Huffman explained, is that "Reddit is for humans." The platform is all about "questions that have no answers."

"'What should I watch tonight?' There's not a factual answer for that — there's just 100 answers. And all of those answers have a different point of view and context," Huffman said. "People like the different perspectives. They like the mess. They like the chaos — that's what being human is."

news.Title: Trump says ex Apple CEO Cook is 'a legend', should replace Huang at Nvidia
news.Content:
Nov 12 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that former Apple Inc Chief Executive Tim Cook should replace ‌Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia .

"NOW THAT Nvidia CEO ‌JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one ​man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple," Trump said on social media. "A Legend replaces a Legend!" he added.

Cook stepped down after a 15-year stint as Apple's CEO in September and is now executive chairman ‌at the iPhone-maker.

Apple and Cook ⁠did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Last year, Cook presented Trump with a custom US-made plaque mounted ⁠on a 24-carat gold stand commemorating Apple's "American Manufacturing Program", after saying it would invest an additional $100 billion in domestic manufacturing.

Huang resigned as CEO and ​a member ​of the board on Thursday after ​reports said he had an ‌affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. Nvidia has announced that Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO.

Trump, who has maintained close ties with top US tech executives in his second term, said on Monday that ‌he had spoken to Huang and the ​CEO told him that he did not ​know the woman linked ​to him was allegedly a spy. Huang is one ‌of Trump's closest allies in Silicon ​Valley, and the ​relationship between the two dates to at least 2025.

Over the past two years, Huang has repeatedly voiced support for the administration's ​agenda and become a ‌regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced ​chips to the Chinese market.

(Reporting by Bhargav Acharya, Ismail Shakil ​and Aditya Soni;Editing by David Ljunggren)

news.Title: Nvidia book author said there are only two real candidates to replace Jensen Huang
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Following this morning's stunning news, the question of who should lead NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) after Jensen Huang is no longer just a matter of corporate succession. It is about whether one of the world's most influential technology companies can maintain its extraordinary momentum without the man who built it.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

According to Tae Kim, author of The Nvidia Way: Jensen Huang and the Making of a Tech Giant , the answer is yes. Despite the shock surrounding Huang's departure following his infidelity with two women, Kim believes NVIDIA has enough leadership talent and institutional strength to thrive under a new chief executive. However, he believes the board should focus on just two candidates: Rene Haas and Ian Buck.

Rene Haas: The experienced business leader

Kim's first choice is Rene Haas, currently CEO of Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) and a former NVIDIA executive.

Haas brings an attractive combination of technical understanding, executive experience and leadership skills. During his time at Arm, he has demonstrated that he can successfully manage a major technology company outside NVIDIA. He also understands NVIDIA's corporate culture and is already familiar with many of its senior executives.

That familiarity could prove invaluable during a leadership transition. According to Kim, former NVIDIA employees have spoken highly of Haas and enjoyed working under him.

His appointment would offer continuity without simply trying to replicate Jensen Huang's leadership style. Haas has the experience and public-facing presence needed to reassure investors, employees, customers and business partners that NVIDIA remains in capable hands.

Ian Buck: The technology visionary

Kim's second candidate is Ian Buck, NVIDIA's vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing.

While Haas represents the experienced corporate leader, Buck represents NVIDIA's technological DNA.

Buck is particularly important because he invented CUDA, NVIDIA's software platform that helped transform the company's GPUs into the foundation of modern accelerated computing and AI development.

Today, he oversees products and technologies used by major cloud providers and other large customers. Kim believes Buck possesses the engineering expertise, customer relationships and respect among employees necessary to guide NVIDIA through its next phase of growth.

Story Continues

His appointment would send a powerful message: NVIDIA's future will remain firmly rooted in technological innovation.

Jonah Alben: The executive NVIDIA cannot afford to lose

Beyond choosing a new CEO, Kim highlights another critical priority: retaining Jonah Alben, NVIDIA's senior vice president of GPU engineering.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

Alben plays an essential role in developing the company's GPU architecture and long-term product roadmap. Kim believes keeping him, alongside Buck, would help ensure that NVIDIA's technological development continues without disruption.

In other words, the board's challenge is not simply finding a replacement for Huang. It must also protect the engineering leadership responsible for NVIDIA's competitive advantage.

NVIDIA's future is bigger than Jensen Huang

Kim acknowledges that Huang's departure marks the end of an extraordinary leadership era. However, he no longer believes NVIDIA's success depends on one individual.

Demand for AI computing remains enormous, and the company's technology, talent and customer relationships provide a strong foundation for continued growth. Even if political pressure, regulation or changes in international markets slow expansion, Kim believes the underlying AI opportunity remains substantial.

His message to NVIDIA's board is straightforward: choose Rene Haas or Ian Buck, retain Jonah Alben and preserve the company's technological direction.

The bottom line? Jensen Huang may have made NVIDIA what it is today, but its future does not have to end with him. Under the right leadership, the company can continue shaping the AI revolution. For Kim, Rene Haas and Ian Buck are the two people best positioned to make that happen.

Prediction markets: Ian Buck leads the field

While Kim's assessment focuses on institutional fit and technological vision, prediction markets are already pricing in the succession race. According to data tracked and analyzed by The Action Network, which aggregates market pricing, trading activity, and historical forecasting accuracy from platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket, Ian Buck has emerged as the frontrunner:

Ian Buck (NVIDIA Executive): 35.5% implied probability

Colette Kress (Interim CEO): 25.5% implied probability

Rene Haas (Arm CEO): 9.1% implied probability

Lisa Su (AMD CEO): 2.4% implied probability

Notably, market data places interim CEO Colette Kress well ahead of Kim's other preferred candidate, Rene Haas. "With Ian Buck leading our analysis at a 35.5% implied probability, followed by interim CEO Colette Kress at 25.5%, NVIDIA's succession remains far from settled," Ben Mendelowitz, Prediction Markets Analyst at The Action Network, said in a statement to Investing.com, noting that the figures reflect a tension between technical expertise and leadership continuity.

Still, market sentiment can shift rapidly. Mendelowitz pointed out that prior to Huang's resignation, tracked market movements showed his exit probability surging from 13.2% to 76.6% in just three days (November 9–12), suggesting succession probabilities could swing just as quickly as new developments unfold.

news.Title: 克瑞斯代理CEO迎重大考驗：輝達下週公布財報　專家曝台股觀察重點
news.Content:
輝達（NVIDIA，NVDA）執行長黃仁勳正式辭職，財務長科萊特・克瑞斯（Colette Kress）接任臨時執行長，市場接下來最關注的，就是她能否穩住投資人信心。尤其輝達美國時間下週二（11月17日）就要公布 2027會計年度第三季財報 ，這也是克瑞斯以臨時執行長身分首次面對市場考驗。 財經專家《籌碼小哥葛》 指出，黃仁勳離開的消息已讓台股提前承受賣壓，接下來除了觀察輝達財報，更要留意AI族群及市場資金如何反應。

【黃仁勳辭職震撼市場 克瑞斯接任臨時CEO】

《籌碼小哥葛》在臉書發文表示，黃仁勳自1993年共同創辦輝達以來，掌舵公司長達33年，帶領輝達從繪圖晶片業者成長為全球AI晶片龍頭。如今黃仁勳辭去總裁、執行長及董事職務，相關異動即刻生效，輝達董事會任命執行副總裁暨財務長科萊特・克瑞斯（Colette Kress）接任臨時執行長，並啟動正式接班人遴選程序。

克瑞斯自2013年加入輝達，長期負責財務管理，也熟悉公司營運與投資人溝通。不過，臨時接掌不代表市場疑慮就此消失。黃仁勳過去不只是公司領導人，更是輝達技術策略與AI產業發展的重要推手，市場擔心的是，少了黃仁勳之後，未來產品藍圖、投資節奏及客戶合作是否仍能維持原有步調。

【下週二公布財報 克瑞斯首次以代理CEO身分面對市場】

《籌碼小哥葛》特別點出，輝達下週二（11月17日，美國時間）就要公布2027會計年度第三季財報，這次財報格外受到關注。克瑞斯過去雖然長期以財務長身分參與財報說明會，但這次將首次以臨時執行長身分面對市場，除了公布財務成績，也得讓投資人了解公司接下來的經營方向。

市場除了關注營收、獲利及下一季財測，也會留意克瑞斯如何說明AI晶片需求、產品交付進度，以及輝達與雲端業者、AI企業之間的合作。若她能清楚傳達既有策略不變、營運與客戶承諾持續推進，或許有助降低市場不安；反之，若對接班與未來布局的說明不夠明確，股價恐仍面臨震盪。

【台股盤中急殺逾1500點 黃仁勳消息成市場變數】

黃仁勳去留消息傳出前，台股才剛經歷連續3個交易日反彈，累計上漲4,555點，市場原本期待多頭氣勢延續。11月12日早盤，台股一度衝上44,525.24點，盤中卻因輝達董事會討論黃仁勳去留的消息發酵，電子權值股陸續翻黑，指數最低下探42,943.50點，盤中高低震盪達1,581.74點。

終場加權指數下跌1,165.28點，收在43,091.87點，跌幅2.63%，成交金額達1兆132.93億元，上漲家數286家、下跌741家，市場賣壓明顯集中在電子與AI相關族群。

《籌碼小哥葛》認為，台股當天下跌，反映市場對黃仁勳可能離開輝達的擔憂。輝達是台灣AI供應鏈的重要客戶，從晶圓代工、伺服器組裝、散熱到PCB，都與其AI產品布局密切相關。短期訂單未必立即受到影響，但投資人更擔心的是，領導層更替是否改變未來產品規畫與投資方向。

【三大法人反而買超 融資減少94億元】

news.Title: Trump says 'there is only one man' to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
news.Content:
President Donald Trump suggested Thursday that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as the head of Nvidia following Huang's abrupt resignation amid scrutiny of his personal conduct and potential national security concerns.

"NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

The president's endorsement comes as Nvidia faces a leadership shake-up following Huang's departure from the artificial intelligence chipmaker he co-founded in 1993.

Nvidia Ceo Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Investigation Into Relationship With Alleged Chinese Spy

Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO on Thursday while its board searches for a permanent successor, considering candidates from both inside and outside the company.

Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO in September after 15 years at the helm and now serves as the iPhone maker's executive chairman. Trump did not indicate whether Cook had expressed interest in taking the helm at Nvidia.

Read On The Fox Business App

Huang's resignation followed reports of two extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.

The allegations raised questions about whether the longtime technology executive could have been targeted by Chinese intelligence, given Nvidia's central role in the global artificial intelligence industry and ongoing U.S.-China tensions over advanced chips.

The reported relationship has fueled concerns about potential foreign intelligence efforts to gain access to sensitive information involving one of America's most strategically important technology companies. However, no evidence has been publicly established that Huang disclosed confidential information or that the woman obtained Nvidia secrets.

Trump had previously defended Huang, saying Monday that he believed the executive's account that he was unaware of the woman's alleged intelligence ties.

Reuters contributed to this report.

news.Title: Who is NVIDIA’s new CEO Colette Kress?
news.Content:
Investing.com -- NVIDIA has appointed longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO following the shock resignation of Jensen Huang, who led the chipmaker for 33 years.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

Kress, 59, has spent more than 13 years at NVIDIA and is regarded as one of its most influential executives, with deep knowledge of the company's operations, financial strategy and relationships with major customers.

She joined NVIDIA in September 2013, following nearly 25 years in finance roles at major technology companies, including Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments.

Before NVIDIA, Kress spent three years as a senior vice president and finance chief at Cisco, overseeing financial strategy, planning and business development. She previously worked at Microsoft for 13 years, including four as CFO of its Server and Tools division.

She holds a bachelor's degree in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

During her tenure, NVIDIA transformed from a company primarily associated with gaming graphics cards into the dominant supplier of AI computing infrastructure. Its annual revenue surged from just over $4 billion in fiscal 2013 to nearly $216 billion in fiscal 2026.

Kress has also become a familiar face to Wall Street, regularly appearing alongside Huang on quarterly earnings calls, discussing financial performance, customer demand, supply constraints and the company's outlook.

Despite her CFO title, analysts say her influence has extended well beyond financial management.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

"She's more than just a CFO," Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co., told CNBC, describing her as more of a chief operating officer.

Ives called Kress a "Swiss Army knife" for NVIDIA, saying she was closely involved in strategic decisions spanning technology, customers and partnerships.

Still, succeeding Huang presents an extraordinary challenge.

Unlike Kress, Huang was an engineer and founder who remained deeply involved in product development, technology decisions and NVIDIA's long-term strategy. His management structure also left the company without a traditional second-in-command.

Story Continues

Kress acknowledged the challenge in Thursday's announcement, saying she was committed to building on the "extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years."

Newly appointed board chairman Harvey Jones expressed confidence in Kress, citing her understanding of NVIDIA's customers, operations and finances.

Her appointment is interim, with the board considering both internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO position. Kress will retain her CFO responsibilities during the transition.

The leadership shakeup comes amid mounting controversy surrounding Huang's reported extramarital affairs, including one involving a Chinese businesswoman suspected by U.S. authorities of having intelligence ties to Beijing.

The allegations prompted an independent board investigation and ultimately preceded Huang's departure. NVIDIA shares plunged more than 12% in early Thursday trading as investors assessed the implications of losing the executive most closely associated with the AI boom.

Kress now faces her first major test almost immediately, with NVIDIA scheduled to report quarterly earnings on November 17.

news.Title: Best Health & Fitness Stocks to Buy on Strong Market Potential
news.Content:
An updated edition of the Sept. 21, 2026, article.

Health and fitness is becoming a regular part of how consumers live and spend, rather than a separate lifestyle choice. More people are paying attention to exercise, nutrition, preventive care and their overall well-being. This growing interest has expanded the market for fitness centers, nutritional products, healthcare services, workplace wellness programs and digital health tools.

Technology is making it easier for consumers to manage their health. Wearable devices and mobile applications help people monitor physical activity, sleep patterns and other health measures. Virtual coaching and connected fitness platforms also provide access to guidance based on individual needs. At the same time, concerns about obesity, chronic diseases and mental health are encouraging people to adopt healthier habits and take preventive steps before medical problems arise.

Major technology companies are investing in health-related services and products. Apple AAPL combines health tracking through the Apple Watch with workout programs offered on Fitness+. Amazon AMZN is expanding its healthcare offerings through One Medical, which provides access to virtual care and AI-supported services. These businesses are bringing fitness, medical care and consumer technology closer together.

The market also offers considerable room for growth. The global health and wellness market is projected to reach $7.76 trillion by 2035, seeing a CAGR of 4.94% from 2026. Greater spending on preventive healthcare, employee wellness programs and government initiatives aimed at improving public health are expected to support demand over the coming years.

Consumer demand is also shifting toward services and products that address specific health goals. Boutique fitness studios, premium wellness clubs, customized nutrition plans and connected health devices are attracting interest among people looking for more personalized options. Companies such as VF Corporation VFC, Garmin Ltd. GRMN and Amer Sports, Inc. AS operate in different parts of this market, offering investors exposure to changing consumer preferences.

For investors, the health and fitness market offers opportunities tied to changing lifestyle habits, wider adoption of digital health tools and increased spending on preventive care. The Health & Fitness Screen identifies companies operating across these areas, helping investors find businesses with exposure to consumer spending on health and wellness.

Story Continues

3 Health & Fitness Stocks to Buy Now

VF Corporation sells running shoes, outdoor clothing, technical footwear and related accessories through brands such as The North Face, Altra, Smartwool and Icebreaker. These products cater to consumers involved in running, hiking, skiing and other physical activities. The North Face offers protective outerwear, performance footwear and outdoor equipment, while Altra focuses on running shoes. Smartwool and Icebreaker provide functional clothing for outdoor use. Through these brands, VFC has built a business serving customers who need specialized products for exercise, sports and outdoor recreation.

The Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) company has gradually expanded its product offerings to reach more customers. The North Face has been developing running shoes alongside its established outdoor clothing business. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, it introduced the Altamesa 2 footwear series, which received a positive initial response across regions. The brand is also working on additional spring and summer products to broaden its seasonal offerings. Its agreement to supply performance apparel to the U.S. Ski and Snowboard Team connects the brand with competitive winter sports. Altra, meanwhile, has expanded from trail-running footwear into road-running shoes, with models including Lone Peak, Torin, Experience Flow and Wild. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

These developments have contributed to growth in VFC's fitness-related businesses. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, The North Face reported 4% revenue growth in constant currency, led by outerwear, shells and equipment. Altra maintained its growth momentum as road-running sales became larger than its trail-running business over recent quarters. Management sees further room to expand Altra in road running, a market it considers much larger than trail running. VFC continues investing in product development and brand awareness, particularly for Altra, while expanding The North Face's footwear and seasonal clothing offerings.

Garmin offers fitness smartwatches, activity trackers, cycling computers and GPS-enabled devices for people interested in exercise, sports and personal wellness. Its products cater to professional athletes, recreational fitness enthusiasts and individuals who want to keep track of their daily activities. Over the years, Garmin has expanded its fitness business from GPS-based sports devices to wearables that provide information about physical activity and overall wellness. Its Outdoor segment also offers adventure watches for running, hiking and other outdoor activities, giving the company a wider presence in the health and fitness market.

Garmin regularly introduces products with new features to meet different fitness needs. In the third quarter of 2026, the Zacks #2 Ranked company launched the CIRQA Smart Band, a screenless wearable that provides fitness and wellness insights. It also announced new Edge cycling computers, including the Edge 1060, which allows hands-free voice control through a built-in microphone and speaker. The Edge Explore 3 targets cyclists of different experience levels. Garmin also expanded its adventure watch collection with the fenix 9 and fenix 9 Pro, offering titanium case options and larger AMOLED displays.

Demand for Garmin's fitness devices has continued to grow. In the third quarter of 2026, Fitness segment revenues increased 16% year over year to $694 million due to higher wearable sales. Operating income reached $231 million, with an operating margin of 33%. The Outdoor segment also reported 20% revenue growth, supported by strong demand for adventure watches following the fenix 9 launch. Management expects Fitness to contribute the most to the company's overall revenue growth in 2026. Garmin continues to develop products for different types of users, from regular exercisers to experienced athletes.

Amer Sports sells sports equipment, footwear, technical clothing and accessories through brands such as Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson, Atomic and Peak Performance. Its products are used in activities such as running, hiking, skiing, tennis and other outdoor sports. The Zacks Rank #2 company operates through three business segments: Technical Apparel, Outdoor Performance, and Ball & Racquet Sports. Amer Sports was traditionally more dependent on sporting equipment, but footwear and apparel have become an increasingly important part of its business. This change has allowed the company to reach consumers who participate in sports, as well as those who prefer comfortable, functional clothing for everyday use.

Salomon provides a clear example of this shift. The brand started with ski equipment before expanding into trail-running shoes, hiking footwear, sportswear and sneakers. Arc'teryx, known for its technical outdoor clothing, has also been developing footwear and women's products. Meanwhile, Wilson has expanded beyond tennis racquets and other sports equipment into performance apparel and footwear. Amer Sports has supported these developments by opening more branded stores and expanding its online sales channels, giving customers more ways to purchase its products.

The growing contribution from footwear and apparel has changed the company's sales mix. These categories are expected to account for 75% of Outdoor Performance revenues in 2026 compared with 54% in 2022. Salomon's footwear and apparel business has recorded a compound annual growth rate of 30% since 2022. Wilson Tennis 360 has also expanded, supported by sales of racquets, clothing and shoes. Arc'teryx continues to develop its product categories and retail presence across different markets. Amer Sports is investing in these businesses while gradually reducing its reliance on traditional sports equipment.

news.Title: SpaceX's Expanding Ambitions: ETFs to Play Its Next Growth Phase
news.Content:
SpaceX SPCX is rapidly evolving from a rocket-launching company into a diversified technology and infrastructure business, with growing exposure to artificial intelligence (AI), satellite communications, commercial spaceflight and telecommunications. While its reusable rockets and Starlink satellite network have established its position in the commercial space industry, its latest investments and strategic partnerships suggest that its growth ambitions extend well beyond Earth orbit.

The company's recent developments are significant for investors. From securing a place in NASA's ambitious Moon Base program to pursuing multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure agreements and expanding its wireless spectrum holdings, SpaceX is positioning itself to benefit from several rapidly growing industries.

NASA's Moon Base Program Opens Growth Opportunity

One of SpaceX's latest developments is its selection by NASA for the next phase of the Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative announced on Nov. 7, 2026.

NASA selected eight companies, including SpaceX, to compete for future lunar cargo-delivery missions under its new CLPS 2 framework. The 10-year program has a combined maximum contract value of $10 billion, while NASA also increased the existing CLPS 1.0 contract value from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion, per Yahoo Finance.

The program is to establish a sustained presence near the Moon's south pole. It will require commercial companies to develop and operate increasingly sophisticated landers capable of transporting scientific equipment, technology and infrastructure to the lunar surface.

SpaceX creates a potential revenue stream through its launch and transportation capabilities. The company is expected to launch communications satellites aboard Starship in 2028, helping establish connectivity between lunar operations and mission-control infrastructure.

This could strengthen SpaceX's position in the emerging lunar communications market, wherein reliable data transmission will be essential for future exploration and infrastructure development.

Lucrative Deals With Tech Behemoths

SpaceX is increasingly positioning itself as a provider of large-scale computing infrastructure, competing with established cloud providers and emerging AI-focused data center operators. Its Colossus and Colossus II facilities in Memphis, TN, are central to this strategy.

SpaceX signed cloud services agreements with Anthropic in May 2026 across its Colossus and Colossus II facilities. Under the agreements, Anthropic committed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, subject to contractual provisions. SpaceX signed a separate cloud services agreement with Google GOOGL. Google agreed to pay $920 million per month for 32 months. At full rates, those two contracts add up to $6.5 billion a quarter. That equals about 86% of Super Intelligence's third-quarter revenues, as quoted on Yahoo Finance.

Story Continues

Together, these agreements represent substantial potential contracted revenues and demonstrate how SpaceX is monetizing its computing infrastructure beyond its AI applications. SpaceX's ability to offer these resources to third-party customers could turn its AI infrastructure into a significant recurring-revenue business.

Per the above-mentioned Yahoo Finance article, speaking at the Baron Investment Conference on Friday, Musk outlined an ambitious growth trajectory for SpaceX, projecting an annualized revenue run rate of more than $100 billion by December 2026 and $500 billion by December 2027.

Strong Quarterly Results Provide Financial Backing

SpaceX's latest financial results indicate that its expansion is already translating into substantial revenue growth.

For the third quarter of 2026, SpaceX reported revenues of $14.6 billion, skyrocketing 161% from $5.6 billion in the year-ago quarter. Net income reached $4.4 billion against a net loss of $1.1 billion a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA surged 306% to $8.8 billion.

The Super Intelligence segment generated $7.56 billion in revenues, while Connectivity contributed $5.25 billion and Space generated $1.77 billion.

Starlink Expansion & Spectrum Investments Could Disrupt Telecommunications

Starlink remains an important contributor to the company's recurring revenues. Its connectivity segment recorded 69% year-over-year revenue growth and a 99% surge in operating income. This reflects rising demand from consumer subscribers, as well as enterprise and government customers.

Starlink already provides broadband connectivity across multiple countries and serves consumers, businesses, airlines, maritime operators and government customers. Its satellite network gives SpaceX an advantage in regions where conventional broadband infrastructure is expensive or difficult to deploy.

SpaceX-Heavy ETFs to Benefit

Baron First Principles ETF RONB has been the largest publicly available ETF holder of SpaceX, with total assets of $341 million.

The fund invested 37.86% of the portfolio in SpaceX. It has an expense ratio of 1.00%. The fund trades with a three-month average trading volume of 144,000 shares.

Roundhill Space & Technology ETF MARS invests across the commercial space ecosystem — launch providers, satellite operators, communications, robotics and related technologies, with assets under management worth $41.3 million.

SPCX has 24.12% of its weightage in the fund's portfolio. It has an expense ratio of 0.75% and trades at a three-month average trading volume of about 26,000 shares.

VanEck Space ETF WARP offers exposure to companies involved in satellite infrastructure, launch services, aerospace and defense technology, with assets under management worth $41.5 million.

SpaceX has a weightage of 20.83% in WARP. The fund charges an expense ratio of 0.50% and trades at a three-month average trading volume of about 38,000 shares.

news.Title: Jensen Huang's exit puts Nvidia's $530 billion web of AI deals under the microscope
news.Content:
Jensen Huang didn't just sell chips for the AI boom. He helped pay for it, and Wall Street is now repricing everyone on his tab.

Huang resigned as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO and left its board Thursday, effective immediately, after reports of two affairs , one involving an alleged Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the company still plans to report earnings Tuesday.

Nvidia stock sank to its lowest level in more than a year, putting it about $2 trillion below its October record at its low. But the selling hasn't hit the AI trade evenly . Nebius ( NBIS ) and CoreWeave ( CRWV ), cloud companies that rent out Nvidia chips, took the worst of it, while rivals Broadcom ( AVGO ) and AMD ( AMD ) and most of Big Tech held up.

That pattern traces the bank of Nvidia .

Nvidia owns stakes in Intel ( INTC ), SpaceX ( SPCX ), CoreWeave, and Coherent ( COHR ), and it has pledged up to $10 billion to Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) ahead of its IPO next week . It also has a preliminary deal to put as much as $100 billion into OpenAI.

Nvidia's latest quarterly filing lists about $530 billion in commitments and guarantees, by Yahoo Finance's count, including roughly $65 billion to rent back cloud capacity from companies like CoreWeave and a guarantee of up to $105 billion on OpenAI's Ohio data center leases.

"It does bring into question what we've been talking about for ... the better part of the last year, which is a lot of these circular relationships," Liz Thomas, chief market strategist at SoFi, said at Yahoo Finance Invest .

What to know about Jensen Huang's resignation:

Nvidia CEO Huang resigns amid affair scandals

Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?

3 challenges for a post-Jensen Huang Nvidia

The pressure points

The first is the dealmaker himself. Huang sat at the center of these deals, and Kress, who signed off on them as CFO, now decides how many more to write.

The OpenAI guarantee pays out only if OpenAI defaults, and the kind of downturn that would sink OpenAI would likely hit Nvidia's own sales at the same time.

Customers are paying slower too. Nvidia's receivables hit $63 billion last quarter, with bills taking about 60 days to collect, up from 45. Nvidia blamed longer terms on big deals.

And its own portfolio is shrinking. The value of Nvidia's largest public stock holdings has fallen by about $24 billion since June, led by Intel.

The money behind the AI build-out was already getting harder to find. CoreWeave's CEO said this week the company won't borrow without collateral at today's high rates. BofA's Savita Subramanian told Yahoo Finance the tech giants are now selling more of their own stock than they buy back, saying they're "net issuers today rather than buying back their stock."

Story Continues

Nvidia's balance sheet is the counterweight, with about $99 billion in cash and securities against $33 billion of debt at the end of July.

Tuesday's earnings report will show whether Kress stands behind the guidance and the commitments, and whether customers are paying on time.

Thomas put the question for next week bluntly.

"Can the market survive without positive results from Nvidia?"

news.Title: Stock market today: S&P 500, Nasdaq sink as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns, stock tanks
news.Content: US stocks dropped on Thursday after chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ) announced CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, dragging down tech stocks. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 0.4%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) dropped 0.6%, backsliding from Wednesday's chip stock-led rally. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) remained flat. Nvidia stock tumbled 7% after trimming losses. The chipmaker has long stood at the heart of the AI investment boom that has powered this year's stock market. Nvidia's web of tie-ups with other AI companies also creates uncertainty about how great the fallout from Huang's affairs and potential dismissal could be for the market broadly. Follow the latest developments on Nvidia's CEO here . Some chipmakers, including Intel ( INTC ) and Micron ( MU ) fell, while others, such as Nvidia rival AMD ( AMD ) rose. In Asia, stocks held steady. The tumult, which is just the latest incident to raise investor doubts about the artificial intelligence trade that has powered this year's stock market, adds even more pressure for everything to go right in Anthropic's planned public debut next week . In a related programming note, Yahoo Finance's annual Invest event is here, and we'll be bringing you insights from our conversations with corporate leaders, including AMD CEO Lisa Su, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, Starbucks ( SBUX ) CEO Brian Niccol, United Airlines ( UAL ) CEO Scott Kirby, and many others. Meanwhile, energy prices sharply reversed course Wednesday with Brent Crude Futures ( BZ=F ) rising about $93 per barrel following a week of declines. The move came after President Trump shared comments that have raised worries that there is no end in sight for the US-Iran conflict. hovered above. While the bond market was closed Wednesday, Wall Street analysts have rapidly adjusted their forecasts for more and bigger interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve following Tuesday's hotter-than-expected inflation report. A more hawkish central bank is viewed as a negative for US borrowers and riskier assets, including cryptocurrencies. Most digital assets were in the red early Wednesday, with bitcoin ( BTC ) tumbling overnight. Major index provider MSCI is officially removing bitcoin's biggest bull, Strategy ( MSTR ), from its USA indices. The CBOE Volatility Index, or VIX ( ^VIX ), rose to around 18.4, just above its average level of 18.2 for 2026, according to Yahoo Finance data. The company's market cap was still below $4 trillion as shares have dropped roughly 30% over the past month. 51 mins ago David Hollerith Stocks fall as Nvidia sinks after Jensen Huang steps down US stocks opened lower Thursday as Nvidia shares sank following CEO Jensen Huang's decision to step down, rattling an artificial intelligence trade that had just begun to recover. Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares tumbled more than 10% before the bell, dragging on other AI-linked stocks after Huang's departure added another layer of uncertainty around the chipmaker. news.Title: Rivian CEO says robotaxis won't end car ownership — he's betting on both
news.Content: Rivian ( RIVN ) CEO RJ Scaringe doesn't think robotaxis will kill car ownership in America — and he's building the company's self-driving strategy around that belief. "I don't think it's the end of car ownership. I think maybe it goes from 95% to 90% [of miles driven in personally owned vehicles]," Scaringe said at Yahoo Finance Invest . His view comes as the EV maker pours investment into autonomy on both the software and hardware sides. Scaringe expects driverless rides to grow fastest in dense cities like New York. But he doesn't see the whole country giving up its cars to "use rideshare services and unplug and plug in car seats." So the company is betting on both sides — unlike Tesla ( TSLA ), which seems to be betting fully on autonomous products like the Cybercab and killing off vehicles like the Model S, Model X , and Cybertruck . For Rivian, the robotaxi is on one side. The company struck a deal with Uber worth up to $1.25 billion to supply as many as 50,000 robotaxi versions of its R2 SUV. The first 10,000 are set for San Francisco and Miami by 2028. "Particularly for places like New York, San Francisco, downtown Seattle, like these more urban dense environments, it's an incredible unlock," Scaringe said. On the other side is a self-driving car for personal use. Scaringe described a Rivian that can "drive you to the airport and drive itself back home" or "go pick up the kids from school." (Scaringe, a parent to three young children, has said in the past that he would love to see that happen.) Fully self-driving cars could shrink a two- or three-car household to one or two vehicles, he said. He expects new models in between, like neighbors co-owning a car that drops one person off at work and then comes back for the other. Those will likely emerge "in the 2030s," he said. The first step is point-to-point driving, where the owner types in an address and the car drives there while the driver supervises. Rivian began inviting select Autonomy+ subscribers into an early access program on Oct. 15, with a wider rollout planned for next year. Scaringe calls it a "staircase" toward Level 4, where the car can drive itself with nobody inside. Getting there depends on how the software develops — and the company's own neural nets. Older self-driving systems relied on handwritten rules, like stay in the lane and don't hit the car ahead. That approach breaks down in complex situations. "You get to a roundabout, and suddenly it's very hard to describe how to behave in a roundabout," Scaringe said. Story Continues Rivian's Large Driving Model (LDM) — powered by a neural net — learns behavior from millions of miles of real driving. Scaringe compared it to a driver from Missouri adjusting to Manhattan: "Okay, those yellow things [cabs] are really aggressive," he joked. Because Rivian sells to consumers, its cars are everywhere, giving the company a diverse dataset for training. But that fleet is far smaller than Tesla's, and Waymo already runs driverless rides in several cities. That's where the R2 comes in to fill in the data pipeline. R2 was Rivian's bestselling vehicle in the third quarter. It helped push deliveries to a record 19,248 and revenue up 38% to $2.155 billion. Still, "mass market" is a stretch for now. The only R2 on sale is the $57,990 Launch Package , and the roughly $45,000 base model isn't due until late 2027. Smaller, cheaper R3 and R4 models will follow. Software is already paying off, however. Software and services revenue rose 45% to $605 million in the quarter , with $354 million coming from its Volkswagen joint venture. The car business still lost money, though, and Rivian expects an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.75 billion to $1.85 billion this year. Despite the spending on AI, Scaringe is no doomsayer about the technology. "AI is ultimately a tool," he said. "It's capable of doing bad things if it's directed to do bad things. But it's not a sentient being." Follow Pras Subramanian on X and Instagram . news.Title: Alphabet and Meta Platforms Pay Dividends. Is Either of Them Worth Owning for Income?
news.Content:
Both Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG) and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) instituted a notable change to their capital allocation policies in 2024. The social media giant moved first. In February of that year, it introduced a $0.50 quarterly dividend. The Google parent followed suit, announcing a quarterly payout of $0.20 in April 2024.

These companies have been wonderful to their shareholders over the years. Both have outperformed the S&P 500 index in the past decade. Capital appreciation was the main driver of returns in investment portfolios.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But now that dividends are a mainstay, do either of these "Magnificent Seven" stocks make sense for investors seeking income-generating opportunities?

Capital allocation has evolved

These companies have raised their dividends in the past couple of years. Alphabet currently pays $0.22 per share, up 10% from the initial distribution. Meta Platforms' dividend is up 5% from the beginning to $0.525 today. While the growth is certainly small, these leadership teams are at least hinting to shareholders that slowly increasing the payouts might be a permanent feature.

There is minimal risk that these dividends come under any pressure. Both businesses have historically operated from a position of financial robustness. In the past five years, Alphabet's quarterly operating margin averaged a fantastic 30.4%. At 36.4%, Meta Platforms' average margin is even better. And combined, they have $67.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents on their balance sheets.

Dividends are well covered by their earnings streams. Through the first nine months of 2026, Alphabet's net income was almost 25 times higher than its dividends, while Meta Platforms' bottom line was nearly 13 times greater than what it paid in distributions to shareholders. From this vantage point, it looks like the payouts are safe.

However, investors shouldn't rush to buy these businesses if all they're after is a meaningful income stream. The dividend yields are tiny. Alphabet, at a dividend yield of 0.31%, and Meta Platforms, at 0.33%, aren't attracting any attention in this regard. These figures are significantly lower than the inflation rate.

There are superior choices out there. The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF , for example, offers a much better dividend yield of 1.07%. More stable consumer stocks, like Coca-Cola , Procter & Gamble , and Altria Group , pay investors sizable amounts. And it's hard to ignore the 10-year Treasury, which currently yields 5%.

Story Continues

There's only one reason to own these tech stocks

Given how small their dividend yields are, Alphabet and Meta Platforms don't exactly cater to income seekers. On the other hand, they still target investors who want to add growth opportunities to their portfolios. These businesses offer the potential for market-beating returns over the next five or 10 years.

Their scale is not an inhibitor. Alphabet posted 25% year-over-year revenue growth in Q3, similar to Meta Platforms' 26% gain. This points to long expansionary runways ahead. These companies are direct beneficiaries of the internet's proliferation.

These management teams have been directing their time and resources to artificial intelligence (AI), which is sucking up capital that might otherwise have gone to raising dividend payouts. Both Alphabet and Meta Platforms will invest hundreds of billions of dollars this year in technical infrastructure to expand compute capacity and support their AI initiatives.

And they're raising external funding to power these ambitions, in turn pausing share buybacks, which historically played a key role in returning capital to investors. Free cash flow has also turned negative. This development will test the market's patience because nobody knows the kinds of returns these substantial AI-related investments will bring. It's impossible to predict when the data center spending boom will peak or who will capture the excess profits.

On an earnings basis, however, these two leading technology stocks trade at very compelling valuations. Market sentiment reflects elevated levels of uncertainty.

news.Title: Qualcomm CEO: AI won't replace your smartphone anytime soon
news.Content:
Meta ( META ) has the Muse charm and AI-friendly glasses.

OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) is still testing an AI-forward hardware device.

Snap ( SNAP ) recently dropped its latest AI smart glasses.

And Tesla ( TSLA ) is starting to pump out humanoid robots.

But despite all the advancements in tech hardware, the good old smartphone will still have a starring role in our lives as AI becomes more powerful, according to Qualcomm ( QCOM ) CEO Cristiano Amon.

"There's something very interesting happening with the phone right now. In the short term, the phone market is, it's bad, right? It's suppressed because of memory prices. The market has been down in 2026, and 2027 is going to be probably flat to down. But the most important thing is that the phone is not going anywhere," Amon said at Yahoo Finance Invest.

Amon explained how AI — particularly agentic AI — will change how we use our phones. "You are going to continue to operate your phone for everything that's relevant to you, your apps, but you're going to have agents. They're going to operate the phone for you, and eventually, certain workloads, you're going to relegate to the agent," he said, adding that phones will "play a very important processing hub for a lot of the content and the sensing, even as workloads shift to glasses and other personal AI devices. So what we are seeing right now in the mobile space, a lot of traction with glasses, a lot of traction with different things like keychains for agents like the Muse, and watches are becoming interesting again, and a lot of processing on the phone. So, phone's not going to go anywhere. Workloads are going to shift, and eventually you're going to have a more powerful phone. We just need to go follow that transition."

Qualcomm remains a major player in the handset market even as it increasingly diversifies its business to auto technology and advanced AI chips.

Handset chips remained Qualcomm's single largest business in the most recent quarter . But smartphone processor revenue dropped 26% year over year to $5.14 billion in its fiscal fourth quarter due to industrywide memory shortages and Apple's ( AAPL ) transition toward in-house modems.

Insights from Yahoo Finance Invest 2026

Qualcomm CEO on tech stock meltdown: 'There is no AI correction' for us

Qualcomm CEO: Elon Musk is serious about SpaceX's cellular network ambitions

Yahoo Finance Company of the Year: Anthropic's AI dominance

Across the entire 2026 fiscal year, smartphone sales accounted for $24.07 billion of the company's $37.21 billion total semiconductor revenue. Sales for the fiscal year dropped 13% from the prior year.

That mobile contraction was partially buffered by aggressive non-handset diversification, led by automotive chip revenue surging 89% to a record $1.99 billion.

Story Continues

"It's interesting when you think about the mobile industry, there's a huge cemetery of companies. You have companies that went from hero to zero, the ones that didn't see the change. We're actually fortunate enough that we survived all of those different transitions," Amon said.

news.Title: ‘That Would Be an Honor’: Elon Musk Answers a Plea to Hire Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s Board Ousts Its CEO of 33 Years Following $600 Billion Plunge
news.Content:
Jensen Huang has lost the job he's held for 33 years. Elon Musk has already said what he'd think of having him.

Nividia's now former co-founder and CEO Huang preempted an explicitly public ouster vote by the board by resigning. However, Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk is making it clear where he stands.

More News from Barchart

Dear SpaceX Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 13

Oracle Stock Just Scored a New $325 Price Target

Nvidia Stock Plunges After Hours as Reports of a Second Jensen Huang Relationship Could Force the CEO Out

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

Financial blog Zerohedge posted "Elon please hire Jensen" on X on Wednesday night. "That would be an honor," Musk replied.

Musk replied hours after The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to remove Huang. The board met late Wednesday to decide his future, and as of early Thursday, Huang had resigned. Nvidia shares fell more than 8% in after hours trading.

The pressure built fast. On Sunday, the board opened an independent investigation into reporting that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." Huang acknowledged an affair in a message to employees the same day. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive who reports directly to him.

Sponsored Content: The company behind the first FDA-cleared AI skin cancer device of its kind is now open to everyday investors. See How to Own a Stake.

A Bromance Built On Chips

Musk's offer didn't come out of nowhere. Over the past year, the two men have tied their companies closer together.

In August, SpaceX announced that it is partnering with Nvidia to design the compute payload for Starmind AI1, the first satellite in its planned network of orbital AI data centers. SpaceX has applied to the Federal Communications Commission to launch up to 1 million Starmind satellites.

"Old friends are the best friends. Jensen rocks," Musk wrote on X on Oct. 15. "The Star Mind computer being co-engineered by SpaceX and Nvidia is far better than almost anyone expects and will reach volume production next year."

Huang Went From Skeptic to Believer

Huang has praised Musk just as warmly, especially about Terafab, the chip factory Tesla and SpaceX are building in Austin, Texas.

"If anybody could do it, he can," Huang said at the All-In Summit in September. "We were on a flight together and we spent a lot of time talking about it. Once he decides to do something, it's hard to stop him. You can't discourage Elon, which is one of his superpowers."

Story Continues

That was a turnaround. When Musk first floated a Tesla chip fab in November 2025, Huang said, "Building advanced chip manufacturing is extremely hard."

Wall Street Is Already Running the Numbers

Nvidia has lost more than $450 billion in market value since the board announced its probe, according to CBS News . Bernstein cut the stock to "market perform" and lowered its price target to $200 from $400.

Before the resignation, Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives estimated Nvidia's fair value at $225 a share without Huang, compared with $300 if he stayed. That's well below the bullish targets Wall Street floated earlier this year.

The board has appointed Harvey C. Jones as chair, and Colette Kress, Nvidia's current executive vice president and chief financial officer, will serve as interim CEO. However, there has been no permanent successor announced. Bloomberg reported that it's working with an outside firm to identify possible replacements. Huang still owns a big stake in the company he built.

Plenty of CEOs would probably want Huang on their team. Musk just said it out loud while Nvidia's board was still deciding whether Huang keeps the job he's held since 1993.

news.Title: Can Nokia's Expanded One New Zealand Deal Accelerate Its AI Growth?
news.Content:
Nokia Corporation NOK is strengthening its footprint in the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven telecommunications market through an expanded partnership with One New Zealand to accelerate the operator's transition toward autonomous networks. The collaboration highlights Nokia's focus on advancing AI-native network operations and supporting the growing demand for intelligent, automated telecommunications infrastructure.

Per the agreement, Nokia will supply its Assurance Center and Autonomous Networks Data Suite to One New Zealand, along with research and development co-creation and consulting services. These solutions will establish a unified and trusted data foundation, enabling the operator to anticipate network conditions, make faster operational decisions and resolve potential issues before they affect customers.

The company will also provide advanced network management capabilities through its glass-box approach, enabling One New Zealand to monitor network operations and understand automated decisions. The expanded deployment will offer greater flexibility to develop AI-driven applications, improve network automation and maintain control over data and operational systems.

The initiative aligns with Nokia's broader strategy to develop programmable, AI-native network infrastructure for the next generation of telecommunications services. As AI adoption increases and network operators seek greater efficiency, reliability and automation, the company is positioned to benefit from rising demand for autonomous network technologies and advanced network management solutions.

How Are Competitors Performing?

Nokia faces competition from Ericsson ERIC and Cisco Systems, Inc. CSCO. Ericsson continues to expand its AI capabilities by developing intelligent network solutions to improve connectivity, performance and energy efficiency. The company is integrating AI into its radio access networks to optimize operations and automate network management. Ericsson is working with VodafoneThree to deploy AI-powered 5G radio technology in the United Kingdom, aiming to improve network capacity, coverage and energy efficiency.

Cisco continues to strengthen its AI infrastructure portfolio with advanced networking technologies designed to support large-scale AI workloads. The company has introduced its Silicon One G302 switching silicon, which offers 51.2 Tbps capacity to enhance data-center connectivity and network performance. Cisco is collaborating with NVIDIA Corporation NVDA to develop advanced optical technology that increases bandwidth capacity and improves connectivity for AI data centers.

Story Continues

NOK's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Nokia shares have gained 24.5% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 17.9%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

From a valuation standpoint, Nokia trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of 1.97, below the industry tally of 4.92.

Earnings estimates for 2026 have remained static at 39 cents over the past 60 days, while those for 2027 have decreased 6% to 47 cents.

Nokia currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Can Intel's Altera Partnership Drive Growth in Edge and Physical AI?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC is expanding its presence in the Edge and Physical Artificial Intelligence (AI) markets through a strategic partnership with Altera to simplify sensor integration and accelerate the development of intelligent systems. The company will combine its processors, connectivity and software technologies with Altera's Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) to meet the growing demand for real-time data processing across industries.

Under the agreement, Intel plans to help Original Equipment Manufacturers simplify the integration of multiple sensors and improve the processing of complex data in sensor-intensive environments. The companies plan to develop modular sensor bridge reference solutions that offer greater flexibility in system design while meeting performance, latency, power consumption and cost requirements.

The company's solutions are designed for applications across healthcare, aerospace and defense and robotics, including advanced medical equipment, next-generation mission systems and intelligent robots. Intel will also make its Open Edge Platform SDK available alongside an Altera SDK to help developers build and deploy edge AI applications more efficiently.

The development could create additional growth opportunities for Intel as demand for edge computing and Physical AI continues to rise. By broadening its computing capabilities, the company aims to address emerging industry requirements and strengthen its position in next-generation AI applications.

How Are Competitors Performing in the AI Space?

Intel faces competition from Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM and Advanced Micro Devices AMD. Qualcomm is expanding its AI business beyond smartphones and connected devices into data centers, enterprise computing and edge applications. The company is improving its AI software capabilities to make it easier to develop and deploy AI applications across different hardware platforms. Qualcomm is working with Amazon to develop custom chips and high-speed optical connectivity for next-generation AI data centers, while expanding its AI offerings across devices and cloud infrastructure.

AMD is strengthening its position in the AI infrastructure market through its Instinct GPUs, EPYC processors and ROCm software platform. The company is advancing its partnership with Meta, with its Helios rack-scale systems now undergoing testing and its processors and GPUs supporting Meta's AI workloads. AMD is expanding its enterprise AI capabilities through partnerships focused on developing open infrastructure solutions for AI workloads across businesses and cloud platforms.

Story Continues

INTC's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Shares of Intel have gained 64.9% over the past year against the industry's decline of 5.4%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Going by the price/book ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 3.22 times book value, lower than the industry average of 15.51.

INTC's earnings estimates for 2026 have decreased 2% to $1.47 per share, while those for 2027 have declined 9.7% to $1.77 over the past 60 days.

Intel currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .
