news.Title: Jim Cramer Is Bullish on These 5 Stocks Amid Nvidia Controversy
news.Content:
After years of unconditionally backing Jensen Huang and Nvidia (NASDAQ), Jim Cramer's confidence in the chipmaker has been shaken by the controversy surrounding its chief executive. And the reasons are understandable.

Cramer's investment thesis on Nvidia has always been closely tied to Huang's leadership. The CNBC host has repeatedly praised Huang as a visionary capable of transforming entire industries through artificial intelligence. He believed so strongly in Nvidia that he even named his dog after the company in 2017.

But with Huang's future now uncertain following allegations involving a suspected Chinese spy, Cramer's longtime conviction is facing a serious test. The controversy has raised questions about Huang's reputation and whether he can continue leading the company.

Cramer recently downgraded Nvidia from a buy to a hold, citing uncertainty surrounding the investigation.

Billionaires Ray Dalio and Philippe Laffont both trimmed their Nvidia stakes in the second quarter, even before this controversy began. See which AI stocks they still own .

That doesn't mean Cramer has turned bearish on the entire stock market (see what Cramer was buying last week ).

While the Nvidia controversy and concerns about massive AI infrastructure spending have made him increasingly cautious, Cramer believes there are still plenty of attractive investment opportunities elsewhere.

During the recent CNBC Investing Club's annual meeting, Cramer and portfolio director Jeff Marks reviewed over 30 stocks in the Club's portfolio, identifying several companies they remain bullish on. Cramer has also continued to highlight investment opportunities outside the increasingly volatile AI trade.

Against this backdrop, we take a look at 10 stocks Jim Cramer is bullish on, ranked by the number of hedge funds holding stakes in them at the end of the second quarter of 2026.

Before this controversy, two well-known billionaires were backing Nvidia as an AI stock. See who they are .

You can click to read our full list on Jim Cramer Is Bullish on These 10 Stocks Amid Nvidia Controversy . The top 5 stocks from that list are mentioned below.

Methodology

To pick the stocks, we went through CNBC's coverage of Jim Cramer's latest stock picks, mainly the reports on his CNBC Investing Club annual meeting. From that coverage, we selected 5 stocks that Cramer is bullish on. We then ranked them by the number of hedge funds holding stakes in each one at the end of the second quarter of 2026, using Insider Monkey's database of 1,000+ hedge funds.

Story Continues

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

You can see the top 5 stocks Jim Cramer is bullish on these days in our video by clicking the image below.

#5. Wells Fargo & Company (NYSE:WFC)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 94

Wells Fargo & Company (NYSE:WFC) is another banking stock Cramer remains optimistic about. In the Nov. 6 CNBC Investing Club review, Cramer and his team highlighted the removal of Wells Fargo's asset cap as an important development for the bank's long-term growth prospects.

The Club praised CEO Charlie Scharf for improving operations and investing in businesses that generate fee-based revenue, including investment banking.

Cramer's team also considered Wells Fargo shares attractively valued and expressed optimism about the company's prospects heading into 2027.

Although the Investing Club did not issue an immediate buy recommendation, its commentary reflected a positive long-term view of the bank's transformation and earnings potential. Goldman Sachs added Wells Fargo to its US Conviction List in July and said the bank is moving from defense to offense. Read Goldman's view here .

#4. Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 99

Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) is one of the enterprise software companies Jim Cramer continues to favor despite growing investor concerns about AI potentially disrupting traditional software businesses.

During the Nov. 6 portfolio review, Cramer and his team expressed confidence in Salesforce's strategy of working with leading artificial intelligence developers.

It's not clear how long Cramer can stay bullish on Salesforce (NYSE:CRM). The AI onslaught is taking a direct jab at Salesforce's business. Microsoft and Alphabet are a growing threat because they spend far more on research and development and run their own clouds. Smaller players such as Palantir and HubSpot are also growing faster than Salesforce. Over the past five years, Salesforce's share of the CRM software market has dropped to 20% from 24%.

Salesforce's profit margins also face pressure because the company does not own a cloud. It rents computing power from Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. Salesforce is moving from charging per user seat to charging for AI usage. As that happens, it will pay more to these cloud providers, which could push its gross margin lower. The same cloud giants also compete with Salesforce, so it has little room to raise prices.

Antipodes Global Fund said in its third-quarter 2026 investor letter that the growth of Agentforce, Salesforce's AI agent platform, is strengthening the company's AI story. Check the full letter here .

#3. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 169

Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) remains one of Jim Cramer's favored long-term investments, even as concerns about artificial intelligence spending have unsettled parts of the technology sector.

During the Nov. 6 CNBC Investing Club review, Cramer and his team reiterated their conviction in Apple as a stock investors should hold for the long term rather than attempt to trade around short-term market fluctuations.

The Club said Apple enjoys a notable advantage in the AI race because it can incorporate technology developed by partners such as Alphabet into its products without committing the same enormous sums to building data centers.

What Cramer is saying actually forms the basis of Apple's bull case. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) has found a low-cost way to compete in AI. It partnered with Alphabet to use the Gemini model to power its new Siri, so it does not need to build massive data centers of its own. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta are spending huge sums on AI infrastructure every year, while Apple keeps its spending low and protects its cash.

The new Siri also makes the iPhone harder to leave. It pulls details from users' messages, emails and photos to give more personal answers. The longer people use it, the more it learns about them, and switching to another phone would mean losing that history. Apple also has a new way to make money from AI. Basic AI features are free today, but management has confirmed that paid tiers are coming.

Billionaire Ken Fisher shares Cramer's long-term view on Apple. Find out if you should buy the stock .

#2. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 273

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) remains one of Jim Cramer's preferred technology stocks as investors increasingly scrutinize the enormous sums being spent on artificial intelligence infrastructure.

In the Nov. 6 CNBC Investing Club portfolio review, Cramer and his team praised Microsoft's financial discipline and its ability to maintain positive free cash flow despite substantial investment in AI and cloud computing.

Cramer believes a slowdown in data center development could benefit Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ) by reducing construction costs and easing pressure on capital spending.

Microsoft already operates extensive data center infrastructure, giving it an advantage over smaller competitors that depend on new construction to expand their businesses.

A slower pace of development could also reduce pressure on capital spending and improve free cash flow, strengthening Microsoft's position amid growing concerns about the sustainability of massive AI investments.

Cramer's bullish view centers on Microsoft's ability to continue benefiting from AI adoption while maintaining a financially resilient business. Microsoft is also a top AI pick of billionaire Ken Fisher, even though the stock barely moved over the past year. Click to read our full analysis .

#1. Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 369

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) is one of Jim Cramer's latest explicit stock recommendations amid concerns about slowing data center development.

In a Nov. 9 CNBC commentary, Cramer said a slowdown in the construction of new data centers could actually benefit established cloud computing companies such as Amazon and Microsoft.

Why? Cramer believes companies with extensive existing infrastructure would be better positioned than smaller competitors whose growth depends on continued construction and financing.

Cramer specifically recommended Amazon shares and discussed the possibility of the stock reaching $300, representing nearly 10% upside from its trading level at the time.

The bullish recommendation followed the CNBC Investing Club's Nov. 6 portfolio review, in which Cramer and Marks expressed confidence in Amazon's latest quarterly performance. Amazon is also one of the four stocks that both President Trump and Nancy Pelosi bought. See the other three picks .

Before its latest earnings report, Amazon was the top AI stock pick shared by Cramer and billionaire Ken Fisher. Read our full take on the stock .

While we acknowledge the potential of AMZN as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Bitdeer: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.Content:
On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, Bitdeer (NASDAQ:BTDR) announced an 89% year-over-year revenue increase to $320.7 million as it transitions power assets into high-performance computing data centers. The company is pivoting from volatile Bitcoin mining to long-term contracted artificial intelligence (AI) cloud infrastructure. Three things management said stand out.

1. Contracted AI Revenue Reaches $7.6 Billion

Bitdeer is securing multiyear contracts for its high-performance computing (HPC, data centers built for intensive AI tasks) infrastructure and cloud services, giving the business visible cash flows that don't depend on cryptocurrency price swings.

Our AI platform now represents approximately $7.6 billion of expected contracted revenue.

-- Haris Basit, Chief Strategy Officer

2. Project Financing Prioritizes Non-Dilutive Capital Growth

Management is backing data center construction with asset-level debt and customer prepayments that cover more than 50% of graphics processing unit (GPU) costs, keeping share dilution low.

We prioritize non-dilutive project level financing wherever contracted cash flows can support it.

-- Michael Potter, Chief Financial Officer

3. Power Capacity Flexible Across Mining and Cloud Computing

With 3.1 gigawatts of total power capacity, Bitdeer monetizes available electricity through Bitcoin mining while preparing sites for long-term data center leases.

We can mine to monetize available power today while we develop infrastructure for long-term HPC leases, and we can invest in GPU capacity when and where we see attractive contracted demand.

Looking Ahead

Demand for artificial intelligence compute outpaces the available power supply, and Bitdeer relies on pre-energized sites, low-cost power, and proprietary hardware to convert mining locations into data centers, while maintaining financing execution and capital discipline.

Our model is built for this environment. Our AI and crypto platforms share one power foundation and complement each other.

The company aims to maximize returns by deploying power where economic value is highest, balancing short-term crypto earnings with long-term data center revenue.

Our objective is simple. Maximize the return on every power asset and protect the balance sheet while we do it.

news.Title: Warby Parker bets on Google AI glasses for growth, but privacy fears still loom
news.Content:
By Danielle Kaye

NEW YORK, Nov 12 (Reuters) - Warby Parker is entering the smart glasses market in partnership with Google and Samsung, betting that demand for the artificial intelligence wearables will balloon in the coming years.

But the New York-based fashion brand, known for its affordable eyewear, is also seeking to ‌head off privacy concerns that have weighed on existing producers of the glasses, most of which embed small cameras allowing wearers to record their ‌surroundings without taking out their phone.

The Warby Parker glasses are broadly similar to Meta smart glasses already available from Ray-Ban and Oakley maker EssilorLuxottica, which have faced regulatory scrutiny from Norway to Australia. Also ​like the Meta glasses, they will connect to an AI assistant, in this case Google's Gemini, for everything from directions to language translation.

The big difference from existing versions on the market is the privacy framework embedded in the glasses from the outset, Warby Parker Co-CEO Neil Blumenthal told Reuters.

Alphabet's Google will not use visuals captured with the glasses to train its AI. The glasses will bar facial recognition of bystanders. And a small white notification light on the front of the glasses automatically turns on when a user ‌starts recording video.

Shoppers will start placing pre-orders from Warby Parker on ⁠Thursday. Ray-Ban's Meta glasses still dominate, representing 81.3% of AI glasses shipments in the first half of this year, according to tech research group Omdia.

But brands from Warby Parker to luxury group Kering — poised to release glasses also in partnership with Google — ⁠are looking to gain a foothold. Global AI glasses shipments more than doubled in the first half of 2026 from a year ago, though growth has slowed since the second half of last year, Omdia data shows.

Meta's AI glasses also include a camera notification light on the front, a Meta spokesperson said, adding that input from safety experts helped inform the privacy features ​on ​its glasses.

CATEGORY CONFRONTS PRIVACY RISKS

Optimism that Warby Parker's "intelligent eyewear" plan will prove to be a ​major growth engine has helped its shares rally by nearly 40% this year, ‌outperforming a 10% gain in the S&P 500.

The company expects an addition of several percentage points to fourth-quarter revenue growth from the new wearable technology, executives said on an earnings call earlier this month.

"As long as the tools provide utility to customers, then we'll be successful," Blumenthal said.

Story Continues

While the core optical backdrop remains soft, smart glasses are poised to be an "increasingly important driver" of Warby Parker's growth outlook, analysts at TD Cowen wrote in a research note last week.

Still, concerns about privacy could slow their pace of growth. One of Britain's biggest pub chains has restricted the use of the frames, Norway's government is planning a temporary ban on the ‌use of AI glasses in certain locations, and Australia is considering barring the use of camera-equipped ​smart glasses in government workplaces.

GOOGLE AIMS TO REBUILD TRUST

Juston Payne, who leads extended reality products at ​Google, acknowledged that public skepticism could be a risk to growth.

"This is ​an area where, understandably, trust was lost," he told Reuters at a demo for the Warby Parker glasses in New York.

Google says ‌it will embed extensive privacy guardrails into the devices to ​prevent tampering with the recording indicator light; redact ​people's faces from video footage before it is sent to Gemini; and ban targeted advertising on the glasses.

"We are going to change this conversation," Payne said. "We are trying to raise the bar."

But it remains to be seen whether those measures will ease concern about widespread surveillance, if the glasses become ​ubiquitous.

"I'm certainly happy to hear that (video footage is) not automatically fed ‌into AI systems for training," said Calli Schroeder, who leads the AI and human rights program at the Electronic Privacy Information Center, an ​advocacy group. "But that still leaves open: a stranger has footage of my kid on their phone. That's concerning no matter how you phrase ​it."

(Reporting by Danielle Kaye in New York; Editing by Christian Plumb and Matthew Lewis)

news.Title: ONTO Falls 14% in 1 Week as Growth Strength Collides With Valuation
news.Content:
Onto Innovation Inc . ONTO has pulled back even as its operating results remain on an upswing. Third-quarter revenues reached a record $409.7 million, while non-GAAP earnings rose sharply and the current-year earnings estimate has increased 2.7% over the past four weeks.

The tension is clear. Demand visibility is improving, but ONTO still carries a valuation premium and sizable customer concentration. That mix leaves investors weighing accelerating semiconductor demand against the execution needed to justify the stock's pricing.

ONTO's Fundamentals Remain Strong Despite the Drop

Third-quarter revenues increased 87.8% year over year to $409.7 million. Non-GAAP earnings rose 165.2% to $2.44 per share, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 32.6% from 21.1% a year earlier.

Advanced nodes reached record quarterly revenues as Atlas G6 adoption expanded across logic and memory. Advanced packaging and specialty devices also set a record, led by Dragonfly G5 and Firefly inspection systems, keeping ONTO exposed to both front-end process control and AI-related packaging demand.

Onto's Backlog Extends Growth Visibility

Backlog increased another 20% in the third quarter to more than $1.3 billion. Some customer commitments extend into 2028, while management expects sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027.

Onto Innovation Inc. Price and Consensus

Onto Innovation Inc. price-consensus-chart | Onto Innovation Inc. Quote

That visibility is supported by multiple product cycles rather than one platform alone. Dragonfly G5 orders, panel-level packaging demand and Atlas G6 adoption are all contributing. Camtek Ltd . CAMT, another inspection and metrology supplier, also reported record third-quarter 2026 revenues, underscoring continued spending in advanced semiconductor packaging.

ONTO's Premium Valuation Leaves Less Room for Error

ONTO trades at 8.2X trailing 12-month enterprise value-to-sales, above its five-year median of 6.0X and the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 7.8X. The multiple remains below the Zacks sub-industry level, but it still limits the margin for execution setbacks.

KLA Corporation KLAC, a much larger process-control competitor, reported $4.14 billion of fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenues and continues to invest across semiconductor process control. Competitive spending at that scale raises the bar for ONTO to sustain product differentiation while converting its growth into durable margins.

Onto Still Faces Concentration and Cost Risks

Four customers accounted for 57.1% of ONTO's revenues during the first nine months of 2026. Taiwan and South Korea together represented about 58.9% of revenues, increasing exposure to customer capital-spending shifts and regional disruptions.

Story Continues

Input-cost inflation and trade restrictions remain additional risks. Inventory rose to $424.2 million at Sept. 30 from $298.3 million at the start of the year, while Semilab USA recorded a $2.8 million third-quarter operating loss. Those factors could offset part of the benefit from higher shipment volumes.

ONTO's Momentum Signal Still Supports Cautious Optimism

ONTO's operating momentum and backlog support the growth case, but the valuation premium and concentration risks argue against treating the pullback alone as proof of a bargain. The stock's near-term profile is stronger than its value characteristics.

ONTO currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Its Momentum Score of B is favorable for momentum-oriented investors, while the Value Score of D and Growth Score of C are less supportive. The VGM Score of C reinforces a mixed style profile, making continued execution and estimate revisions important to the investment case. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: ONTO Raises Q4 Outlook as AI Packaging Demand Drives Record Growth
news.Content:
Onto Innovation Inc. ONTO raised its fourth-quarter outlook after record third-quarter revenues and broader adoption across advanced packaging and advanced nodes. The update shows that AI-related semiconductor investment is translating into higher demand for the company's process-control tools.

The next question is durability. Backlog now exceeds $1.3 billion, while customer commitments extend into 2028 in some cases. That visibility gives ONTO a longer runway than a single strong quarter would imply.

ONTO's Q4 Guidance Points to Another Record Step-Up

Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $430 million to $450 million. The midpoint implies sequential growth of more than 7% and would bring full-year 2026 revenues to about $1.49 billion, representing growth of more than 45%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Profitability is expected to improve alongside the revenue increase. ONTO projects fourth-quarter non-GAAP gross margin of 57.7-58.3% and non-GAAP operating margin of 33.5-34.5%, while non-GAAP earnings are expected at $2.59-$2.79 per share.

Onto's Dragonfly G5 Is Scaling With AI Packaging

Advanced packaging and specialty-device revenues increased 35% sequentially in the third quarter, with Dragonfly driving much of the growth. Dragonfly G5 has reached more than 10 customers, and 2027 purchase orders already represent twice its expected 2026 revenues.

The demand backdrop extends beyond ONTO. Camtek Ltd . CAMT, which supplies inspection and metrology systems to advanced semiconductor markets, reported record third-quarter 2026 revenues of $161.3 million and expects 2027 revenues to exceed $800 million. Its outlook also cites advanced packaging demand tied to AI.

ONTO's Atlas G6 Expands Advanced-Node Exposure

Advanced-node revenues reached about $135 million in the third quarter, with memory contributing roughly 60% and logic about 40%. Atlas G6 adoption helped the business reach a quarterly record as customers increased process-control intensity in newer logic and memory nodes.

Management described Atlas G6 as the fastest optical critical dimension platform launch in ONTO's history. KLA Corporation KLAC, a larger semiconductor process-control supplier, reported $3.75 billion of semiconductor process-control revenues in its September quarter, up 29% year over year, reinforcing the scale of investment across this market.

Onto's Backlog Extends the AI Spending Cycle

Backlog increased about 20% in the third quarter to more than $1.3 billion. Management expects sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027, while some orders in panel-level packaging extend into 2028.

Story Continues

The backlog is not being driven by longer tool lead times. Management said customers are planning to secure equipment for multiyear production ramps, and the company has not seen lead-time extensions across its product portfolio. That distinction supports the view that visibility reflects customer investment schedules rather than supply constraints.

ONTO's Near-Term Signals Support the Growth Narrative

The operating picture remains favorable, but valuation and execution still matter. ONTO trades above its five-year median on trailing enterprise value-to-sales, while customer concentration, input costs and the integration of newer investments remain risks.

ONTO currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Its Momentum Score of B complements the favorable near-term earnings-revision backdrop, including a 2.7% increase in the current-year earnings estimate over the past four weeks. The Value Score of D, Growth Score of C and VGM Score of C are less supportive, suggesting investors should weigh the improving earnings trend against valuation and execution demands. news.Title: Is ONTO Worth Buying as Earnings Surge but Valuation Stays Elevated?
news.Content:
Onto Innovation Inc . ONTO is delivering faster earnings growth, broader AI-related demand and improving profitability. The question is whether those gains are sufficient to offset a valuation that remains above its own historical norm.

Backlog, estimate growth and margin expansion support the bull case. Still, capital returns have softened, acquired businesses add execution demands and the stock's valuation leaves less room for disappointment.

ONTO's Earnings Growth Has Accelerated Sharply

Third-quarter revenues rose 87.8% year over year to a record $409.7 million. Non-GAAP operating income increased 189.8% to $133.5 million, while non-GAAP earnings reached $2.44 per share, up 165.2%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The earnings outlook remains constructive. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for 2026 earnings of $8.25 per share and 2027 earnings of $12.44, implying a 50.8% increase next year. The estimate for 2026 earnings has also moved 2.7% higher over the past four weeks.

Onto's AI Exposure Is Broadening Across Products

Dragonfly G5 adoption has expanded to more than 10 customers across high-bandwidth memory and 2.5D packaging. Purchase orders already received for 2027 represent twice the platform's expected 2026 revenues, while Atlas G6 is gaining traction across logic and memory applications.

Advanced-packaging revenues are expected to rise more than 80% in 2026, with management anticipating growth of more than 35% in 2027. Camtek Ltd . CAMT, another inspection and metrology supplier, reported record third-quarter 2026 revenues of $161.3 million and expects 2027 revenues to exceed $800 million, reflecting continued demand in advanced semiconductor packaging.

ONTO's Margin Expansion Strengthens the Bull Case

Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 57.6% in the third quarter from 54% a year earlier. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 32.6%, compared with 21.1% in the prior-year quarter.

Management expects fourth-quarter non-GAAP gross margin of 57.7%-58.3% and sees further improvement in 2027. The extended-factory model, regionalized supply chains and productivity measures support an expectation for roughly 50 basis points of gross-margin expansion per quarter over the next several quarters.

Onto's Valuation and Capital Returns Temper the Upside

ONTO trades at 8.2X trailing 12-month enterprise value-to-sales, above its five-year median of 6.0X and the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 7.8X. That premium places more weight on continued revenue growth and margin execution.

Story Continues

Trailing 12-month return on invested capital is 9.7%, below the company's 10-year median of 11.8%. The $720 million Rigaku investment expanded the capital base, while Semilab USA posted a $2.8 million operating loss in the third quarter. KLA Corporation KLAC, a larger process-control competitor, reported $4.14 billion in fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenues, underscoring the scale and competitive intensity of the market.

ONTO's Ranking Mix Favors Selectivity Over Chasing

The setup favors selectivity rather than treating earnings momentum as an automatic buy signal. ONTO's growth visibility and margin profile are improving, but the valuation premium and lower capital returns argue for discipline on entry price.

ONTO currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Its Momentum Score of B is supportive, while the Value Score of D, Growth Score of C and VGM Score of C show a less uniform style profile. The mix points to favorable near-term earnings-revision momentum, but investors focused on value or broader style strength may prefer to wait for a more balanced risk-reward setup. news.Title: Silicon Motion Vs. Qualcomm: Which Chipmaker Has More Potential?
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO and Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM are premier semiconductor firms with exposure to smartphones, automotive electronics and AI-driven technologies. Silicon Motion is a leading developer of microcontroller ICs for NAND flash storage devices. The semiconductor firm also designs, develops and markets high-performance, low-power semiconductor solutions for original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and other customers.

Qualcomm offers high-performance, low-power chip designs for mobile devices, PCs, XR (Extended Reality), automotive, wearable, robotics, connectivity and AI use cases. The company boasts a comprehensive intellectual property portfolio comprising 4G, 5G and other technologies. Qualcomm's brands include Snapdragon systems-on-chip, FastConnect Wi-Fi and Bluetooth systems, and Qualcomm-branded 4G, 5G and IOT equipment. The company is currently integrating on-device generative AI into all of its product lines.

Let us delve a little deeper into the companies' competitive dynamics to understand which of the two is relatively better placed in the industry.

The Case for SIMO

Silicon Motion has established itself as the leading merchant supplier of client SSD (solid state drive) controllers to module makers, including most market leaders in the United States, Taiwan and China. The company believes that it is well-equipped to adapt to industry changes as it has collaborated with flash vendors to develop proprietary controller technology to overcome the existing weakness of 3D NAND and outshine peers. Silicon Motion has commenced initial sales of 3D SSD controllers to flash partners. It expects this controller to be a significant SSD controller growth driver for the next year, as NAND Flash partners' 3D capacity expands.

Silicon Motion operates a fabless business model, focusing on chip design while outsourcing manufacturing to foundries like TSMC. Consequently, the company has a low capital investment requirement as it does not need expensive fabrication plants, enabling it to adopt advanced manufacturing nodes quickly, leading to higher margins compared to integrated manufacturers. This allows the company to focus on innovation and product development rather than manufacturing complexity. The key growth drivers for SIMO include AI and high-performance computing, cloud data centers, automotive storage, smartphones and mobile devices. Each of these end markets is growing fast and offers lucrative growth potential. Over the past 10 years, the company has shipped more than 5 billion controllers cumulatively – more than any other company in the world. Silicon Motion ships more than 750 million NAND controllers on average every year.

However, sluggishness in the global economy is likely to weigh on the company's wireless and broader semiconductor market. The demand for PCs and smartphones in the end market continues to be soft as numerous suppliers are focusing on reducing their inventory levels. The near-term price fluctuation in the PC market remains a concern. Silicon Motion continues to acquire a large number of companies. While this improves revenue opportunities, business mix and profitability, it adds to integration risks. Moreover, the semiconductor industry is highly dynamic as it is prone to swift technological changes, stiff competition from evolving industry standards and declining average selling prices.

Story Continues

The Case for QCOM

Qualcomm is well-positioned to meet its long-term revenue targets, driven by solid 5G traction, greater visibility and a diversified revenue stream. The company is increasingly focusing on the seamless transition from a wireless communications firm for the mobile industry to a connected processor company for the intelligent edge. Qualcomm is witnessing healthy traction in edge networking, which helps transform connectivity in cars, business enterprises, homes, smart factories, next-generation PCs, wearables and tablets. The automotive telematics and connectivity platforms, digital cockpit and C-V2X solutions are also fueling emerging automotive industry trends such as the growth of connected vehicles, the transformation of the in-car experience and vehicle electrification.

The company is aiming to extend its Oryon CPU and AI acceleration beyond smartphones into PCs and servers. Management observed that its 2026 Snapdragon X2 PC platforms are in production and positioned to enable always-on agentic experiences, supported by a Hexagon NPU delivering up to 85 TOPS. Qualcomm is entering the custom silicon space with a leading hyperscaler and expects initial shipments in the December quarter, adding a revenue stream that is not tied to handset unit cycles. The Alphawave buyout has added high-speed wired connectivity IP and custom silicon capabilities to help accelerate the company's expansion into data centers.

Despite efforts to ramp up its AI initiatives, Qualcomm has been facing tough competition from ASML Holding N.V. ASML in the AI PC market. A shift in the share among OEMs at the premium tier has reduced Qualcomm's near-term opportunity to sell integrated chipsets from the Snapdragon platform. Memory supply constraints and related pricing are adversely impacting its handset revenues as OEMs (particularly in China) continue to draw down channel inventory.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for SIMO & QCOM?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Silicon Motion's 2026 sales indicates a year-over-year rise of 120.9%, while that for EPS suggests growth of 278.9%. The EPS estimates have been trending northward (up 20.5%) over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Qualcomm's fiscal 2027 sales implies year-over-year growth of 4.4%, while that of EPS suggests a decline of 5.7%. The EPS estimates have trended down 0.9% over the past 60 days.

Price Performance & Valuation of SIMO & QCOM

Over the past year, Silicon Motion has soared 112.1% compared with the industry's growth of 79.2%. Qualcomm is up 0.5% over the same period.

Qualcomm looks significantly more expensive than Silicon Motion from a valuation standpoint. Going by the price/sales ratio, SIMO's shares currently trade at 2.33 forward sales, lower than Qualcomm's 4.12.

news.Title: Factbox-Who is Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress?
news.Content:
Nov 12 (Reuters) - Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress is set to take over as interim CEO from Jensen Huang, the company said on Thursday, putting her in charge ‌of the chipmaker whose processors power the world's most advanced supercomputers and AI data ‌centers.

The appointment comes after the board ousted co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of two extramarital affairs, one with ​a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.

Here are five facts about Kress:

CFO SINCE 2013

Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 as executive vice president and chief financial officer and has held the post since. She has appeared alongside Jensen Huang on the company's quarterly earnings calls.

Nvidia's revenue was $4.13 billion in the ‌fiscal year she joined and $215.9 ⁠billion in fiscal 2026.

CAREER BEFORE NVIDIA

Before Nvidia, Kress spent eight years in finance roles at Texas Instruments, then worked at Microsoft from 1997 to 2010. At ⁠Microsoft, she became chief financial officer of the Server and Tools division in 2006, with responsibility for its financial strategy, planning and reporting.

She moved to Cisco in 2010 as senior vice president and chief financial ​officer ​of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organization, where ​she was responsible for financial strategy and ‌business development. She left for Nvidia in 2013.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Kress holds a bachelor of science degree in finance from the University of Arizona and a master of business administration degree from Southern Methodist University, according to Nvidia's annual report filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

She joined Nvidia after nearly 25 years in finance roles at major technology companies, Fortune reported in 2024. She ‌told Fortune Nvidia was the smallest company she had ​worked for when she started there in 2013.

CONTRACT TERMS

Executive officers ​at Nvidia are employed at will and ​have no individual employment, severance or change-in-control agreements, according to the company's ‌proxy statement. Nvidia has said in earlier filings ​that many of its ​peer companies offer such agreements.

Regulatory filings show Kress' pay includes restricted stock units, including a March 2026 award that vests over four years.

WEALTH

Forbes ranks Kress No. 32 on its 2026 ​list of America's richest self-made ‌women. Her shares in the chip firm were valued at roughly $750 million, as of ​Wednesday's close, down from more than $1 billion at the stock's peak last month.

(Reporting by ​Akash Sriram in Bengaluru; Editing by Pooja Desai)

news.Title: A $548 Million Reason to Watch Qualcomm Stock Here
news.Content:
Alphabet (GOOGL) recently disclosed a $548 million stake in semiconductor company Qualcomm (QCOM), marking its first investment in the company and adding to a list of investees, including the likes of SpaceX (SPCX), Arm (ARM), and UiPath (PATH). Of those, SpaceX is easily the biggest holding at roughly $83.7 billion.

Thus, in comparison, Alphabet's investment in Qualcomm is quite modest. Yet the possibilities and rationale behind the stake are anything but.

More News from Barchart

Dear SpaceX Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 13

Oracle Stock Just Scored a New $325 Price Target

Nvidia Stock Plunges After Hours as Reports of a Second Jensen Huang Relationship Could Force the CEO Out

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

About Qualcomm Stock

Founded in 1985, Qualcomm's historical significance comes from its role in developing and commercializing CDMA technology. Its innovations helped establish the foundations of 3G mobile networks and contributed to the evolution of 4G LTE and 5G. Currently, its principal operations are divided into three segments: Qualcomm CDMA Technologies (QCT), Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL), and Qualcomm Strategic Initiatives (QSI).

Valued at a market capitalization of $185 billion, QCOM stock is up about 3% year-to-date (YTD). Notably, the stock offers a dividend yield of 2.15%. Further, the company has raised its dividend consecutively for the past 22 years and returned close to $2 billion to shareholders in the most recent quarter.

But dividends and share repurchases were certainly not the reasons behind Alphabet's investment in Qualcomm. Let's take a closer look.

Solidifying a Long Relationship

To start, we should note that Alphabet's recent investment in Qualcomm is likely a consequence of the latter acquiring Modular for $3.9 billion in July 2026. Modular develops an AI-native software platform that enables AI applications to run efficiently across different hardware architectures. Google Ventures was already an investor in Modular and thus received nearly 3 million Qualcomm shares as a consequence of the acquisition.

Having said that, this investment can bring mutual benefits. For Qualcomm, its Snapdragon processors power a large proportion of premium Android smartphones, and Google controls the Android operating system and several of the most widely used AI services on those devices. Deeper collaboration would allow Qualcomm to demonstrate that its hardware is optimized for Google's latest software and AI workloads. This is commercially valuable when smartphone manufacturers decide which processors to use in their premium devices. Additionally, it would help Qualcomm defend its position against competitors such as MediaTek and Apple (AAPL), which are developing increasingly sophisticated on-device AI capabilities.

Story Continues

The second potential benefit is access to Google's AI models and cloud infrastructure for automotive and other enterprise applications. Qualcomm can sell more than a processor when it offers automakers an integrated solution combining computing hardware, software, connectivity, and AI services. Google's Gemini models and Google Cloud capabilities would make Qualcomm's automotive platforms more compelling to manufacturers seeking to develop intelligent vehicles. In turn, Qualcomm could provide Google with a hardware platform and established industry relationships through which its AI services can be deployed.

Lastly, Qualcomm's fledgling data-center business can receive a serious thrust, as it seeks to clock $15 billion in revenue by fiscal 2029 from the segment. While its $60 billion commitment from Amazon (AMZN) is substantial, the company is also targeting other major hyperscalers like Google, Microsoft (MSFT), and Meta Platforms (META).

Qualcomm's Q4 Report Showed Hiccups

Qualcomm's most recent results for the fourth quarter of 2026 had some undeniable issues, chief among them being the decline in core handset revenues. However, Q1 earnings guidance that missed Wall Street's expectations led to a 9.5% nosedive in QCOM stock. In my view, that decline was unwarranted for a company boasting some solid fundamentals.

Revenue fell 7% year-over-year (YOY) to $10.4 billion. Handset revenue fell 26% YOY to $5.1 billion, as management attributed the slowdown to high memory prices affecting smartphone demand. On the flip side, automotive revenue jumped 89% on a YOY basis to $1.99 billion. Licensing revenue moved 7% lower to $1.3 billion.

Meanwhile, earnings eased by 28% YOY to $2.17 per share, yet that was just enough to beat the consensus estimate of $2.16 per share. Out of the past nine quarters, Qualcomm's earnings have surpassed Street expectations on eight occasions.

For Q1 fiscal 2027, Qualcomm expects revenue between $10.4 billion and $11.2 billion. At the midpoint, this comfortably surpasses the consensus estimate of $10.55 billion. However, earnings guidance led to the recent share price decline, with the company forecasting a range of $2.15 to $2.35 per share. The midpoint of $2.25 comes in lower than the consensus estimate of $2.32 per share.

What should be slightly more concerning is the roughly 20% YOY fall in net cash provided by operating activities for fiscal 2026 to $11.1 billion, as inventories grew significantly YOY to $2.05 billion, reflecting poorly on the company's demand situation. Overall, Qualcomm closed the quarter with a cash balance of $4.6 billion and capital expenditures of just $2.5 billion for the year. The cash balance was also higher than its short-term debt level of $2.5 billion.

Qualcomm stock trades at relatively reasonable levels, though. While its price-to-cash flow (P/CF) ratio of 18.4 times is just below the sector median of 18.7 times, the forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 23.9 times and price-to-sales (P/S) multiple of 4.2 times are above the respective sector medians.

What Do Analysts Think of QCOM Stock?

Overall, analysts have a consensus "Hold" rating for QCOM stock. Out of 34 analysts covering the stock, nine have a "Strong Buy" rating, two have a "Moderate Buy" rating, 19 have a "Hold" rating, one has a "Moderate Sell" rating, and three have a "Strong Sell" rating. The mean target price of $191.21 denotes potential upside of 8% from current levels.

news.Title: Can HPE Sustain Growth Amid Evolving AI Market Dynamics?
news.Content:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE has been a key beneficiary of rising artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending, as hyperscalers and leading technology companies continue to ramp up investments in AI capabilities. However, the growing concentration of AI investments among a handful of hyperscalers and infrastructure providers has raised concerns about the distribution of growth opportunities across the industry.

Against this backdrop, the November 2026 sell-off in AI and semiconductor stocks has heightened investor concerns, raising the question: Can HPE sustain growth amid evolving AI market dynamics? HPE's strongest defense against the AI market correction is its diversified infrastructure portfolio, which allows it to capture spending across multiple technology categories rather than depending exclusively on demand for AI servers.

HPE's diversified portfolio spanning networking, traditional servers, storage, hybrid cloud, GreenLake and financial services could help cushion weakness in AI-related spending. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Cloud & AI revenues reached $9 billion, up 25% year over year, with a 17% operating margin. Server revenues rose 35%, while traditional server orders increased 75% as customers favored AI-ready configurations and higher-value systems.

The Juniper acquisition is broadening HPE's reach across campus and branch, data center switching, routing and security, while integration remains ahead of schedule. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Networking revenues were $2.9 billion, up 10% on a normalized basis, and operating margin was 22%. Normalized orders rose 36%, with data center switching and routing orders up high double digits and campus and branch orders up low teens.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, GreenLake customers increased 18% year over year to 52,000 from 44,000, while management cited higher net retention as customers broadened usage of software and intelligent cloud services. The platform is reinforced by Morpheus for multi-cloud orchestration and OpsRamp for monitoring and observability. Given these factors, HPE's diversified portfolio, expanding networking business and growing GreenLake adoption provide multiple growth drivers beyond AI servers. However, sustained growth will depend on execution, demand resilience and profitability.

How Competitors Fare Against HPE

Hewlett Packard Enterprise's closest competitors in this domain are Dell Technologies DELL and Cisco CSCO. Dell AI Factory combined with NVIDIA is arguably the most direct alternative for HPE private cloud AI.

Story Continues

Dell provides pre-integrated GPU servers, storage, networking and software for enterprise AI and competes head-to-head with HPE for Fortune 1000 AI deployments. Cisco focuses on AI networking and integrated AI Pods. Cisco has started competing strongly with HPE after acquiring Splunk and through its partnership with NVIDIA.

HPE's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Hewlett Packard Enterprise shares have skyrocketed 109.2% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry's growth of 79.1% and the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 6.3%.

news.Title: Wall Street Analysts Believe ON Semiconductor Corp. (ON) Could Rally 29.15%: Here's is How to Trade
news.Content:
ON Semiconductor Corp. (ON) closed the last trading session at $73.62, gaining 0.4% over the past four weeks, but there could be plenty of upside left in the stock if short-term price targets set by Wall Street analysts are any guide. The mean price target of $95.08 indicates a 29.2% upside potential.

The mean estimate comprises 26 short-term price targets with a standard deviation of $15.96. While the lowest estimate of $68.00 indicates a 7.6% decline from the current price level, the most optimistic analyst expects the stock to surge 69.8% to reach $125.00. It's very important to note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.

While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.

But, for ON, an impressive average price target is not the only indicator of a potential upside. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens this view. While a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't gauge how much a stock could gain, it has proven to be powerful in predicting an upside.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?

They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.

However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.

Story Continues

That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.

Here's Why There Could be Plenty of Upside Left in ON

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. That's because empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 2.2% over the past month, as 11 estimates have gone higher compared to no negative revision.

Moreover, ON currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much ON could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

news.Title: Will Content Capex Weigh on Netflix's Free Cash Flow Trajectory?
news.Content:
Netflix 's NFLX elevated content investment is drawing fresh attention to its free cash flow trajectory. In the third quarter of 2026, cash additions to content assets totaled $5.16 billion against content amortization of $4.24 billion, a ratio of about 1.22x. For the first nine months, cash content spend reached $14.93 billion versus amortization of $12.77 billion, or roughly 1.17x, running above the company's full-year expectation of about 1.1x.

Despite the heavier outlay, cash conversion held up. Operating cash flow rose to $3.2 billion from $2.8 billion a year ago, while free cash flow increased 8% to $2.88 billion. Year-to-date free cash flow stands at about $9.5 billion, aided by a strong $5.09 billion in the first quarter, though the second quarter was softer at $1.53 billion. Purchases of property and equipment remained modest at $279 million in the third quarter.

Guidance, however, points to a more measured path. Netflix trimmed its 2026 free cash flow outlook to about $12 billion from $12.5 billion, citing primarily the expected fourth-quarter closing of a real estate transaction, which implies roughly $2.5 billion of fourth-quarter free cash flow. The company expects fourth-quarter revenues of $13.4 billion and a 26% operating margin, including a 120-basis-point hit from headcount reductions, while guiding full-year revenues of $51.1 billion and a 31.5% operating margin. Streaming content obligations climbed to $25.2 billion from $24 billion at 2025-end.

The holiday pipeline is cash-intensive but revenue-supportive. The fourth-quarter slate includes the NFL's Thanksgiving Eve game, a Christmas Day NFL doubleheader, the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua bout, The Diplomat Season 4, Lupin: Part 4 , the final season of Emily in Paris and the film The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth . While front-loaded spending may cap near-term free cash flow expansion, live events and tentpole releases could support engagement and monetization, keeping the longer-term trajectory intact.

How Netflix's Streaming Rivals Balance Spending and Cash Flow

Disney DIS and Amazon AMZN face similar trade-offs. Disney projects fiscal 2026 content spend of about $24 billion, alongside roughly $9 billion of capital expenditures. Disney's fiscal third-quarter free cash flow rose 63% to $3.1 billion, though nine-month free cash flow declined 24% to $5.7 billion amid higher tax payments and sports content spending. Amazon is backing Prime Video with live sports, including Thursday Night Football and NBA on Prime, but its cash profile is driven largely by infrastructure investment. Amazon reported a trailing 12-month free cash outflow of $42.4 billion and still expects 2026 cash capital expenditures of approximately $220 billion.

Story Continues

news.Title: Hims & Hers Bounced Back 9%, But Its Earnings Reveal a Costly Trade-Off
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Hims & Hers Health, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Hims & Hers shares tumbled this week after a Q3 earnings and revenue miss, remaining far below their 2025 highs despite a partial rebound.

The company lowered its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance amid falling subscriber numbers, compressed gross margins, and reduced weight-loss marketing spending.

The FTC lawsuit over alleged privacy and billing violations expanded to include five more states, adding to legal pressure alongside a separate securities class action.

Even a nearly 9% rebound on Wednesday, Nov. 11, couldn't undo a punishing start to the week for Hims & Hers Health (NYSE: HIMS). Shares had already plunged nearly 12% ahead of Monday evening's Q3 earnings report, and disappointing results—a double miss—sent the stock tumbling another 16.6% on Tuesday.

The damage extends well beyond this week's sell-off. Even after Wednesday's recovery, HIMS remains roughly 47% below its July 6 year-to-date high and 71.5% below its all-time high in 2025.

→ D-Wave Quantum Has Long-Term Potential, But Is Now the Time to Buy?

A sustained recovery could prove challenging. With mounting legal troubles, compressed margins, and a reduced full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook, Hims & Hers faces growing pressure to prove its long-term growth strategy can deliver stronger profitability.

Hims & Hers' Earnings Miss Streak Continues

The earnings shortfall was far more pronounced than the revenue miss, which came despite continued strong sales growth.

→ Archer Aviation's FAA Certificate Is a Milestone, But It Isn't the Final One

Earnings per share (EPS) of three cents fell significantly short of the analyst consensus of 6 cents. Revenue, which came in at $890.4 million, was up 49% year over year (YOY) but slightly below the approximately $893 million consensus estimate.

The EPS miss was Hims & Hers' third in a row and fifth in the last six quarters, while the revenue miss was its third in the past four quarters.

→ 3 Stocks Wall Street Likes More Than the Market Does

Subscriber growth was a mixed bag. The company ended Q3 with nearly 2.8 million subscribers, up 13% YOY but approximately 100,000 fewer than in Q2. The figure also fell short of the 3.04 million subscribers expected by analysts.

Management attributed the quarter-over-quarter subscriber decline to reduced U.S. weight-loss marketing and international brand migrations. In his earnings call comments, CEO Andrew Dudum acknowledged that the company is currently in the process of trading "near-term subscriber growth for a stronger position in the years that follow."

Story Continues

Hims & Hers also tightened its full-year revenue outlook to a range of $3.13 billion to $3.15 billion, from a previous range of $3.1 billion to $3.3 billion.

At the same time, management lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA expectations from a range of $275 million to $325 million to $257 million to $277 million. The company attributed the adjustment to planned pricing and marketing investments in the United Kingdom and Germany, along with the timing of deferred weight-loss membership revenue.

For the quarter, Hims & Hers posted a net loss of $33 million, equivalent to a GAAP loss of 14 cents per share, following net income of $15.8 million in Q3 2025. Gross margin was 57%, down from 64% in Q2 and 74% a year earlier, while free cash flow of $26 million marked a notable YOY drop from $79.4 million.

Hims & Hers' Growth Opportunities Come With a Catch

Despite the slight revenue miss, monthly revenue per average subscriber rose 30% YOY to $105.

International expansion provided another bright spot, with revenue outside the United States surging 321% to $233.3 million.

However, approximately $135 million of that revenue came from the company's acquisition of Eucalyptus.

Although management lowered its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance, it had expressed increased confidence in August about achieving its longer-term 2030 targets of at least $6.5 billion in revenue and $1.3 billion in adjusted EBITDA.

Expanded services and products offer another glimmer of hope. According to Dudum, Hims & Hers AI-native infrastructure positions the company "to launch treatments of increasing complexity, including testosterone replacement therapy [in Q4] and our Peptides+ offering later [in November]."

Additionally, Hers-branded revenue is approaching $1 billion in 2026, which supports the company's decision to scale its dermatology and menopause businesses.

Dudum also highlighted the company's ongoing partnerships with Big Pharma mainstays Novo Nordisk (NYSE: NVO) and Eli Lilly (NYSE: LLY), which allow patients to complete virtual consultations, receive prescriptions, and purchase FDA-approved, brand-name GLP-1 weight-loss medications directly through the Hims & Hers telehealth platform.

The Eli Lilly agreement, which was announced on Nov. 6, helps expand access to Zepbound and Foundayo. Previously, patients seeking Lilly's weight-loss medications through Hims & Hers had to leave the platform to complete their purchases through LillyDirect.

The move levels the playing field with Novo Nordisk, which has been offering its weight-loss medications Wegovy and Ozempic on Hims & Hers' platform since March 2026. The agreement also marked a turning point in their relationship, with Novo Nordisk agreeing to dismiss its patent-infringement lawsuit over compounded semaglutide without prejudice.

For Hims & Hers, the availability of both companies' GLP-1 offerings could support long-term revenue growth. However, the shift toward lower-margin branded weight-loss medications, along with international expansion, has contributed to significant gross-margin compression. That leaves investors weighing the potential for a larger customer base against the challenge of restoring stronger profitability.

FTC Lawsuit Expands as Hims & Hers Faces Shareholder Claims

Legal pressure intensified further on Nov. 10, when the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) announced that five additional states—Arizona, Florida, Nebraska, Ohio, and Wisconsin—had joined its lawsuit against Hims & Hers.

The agency originally filed the case on July 29 alongside the Utah Division of Consumer Protection and Los Angeles County Counsel acting on behalf of California. The regulators sued Hims & Hers over alleged privacy and billing violations.

That suit alleges that the company shared consumers' sensitive health information with third-party advertising platforms, including Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) and Snap (NYSE: SNAP), despite promising patient privacy.

According to the complaint, Hims & Hers made subscriptions difficult to cancel, routinely processed initial refill charges 10 days before consumers' selected cadence, and charged for prescriptions almost immediately after consumers submitted an intake form, despite telling them that they could first consult with a medical provider to find a treatment that is "right for them."

Separately, on Sept. 1, a securities class action was filed against Hims & Hers on behalf of shareholders who purchased or acquired the company's stock between Aug. 4, 2025, and July 29, 2026.

The securities lawsuit alleges that Hims & Hers and certain executives violated the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 by making materially misleading statements about the company's business, operations, and prospects and failing to disclose that its privacy and billing practices could expose the company to regulatory scrutiny and potential financial penalties.

Hims & Hers disputes the allegations in the FTC case and has said it intends to vigorously defend itself against the FTC's claims.

Hims & Hers' Next Test: Subscribers and Margins

Wednesday's rebound offered some relief, but the next few quarters will provide a clearer picture of whether Hims & Hers' growth strategy is working.

Management expects reduced U.S. weight-loss marketing to remain a headwind for subscriber growth in Q4, with a renewed marketing push planned for Q1 2027 as the company expands its treatment offerings.

For investors, the key will be whether those efforts can restore subscriber momentum without putting further pressure on gross margins and cash flow.

The expanding FTC lawsuit adds another layer of uncertainty, making sustained improvement in the company's operating performance especially important.

news.Title: Strategy Expands Cloud Subscriptions: Can Software Revenues Recover?
news.Content:
Strategy Inc. MSTR is witnessing strong growth in its cloud subscription business as customers increasingly migrate from traditional on-premises software licenses to cloud-based services. However, declining product license and support revenues continue to weigh on overall software performance, raising questions about the pace of recovery.

In the third quarter of 2026, subscription services revenues surged 49.2% year over year to $68.6 million, accounting for nearly 55% of total software revenues. However, overall software revenues declined 2.6% to $125.4 million. Product license revenues plunged 77.9% to $3.8 million, while product support revenues fell 26.3% to $37.7 million. The growth in subscriptions has not yet fully offset weakness in legacy offerings.

The cloud transition is gaining traction. Subscription revenues increased 53.6% to $190.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, lifting their contribution to total software revenues to 51.2% from 35% a year earlier. Higher cloud adoption, increased usage by existing customers and new contracts are supporting this growth. Subscription gross margin also improved to 72% from 57.4% in the prior-year quarter, reflecting better profitability in the expanding business.

Strategy's cloud-native analytics platform, Strategy Mosaic and generative AI capabilities offer additional opportunities to strengthen customer engagement and drive subscription adoption. However, the company faces challenges from customer attrition, rising cloud infrastructure expenses and competition.

Strategy's software business is making progress toward a recurring-revenue model, but a sustained recovery remains uncertain. Continued subscription growth, improved underlying profitability and the ability to offset declining legacy revenues will be critical to restoring momentum.

How Are Strategy's Competitors Faring?

Microsoft MSFT reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $92.3 billion, up 19% year over year. Microsoft Cloud revenues increased 30% to $63.9 billion, while Azure revenues surged 48%. Its Power BI and Microsoft Fabric platforms offer cloud analytics, data integration and AI-powered capabilities, intensifying competition with Strategy's enterprise software business.

Salesforce CRM reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $11.3 billion, up 11% year over year. Subscription and support revenues rose 12% to $10.8 billion. Agentforce and Data 360 annual recurring revenues came in at $3.9 billion. Its Tableau platforms provide cloud-based analytics and AI-driven insights, challenging Strategy's software offerings.

Strategy shares have gained 26% over the past three months, outperforming the broader industry and the S&P 500 Index.

news.Title: Apple Is Hovering Around an All-Time High Despite the Broader Tech Sell-Off. Will New Products Like the iPhone Duo and HomeView Give Apple Even More Room to Run?
news.Content:
The last few weeks have been difficult for technology investors. This is indicated by the 12% decline of the Vanguard Information Technology ETF since the start of October (as of Nov. 11).

Investors can blame the recent slide on Nvidia shares tanking. In addition to the chief executive officer's latest troubles , the market worries about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Even the smallest shift in sentiment can have a pronounced impact given how important these sorts of businesses are right now.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Amid the turmoil, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) looks like a winner. It's currently trading in record territory, with shares up 31% this year. The $5.2 trillion market capitalization easily makes it the world's most valuable company. It makes sense if investors view this as more of a consumer staples stock rather than a pure tech stock.

The business continues to operate as it always has, with fresh product releases a cornerstone of the strategy. The iPhone Duo and HomeView are the most notable launches. Will these innovations give Apple shares more room to run?

Skipping the arms race

The stock's recent strength underscores its unique AI strategy. This business has not participated in the extraordinary infrastructure boom that's seeing its tech peers spend hundreds of billions of dollars on data centers, often raising external capital to do so. Capital outlays of this size naturally increase the financial risk investors must deal with.

And this puts the AI trade on fragile ground. The market wants rapid growth to continue for hyperscaler cloud platforms and the leading AI labs. No one can accurately predict what the industry will look like in two to three years, which is the problem that introduces immense uncertainty.

Apple is standing by itself. It collected $136 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2026 (ended Sept. 26), thanks to just $9 billion in capital expenditures. Investors have always appreciated the financial strength this business operates with.

Even during a major technological wave that encourages heavy spending, its profitability has held up. Management's discipline is why certain Apple bulls might be comfortable calling this a safe-haven stock .

Own it for quality, not for huge returns

A premium brand defined by pricing power, customer loyalty, and an unmatched ecosystem make Apple an elite company. And the constant focus on innovation keeps consumers interested. But investors face a trade-off. In exchange for owning such a high-quality business, you give up the potential to capture outsize returns.

Story Continues

The valuation could be a headwind. Shares are at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 36.4, which doesn't present investors with a margin of safety. You essentially have to believe the market will continue to assign a high multiple to the stock.

Growth will also naturally slow. According to sell-side analyst estimates, Apple's revenue and earnings per share are expected to increase by just 27% and 31%, respectively, over the next three years.

This is accounting for the impact new products will have. The iPhone Duo immediately saw incredible demand. But the consensus view is that it will only represent 7% of iPhone revenue this fiscal year.

And it's too early to draw any conclusions about HomeView. However, this will have a tiny near-term financial impact even if tens of millions of units are sold.

These could end up being extremely successful products. The issue is that Apple is so massive, with fiscal 2026 net sales coming in at $479 billion. It's virtually impossible to move the financial needle at this size.

This isn't to say that the stock can't continue its ascent. It's just important that investors set the right expectations if they do choose to buy Apple.

news.Title: Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Shares of this chipmaker have returned -31.2% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -2.4% change. The Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, to which Marvell belongs, has lost 14.4% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Marvell is expected to post earnings of $1.10 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +44.7%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -0.2%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $4.21 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +48.2%. This estimate has changed -0.2% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $7.42 indicates a change of +76.2% from what Marvell is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.8%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Marvell.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Projected Revenue Growth

Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.

For Marvell, the consensus sales estimate for the current quarter of $3.16 billion indicates a year-over-year change of +52.2%. For the current and next fiscal years, $12.06 billion and $19.89 billion estimates indicate +47.1% and +65% changes, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Marvell reported revenues of $2.74 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +36.5%. EPS of $0.94 for the same period compares with $0.67 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.71 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +1.03%. The EPS surprise was +1.08%.

Over the last four quarters, Marvell surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Marvell is graded F on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Conclusion

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Marvell. However, its Zacks Rank #2 does suggest that it may outperform the broader market in the near term.

Chicago, IL – November 12, 2026 – Stocks in this week's article are Micron Technology MU, NVIDIA Corp. NVDA and Sandisk Corp. SNDK.

Micron & 2 Profitable Stocks to Buy Now for Explosive Upside

news.Title: Onto Innovation's Q3 Cash Flow Hits $79M: Is Momentum Sustainable?
news.Content:
Onto Innovation ONTO delivered improved cash generation in the third quarter of 2026, supported by strong semiconductor equipment demand and operational efficiency.

The company generated approximately $79 million in operating cash flow, up from roughly $62 million in the preceding quarter. The company ended September 2026 with $1.25 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, which includes free cash flow generated in the quarter. However, it is lower than $1.88 billion reported at June-end, mainly due to the $720 million payment made to acquire a 27% stake in Rigaku, which was completed in August.

The company's strong financial performance underscores its cash-generating potential. Third-quarter revenues surged 88% year over year and 19% sequentially to $410 million. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 60 basis points sequentially to 57.6%, while non-GAAP operating margin reached 32.6%. Management attributed improving profitability to higher productivity, the extended factory model and better operating leverage.

Looking forward, strong demand from advanced packaging and advanced nodes should support top-line expansion. Onto Innovation's backlog increased to more than $1.3 billion during the third quarter. Management cited strong customer demand and visibility into investment plans extending multiple years. It expects full-year 2026 revenue growth to exceed 45% year over year and anticipates sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027.

Onto Innovation Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Onto Innovation Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Onto Innovation Inc. Quote

The company expects fourth-quarter revenues between $430 million and $450 million, with non-GAAP operating margin in the range of 33.5%-34.5%.

However, cash flow sustainability warrants attention. Operating cash flow for the first nine months of 2026 declined to $166.6 million from $233.3 million a year earlier, reflecting higher inventories and the timing of customer collections.

Moreover, cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities increased to $1.25 billion at September-end from $639.6 million as of Jan. 3, 2026, supported mainly by cash provided by financing activities. In May, ONTO issued $1.5 billion of 0% convertible notes due in 2031. The financing generated about $1.2 billion of net cash after nearly $300 million worth of share repurchases, capped calls and transaction costs.

Balance Sheet Snapshot for Peers

KLA Corporation KLAC remains a formidable competitor. The company generated free cash flow of $1.34 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, supported by operating cash flow of $1.53 billion. Revenues jumped 29% year over year and 13% sequentially to $4.14 billion, driven by AI-related investments and increasing process-control intensity across edge devices and advanced packaging. KLA ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities against $5.95 billion in debt.

Story Continues

Looking ahead, management expects December-quarter revenues of $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million.

Nova Ltd. NVMI generated $132 million in free cash flow in the third quarter of 2026, bringing the nine-month total to approximately $206 million. Revenues increased 28% year over year and 13% sequentially to $287.8 million, supported by robust demand for memory and advanced packaging solutions. Nova exited the quarter with approximately $1.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents, bank deposits and marketable securities.

For the fourth quarter, management projects revenues between $305 million and $315 million. Growing adoption of its Nova WMC platform across logic and HBM applications, alongside continued investments in advanced metrology solutions, is strengthening the company's competitive position.
