news.Title: Alphabet's Cloud Business Doubled, but the Stock Plunged. Here's What a $5,000 Investment Could Be Worth by 2030.
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) reported third-quarter earnings on Oct. 28. Since then, the stock sold off and hasn't recovered. It was down more than 10% since reporting earnings, which is no small amount considering that Alphabet is one of the world's largest companies.

However, Alphabet's sell-off was more focused on its spending rather than its growth. I think this is a very short-sighted view by the market, and it's why Alphabet stock should be considered a strong buy right now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

If the company keeps up the pace, a $5,000 investment could be worth $11,000 by 2030. Here's how.

Google Cloud is the highlight of the company

Alphabet's business was built on Google Search. However, a new segment is starting to lead the company: cloud computing . Google Cloud is one of the largest cloud computing firms in the world and could start closing the gap, due to how fast it's growing.

In Q3, its revenue rose 103% year over year to $30.7 billion. Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the industry leader and generated $46 billion in Q3, growing at 39%. So, Google Cloud has a chance to start catching up to Amazon over the next year, but not all of its revenue is recurring.

For the most part, cloud computing revenue can be recognized as recurring, as clients pay for usage, which is generally fairly recurring revenue. However, Alphabet is starting to sell its proprietary artificial intelligence computing chips to certain firms, which is boosting its revenue.

Unfortunately, Alphabet doesn't provide investors with Tensor Processing Unit sales figures, so it's impossible to parse how much revenue is from chip sales and how much is from a more recurring revenue stream. The best clue investors have is that Alphabet stated that cloud revenue makes up the "vast majority" of revenue and that the growth rate, excluding TPU sales, was "incredibly strong." However, 2027 will include far more chip sales, which could affect the 2027 revenue guidance investors may see during Q4.

However, the legacy business wasn't the greatest for Alphabet. Google Search had an OK quarter, with revenue growing 12% year over year. YouTube didn't fare any better, with revenue rising 9% year over year. But Alphabet's total revenue rose at a 25% year-over-year rate, thanks to the strength of Google Cloud, which now makes up nearly a quarter of its total business.

Story Continues

But where will that take the stock by 2030? Let's take a look.

Google Cloud will take the company to new heights

Many in the cloud computing industry project several years of strong growth driven by rising AI workloads . Google Cloud's peers are growing at a 40% rate, but with Google Cloud's TPUs becoming a popular alternative to GPUs for running workloads, I think it will grow faster than its peers, growing at a 50% rate. This will help boost Alphabet's overall growth rate, and a 20% companywide growth rate from now until 2030 isn't out of the question. If Alphabet does that, it could have trailing 12-month revenue totals of just over $1 trillion.

GOOG Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts

Trillion-dollar revenue companies are quickly approaching, and Alphabet will be among the first to reach this mark. If it can deliver a 30% profit margin and trade for 25 times earnings, that would value the stock at $7.7 trillion. Alphabet currently has a $3.5 trillion valuation, so this would transform a $5,000 investment today into about $11,000.

That's a great, market-beating investment, and investors should use today's sale price as a smart buying opportunity for Alphabet stock.

news.Title: Netlist's Q3 Sales Surge 149%: Can the Momentum Continue?
news.Content:
Netlist, Inc. NLST delivered robust third-quarter 2026 results, with net sales increasing 149% year over year to $105.1 million. The quarterly performance was supported by strong demand for AI and data center memory products and the commencement of licensing revenues under its Samsung agreement.

Netlist's third-quarter product sales increased 43% year over year to $60.2 million, reflecting healthy demand from AI and data center customers. The company also recognized $44.9 million in licensing revenues under its Samsung agreement, significantly strengthening the overall revenue base.

Expanding licensing portfolio and favorable market conditions are likely to sustain Netlist's growth momentum going forward.

Looking ahead, the company expects fourth-quarter 2026 product sales to increase substantially from the third quarter, supported by rising demand for its products and initial Samsung product sales under the product supply agreement.

Netlist, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Netlist, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Netlist, Inc. Quote

Meanwhile, its recently concluded Micron agreement provides another growth catalyst. Beginning in the fourth quarter, Netlist expects combined quarterly licensing revenues of approximately $73 million from Samsung and Micron, translating into an annualized run rate of $292 million.

Netlist remains focused on portfolio expansion to boost its presence in the AI memory market. The company recently announced next-generation LIGHTNING Ultra-Low Latency DDR5 RDIMMs for Agentic AI workstations and servers. The DDR5-6000 and DDR5-6400 products are designed to boost responsiveness in memory-sensitive AI and enterprise workloads.

The new products target agentic AI workstations and servers, multi-agent systems, retrieval-augmented generation, large language models and vector databases. Applications also extend to high-frequency trading, scientific computing and electronic design automation, cloud infrastructure and data analytics.

While recurring licensing revenues provide a relatively predictable foundation, continued expansion in the product business will determine whether Netlist can maintain its impressive growth trajectory.

Revenue Performance for Peers

Netlist operates in a highly competitive memory market alongside established players, including SK hynix SKHY and Rambus RMBS.

Rambus' third-quarter 2026 revenues of $218.3 million jumped 22% year over year, buoyed by demand for advanced memory solutions for next-generation AI and data center infrastructure. Product revenues increased 22% to $114.3 million.

Story Continues

For the fourth quarter, Rambus expects revenues between $227 million and $233 million, with product revenues projected at $127-$133 million, implying 34% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Increasing AI infrastructure investments and expanding adoption of DDR5 solutions are expected to sustain growth. Management anticipates strengthening demand heading into 2027.

South Korea-based SK hynix has a strong presence across DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory ("HBM") markets. Third-quarter 2026 revenues were KRW 104.6 trillion, soaring 328% year over year and 32% sequentially. Growth was driven by rising DRAM and NAND prices, and robust demand trends.

Management highlighted that the mass production and shipments of HBM4 began in the third quarter, while shipments of server DDR5 increased more than 40% sequentially. For the fourth quarter, management expects DRAM shipment volume to increase a mid-20% sequentially, while NAND bit shipments are projected to rise by a mid-single-digit percentage.

news.Title: 2 Memory Stocks to Buy and Hold Through 2030
news.Content:
Memory stocks have had quite the year in 2026. Two of the best performers are Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) and Micron (NASDAQ: MU), which are each among the top five best-performing stocks in the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) this year.

Sandisk holds second place, rising around 270%, while Micron has risen about 150%. However, I think both of these stocks are due for more over the next few years, and all investors have to do is listen to what they're saying.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

I think these two will be great stocks to buy and hold over the next few years, and could deliver monster returns.

Both stocks are incredibly cheap versus the broader market

Memory chips are required for many devices to function. Long-term data storage utilizes NAND memory, such as in solid-state drives (SSDs). Computing units need DRAM memory to function, and these are being deployed heavily in data centers for computing power.

While memory chips are necessary, there isn't much to differentiate one memory chip from another. With no competitive advantage, memory chips basically became a commodity. As a result, pricing depends heavily on supply and demand. This makes memory chips a cyclical industry, and investors have historically given companies in these fields deep discounts to avoid losing vast sums of money when the cycle turns.

That's what the market is betting will happen for Micron and Sandisk. With the AI build-out in full force and consuming all available memory, demand for chip production capacity for their products has never been higher. With production capacity sold out, prices have also skyrocketed. This has led to ludicrous growth rates for each company, but the market isn't valuing them fully because of their cyclical nature.

MU PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

For reference, the S&P 500 trades at 19 times forward earnings, so if both stocks just had a market-average valuation, they would rise nearly 5 times in value. But because the market is betting on a downturn, they're cheap.

The memory chip industry is being reshaped

Both of these companies are taking steps to reduce the cyclical nature of their businesses. Instead of selling products on the open market, both are now entering into long-term agreements with their clients. Sandisk calls this its "New Business Model" (NBM), and a large chunk of its revenue is coming from these agreements. Micron is doing the same thing and has locked in approximately 35% of revenue through 2030 with these types of contracts.

Story Continues

Why is this a big deal? It raises the floor for the companies. Instead of dealing with a significant pricing decline as demand falls when the AI build-out ends, there are floor pricing levels with their clients that keep the business running well. So, Micron and Sandisk may not see the massive pricing highs they're seeing now ever again, but they won't experience the lows that result in the stocks not being highly valued. This means the market should reprice the stock accordingly, which could lead to massive upside in the near future.

Furthermore, the industry has been sold out for many years, and Micron told investors that market conditions in 2027 and 2028 will likely be tighter than in 2026. The reality is that the memory space will be tied up for multiple years, likely through 2030, and these two stocks will make for excellent investments during that time. There's a good chance memory stocks will become a hot commodity sometime in the near future, and that makes now the perfect time to load up on them.

news.Title: Tesla to Wind Down Cybertruck: Can Cybercab Justify the Shift?
news.Content:
Tesla TSLA is making room for a different future at its Gigafactory Texas plant. The company is expected to bring Cybertruck production to a close in fall 2027, with the factory space eventually being used to build Cybercab, its driverless vehicle. The move comes as the electric pickup struggled to attract mass-market buyers and fell short of the sales volumes Elon Musk once envisioned.

This is not simply a decision to stop making an underperforming model. It reflects Tesla's growing preference for autonomy and robotics over some parts of its traditional vehicle business. The bigger question is whether these newer ambitions can generate enough business for the company.

Cybertruck Struggles to Meet Its Sales Ambitions

When Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck, Musk set an ambitious target of selling 250,000 units annually. Its unconventional design attracted plenty of attention, but the initial excitement did not translate into sustained demand.

Per CNBC, Cox Automotive estimated that Tesla sold just 20,237 Cybertrucks in the United States in 2025, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Several recalls have added to the model's challenges, while its high price has limited its appeal to a wider pool of buyers.

Production capacity further highlights the mismatch. Tesla had installed capacity to produce more than 125,000 Cybertrucks annually, but the vehicle was selling at a pace of roughly 30,000 units a year before the wind-down announcement last Friday. That leaves considerable manufacturing capacity underutilized.

Tesla has now stopped accepting orders for the Premium AWD version, leaving the Cyberbeast as the only available configuration. Its price has increased by $7,500 to $109,990. Buyers placing orders now are being given delivery estimates between March and June 2027. Musk has said production will continue until the end of summer 2027 to work through the remaining backlog.

An interesting part of the sales story is SpaceX SPCX. Musk's aerospace, communications and AI company purchased $131 million worth of Cybertrucks last year at Tesla's suggested retail price, according to a SpaceX financial filing. While these purchases contributed to demand, they also raise questions about how much of the Cybertruck's sales momentum came from buyers outside the broader retail market.

Tesla is not alone in discovering how difficult it is to make electric pickups profitable. Ford F, which operates in the highly profitable U.S. pickup market, has also struggled to make its electric F-150 Lightning commercially viable and has decided to discontinue the model. Ford continues to report losses in its EV business but is working on a more affordable electric pickup. This highlights the difficulty of building a profitable electric truck business, even for established automakers with strong pickup franchises.

Story Continues

Cybercab and Optimus Become Tesla's Priorities

The factory space freed up by the Cybertruck's departure is expected to support Cybercab manufacturing. Cybercab is designed as a two-seat, fully autonomous vehicle without a steering wheel or pedals.

Musk sees Cybercab as central to Tesla's transportation-as-a-service strategy, in which autonomous vehicles could generate revenues by providing paid rides rather than relying solely on individual vehicle sales. If successful, this model could create recurring revenue opportunities and change how Tesla generates returns from its vehicle fleet.

But the economics are still a big question mark. Tesla must show that its technology can handle driverless operations reliably, win the necessary regulatory permissions and attract enough customers to support a commercially viable service. Manufacturing Cybercab at scale will matter only if the company can put those vehicles to productive use and earn attractive returns from them.

Tesla's focus on robotics is also increasing. The company has repurposed the Model S and Model X production lines at its Fremont factory to scale production of Optimus, its humanoid robot. Tesla ended Model S and Model X production in spring, citing its growing focus on autonomy. The Cybertruck wind-down further reinforces this strategic shift away from some of its existing vehicle programs.

Final Thoughts

Tesla's decision to wind down Cybertruck production makes sense given the truck's weak sales, underutilized capacity and limited progress toward its original volume ambitions. Cybercab has the potential to open up a new market for Tesla, but the company is yet to prove that its autonomous ride-hailing model can work at scale. Optimus is an even longer-term opportunity, with commercial returns still to be demonstrated.

Cybercab may eventually make the shift worthwhile, but until Tesla proves that driverless rides can become a profitable business, the opportunity remains more promise than payoff.

news.Title: Tesla's Texas Robotaxi Fleet Tops Waymo: Should You Get Bullish?
news.Content:
Tesla TSLA has received an encouraging boost to its robotaxi ambitions, reportedly overtaking Alphabet 's GOOGL Waymo in Texas in terms of registered autonomous vehicles. The development strengthens the case for autonomy as an increasingly important growth driver for Tesla. But before getting too excited, investors should remember that expanding a fleet is one thing and building a profitable robotaxi business is another.

Tesla's Texas Fleet Growth Is Hard to Ignore

According to Teslarati, Texas Department of Motor Vehicles records as of Nov. 10 show 1,302 vehicles registered under Tesla Robotaxi, LLC, narrowly ahead of Waymo's 1,297. Tesla's fleet includes 729 Model Y vehicles (accounting for 56% of the total) and 573 purpose-built Cybercabs (44% of the total). Waymo's fleet primarily comprises Jaguar I-PACE vehicles, alongside its newer Zeekr-based Ojai minivans.

The speed of Tesla's expansion is noteworthy. When Texas' autonomous vehicle registry became publicly available in late May 2026, Tesla had just 42 vehicles listed, compared with several hundred for Waymo. Its authorized fleet has since grown more than 30-fold, reflecting substantial Model Y additions and a growing Cybercab presence.

The Cybercab represents a significant milestone for Tesla, as the two-seat vehicle is specifically designed for fully autonomous operation without requiring human intervention. Waymo isn't Tesla's only rival. Amazon 's AMZN Zoox— another purpose-built robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals— has been running paid rides in Las Vegas and is working to bring commercial service to San Francisco and Austin, putting it on a very similar playbook to Cybercab.

Tesla has also been pushing its robotaxi service beyond its original Austin operating area toward San Antonio and Dallas. The company is making progress in turning its autonomy ambitions into an actual service rather than simply showcasing technology.

Why Tesla's Fleet Lead Doesn't Tell the Whole Story

The milestone is encouraging, but fleet numbers alone do not provide the full picture of competitive strength.

For starters, registered vehicles are not necessarily active robotaxis carrying paying passengers. A larger fleet does not automatically translate into more rides, higher utilization or better economics. Also, Alphabet's Waymo operates beyond Texas, making this comparison particularly narrow.

The Cybercab numbers deserve attention, too. Tesla's 573 purpose-built vehicles represent meaningful progress, but Model Y remains the larger part of its fleet. Investors should watch whether future additions increasingly consist of Cybercabs, which would provide a clearer indication that Tesla is scaling its dedicated robotaxi platform.

Story Continues

Ultimately, the bigger opportunity is not simply deploying vehicles but making each one generate meaningful revenues. This requires sufficient passenger demand, frequent rides and a service that can operate reliably across multiple cities.

Tesla's Robotaxi Progress Needs More Proof

Tesla's Texas fleet milestone is promising. Its rapid expansion underscores that the company can deploy vehicles at scale and is making progress toward its autonomy ambitions.

However, getting ahead of Waymo on a state registry is way easier than getting ahead in robotaxi economics. Tesla still needs to demonstrate strong vehicle utilization, sustainable operating economics and successful expansion into additional markets.

The development makes the robotaxi opportunity more credible, but it doesn't really make us bullish on the stock yet. Investors should remain cautiously constructive until Tesla starts showing that its growing fleet can translate into a scalable, profitable business.

news.Title: Morning Bid: Nvidious
news.Content:
By Mike Dolan

Nov 12 (Reuters) - Just when tech stocks looked to be finding their feet again, chip behemoth Nvidia plunged almost 10% overnight on reports its board may now oust troubled CEO Jensen Huang.

The board met late on Wednesday and although there has ‌been no formal announcement yet, the Wall Street Journal reported it was about to remove him.

A potential ouster of Huang, which would ‌set off a flurry of speculation about his replacement with no obvious succession plan in place, comes after he confessed to having an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be spying ​for China.

Pressure mounted further on Wednesday after the New York Times reported a second affair with a more junior Nvidia executive. Political reverberations from the allegations have also rattled the US administration.

If out-of-hours trading is confirmed after the bell today, the cumulative Nvidia share price loss this week would mean well over half a trillion dollars will have been wiped off its market cap.

It would certainly reverse the bounce in its stock and the wider tech sector on Wednesday, when data ‌center firm CoreWeave's battered shares jumped back almost 25% ⁠on a surprising earnings beat. Stock indexes across the world are on the back foot again due to the latest Nvidia twist.

One company that won't thank Nvidia for the timing of all this volatility will be AI giant Anthropic - ⁠currently roadshowing its mega IPO amid shifting sands on its valuation.

Elsewhere, with bond markets closed for Veterans Day on Wednesday, it fell to the dollar to absorb the hot October inflation update and re-upped Federal Reserve rate hike bets, with the greenback's DXY index surging to its highest level since Donald Trump's tariff shock in April ​last ​year.

But even this thinking has been affected by the Nvidia and tech sector turbulence. Yesterday, ​Fed futures had been pricing a small chance of a ‌50-basis-point rate hike next month but that seems to have been removed again overnight in favor of just a quarter-point move.

Otherwise, the big economic release so far on Thursday was a punchy 0.7% rise in Britain's GDP in the third quarter - its fastest growth rate in two years and bringing growth for the year so far to its fastest outside the pandemic in almost a decade.

Once again, even though the lift was broad-based and would be more than 2.5% on an annualized basis, AI-related business activity was cited as one factor despite this year's Iran-related oil price shock.

CHART OF THE DAY

Britain's economy ‌grew at the fastest rate in two-and-a-half years in the third quarter of 2026, helped ​by a boost from AI and extending a strong first half even in the face ​of an oil shock that many had said could trigger recession.

Story Continues

At ​an annualized pace of more than 2.5%, the UK economy is now expanding at its fastest in almost a decade - ‌when the wild swings around the pandemic are stripped out.

• US 30-year bond auction (1 p.m. EST)

• US corporate earnings including Cisco Systems

• Fed's Michael Barr, Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack, Chicago Fed's Austan Goolsbee, San Francisco Fed's Mary Daly, Kansas City Fed's Jeffrey Schmid and New York Fed's John ​Williams speak

news.Title: Ron Baron Says Tesla (TSLA) Could Climb Within a Decade. Ark’s Model Leans on Robotaxis
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA ) ranks 8th on our newly published list of the 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade .

On November 5, the S&P 500 fell 4.36%, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash, with roughly $3 trillion in value wiped off S&P 500 companies. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.52% to slip into a correction, and chip stocks took the hardest hit, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling about 12%, its worst day since 2020. The slide followed a rough October, when the technology sector of the S&P 500 lost 6.8%, its biggest monthly drop since March 2025, while defensive groups such as consumer staples had a record month. Growth stocks tend to feel these swings first, because their prices rest on the promise of faster sales and earnings than the rest of the market.

Investors Question the Cost of AI

The worry behind the selling is money. Investors are asking how companies will pay for their enormous artificial intelligence budgets and whether the returns will justify them. The midterm election results added a second concern, as investors began questioning whether the pace of data center construction could slow if new rules follow, which would weigh on AI spending. Our ranking of semiconductor stocks to hold for the next decade covers more of the group that took the sharpest hit.

Why a Ten-Year View Looks Past One Bad Month

A growth stock is a share in a company expected to grow its sales and earnings faster than the market average. These companies usually reinvest profits instead of paying dividends, so shareholders are rewarded through a rising share price, which is why the shares often carry high price-to-earnings ratios. A high multiple is not automatically expensive if the growth keeps coming, but it leaves little room for disappointment, and a stock priced for strong growth can fall sharply when the numbers fall short. Time helps in the other direction, because returns that stay invested earn returns of their own, a snowball effect that builds the longer the money is left alone.

The economy is adding another variable. October's jobs report showed payrolls up 165,000, far above the 65,000 economists expected, and traders now put the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December above 75%. Edward Jones senior global strategist Angelo Kourkafas called it a "blowout jobs report." A strong economy is good for business, but higher interest rates make far-off earnings worth less today, which tends to weigh most on growth stocks. For readers hunting for bargains after the pullback, our list of undervalued growth stocks is a place to start. For long-term holders, the more useful question is not what the market does next month but which companies can keep compounding through several more months like this one.

Story Continues

Tesla qualified as a growth stock mentioned by at least three sources, with a market cap of $1.49 trillion and 116 hedge fund holders in Q2 2026.

Ron Baron, founder of Baron Capital, told CNBC that Tesla could reach $2,000 to $2,500 a share within ten years. Cathie Wood's Ark Invest has published a similar long-range view, a $2,600 target for 2029 that rests on robotaxis supplying nearly 90% of Tesla's enterprise value. Take the robotaxi out, and Ark's own model falls sharply.

The company began giving Robotaxi rides in Cybercabs in Austin late in the quarter, and cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles grew eightfold from the prior quarter, driven by sustained double-digit weekly growth. It ended the period with its largest backlog for passenger vehicles in four years and its highest-ever order rate and backlog in energy storage, a business Tesla says is critical to data center uptime.

Management said battery availability, not demand, was the limit on how many cars it could build, and that it made more progress in securing future supply. If that supply arrives, more of the backlog can turn into deliveries, which is the practical bridge between today's order book and the bigger robotaxi and energy plans long-term holders are waiting on.

While we acknowledge the potential of TSLA as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Tesla FSD Gains Ground in Europe: Is EU-Wide Approval Near?
news.Content:
Tesla TSLA is making progress toward expanding its Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology across Europe. Finland has become the 11th European Union (EU) country to grant provisional approval for the system, adding momentum ahead of an EU-wide vote expected next month.

However, national approvals do not guarantee clearance across the bloc. Tesla has won support in several markets but is yet to secure backing from any of the EU's largest member states.

Finland Approval Adds to Tesla's European Momentum

Finland's transport authority, Traficom, fast-tracked its decision, pointing to the changes Tesla has made to the system and the need to give local drivers time to become familiar with it before severe winter conditions.

The changes include reducing the maximum speed offset from 50% to 10% and resetting it to zero every time the vehicle starts. Tesla also renamed its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) technology to Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe.

The name change is significant because regulators have questioned whether the FSD label accurately describes the system's capabilities. Despite its name, the technology does not make a vehicle fully autonomous. Drivers must remain attentive and responsible for the driving task, even when the system assists with steering, acceleration and braking.

Finland's decision follows a series of approvals across Europe, including the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, Czechia, Croatia, Slovakia and Latvia. With Finland joining the list, Tesla now has approvals in 11 EU countries and 19 countries worldwide.

However, several of these European approvals have relied on recognizing the regulatory framework initially established by Dutch authorities. This has helped Tesla expand its footprint, but the broader regulatory challenge remains.

EU-Wide Approval Remains the Bigger Test

Tesla still needs support at the EU level. An approval requires a qualified majority— at least 15 member states representing 65% of the bloc's population.

This is where the lack of support from larger EU economies becomes important. Winning approval in smaller markets is encouraging, but securing backing from major member states will likely be critical to getting the technology cleared across the bloc.

The EU's Technical Committee for Motor Vehicles is expected to decide in December. If approved, the decision could apply across the bloc in about three weeks. A rejection would invalidate the national approvals already granted, making the vote critical to Tesla's European plans.

Story Continues

How Are Other Players Advancing in Autonomy?

The competition in autonomous driving also highlights how different companies are pursuing different paths. Alphabet 's GOOGL Waymo is preparing to bring its driverless ride-hailing service to Munich, Germany, with commercial operations targeted toward the end of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance.

Mobileye MBLY is moving beyond German testing toward planned driverless robotaxi deployments, including a roughly 100-vehicle fleet in Orlando in 2027.

Rivian RIVN is also pursuing supervised autonomy through its Autonomy+ package, including an upcoming Point to Point feature that will navigate a selected route under continuous driver supervision.

Wider FSD Adoption Supports Tesla's Growth

The regulatory push matters to Tesla's effort to build recurring software revenues beyond vehicle sales. Tesla's paid FSD customer base rose 67% year over year to 1.74 million in the third quarter of 2026. More than 75% of new vehicle deliveries in North America included paid FSD subscriptions at delivery. Increasing subscription adoption should strengthen Tesla's software revenues, while wider geographic availability could support vehicle demand and improve long-term profitability.

Access to more markets could widen the customer base and make Tesla vehicles more attractive to buyers interested in driver-assistance features. Still, approvals alone will not ensure subscription growth. Actual adoption will depend on customer willingness to pay, the usefulness of the technology and Tesla's ability to meet local regulatory requirements.

Will National Wins Translate Into EU Approval?

Tesla is making meaningful progress in Europe, and Finland's approval adds to the momentum. However, EU-wide approval is not yet within reach. The lack of backing from major member states remains a hurdle, while the December vote could either validate Tesla's progress or put existing national approvals at risk.

For investors, wider FSD availability offers a promising software revenue opportunity, but it is too early to factor in a broad European rollout. Tesla is getting closer, but the biggest regulatory test is still ahead.

news.Title: Dear Amazon Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 19
news.Content:
It has been a rough ride for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks lately, and e-commerce giant Amazon (AMZN) has hardly been spared. The company's aggressive spending on AI infrastructure has weighed on investor sentiment, with Wall Street increasingly eager to see when these massive investments will translate into meaningful returns. However, the clouds hanging over the stock may finally be beginning to clear, as renewed analyst confidence and a string of product announcements breathe fresh life into Amazon's growth story.

On Tuesday, Amazon made a bold move into robotics, launching a new security business featuring two autonomous products: a flying indoor camera for homes and a mobile security robot for businesses. The move takes Amazon beyond its traditional home-security offerings and signals bigger ambitions in the robotics market. Investors welcomed the announcement, sending shares up approximately 1.5% on Tuesday. But robotics wasn't the only headline grabbing attention.

More News from Barchart

Oracle Stock Just Scored a New $325 Price Target

Dear SpaceX Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 13

Nvidia Stock Plunges After Hours as Reports of a Second Jensen Huang Relationship Could Force the CEO Out

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

Amazon also unveiled plans for its 2026 holiday shopping blitz, announcing that Black Friday Week and Cyber Monday deals will run from Nov. 19 through Nov. 30. The 12-day event will feature millions of offers across electronics, home goods, apparel, beauty, and toys, alongside grocery promotions, personalized shopping tools, and live sports programming. In fact, this year's campaign promises even more shopping excitement, with daily themed deals spanning technology, fashion, and premium gifts.

For the first time, Amazon will drop deals twice on both Black Friday and Cyber Monday, at midnight and 8 a.m. Pacific time, with select discounts reaching up to 60%. With new robotics ambitions and the crucial holiday shopping season on the horizon, Amazon is giving investors plenty to watch. Can these catalysts help turn the tide for AMZN stock? Let's take a closer look.

About Amazon Stock

From changing the way people shop to powering businesses and the broader digital economy, Amazon has built an empire that stretches well beyond e-commerce. Headquartered in Seattle, the technology giant operates across online retail, third-party seller services, digital advertising, subscriptions, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence. Its extensive portfolio includes the flagship Amazon marketplace, Prime memberships, Prime Video, Kindle, Alexa, and an expanding range of AI-powered services.

Story Continues

Amazon's vast business empire is divided into three primary segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). While its North American and International divisions drive retail, advertising, and subscription revenue across global markets, AWS provides businesses, governments, and developers with cloud computing, data storage, database management, and AI solutions.

Backed by an extensive global footprint, a sprawling fulfillment and logistics network, and an expanding cloud infrastructure business, Amazon has transformed itself from an online retailer into a diversified technology powerhouse. Yet, even a company of Amazon's scale hasn't been immune to Wall Street's changing sentiment.

Despite its dominant position across multiple industries and a market capitalization of approximately $2.93 trillion, AMZN shares have faced pressure as investors weigh the company's aggressive AI spending against the potential returns. Concerns over how quickly these massive investments will translate into meaningful profits have kept sentiment in check. However, a series of recent developments appears to be giving the stock fresh momentum.

Amazon has gained 9.1% over the past year, slightly trailing the S&P 500 Index ($SPX), which has advanced 10.1% over the same period. The picture looks considerably brighter in 2026, with AMZN now up 17.4%, comfortably ahead of the broader market's 9.9% gain. More recently, the stock has picked up steam, surging 8.1% over the past five trading sessions, while the S&P 500 has slipped marginally. The latest rally suggests that investors may be warming up to Amazon's growth prospects once again.

A Closer Look At Amazon's Q3 Earnings Report

Amazon's fiscal 2026 third-quarter earnings, released on Oct. 29, offered investors a mixed picture, with its massive AI ambitions increasingly becoming a double-edged sword. Despite continued strength in its cloud business, the company fell short of Wall Street's expectations on both revenue and earnings, sending shares down 1.4% in the following trading session. Slower retail growth, mounting infrastructure costs, and a weaker-than-expected bottom line added to concerns over how quickly Amazon's aggressive investments will begin delivering returns.

On the revenue front, Amazon generated $201.9 billion in net sales, up 12% from $180.2 billion in the same quarter last year. Adjusting for the unfavorable $0.9 billion impact of foreign exchange movements, revenue growth would have been 13%. However, the result still came in slightly below analysts' consensus estimate of $202.3 billion. The biggest bright spot was Amazon Web Services (AWS), which continued to demonstrate why it remains central to the company's growth story.

AWS revenue jumped 39% year-over-year to $46 billion, marking its strongest growth rate in nearly five years. The acceleration highlights booming enterprise demand for AI infrastructure and cloud services, further supported by an expanding backlog worth hundreds of billions of dollars. However, Amazon's retail operations, which account for the largest share of its revenue, delivered a more modest performance.

North America segment sales grew 6% year-over-year to $112.9 billion, while International revenue increased 5% to $43.1 billion. Earnings offered little relief either. Amazon reported earnings per share (EPS) of $1.89, down from $1.95 in the year-ago quarter and below Wall Street's estimate of $1.96. Perhaps the biggest concern was the mounting cost of keeping Amazon's AI ambitions on track.

Its aggressive infrastructure spending is beginning to weigh heavily on cash generation. Trailing-12-month free cash flow swung to an outflow of $42.4 billion, compared with an inflow of $14.8 billion for the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2025. The sharp deterioration was largely driven by a $94.8 billion year-over-year increase in purchases of property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales and incentives, reflecting the company's substantial investments in AI infrastructure.

The scale of Amazon's spending spree is particularly striking. Capital expenditures reached $77.3 billion during the quarter, more than twice the $35.1 billion recorded in the same period last year. And there is little indication that management plans to ease off the accelerator. Amazon maintained its forecast for approximately $220 billion in cash capital expenditures for full-year 2026, underscoring the scale of its commitment to expanding AI and cloud infrastructure.

Still, Amazon offered investors a more encouraging outlook for the all-important holiday quarter. Management expects fourth-quarter net sales to land between $240 billion and $247 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 12% to 16%. The forecast includes an approximately 60-basis-point headwind from unfavorable foreign exchange movements. On the profitability front, operating income is projected to range from $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion, compared with $25 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025.

What Do Analysts Think About Amazon Stock?

Wall Street's bullish stance on Amazon remains firmly intact, with the stock commanding a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. Among the 56 analysts covering the company, 48 recommend a "Strong Buy," five assign a "Moderate Buy" rating, and three advise "Hold." The average price target of $328.33 suggests potential upside of about 21.2%, while the Street-high target of $405 signals a possible 50% gain from current levels.

Conclusion: Buy NVDA Stock Now

news.Title: Onto Innovation's 57.6% Gross Margin: Can It Rise Further in Q4?
news.Content:
Onto Innovation Inc. ONTO continues to make progress in improving profitability, supported by operational efficiencies and strong demand across its product portfolio. In the third quarter of 2026, the company reported a non-GAAP gross margin of 57.6%, reflecting a sequential improvement of 60 basis points (bps). This represents an expansion of 300 bps compared with the fourth quarter of 2025, highlighting the effectiveness of its ongoing operational improvement initiatives.

The margin expansion reflects Onto Innovation's continued focus on transitioning to an extended factory model, improving operational productivity and enhancing manufacturing efficiency. The company has benefited from operating in lower-cost labor markets, reducing exposure to duties and tariff-related risks, and localizing supply chains. These initiatives have also helped lower freight expenses by reducing the need to transport components across regions.

Strong revenue growth has accompanied these improvements. Third-quarter revenues reached approximately $410 million, increasing 19% sequentially and nearly 90% year over year. Advanced packaging and specialty device products recorded 35% sequential growth, supported by strong Dragonfly adoption and a recovery in power and specialty device inspection businesses.

Onto Innovation expects its gross margin expansion to continue in the fourth quarter. Management anticipates an additional 50-bp improvement, bringing gross margin slightly above 58%. This would represent a cumulative improvement of approximately 350 bps since the fourth quarter of 2025.

The company also raised its fourth-quarter revenue guidance to $430-$450 million, representing sequential growth of more than 7% at the midpoint. Operating margin is projected to reach 34% at the midpoint of guidance compared with 32.6% in the third quarter.

Management expects further gross margin expansion in 2027, indicating that an average quarterly improvement of approximately 50 bps is a reasonable expectation. However, rising component costs and supply-chain pricing pressures remain challenges. Onto Innovation is addressing these headwinds through design modifications, reduced memory usage and additional productivity improvements, while maintaining its focus on sustained margin expansion.

Taking a Look at ONTO's Competitors

KLA Corporation 's KLAC non-GAAP gross margin reached 62.7% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, slightly exceeding the midpoint of management's guidance. Non-GAAP operating margin improved 240 bps sequentially to a record 46.1%, driven by higher revenues and operating leverage. However, elevated memory component costs continue to pressure margins, while optics lead times and a less favorable business mix remain additional headwinds. For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, management expects non-GAAP gross margin of 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point. Cost-reduction measures, memory optimization and pricing initiatives are expected to support a return to the 63-64% gross margin target by mid-to-late 2027 into 2028.

Story Continues

Applied Materials ' AMAT margins are benefiting from value-based pricing, improved cost efficiency and growing demand for advanced semiconductor technologies. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, non-GAAP gross margin expanded 150 bps year over year to 50.4%, marking the 13th consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth. Semiconductor Systems' non-GAAP gross margin increased to 55.4% from 53.5% a year ago. Non-GAAP operating margin improved to 34% from 30.7%, reflecting stronger operating leverage. The company expects fourth-quarter non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 50.4%, supported by a favorable product mix and increasing demand for higher-value AI-related applications, alongside continued cost improvements.

news.Title: Nvidia's future, AI's road forward, and an inflation-battered economy: Welcome to Yahoo Finance Invest 2026!
news.Content:
It has been an interesting November for the markets ahead of Yahoo Finance's annual Invest event .

First, the entire tech sector got crushed following Election Day , amid fears that Democrats would bring pitchforks to AI data center sites and impose a heavy hand on regulations in D.C. Weak free cash flow trends at hyperscalers like Amazon ( AMZN ) and Meta ( META ) did nothing to temper this negative sentiment.

Then the godfather of artificial intelligence — Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang — admitted to an affair, believed to be with a reported Chinese spy. Just as Nvidia stock began to stabilize, a report of a second affair sent shockwaves through the tech sector as the board met to decide the fate of once-untouchable Huang.

Through all these twists and turns, I am amazed by Wall Street's relentless optimism on tech. Earnings estimates for tech continue to float higher as if there were no blue wave and hyperscalers' aggressive AI investment wasn't pressuring their profits.

That optimism was evident when Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) said it would seek a valuation of more than $1.3 trillion for its IPO, expected Nov. 19 or Nov. 20 . You saw that on CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) earnings call this week, with CEO Mike Intrator hyping the demand he has in his business.

Maybe we call this blind optimism in tech. Sort of like what investors have with celebrity CEOs like Jensen Huang.

On the other side, we have the broader stock market limping into year-end after being battered repeatedly.

The year has been defined by whiplash as the US war on Iran sparked an aggressive oil price shock that pushed crude past $100 per barrel and reignited stubborn headline inflation.

To combat persistent price pressures — as seen in this week's October CPI reading , for example — Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh executed the first interest rate hike of the cycle in September, lifting the policy rate to 3.75% to 4%. Calls are now rising for the Fed to lift interest rates by 50 basis points at its final policy meeting in December.

The S&P 500 is up 9.5% year to date, outperforming the Dow Jones Industrial Average's ( ^DJI ) 8.5% advance and the 7.5% rise for the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ).

I think Yahoo Finance's annual Invest event couldn't have come at a better time.

For one, you need in-depth views on what's driving the markets right now. And two, we can all use some new ideas for 2027.

news.Title: 台積電聯發科漲一大段了！阮慕驊曝AI下一棒往外圍找：一路擴散到5族群
news.Content:
台股今（12）日終場收在43091.87點，大跌1165.28點，跌幅2.63%，失守43100點關卡。資深財經媒體人阮慕驊指出，以昨日台股噴漲1545點來看，證明AI還沒結束，只是會在哪？他認為要往「外圍」找，且一路擴散到5大族群。

阮慕驊表示，講到AI，可能投資人腦中浮現的大概就是台積電、聯發科、台達電。但他認為，這幾家很強，沒話說，但股價也漲了一大段了，該進去的錢差不多都進去。所以現在的問題不是AI會不會結束，而是下一棒會交給誰。

阮慕驊說，他的看法是「往外圍找」，AI一開始是晶圓代工、先進封裝在吃，現在已「 一路擴散到散熱、電源、PCB、光通訊，甚至Edge AI 」。這中間有一批公司，以前根本沒人把它當AI股，結果因為接到新客戶、改了產品線，突然就走出一條新的成長曲線。麻煩的是，這種股票，被動式ETF通常買不到。因為它市值還不夠大，等它擠進前50大，股價早就飛了。

阮慕驊接著提到，主動復華台灣新星（00418A）昨天掛牌，首日收10.41元，漲4.31%，成交量爆出26萬張，擠進主動式ETF前 3 名，第一天跑贏大盤，人氣很旺。他說，00418A就是想抓這段。它的選股範圍拉到市值前300大，大型股放5成左右，爆發新興放2到3成，轉型傳產放1到2成。

阮慕驊表示，大型股顧底，後面那兩塊才是它真正要拚的地方。經理人提過的方向，像是記憶體擴產帶動的矽晶圓，還有從車用延伸到機器人的功率半導體，都是這種「以前不算AI，現在算了」的例子。

阮慕驊認為，時機上00418A算幸運，10月29 成立，剛好碰到台股大修正，手上有現金，可以慢慢撿。到11月10日，淨值9.98元，幾乎守住10元。同一段時間主動統一台股增長（00981A）淨值跌了快 13%，00406A跌了14%多。

阮慕驊指出，當然人家是滿手股票挨跌，它是拿現金在等，起跑點本來就不一樣，但成本墊得比較低，這是事實。不過也要潑一點冷水的是，傳產轉型，不是每家都會成功，而且市場很愛搶先炒，股市最熱的時候進去，往往就是買在高點。所以掛牌後，先別急，看一下它到底買了哪些轉型股、哪些新興股，各放多少。還有，明星經理人加新掛牌，第一天溢價可能不小，市價跟淨值差太多就先等等。

00418A今日終場收9.90元，跌幅4.90%。

news.Title: Semiconductor ETFs to Buy as Qualcomm Plunges Despite Q4 Earnings Beat
news.Content:
Shares of Qualcomm QCOM plunged 9.5% on Nov. 5, despite the company delivering better-than-expected fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues and earnings. The decline was primarily led by a weak profit forecast for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and a 26% year-over-year collapse in QCOM's handset chip revenues.

Democrats' victory in the U.S. House and Senate fueled concerns about a potential slowdown in data-center development (that hit semiconductor names across the board), which further weighed on QCOM shares last week.

This sharp pullback — part operational reset, part external shock — might offer an opportune moment for investors eager to capture Qualcomm's accelerating diversification into automotive and data center silicon.

However, factors like Apple's accelerating modem insourcing and softer guidance for the QCT segment's profit margins, including a 3-point dilution from adding data center operations, could raise concerns and dampen investor confidence in the stock. The memory-cost crunch squeezing global smartphone demand adds another layer of near-term uncertainty.

Democrats' sweeping midterm victories reignited concerns about stricter regulations governing data-center expansion, dampening investor sentiment toward companies with significant exposure to the sector. Against this backdrop, Qualcomm's data-center ambitions, though still sub-scale relative to its handset business, could face pressure from the same political uncertainties that weighed on semiconductor stocks last week.

Against this backdrop, investors seeking to capitalize on Qualcomm's growth potential while mitigating company-specific risks may consider investing in semiconductor exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with meaningful exposure to QCOM rather than investing directly in the stock.

This will let investors gain from Qualcomm's automotive division's growth and the upside of other semiconductor leaders, while reducing exposure to the volatility associated with the company's capital-intensive expansion.

But before diving straight into these ETFs, let us check Qualcomm's overall performance in the quarter in terms of other metrics.

A Look at QCOM's Q4 Results

Qualcomm's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings beat the Zacks consensus estimate by 0.4%, while revenues surpassed the consensus mark by 2.9%.

The company's QCT Automotive segment generated $2 billion in revenues for the first time, marking 89% year-over-year growth, driven by increased adoption of integrated module products for its fifth-generation compute platforms.

Story Continues

QCT IoT revenues increased 4% year over year to $1.9 billion, driven by 20% growth in its industrial, networking and robotics product category.

As of September 2026, QCOM returned $2 billion to stockholders, including $1 billion each in share repurchases and dividends.

Qualcomm expects QCT handset revenues to decline by a mid-single-digit percentage sequentially in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, as continued weakness in Apple-related revenues offsets growth in Android revenues.

The QCT Data Center segment is projected to generate revenues in excess of $650 million, driven by commencements of shipments to custom silicon customers.

Qualcomm expects its QCT non-handset revenues, comprising Automotive, IoT and data center businesses, to increase more than 60% year over year in fiscal 2027.

Qualcomm-Heavy ETFs to Buy

First Trust NASDAQ Semiconductor ETF FTXL

This fund, with net assets worth $1.05 billion, offers exposure to 37 U.S. semiconductor companies. QCOM enjoys the first spot in this fund, holding 9.08% of its assets.

FTXL has surged 61.8% year to date and charges 60 basis points (bps) in fees. It sports a Zacks ETF Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Invesco PHLX Semiconductor ETF SOXQ

This fund, with a market value worth $2.81 billion, includes 31 companies engaged in the semiconductor business. QCOM holds the seventh spot in this fund, with 4.70% of its assets.

SOXQ has soared 49.1% year to date and charges 19 bps in fees. It sports a Zacks ETF Rank #1.

VanEck Semiconductor ETF SMH

This fund, with net assets worth $65.74 billion, includes 26 companies involved in semiconductor production and equipment. QCOM holds the ninth spot in this fund, with 4.41% of its assets.

SMH has rallied 40.8% year to date and charges 35 bps in fees. It sports a Zacks ETF Rank #1.

news.Title: 台積電傳資料外洩! 4.6萬筆員工個資遭兜售 駭客開價725萬
news.Content: 財經中心／陳孟暄　陳裕霖　台北報導 近期台灣接連爆出多起重大資安事件，包含永豐銀行、91APP等都遭駭客攻擊，沒想到，護國神山台積電也驚傳資安危機，有駭客在地下論壇販售4萬6000筆台積電員工資料，對此，台積電回應，已經掌握相關情況，正與相關單位配合調查 過往徵才會上，求職者擠滿攤位，人人都想進的科技大廠台積電，如今卻驚傳資安危機！ 有駭客在地下論壇，公開兜售疑似台積電員工個資，賣家聲稱取得6.9GB、共4萬6千筆員工資料，開價3顆比特幣，以11號行情換算，約台幣725萬元，甚至放話，若一週內沒找到買家，就要公開全部資料。 台積電驚傳員工個資外洩事件，駭客開價3枚比特幣。（圖／翻攝駭客論壇） 資安專家 查士朝：「第一個，造假機會是滿高的，第二個來講，即便不是造假，其實還是有很多資料源，可以拼湊出類似像這樣的資料，包括說有一些像是人力銀行之前有一些資料有掉過，那當然有可能說有人投履歷的這個資料等等」。 賣家還釋出一份樣本檔案，每一筆內容包含姓名、生日、職稱等個資，甚至連緊急聯絡人的電話、住址，通通列得一清二楚，消息在網路上瘋傳，讓網友驚呼''台灣的資安怎麼了，最近先是91APP，再來永豐銀行，現在連護國神山都守不住了嗎？''，也有人無奈表示，''會很意外嗎，開始工作半年後，常常有各大銀行、保險、信貸打來推銷''，看看台積電週四股價，盤中最低觸及2355元，截至上午11點半，跌幅收斂，股價下跌15元，來到2380元，個資外洩是否衝擊台積電營運，專家這樣說。 台積電傳資料外洩! 4.6萬筆員工個資遭兜售 駭客開價725萬。(圖／民視財經網) 資安專家 查士朝：「(台積電)他們的防禦機制應該都到了一個程度，不見得會真的影響到他們的一些工廠或者一些相關機密資料的部分，AI 它不會休息，各種可能都會去嘗試，(建議公司)要時時刻刻去保持它的一個更新，兩個小時內沒有完成更新，可能你要斷網或者是暫時停止服務等等」。 對此，台積電表示，已掌握此情形，正與相關雲端服務供應商及調查機關密切合作，至於是否真的有資料外洩，仍有待進一步調查。

news.Title: Are Wall Street Analysts Predicting NXP Semiconductors Stock Will Climb or Sink?
news.Content:
Eindhoven-based NXP Semiconductors N.V. (NXPI) provides semiconductor products in the United States and internationally. The company has a market cap of $65.9 billion and offers microcontrollers, application processors, communication processors, wireless connectivity solutions, radio frequency devices, security controllers, and semiconductor-based environmental and inertial sensors.

NXPI shares have rallied the broader market over the past year and surged 32.9% compared to the S&P 500 Index's ($SPX) 11.3% gain. Moreover, in 2026, the stock has grown nearly 24.2%, outperforming the SPX's 11.3% rise.

Focusing on its industry benchmark, the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) has risen 19% over the past year, underperforming the stock. In 2026, XLK surged 21.1% as well and lagged behind the stock.

On Oct. 28, NXPI stock rose 5.7% after releasing impressive Q3 2026 earnings. The company's quarterly revenue rose 19.3% from the prior year to $3.8 billion and beat Street estimates. Moreover, its adjusted EPS was $4.20, also beating consensus estimates. NXPI now expects per-share earnings to range from $4.14 to $4.58 and revenue to range from $3.75 billion to $3.95 billion for the fiscal fourth quarter.

For the quarter ending in December, analysts expect NXPI's EPS to rise 35.4% year over year to $13.81. Moreover, the company has surpassed analysts' consensus estimates in three of the past four quarters, while missing on one occasion.

Among the 26 analysts covering the stock, the consensus rating is a "Moderate Buy." That's based on 14 "Strong Buy" ratings, two "Moderate Buy" ratings, nine "Holds," and one "Strong Sell."

The configuration has grown bearish over the past months, with the stock now having 14 "Strong Buy" ratings, down from 15 two months prior.

On Oct. 28, TD Cowen analyst Joshua Buchalter maintained a "Buy" rating for NXPI stock and raised its price target from $275 to $280.

NXPI's mean price target of $297.46 offers 10.4% upside from the current market price. Its Street-high target of $400 suggests a robust 48.4% upside potential from current price levels.

news.Title: Apple is the Best-Performing AI Stock in the “Magnificent Seven” This Year, and Alphabet is the Worst. Here’s the Better Buy for 2027.
news.Content:
The "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks are known for their strength in earnings and stock performance. These well-established powerhouses have led the S&P 500 on its bull market journey, helping the benchmark to climb 78% over the past three calendar years. But this year has been a bit rocky for technology companies, as investors worried about a variety of challenges -- from rising inflation to the risk of a potential slowdown in AI spending.

As a result, four of the "Magnificent Seven" companies are heading for gains this year, and the other three are on track to post declines. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) is the best performer by far, advancing 29%, while Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) is the worst-performing AI stock, declining more than 8%. (Though Tesla , down 15%, is also present in AI, it's primarily an electric vehicle player.)

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Which stock -- Apple or Alphabet -- makes a better buy for 2027? Let's find out.

Image source: Getty Images.

The case for Apple

Apple doesn't need much of an introduction. The company has become a household name thanks to the popularity of its iPhone, the world's top-selling smartphone, as well as other leading products such as the Mac and iPad. Apple's solid moat, or competitive advantage , is its brand. Customers like the products so much that they keep coming back, even when the company raises prices as it did recently.

In fact, Apple just reported September quarter records in total revenue, iPhone revenue, and earnings per share. And Apple is now launching new products, including its first foldable smartphone and a touchscreen Mac, items that could generate revenue gains during the holiday season and beyond.

Apple didn't soar as much as other tech giants in the earliest stages of the AI boom, as it took a slower approach to the technology. But it recently launched a new Siri AI assistant, and this, along with other AI features across its devices, makes it a solid AI player today.

Though Apple stock has outperformed other "Magnificent Seven" stocks, these new products, along with excitement about new chief executive officer John Ternus' product expertise, could lead to further gains.

The case for Alphabet

Alphabet may not be a household name, but its biggest business is: I'm talking about Google Search. Many of us use the platform on a daily basis, and this helps the company generate revenue -- as advertisers promote across the Google platform to reach consumers.

Story Continues

This tremendous amount of revenue, along with the growth of Alphabet's core offerings through Google Cloud, has helped the company fund its AI presence. Alphabet makes AI chips, has developed the large language model Gemini, and sells these as well as products and services of others through Google Cloud. Amid the AI boom, Google Cloud's revenue has soared. In the recent quarter, it climbed 103% to more than $30 billion, and Alphabet is investing heavily in the AI infrastructure build-out to address current needs of its customers as well as future needs.

In spite of strong growth and forecasts for more on the horizon, Alphabet stock has declined this year. Investors have worried that Alphabet and other cloud providers are overspending on the build-out, and that the revenue opportunity may fall short of expectations. That's left Alphabet stock looking cheap, and this could attract bargain-hunting investors.

The better buy for 2027

Alphabet is clearly cheaper than Apple right now.

AAPL PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

Some investors might take advantage of the opportunity and pile in -- that would be a wise move because the company's long-term story is bright. But, for 2027, Apple might continue to outperform. This is thanks to the company's recent releases, and as I mentioned above, Ternus' experience in developing Apple products could spur excitement among investors about what's next.

Investors may also like that Apple is less vulnerable to a potential slowdown in the AI build-out. Democrats may favor a slower pace when it comes to constructing new data centers, and they might support AI regulation too. All of this could weigh on Alphabet in the coming year.

So, though Alphabet and Apple are both great long-term stocks to own, Apple is the best AI stock in the "Magnificent Seven" to buy for 2027.

news.Title: 台股穩定措施何時退場　金管會：視情勢調整無預設立場
news.Content:
（中央社記者高華謙、蘇思云台北2026年11月12日電）台股上週大跌，金管會11月9日起祭出5大穩定股市措施，外界關注措施何時退場。金管會表示，後續關注國際金融情勢變化與國內資本市場適時調整，目前並無預設立場或預定退場時間，要看整體情勢變化而定。

金管會上週五宣布，11月9日起祭出5大措施，包含調降每日盤中借券賣出委託數量、調升融券保證金成數、放寬信用交易應補繳差額的抵繳擔保品範圍，並鼓勵上市櫃公司適時評估實施庫藏股、適時召開法說會對外說明公司營運現況。金管會透過調降每日盤中借券賣出委託數量、調升融券保證金成數等作法打擊空方氣勢，被市場視為廣義的「限空令」。

金管會證期局主秘王秀玲今天在例行記者會表示，自9日至11日，集中市場借券賣出成交值占市場成交值比重介於1.7%至2%間，都低於11月6日的2.97%；借券賣出成交值介於163.52億元至175.15億元之間，也低於11月6日的392.7億元。

王秀玲表示，自9日至今天下午1時30分，台股集中市場漲幅8.54%，同期間日本漲5.80%、韓國漲5.28%；另外，9日至11日期間美國那斯達克漲3.61%、美國費半漲12.50%。

針對如何評估這4天來實施5大措施的成效，王秀玲表示，金管會每天都持續關心相關數據並綜合考量，很難單看某一天就認定成效好壞，必須持續評估與觀察。

至於5大措施實施期限到何時、是否會參考哪些指標決定是否停止實施。王秀玲指出，金管會基於維持證券市場秩序與穩定性採行措施，後續會持續關注國際金融情勢變化與國內資本市場做適時調整，目前沒有預設立場或預定時間，還是要看整體情勢變化。

媒體追問，去年金管會因應美國對等關稅祭出3大救市措施，是採每週檢討，這次是否比照辦理。王秀玲指出，「上次是最特別的」，以每週觀察是否延續措施，但基本上歷次穩定措施都是持續實施、觀察，再評估何時可以解除，「今年模式會跟以往比較像」。

台股基本面方面，王秀玲表示，今年截至10月底本益比約24.92倍，現金殖利率1.63%，加計股票股利為1.67%，上市櫃公司今年截至10月底累計營收約55.18兆元，較去年同期成長39.4%。

王秀玲指出，截至11月11日，信用交易整戶擔保維持率為179.76%，高於券商規定的130%最低追繳門檻；整體市場借券賣出占市場成交值比率為1.87%。

news.Title: 台股雪崩「一票人急問ETF該賣嗎」？他曝「關鍵操作」訊號全說
news.Content: 財經中心／綜合報導 台股今（12日）上演震盪行情，儘管前一天美國費城半導體指數大漲5.66%，台股卻未能延續漲勢，盤中一度翻紅，隨後賣壓迅速湧現，終場下跌1165.28點、收在43091.87點，跌幅2.63%，台積電（2330）也下跌55元、收在2340元。面對市場劇烈波動，臉書粉專「工程師的存股致富之路」發文分析，認為短線資金獲利了結是這波下跌的原因之一，但他依舊看好明年AI產業發展，並針對不同類型的ETF投資人提出操作建議，強調長期投資者不必因為短期震盪急著賣出持股。 臉書粉專指出，儘管前一天美國費半指數大漲5.66%，台股卻未能延續漲勢，午後賣壓更迅速湧現。（示意圖非關本新聞／民視新聞資料照） 臉書粉專「工程師的存股致富之路」指出，儘管美國費半指數前一交易日強勢上漲，但台灣、日本及南韓股市卻未同步走高，台股午後更由紅翻黑，電子權值股全面承壓，其中台積電下跌55元、聯發科（2454）下跌140元、台達電（2308）下跌55元。他分析，目前市場關注輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳捲入的爭議，以及公司未來領導層可能出現的變化，不過即使發生黃仁勳離開輝達的極端情境，他認為對台積電的影響仍相對有限，原因在於輝達GPU高度依賴台積電的先進製程，而其他ASIC晶片代工需求也有機會填補訂單空缺。他表示，自己依舊看好明年AI發展帶動台股與美股表現，但提醒短期股價波動可能相當劇烈。 粉專分析，目前市場關注輝達執行長黃仁勳相關爭議，但他認為即使輝達領導層出現變動，對台積電的影響仍相對有限。（圖／民視新聞資料照） 至於近期受到投資人關注的ETF，009816今日下跌0.32元、收在15.03元，粉專分析，過去3天受到國安基金進場護盤消息帶動，內資推升大盤，但在短線交易者陸續獲利了結之下，今日出現回檔並不意外，他認為009816最理想的走勢並非短時間急漲，而是隨著投機資金逐漸退場，讓股票慢慢轉移到長期投資人手中，未來若外資重新回頭買超，才有機會朝16元、17元方向邁進。 另一檔ETF 009823則上漲0.04元、收在10.62元，粉專指出，雖然近期漲幅不如009816，但也正逐漸收復先前跌幅，粉專觀察市場仍在觀望輝達董事會如何處理黃仁勳相關爭議，若公司領導層出現重大變動，可能影響投資人信心；反之，若事件獲得妥善處理，市場也有機會重新評估輝達股價，不過相關發展仍存在不確定性，後續有待公司進一步說明。

news.Title: Greg Abel Has Plowed $14.4 Billion Into Warren Buffett's Favorite Stock This Year, and It's Not Apple
news.Content:
Warren Buffett served as the chief executive officer of the Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA)(NYSE: BRKB) holding company from 1965 to 2025. Under his leadership, it became a $1 trillion conglomerate with several wholly owned subsidiaries, a $350 billion stock portfolio, and over $300 billion in cash.

Buffett selected one of his longtime deputies, Greg Abel, to step into the CEO role at the start of 2026. It won't be easy for Abel to replicate his predecessor's success, but he has purchased $14.4 billion worth of Buffett's favorite stock so far this year, which is always a popular move with shareholders.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Berkshire stock obliterated the S&P 500 during Buffett's tenure

Berkshire was a textiles manufacturer when Buffett acquired a controlling stake in 1965. Its business was struggling, and after deciding it was no longer viable, he turned it into a holding company for his various investments.

Berkshire now wholly owns a number of insurance providers, consumer brands, logistics giants, and utilities, which it manages privately. They produce significant cash flow that the conglomerate often uses to purchase minority stakes in other companies, compounding shareholders' returns.

Buffett liked to invest in companies with steady growth, consistent profits, and experienced management teams, but he especially liked those with shareholder-friendly initiatives like stock buyback programs and dividend schemes, because they supercharged Berkshire's returns.

For example, Buffett acquired 400 million shares of Coca-Cola between 1988 and 1994 for around $1.3 billion. He never sold a single share; the position is now worth a whopping $38.2 billion, and it will pay Berkshire $848 million in dividends this year alone. Buffett's long-term investment in American Express produced similar results.

Buffett also famously invested $38 billion in Apple between 2016 and 2023. The stake was worth over $170 billion at the start of 2024, which represented half the value of Berkshire's entire portfolio. Buffett and his team had sold 75% of the position by the end of 2025 to cash in some gains and reduce concentration risk, but it remains one of the conglomerate's most successful investments ever.

Berkshire stock delivered a compound annual return of 19.7% during Buffett's 60-year tenure, crushing the S&P 500 index, which returned an average of 10.5% per year over the same period. Had an investor parked $500 in Berkshire stock in 1965, they would have been sitting on $24.2 million by the time Buffett stepped down at the end of 2025, whereas the same investment in the S&P would have grown to just $199,851.

Story Continues

Buffett bought $77.8 billion worth of Berkshire stock between 2018 and 2024

Buffett struggled to identify worthy investment opportunities in the years leading up to his retirement. Berkshire had become so large that very few stocks in the U.S. (that he didn't already own) could produce enough growth to move the needle, which is why he diversified into countries like Japan toward the end of his tenure.

As a result, Buffett decided to return some of Berkshire's growing cash pile to shareholders. Between 2018 and 2024, he authorized $77.8 billion worth of stock buybacks, meaning Berkshire purchased its own shares on the open market. This reduced the number of shares in circulation, and thus made each remaining share more valuable.

Buybacks give investors control over when they crystallize their gains for tax purposes, so Buffett preferred them to dividend payments, which are taxed almost immediately.

By spending more money on buybacks than he invested in any other company throughout his career, Buffett clearly believed Berkshire was capable of delivering better returns than practically any other company of similar size, and its long-term track record against the S&P 500 is proof.

Buybacks have returned under Greg Abel

Buffett didn't authorize any stock buybacks during his final year as CEO, likely because he wanted to leave his successor, Greg Abel, with as much cash as possible to take Berkshire into its new era.

Abel is already making big moves, having invested over $20 billion in Google parent Alphabet so far. But he also restarted Berkshire's buyback machine, authorizing $235 million worth of repurchases in the first quarter of 2026, followed by a further $4.5 billion in the second quarter, and then a whopping $9.6 billion in the third quarter.

That's $14.4 billion returned to shareholders in Abel's first nine months at the helm.

Berkshire can repurchase its own shares at management's discretion as long as the value of its cash and cash equivalents remains above $30 billion. The company currently has over $352 billion in dry powder, so there is plenty of room for Abel to get more aggressive in the coming quarters.

news.Title: 外資連11賣　買超台玻逾14萬張居冠
news.Content:
（中央社記者何秀玲台北2026年11月12日電）台股今天跌1165.28點，收在43091.87點，成交值新台幣1兆132.93億元；三大法人合計買超51.6億元，其中外資連11個交易日賣超，賣超前10名以電子股為主，群創 (3481) 逾3萬張居冠；買超以台玻 (1802) 逾14萬張居首。

根據台灣證券交易所統計，三大法人合計買超51.6億元，其中自營商賣超65.41億元，投信買超123.85億元，外資及陸資賣超6.84億元。

外資賣超前5名，以群創3萬4542張最多，主動中信台灣收益（00406A）2萬2499張居次，其餘依序為仁寶 (2324) 、元大台灣50反1（00632R）及廣達 (2382) 。

外資買超前5名，以台玻14萬326張居冠，主動統一台股增長（00981A）2萬4607張居次，其餘依序為GIS-KY (6456) 、元大金 (2885) 及華航 (2610) 。

萬寶投顧執行長王榮旭接受中央社記者電訪表示，台股前波下跌約1萬2000點，近幾個交易日反彈逾6000點，約收復前波跌幅一半，逼近月線後面臨技術面壓力。

路透引述知情人士報導，輝達董事會開會討論是否撤換執行長黃仁勳，輝達股價在美股盤後交易一度重挫逾8%，王榮旭研判，部分投資人擔心輝達股價走弱拖累美股，提前賣股避險，加重台股尾盤賣壓；從今天外資現貨小幅賣超、台指期淨空單減少來看，他認為外資並非尾盤下殺主因。

王榮旭指出，輝達股價走弱之際，部分AI概念股已有回升，AI供需及供應鏈基本面也未見明顯變化。相關個股自10月以來已歷經一波修正，市場對利空的反應有鈍化跡象。他認為，若輝達人事結果明朗，有機會視為利空出盡。

展望後市，王榮旭表示，短線觀察5日線約42284點，若指數回測後能反彈，短線上漲走勢有望延續；若無新的重大利空，即使大盤再度探底，跌破前波低點37837點的機率較低。至於台股能否挑戰5萬點，他認為，基本面未變，後續有機會反彈。

news.Title: 金管會「限空令」奏效 台股漲幅優於日韓
news.Content:
金管會今日公布自11月9日上路的「限空令」成效，根據數據顯示，盤中借券賣出的金額已經較實施前明顯下降，且執行到今日止，台股上漲8.54％，而日本與韓國則分別漲5.80％、5.28％，顯見金管會限空令發揮效用。

首先，盤中借券賣出委託數量限額自11月9日調整為3％，實施以來截至11月11日止，集中市場借券賣出成交值佔市場成交值比重介於1.7％至2％之間，均低於實施前一日(11／6)的2.97％；借券賣出成交值介於163.52億元至175.15億元之間，亦低於實施前一日的392.7億元，。

統計穩定措施實施以來至11月12日，台股集中市場漲幅8.54％，同期間日本漲5.80％、韓國漲5.28％，另11月9日至11日期間美國那斯達克漲3.61％、美國費半漲12.50％。

115年截至10月底本益比約24.92倍，現金殖利率1.63％(加計股票股利為1.67％)，上市櫃公司115年截至10月底累計營收約55.18兆元，較去年同期成長39.4％。截至115年11月11日，信用交易之整戶擔保維持率為179.76％，整體市場借券賣出占市場成交值比率為1.87％。

台股受到美國期中選舉影響，6日大幅震盪，盤中一度跌近3800點，創盤中最大跌點。金管會6日公布5大台股措施，包含，調降每日盤中借券賣出委託數量，由原不超過該種有價證券前30個營業日之日平均成交數量之30％調降為3％；上市及上櫃有價證券之最低融券保證金成數由90％調整為130％。

投資人經證券金融事業或證券商同意，除115年3月30日已將上市(櫃)股票零股及興櫃股票納入抵繳擔保品範圍外，並得以具有市場流動性且能被客觀合理評估價值之其他多元擔保品，補繳融資自備款或融券保證金差額，例如複委託之外國有價證券；現行上市櫃公司買回庫藏股已採電子化申報，鼓勵上市櫃公司可視自身資金調度、財務狀況及買回目的，適時評估實施庫藏股。

鼓勵上市櫃公司適時召開法人說明會或參與主題式業績發表會，主動對外說明公司營運現況、財務表現、產業展望及未來發展策略。

news.Title: Intel's CEO Bought $9.7 Million of Stock Right After It Plunged 29%. I'm Not Ready to Follow Him In.
news.Content:
Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought 150,000 shares on Nov. 2 through a family trust, paying a weighted average of around $64.73 a share, or about $9.7 million total.

The purchase came one trading day after Intel stock plunged 29% on Oct. 30.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The company had just guided for $0.25 of non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share in the fourth quarter, down from $0.52 in the third. As I write, the stock trades near $62, a little under what Tan paid.

How has Intel stock done after its CEOs bought shares before? Over the past decade, Intel CEOs bought stock on the open market on 24 different days with at least a year of trading since. Twelve months later, shares were higher after 12 of these days and lower after the other 12. The median result was a fall of around 2%, leaving out dividends.

Put another way, a CEO buy has shown investors little about where Intel stock would be a year later. And I think the sample is even thinner than 24 sounds.

Image source: Intel.

Two CEOs, two records

All of those purchases came from two people. Brian Krzanich, CEO until mid-2018, didn't make open-market purchases in that period.

Bob Swan, who ran Intel as interim CEO from mid-2018 and then as CEO until February 2021, bought on seven days. Shares had risen 12 months later in six of those cases, by between 7% and 22%.

But six of his seven purchases were made under trading plans he set up beforehand (plans that let executives buy or sell on a fixed schedule), so they arguably say little about his timing. His only loser, on Jan. 25, 2021, came 12 days after Intel said that Pat Gelsinger would replace him. The stock was 8% lower a year after that buy.

Gelsinger's record went the other way. He bought shares on 17 days from October 2021 to November 2024, in every calendar quarter of that stretch. The stock fell over the next 12 months after 11 of those purchases, and two of the six gains were below 1%. Shares he bought on Jan. 29 and Feb. 1, 2024, at roughly $43, were worth about 55% less a year later. But shares he bought on Feb. 23, 2023, climbed 68%.

Is 24 purchases enough to go on?

Probably not. Several of these purchase days were within a week of each other -- Nov. 29 and Dec. 6 in 2018, for example -- so their 12-month periods covered almost the same stretch of trading. Counting each of those four pairs once, the record shrinks to around 20 separate choices by two people.

Story Continues

The results also read more like a record of each CEO's era than of his timing. Swan bought while the stock mostly held between about $42 and $68 a share.

Gelsinger, though, kept buying as shares dropped from roughly $49 at his first purchase to below $19 by September 2024. Buying quarterly, he caught both the 2023 rebound and the 2024 collapse.

Tan is buying on a far bigger scale

Tan's purchase does stand out. At around $9.7 million, it's almost 20 times the size of Gelsinger's largest single-day buy, about $500,000, and over six times Swan's biggest. What's more, the Nov. 4 filing doesn't flag it as part of a prearranged trading plan.

It also follows around $10 million of stock Tan bought on Aug. 11 at $95 a share, the same price Intel set for its $23 billion stock offering that month. That purchase is too recent to count yet. The shares worth around $25 million that Tan got directly from Intel in March 2025 under his offer letter aren't in the record either, because he didn't buy them on the open market.

Sure, a purchase this big tells me Tan thinks shares are worth more than he paid. It doesn't tell me when the business turns.

Revenue in Intel's data center and AI segment grew to $7.3 billion in the third quarter, up 78% from a year ago. But management expects PC weakness to last at least through the first half of 2027, which may leave profits under pressure for several more quarters.

And the stock still isn't cheap. Given what analysts expect Intel to earn in 2027, its price-to-earnings ratio is around 35.

Over the past decade, how Intel stock did in the year after a CEO purchase came down to the business, not to who was buying. With quarterly profits set to drop by more than half, I'm not ready to follow Tan in at this price.

news.Title: 主動ETF新兵搶鋒頭！00413A掛牌首日漲8.4% 奪科技型主動式ETF首秀冠軍
news.Content:
▲主動ETF新兵搶鋒頭！00413A掛牌首日漲8.4%，奪科技型主動式ETF首秀冠軍。（圖/PEXELS）

新掛牌主動式ETF的第一張成績單出爐，主動玉山關鍵科技（00413A）於11月11日正式上市，收盤來到10.84元；若以10元發行價計算，掛牌首日累計漲幅達8.4%，在目前科技型主動式ETF中，寫下掛牌首日相對發行價漲幅最高紀錄，也讓這檔AI科技ETF新兵一上市就搶下市場目光。

值得注意的是，00413A不只ETF本身首日表現亮眼，旗下多檔關鍵科技持股也同步大漲。持股比重5.25%的創意終場大漲9.97%，穎崴上漲9.95%，旺矽漲9.94%，健策上漲8.12%，南電也上漲7.46%；大型權值股方面，台積電上漲4.81%、聯發科上漲4.18%、欣興上漲4.35%，形成大型權值股與中型成長股同步上攻的格局。

市場人士指出，00413A的持股結構並非只集中在單一AI題材，而是從晶圓製造、ASIC設計、先進封裝測試、散熱、PCB與ABF載板等不同環節布局。今日盤面中，創意代表ASIC與客製化晶片需求，旺矽與穎崴則受惠高階測試需求，健策切入散熱與半導體零組件，南電則卡位高階載板，顯示AI資金並非只回到台積電等大型權值股，而是開始往供應鏈中的關鍵環節擴散。

其中，00413A第一大持股台積電權重約9.52%，第二大台光電5.73%、第三大聯發科5.60%，加上創意、奇鋐、健策、欣興、旺矽、日月光投控、台達電等，組成從晶片、伺服器、散熱到封裝測試的完整AI供應鏈布局。

市場人士認為，主動式科技ETF真正的差異，不只是「有沒有買到AI」，而是能不能在AI產業不同階段，把資金配置到真正有訂單、有技術門檻與成長性的公司。00413A掛牌首日不僅從10元發行價站上10.84元，旗下多檔持股也同步強勢，首日即交出科技型主動式ETF中相對發行價漲幅最佳的成績單。首日紅盤可能只是起點，隨著AI行情從大型權值股擴散至關鍵供應鏈，下一波成長機會有望由不同科技族群接棒。對看好AI長線趨勢的投資人而言，不妨趁產業輪動之際，透過00413A一次布局多檔AI關鍵科技股，掌握後續成長契機。

news.Title: 投資人勇者無懼 台股ETF受益人上周增49.2萬人 總人數破2025萬人
news.Content:
台股上周大指數下挫5510點，累計跌幅達12.19％，創下史上最大單周跌點紀錄；不過，台股投資人勇者無懼，台股ETF受益人數不僅連續4周創新高，根據集保戶統計資料顯示，台股ETF受益人數上周增49.2萬人，總人數突破2025萬人，今年來增加807萬人。

以單檔人數變化來看，包括0050、00685L、00919、0056、00927等共28檔台股ETF受益人數同步創高，其中，元大台灣50(0050)上周增加13.2萬受益人增加最顯著，元大台灣50正2(00631L)昨規模也正式突破3000億元大關，整體來說，正二、高息型、市值型人氣相對旺。

群益投信台股ETF研究團隊表示，以台股來說，台股已經拉回整理一波，目前正是逢低分批布局的好時點，穩健投資人可以台股高息ETF為核心配置穩固資產。積極型投資人也可以趁大幅回檔買入正二，但台股正2 ETF的運作機制為每日重新平衡，當市場下跌時，資產縮水的幅度也會被加倍放大，投資人須考量自身理財目標與投資屬性，控制好投資風險，分批佈局參與第四季投資契機。

群益台灣精選高息（00919)基金經理人謝明志表示，台股基本面有撐，長線來看，每次回檔都是中長線成長的佈局良機。對投資人而言，面對大盤大漲大跌的情況，建議投資人可以選擇有息收保護、波動相對個股低的台股高息型ETF。

news.Title: 《台股盤後》大跌1165點，43K失而復得/險守10日線
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-12 16:08:44 新聞中心 發佈

台股今(12)日開低後陷入震盪，雖有玻璃陶瓷族群表現突出，但仍不敵台積電、聯發科、台達電、日月光投控等電子權值股走弱影響，加上盤中塑膠、電腦及週邊設備與電子通路族群亦顯疲態，拖累加權指數臨近午盤後跌勢逐步擴大、最低一度失守43000點大關，終場則以43091.87點作收，大跌1165.28點或2.63%、險守10日線，成交量放大至1兆132.94億元。

AI雲端運算基建供應商CoreWeave財報創佳績並上修全年展望，紓解AI投資疑慮、並帶動相關概念股全面反攻，美國四大指數11日也全面收高。亞洲股市方面，跟隨美股昨日走揚腳步，激勵日經225指數早盤續揚，不過盤中賣壓湧現、終場收跌0.70%；韓國KOSPI指數也收跌0.61%。

台股今日震盪走低、市場賣壓明顯升溫，上下震盪幅度超過1500點，險守43000點大關。電子權值股多數走弱，台積電未能延續近日漲勢，早盤開低在2385元，盤中跌幅加劇，終場收2340元，下跌2.30%，失守月線關卡，南電、健策也雙雙打入跌停，台光電、奇鋐、欣興重挫逾8%，緯穎、廣達、川湖、鴻勁、日月光投控同步走低。

29大類股表現方面，今日以電子零組件類股跌幅最深、下跌5.97%，其次依序為塑膠類股跌5.30%、電腦及週邊設備類股跌4.93%。然而，在市場波動加劇下，仍有部分傳產與防禦型族群逆勢抗跌，其中玻璃陶瓷類股表現最強，漲幅達5.93%，食品類股收漲1.00%、生技醫療類股漲0.85%，走勢皆相對穩健。

三大法人動向方面，今日三大法人合計買超51.60億元；其中，自營商賣超65.41億元，投信買超123.85億元，外資及陸資賣超6.85億元。
