news.Title: MP Gains 2% After Q3 Earnings Beat: Reason Enough to Buy the Stock?
news.Content:
MP Materials MP delivered a stronger-than-expected third-quarter 2026 performance on Nov. 5, driven by robust growth in rare earth production, higher NdPr sales volumes and improved pricing. Revenues surged 176% year over year to $147.7 million while adjusted earnings swung to a profit of 4 cents per share from the loss of 10 cents in the year-ago quarter. The company also made progress in expanding its domestic magnet manufacturing operations, marking another step toward strengthening its position in the U.S. rare earth supply chain.

MP shares have gained 2% since the earnings release. However, the recovery has done little to offset the stock's broader weakness. MP stock has declined 27.3% year to date, trailing the Zacks Mining - Miscellaneous industry's growth of 7.4%, the Zacks Basic Materials sector's 8.2% gain and the S&P 500's rise of 8.7%. Peer Energy Fuels UUUU has declined 52% year to date while Lynas Rare Earths Limited LYSDY advanced 14.1%.

MP's YTD Price Performance Against Industry, Sector, S&P 500 & Peers

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Before addressing the critical question of how investors should position themselves regarding the stock, let us first review the company's third-quarter results.

High NdPr Volumes and Pricing Drive MP's Revenue Growth

MP Materials produced 1,018 metric tons of neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr), up 41% year over year, reflecting stronger output from the company's separation and finishing operations at Mountain Pass. NdPr sales volumes surged 94% to 1,020 metric tons.

The Materials segment's revenues soared 322% year over year to $133.5 million. NdPr oxide and metal revenues surged 227% to $100.96 million, benefiting from higher sales volumes and stronger market pricing.

In September 2026, the company had entered into a one-time sale agreement with a U.S. aerospace and defense customer, under which it sold $31.6 million of a mixed heavy rare earth product containing samarium, europium, gadolinium and other heavy rare earths (SEG+) during the third quarter of 2026.

The Magnetics segment's revenues declined 15% year over year to $18.6 million, reflecting slightly lower magnetic precursor product sales as the company advanced the start-up of magnet production at its Independence Facility.

MP's total revenues rose 176% year over year to $147.7 million. MP also recorded $8.11 million in income tied to a price protection agreement (PPA) with the Department of War (DoW).

MP achieved another important commercial milestone during the quarter by completing the magnet qualification process with General Motors Company (GM). Management expects saleable magnet deliveries and associated revenues to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026, supporting the company's transition toward higher-value downstream operations.

Story Continues

Higher Costs Lead to Operating Losses for MP

Despite the strong revenue growth, MP continues to face considerable cost pressures as it expands beyond rare earth concentrate production into separated products and magnets.

Cost of sales increased 76.6% year over year in the third quarter, reflecting higher sales volumes of NdPr oxide and metals. Selling, general and administrative expenses rose 33.8%, primarily due to higher personnel costs associated with downstream expansion. Start-up expenses also climbed significantly to $14.15 million from $1.41 million a year earlier as initial magnet manufacturing activities gathered pace.

Advanced projects and development expenses declined sharply to $1.90 million from $19.03 million, partly reflecting the absence of transaction-related expenses incurred in the prior-year period.

Despite the higher expenses, MP's consolidated adjusted EBITDA improved substantially to $41.14 million from a loss of $12.57 million in the year-ago quarter. The operating loss narrowed to $22.06 million from $67.02 million, reflecting higher revenues and PPA-related income, which partly offset increased operating expenses.

However, costs are likely to remain elevated in 2026 and 2027, as producing separated rare earth products and magnetic materials involves significantly higher costs than concentrate production. Costs associated with magnetic precursor products and start-up costs are also likely to increase further in the coming quarters.

MP Sees Downward Revision Activity in Earnings Estimates

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MP Materials' 2026 revenues indicates a 99% increase year over year. The estimate for earnings is currently pegged at a loss of 3 cents per share, narrower than the loss of 24 cents reported in 2025.

For 2027, the consensus estimate points to revenue growth of 58.8%, with earnings expected to reach 66 cents per share.

MP's growth outlook remains strong, but the Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings for both 2026 and 2027 has moved down over the past 60 days. It suggests that analysts are becoming more cautious about its near-term profitability.

MP Materials Stock Trades at a Premium

MP stock is trading at a forward 12-month price/sales multiple of 9.33X, significantly higher than the industry's 1.46X. MP has a Value Score of F, reflecting this expensive valuation, with the forward sales multiple also standing above the broader Basic Materials sector's valuation and the company's five-year median.

Energy Fuels trades at an even steeper multiple of 12.86X, while Lynas Rare Earths appears comparatively cheaper at 7.76X.

Partnerships and Capacity Expansion Support MP's Growth

Despite near-term profitability challenges, MP continues to make progress on several strategic initiatives that could strengthen its competitive position in the rare earth and magnet markets.

During the third quarter, the company advanced the refining of its SEG+ production stream and expects to begin producing separated terbium and dysprosium by the end of 2026. Under its partnership with the U.S. Department of War, MP has also committed to expanding its heavy rare earth refining capabilities to include samarium oxide separation and recommissioning the chlor-alkali facilities at Mountain Pass.

Its agreement with Apple Inc. AAPL represents another important growth opportunity. Under the partnership, MP plans to develop and install scaled magnet recycling capabilities at Mountain Pass, with dedicated capacity for both NdPr and heavy rare earth separation.

Meanwhile, construction of the 10X facility remains on track, with commissioning expected to begin in 2028. The facility is designed to produce approximately 7,000 metric tons of magnets annually. Combined with the 3,000-metric-ton annual capacity of the Independence facility, MP's total U.S. magnet production capacity is expected to reach 10,000 metric tons.

Is MP Stock a Buy After Its Q3 Earnings Beat?

MP Materials' latest quarterly performance highlights meaningful progress in expanding production, increasing NdPr sales and developing its domestic magnet manufacturing business. Its strategic partnerships with the U.S. Department of War, Apple and General Motors further strengthen its long-term growth prospects.

However, the investment case is less compelling from a near-term valuation and earnings perspective. Operating losses persist, expansion-related costs remain elevated and downward earnings estimate revisions point to continued uncertainty around profitability. Moreover, MP trades at a substantial premium to the industry despite its significant year-to-date underperformance.

Given these concerns, investors may prefer to remain on the sidelines for now. MP Materials currently carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

news.Title: Stock Market News for Nov 12, 2026
news.Content:
Wall Street ended higher on Wednesday, led by gains in technology stocks as Apple reached a fresh all-time closing high. Market participants continued to digest third-quarter earnings results and assess economic data. The Nasdaq Composite, the Dow and the S&P 500 ended in positive territory.

How Did the Benchmarks Perform?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) rose 0.5%, or 254.60 points, to close at 52,486.49. Eighteen components of the 30-stock index ended in positive territory, while 12 ended in negative territory.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.6% to close at 25,466.19.

The S&P 500 gained 1.3% to end at 7,619.38. Out of the 11 sectors of the broad-market index, 10 ended in positive territory while one ended in negative territory. The Information Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK), the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) and the Industrials Select Sector SPDR (XLI) rose 2.7%, 1.8%, and 1.3%, respectively. The Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) fell 0.4%.

The fear gauge, the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), decreased 10.1% to 17.49. A total of 14.74 billion shares were traded on Wednesday, lower than the last 20-session average of 18.68 billion. The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and no new lows, and the Nasdaq Composite recorded 77 new highs and 159 new lows.

Apple Hits Fresh Record High

Apple Inc. AAPL shares climbed 2% on Wednesday to close at a record $355.63, extending the stock's recent rally. The shares touched an intraday high of $355.91, surpassing the previous peak of $355.38 recorded on Nov. 5. Trading volume reached approximately 34.28 million shares. The market capitalization is roughly $5.1 trillion. Apple currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Quarterly Earnings Results

ICL Group Ltd reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings per share of 1 cent, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 11 cents. Total revenues of $1.91 billion missed the consensus estimate by 10.31% compared with $1.85 billion in the year-ago quarter.

Sonos, Inc. reported fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of 4 cents per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 3 cents. Total revenues of $344.44 million beat the consensus mark by 1.23% and increased from $287.9 million in the prior-year quarter.

Mercury Systems, Inc. reported first-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of 52 cents per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 28 cents. Total revenues of $253.15 million beat the consensus mark by 3.67% and increased from $225.21 million a year ago.

Story Continues

Consequently, the stock prices of ICL Group Ltd ICL fell 2.1% while Sonos, Inc. SONO and Mercury Systems, Inc. MRCY rose 12.9%, 12.9%, respectively.

Economic Data

Per a government report, for the week ended Oct. 30, 2026, Commercial crude oil inventories (excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve) decreased 0.9 million bpd to 409.8 million bpd.

news.Title: 【Follow法人】外資狂掃台玻14萬張！反手砍台積電92億元 群創也遭賣逾3萬張
news.Content:
（下午4點43分更新買賣超個股）

台股今（12）日重挫1,165點，外資僅賣超6.84億元，連續11個交易日累計提款8,312.52億元。資深台股分析師蔡明翰表示，近期台股連續反彈，外資態度已逐漸轉向偏多，不過目前仍處於信心較脆弱的階段，若美股半導體跌勢擴散，仍可能重新轉趨保守。觀察外資買賣超個股，台玻（1802）獲外資大舉買超逾14萬張，登上買超冠軍；反觀權王台積電（2330）卻遭外資提款約92億元，面板股群創（3481）也遭賣超逾3萬張。

外資今日賣超前三大：群創、00406A、仁寶

外資今日賣超以面板股群創（3481）居冠，單日遭調節3.4萬張；主動中信台灣收益（00406A）遭賣超2.2萬張排名第二；電腦大廠仁寶（2324）則遭賣超1.7萬張，位居第三。

其餘個股方面，AI伺服器大廠廣達（2382）遭外資賣超1.3萬張，英業達（2356）也遭調節1.2萬張；ETF方面，除了主動中信台灣收益外，元大台灣50反1（00632R）及元大高股息（0056）也進入賣超前十大，共有3檔ETF入列。

值得注意的是，權王台積電（2330）今日也遭外資賣超3,955張，以今日收盤價計算，外資單日調節金額約92.54億元。

外資今日買超前三大：台玻、00981A、GIS-KY

觀察外資今日買超個股，玻璃股台玻（1802）以買超14萬張高居第一；主動統一台股增長（00981A）獲外資買超2.4萬張排名第二；GIS-KY（6456）則獲加碼1.8萬張，位居第三。

其餘個股方面，金融股元大金（2885）獲外資買超1.84萬張，華航（2610）獲買超1.83萬張；面板股友達（2409）也獲加碼逾萬張。值得注意的是，外資今日買超前十大共有4檔金融股入列，包括元大金、玉山金（2884）、兆豐金（2886）及凱基金（2883）。

外資賣超縮手能否轉買？分析師：已有偏多跡象

蔡明翰表示，外資操作通常比大盤反應慢約3至4天。台股前幾個交易日連續反彈，市場情緒逐漸由悲觀轉向偏多，但外資仍持續賣超，直到今日才明顯縮手。他認為，外資目前已有轉向偏多的跡象，但由於才剛開始調整，信心仍相對脆弱。

蔡明翰指出，外資後續能否由賣轉買，仍須觀察輝達（NVIDIA）相關事件對美股的影響，尤其跌勢是否擴散至其他半導體股。若跌勢進一步擴大，外資可能重新轉趨保守；反之，若影響未擴散，外資後續買盤則有機會更加積極。

至於自營商今日賣超65.40億元，蔡明翰認為，自營商部位相對較小，操作偏向短線，通常跟隨市場走勢調整，難以單獨左右大盤方向。他指出，今日台股下跌的關鍵並非賣壓特別沉重，而是先前連續反彈後，市場追價意願降低，買單明顯減少，進一步放大跌勢。

台股大跌逾千點 三大法人逆勢買超51億元

根據證交所公布籌碼動向，三大法人今日合計買超51.59億元。其中，外資今日縮手僅提款6.84億元，已呈連11賣，累計賣超8312.52億元。

投信也延續買超，投信今日合計買超123.85億元，呈連23買。

自營商則是由買轉賣，今日賣超65.40億元，其中自行買賣賣超29.80億元，避險操作賣超35.60億元。

台股今日終場收在43,091點，下跌1,165點，失守4萬4千點大關，成交量約1.04兆元。權王台積電（2330）終場收在2,340元，下跌55元。

湯暖萱／財經特派記者，主跑主計處、營建、百貨紡織等

news.Title: 黃仁勳爭議衝擊 台股巨震1581點又回防4萬3
news.Content:
[ 非凡新聞 ]記者黃友柔,攝影謝隆証

輝達相關爭議持續延燒，衝擊台股表現，今（12）日早盤雖然一度衝上44525點，不過隨後指數一路走低，最低下探42943點，高低震盪將近1600點。電子權值股普遍疲弱，台積電、聯發科還有台達電通通收黑，儘管玻纖布還有光電族群逆勢撐盤，最後仍不敵空軍賣壓，指數終場下跌1165點，收在43091點，成交量大約1.01兆元。

加權指數一下上、一下下，就像一張狂跳的心電圖，上漲好開心、翻黑又擔心。儘管美股周三集體收紅，但是輝達受到利空消息干擾，盤後一度暴跌9%，導致台積電股價跟著疲弱，聯發科、台達電也陷入整理，大盤上沖下洗，44000點得而復失。

第一金投顧董事長 黃詣庭：「從上周五的低點到昨天收盤，其實已經上漲超過6400點，相較之下這一波從高到低大概跌了12000點，也就是說本波反彈已經是跌幅的一半以上，所以開始會有一些調節性的賣壓開始出籠，再加上說上方開始又會面臨到均線的反壓。（但）目前來看的話本波反彈是非常的強勁，主要還是受到國安基金進場，還有就是金管會的禁空令讓市場信心恢復，再加上美股有回穩的現象，科技股出現反彈所帶動。」

盤面上強勢走高族群，包括面板股友達上揚，華通受惠Space X題材上漲，高階玻纖布需求強勁。不過另一方面，在MSCI明晟公布最新半年度調整後，景碩、南電、台燿都從小型股指數升級至標準指數，股價卻重挫，而相關調整預計11月30後收盤後生效。

好在從籌碼面來看，外資態度似乎悄悄出現轉變。

兆豐投顧董事長 留政鈺：「昨（12）天外資基本上賣壓已經縮減到8億元以下，今年以來外資賣超3.02兆，以及11月大概就賣6500億。不過比較好的是，台積電基本上昨天外資是買了142億，買了6038張，那今年以來外資賣超台積電是2.28兆，所以第一個台積電是外資賣壓止跌的一個訊號，那第二個是今天早上MSCI的一個調整，基本上比較好的是權重調整、調高0.03百分點。」

隨著美國期中選舉消息面因素逐漸弱化，加上市場對於雲端服務業者的投資成本上升疑慮淡化，專家認為台股基本面堅實，年底前高點仍然可期。（記者黃友柔、謝隆証／台北採訪報導）

news.Title: 輝達概念股慘綠！台股收跌1165點 法人曝後市三劇本
news.Content:
台股今（12）日開高走低，盤中雖一度上漲逾200點，但翻黑後跌幅迅速擴大，尾盤以43091點作收，下跌1165點，跌幅2.63%，成交量來到1.01兆元；台積電、鴻海等一票輝達概念股也綠一片，唯獨金融股收紅撐盤。

進一步觀察輝達概念股，受黃仁勳再爆出第2起婚外情影響，輝達盤後股價重挫8%，連帶影響台廠輝達概念股也下挫，台積電下跌55元，收2340元，跌幅2.3%，鴻海來到240元，下跌0.83%，健策跌停，奇鋐下挫8.72%，廣達、緯穎重挫逾6%，台達電跌逾4%，緯創也下跌逾2%。

針對黃仁勳近期捲入桃色風波，國泰證券期貨分析師郭經緯表示，未來有三大走向：

第一， 調查疑慮解除、沒違反國安法 ：黃仁勳安全下樁，此將激勵輝達概念股強勁反彈，但認為發生機率最低。

第二， 風暴擴大，黃仁勳被迫請辭 ：發生機率約40%，輝達供應鏈全面承壓，台股不排除回測11月6日的低點37837點，打出第二隻腳。

第三， 黃仁勳退居幕後 ：留任董事長但交出執行長職務，發生機率最高。若管理層順利交接，台積電、AI伺服器與零組件可望回歸訂單及獲利基本面，市場信心逐步修復。

（封面圖／東森新聞）

news.Title: 台股收盤／台積電跌55元！台股慘跌1165點　類股又一片慘綠
news.Content:
美股週三（11日）四大指數全面收紅，AI概念股強勢反彈，未料台股今（12）日不漲反跌，盤中賣壓持續擴大，尾盤更出現明顯殺盤。加權指數終場收在43,091.87點，大跌1,165.28點，跌幅2.63%，失守43,100點關卡，成交金額高達1兆132.93億元；代表中小型股的櫃買指數同步走弱，終場收在335.73點，下跌8.38點，跌幅2.44%，成交金額2,783.19億元。兩市合計成交金額達1兆2,916.12億元。

美股四大指數齊揚　台股開高後賣壓湧現

美股週三（11日）四大指數全面收高，AI雲端業者CoreWeave第三季營收優於預期，並上調全年財測，激勵股價飆漲近25%，帶動人工智慧（AI）概念股反彈。輝達結束連續兩個交易日跌勢，那斯達克指數上漲1.60%，費城半導體指數更勁揚5.66%，為科技股帶來反彈契機。

不過，美股科技股反彈氣勢未能延續至台股。從今日盤勢觀察，加權指數早盤一度向上反彈，但隨後賣壓逐漸湧現，指數由紅翻黑，上午11時後跌勢進一步擴大，午後更一路向下探低，終場收在43,091.87點，接近當日低檔。

台股今日成交金額突破兆元，顯示市場交投相當熱絡，但指數卻大幅下挫，反映高檔震盪加劇，資金調節壓力沉重。權王台積電（2330）下跌55元，收在2,340元，聯發科、南亞、南亞科等電子權值及記憶體股同步走弱，拖累大盤重挫逾千點，市場呈現價跌量增格局。

倫元投顧陳學進分析師認為，盤中指數一度上漲268點、上探至44525點；不過，由於美AI監管政策不確定性尚未消除，外資期貨空單居高不下、現貨一路調節動作不斷，加上AI晶片霸主黃仁勳桃色風波愈演愈烈，盤後股價應聲暴跌逾9%，以及月線與季線蓋頭反壓，仍有待時間化解，，台股連5日大漲6688點後，雖然在利空未除、以及市場信心尚未完全恢復過來之前，短線上將有震盪拉回整理的必要，且下檔於11/9日止跌長紅K棒40347~41661點區間附近有撐下，預期11月行情將可望處在於40000~45000點區間反覆震盪、個股輪動表現的機率居多，投資方向將由過去缺料漲價與題材推升，轉向基本面升級、技術門檻提高及實際訂單成長；首先是ASIC與AI伺服器，Google TPU、AWS Trainium及NVIDIA Vera Rubin陸續放量，帶動IC設計服務、伺服器組裝與高速互連需求；其次是高階PCB、CCL、ABF載板及先進封裝，隨M8/M9材料升級、晶片封裝面積擴大及製程難度提高，具備高階產品認證與實際量產訂單的廠商，將持續擴大獲利；第三是CPO、NPO及矽光子，隨800G、1.6T光通訊產品滲透率提升，高速光互連將成為降低傳輸功耗的重要技術方向；第四是半導體設備、廠務工程及矽晶圓，受惠先進製程與記憶體新廠陸續量產，帶動設備及材料需求成長，因此，面對指數處於40000~45000點區間反覆震盪的過程中，策略上除了宜把握「急漲不追、急殺不空」的原則。

台積電跌55元拖累大盤　聯發科、南亞重挫

觀察今日成交值排行前段班個股，台積電（2330）仍是市場交易焦點，終場收在2,340元，下跌55元，跌幅2.30%，成為拖累大盤的重要權值股之一。IC設計龍頭聯發科（2454）同步走弱，收在3,850元，下跌140元，跌幅3.51%；南亞（1303）跌勢更為沉重，收在293元，下跌20元，跌幅達6.39%。記

news.Title: Micron vs. Sandisk: The AI Memory Supercycle Is Big Enough for Both, but Here's the Better Buy.

This has impacted not just the cost of AI data centers, but also the cost of smartphones, PCs, and other electronic devices. This has benefited the stocks of both Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) and Micron (NASDAQ: MU), which have been two of the market's biggest winners ...
news.AI_Summary:
• Sandisk (SNDK) and Micron (MU) have benefited significantly from the AI memory supercycle, with Sandisk shares up over 200% and Micron up around 150% year-to-date.
• The AI build-out has created a bottleneck in memory, driving up prices for both DRAM (Micron) and NAND (Sandisk) due to high demand for AI data centers and consumer electronics.
• Micron derives approximately 73% of its revenue from DRAM and 26% from NAND, while Sandisk is a pure-play NAND manufacturer.
• High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), a special form of DRAM, is in high demand, manufactured using EUV lithography, leading to competition for capacity among DRAM makers like Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix.
• Both companies are seen as attractive buys with extremely low forward P/E ratios of 4 times or less, benefiting from secular AI tailwinds and long-term deals.
news.Keywords: AI memory, DRAM, NAND, HBM, secular tailwinds

news.Title: SpaceX investors confront a painful post-election reality
news.Content:
SpaceX appeared to be enjoying a strong run after reporting an impressive third quarter, with revenue rising 161% and net income more than doubling Wall Street expectations, according to the firm's Q3 8-K earnings release .

But the momentum quickly faded as Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress in the 2026 midterm elections, triggering a sharp investor reaction.

Between election night and Nov. 5, 2026, SpaceX and Tesla lost approximately $456 billion in combined market value. SpaceX shares fell 12.5% in two sessions, CNBC reported , dropping below its June 2026 IPO price of $135.

However, the sell-off may reflect more than a temporary market reaction. It also highlights growing political and regulatory challenges that could affect SpaceX's long-term ambitions.

Also read: Elon Musk sends a strong memo to SpaceX and Tesla stock investors

How the Democratic win pushed SpaceX shares below IPO price

SpaceX's market capitalization fell to about $1.68 trillion by the close on Nov. 5, 2026, roughly 87% of its pre-election value, Fortune reported .

Musk spent $446 million on Republican candidates during the cycle, yet key allies lost Texas governor and Senate races to Democrats, the Washington Post confirmed .

Deutsche Bank warned of "incremental headwinds" for SpaceX as investors sold Musk-linked stocks, even while the S&P 500 gained 1.6% that session, CNBC reported.

Keith Snyder, senior equity analyst at CFRA Research, told Fortune the sell-off was a knee-jerk reaction to the midterm results. He added that Musk's heavy political involvement has introduced a form of reputational exposure his companies didn't have before the election.

The nail that sticks out gets hammered first, and Musk has certainly stuck out, especially in government, whether it be donations, the election, and any of the feathers he ruffled while he was at DOGE .

That exposure could grow as SpaceX expands beyond its traditional aerospace and satellite businesses into artificial intelligence.

SpaceX's growing AI business creates new regulatory risks

SpaceX's risk profile has changed since its June 2026 debut because artificial intelligence now generates most of the company's revenue and drives its capital spending.

The Super Intelligence (SI) division produced $7.56 billion in third-quarter revenue, roughly 52% of the $14.57 billion total, SpaceX disclosed .

That concentration means any policy restricting data center construction cuts directly into SpaceX's primary business rather than a secondary line of business.

Story Continues

Capital spending reached $19.6 billion in the third quarter, with management projecting even higher outlays for the fourth quarter.

More SpaceX:

Goldman Sachs revamps SpaceX stock estimates before crucial earnings test

Musk called Anthropic 'evil'; SpaceX's deal with it nearly doubled

Morgan Stanley doubles down on SpaceX stock verdict for investors

SpaceX's acquisitions of xAI in February 2026 and the AI coding platform Cursor in August 2026 cemented the company's position as one of the world's largest AI operators. Cursor alone contributed $608 million in revenue during the quarter, showing how quickly SpaceX is converting AI acquisitions into earnings.

Connectivity remained the most profitable segment, generating $5.25 billion in third-quarter revenue with $2.37 billion in operating income. The division's steady profitability gives SpaceX a revenue floor that supports its aggressive spending on both AI infrastructure and Starship development.

Tesla merger and data center expansion face mounting political pressure

JPMorgan called a Tesla-SpaceX merger "strategically coherent on paper" but flagged a "practical bottleneck" of multi-jurisdictional approvals, especially in China, Investing.com reported .

On SpaceX's Oct. 20, 2026, call, Musk confirmed both boards formed special committees to study a combination, while warning a deal is not "a certainty," Bloomberg Law reported .

Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, noted that Congress can slow a merger through hearings but cannot block a private transaction on its own. Extended Congressional scrutiny could still push the projected 2027 closing date further out and add uncertainty for investors in both companies.

Data center restrictions threaten SpaceX's expansion, particularly in Texas, where Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on pausing construction.

Goldman Sachs estimated that Democratic wins across state and local races could trigger temporary moratoria affecting about 45% of planned national capacity, as summarized by Walter Bloomberg on X .

SpaceX committed to roughly $40 billion in GPU financing with Apollo Global Management for Nvidia Vera Rubin processors. Those chips are set for delivery in the first half of 2027, creating a timing risk if data center permitting stalls in key states.

The hardware could arrive before the facilities meant to house it are operational, stranding billions of dollars in committed capital.

3 signals that will determine whether the sell-off lasts

SpaceX shares rebounded 8.62% on Nov. 6, 2026, but remained below its June IPO price.

The recovery offers some relief, but the concerns behind the sell-off remain. Political uncertainty, potential AI regulations, and delays to data center construction could all affect SpaceX's growth plans.

Goldman Sachs identified the duration of moratoria as the decisive factor, warning that an extended freeze shifts the impact from a temporary delay to a lasting loss of capacity, Reuters reported .

Starship's development is another important indicator. Stifel highlighted the upcoming Flight 15 mission as a key milestone for the rocket's reusability and SpaceX's longer-term orbital computing ambitions, according to Investing.com .

Construction permit timelines in Texas, Georgia, and other key states will also determine how quickly SpaceX can expand its AI infrastructure and put its planned computing hardware to work.

Together, these factors will help determine whether the recent decline was a temporary reaction to the midterm results or the beginning of a longer-term reassessment of SpaceX's growth prospects.

Related: Elon Musk sends startling message on SpaceX, Tesla merger

news.Title: If SpaceX and Tesla Merge, Here's What a $10,000 Investment in the Combined Company Could Be Worth by 2030
news.Content:
Elon Musk is considering merging his two business empires under one corporate umbrella. Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) and Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) have both formed committees to explore the potential merits of a merger, which could lead to a proposal in the near future. This would put electric vehicles, battery packs, rocket launches, satellite internet, and artificial intelligence ( AI ) business lines under one roof.

What could a $10,000 investment in a combined SpaceX and Tesla business be worth in 2030? For anyone interested in these stocks after a merger, it pays to do the valuation math.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

SpaceX's fast growth and steep valuation

SpaceX made its public debut earlier this year, and now sports a market cap of almost $1.9 trillion. It has quickly become one of the largest stocks in the world by market cap and is already larger than Tesla on this metric.

The business is still small compared to megacap technology standards. Revenue was $14.6 billion last quarter, up 161% year over year. This is mainly due to the Starlink satellite internet business and the company's investments in AI infrastructure. Connectivity revenue grew to $5.25 billion in the quarter, up 69% year over year, and AI revenue was $7.56 billion, up more than 10-fold from the same quarter a year ago.

Both connectivity and AI are growing rapidly for SpaceX, but the business remains quite small relative to its market cap. It has a trailing price-to-sales ratio (P/S) of 56, one of the most expensive in the entire stock market today, indicating investors are expecting massive amounts of revenue growth in the years ahead.

Tesla's slow growth and steep valuation

Tesla is a much larger business than SpaceX, with revenue exceeding $100 billion over the past 12 months. However, it is growing much more slowly.

In fact, last quarter, it didn't grow at all. Tesla's Q3 revenue was little changed year over year as it struggles to continue scaling its electric vehicle (EV) business, which still accounts for the majority of its business today. Huge investments are being made in self-driving cars and humanoid robots, but the technologies are still financially irrelevant for the business right now.

Tesla may trade at a lower P/S ratio than SpaceX at 13, but it is nowhere near a cheap stock. It has a price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) of 417, and its earnings have been declining for years now. Tesla's EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes) peaked at nearly $15 billion in late 2022 and has since fallen to $3.63 billion.

Story Continues

That is not a great trend. Why would that turn the corner in the years ahead if revenue isn't growing?

TSLA EBIT (TTM) data by YCharts

What could the combined business be worth?

A Tesla and SpaceX merger has a lot of promise because both businesses play at the leading edge of technological innovations. If AI infrastructure grows unabated, satellite internet disrupts all connectivity, and humanoid robots dominate work around the globe, then sure, a $10,000 investment in Tesla and SpaceX today could be worth more by 2030.

I think it is highly unlikely to actually happen over this short time span. Today, if you add up both market caps for Tesla and SpaceX, you get a value of nearly $3.5 trillion. It is going to be incredibly difficult for these businesses to generate earnings by 2030 sufficient to warrant a $3.5 trillion valuation, and that is before accounting for share dilution. A $10,000 investment in Tesla and SpaceX could be worth much more in 2030, but I think it is likely to be worth less.

news.Title: Dell Technologies vs. Taiwan Semiconductor: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
As the artificial intelligence revolution accelerates, investors are looking for the best way to profit from the massive hardware requirements. Two giants, Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (NYSE:TSM), offer very different ways to play this trend.

Dell provides the physical servers and storage that companies need to run complex software, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing acts as the essential foundry for the world's most advanced chips. Comparing them requires looking at how hardware demand translates into consistent earnings for both businesses.

The case for Dell Technologies

Dell Technologies provides client devices, servers, and storage solutions for the data and AI era. The company serves a diverse group of large enterprises, government institutions, and individual consumers through a direct sales force and a global network of partners. Its Infrastructure Solutions Group is particularly focused on AI-optimized servers, traditional servers, and networking tools, while the Client Solutions Group handles personal computing for businesses and individuals.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 30, 2026, revenue reached around $113.5 billion, which was an increase of roughly 18.8% compared with the prior fiscal year. Net income for the period was approximately $5.9 billion, indicating a net margin of roughly 5.2%. This growth was driven by the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure and a recovery in the broader client device market across global markets.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is negative 12.8x. This value indicates that total liabilities exceed shareholder equity, a situation that requires consistent cash generation to meet ongoing obligations. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, is close to 0.9x. Free cash flow reached around $8.6 billion in the fiscal year ended Jan. 30, 2026, which is the cash remaining after paying for operations and equipment.

The case for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., also known as TMSC, operates as a pure-play foundry, meaning it manufactures chips designed by other companies rather than selling its own brands. Its services are essential for high-performance computing, smartphones, and the automotive industry. Most of the world's most advanced semiconductor stocks rely on its manufacturing, including designs from Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO).

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached around $115.8 billion, a jump of approximately 31.6% compared with the prior fiscal year. The company reported net income of roughly $51.6 billion for that period. This resulted in a net margin of about 44.6%, which is the percentage of revenue remaining after all costs are paid, demonstrating a dominant position in advanced node production.

Story Continues

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carries a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.2x. This indicates a low level of debt relative to its equity. The current ratio, which shows how easily a company can cover short-term liabilities, is roughly 2.5x. Free cash flow reached approximately $30.2 billion in the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, providing ample capital to invest in next-generation silicon facilities.

Risk profile comparison

Dell Technologies faces intense competition from other hardware and software providers in a rapidly changing market. The company also deals with potential supply chain disruptions and relies on limited-source vendors for certain critical components. Furthermore, cybersecurity threats and rapid technological obsolescence require constant product transitions and significant research spending to remain competitive.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing operates in a highly capital-intensive industry that requires constant investment in new production nodes to maintain its lead. Geopolitical instability and changes in global trade policies could impact its ability to serve international markets from its primary facilities. The company also faces risks related to regulatory compliance and the possibility of shifting demand in the consumer electronics sector.

Valuation comparison

Dell is cheaper based on its Forward P/E , using future earnings estimates, and its P/S ratio, which measures sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

AI demand has Taiwan Semiconductor selling as much as it can produce.TSM's 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer chips underpin AI technologies and other high-speed processes, so that as long as token usage (which is the base measurement of blocks of data used in AI) exceeds projections, TSM continues to beat estimates. Also bound to help is the construction of $165 billion in plants in Arizona, sparked by grants under Biden, which will also focus on chip formats and AI research and development. Building more in the U.S. also helps the business sidestep Trump's tariffs.

TSM is uniquely positioned to capture AI acceleration as agentic AI expands silicon demand beyond accelerators to CPUs and networking chips. The overall outlook for the business remains bullish. Wall Street sees fiscal 2026 revenue coming in 42% higher than 2025, with net income leaping 63% for the year, according to consensus estimates.

Despite its already massive size, Dell's sales are expected to rise a staggering 51% to $171.3 billion in fiscal 2027, with more than $11 billion in both net income and free cash flow. While Dell still sells the laptops that originated the business, the story is all about AI. The business is selling AI-optimized servers hand over fist, with management expecting more than $60 billion in AI server sales in FY 2027, almost triple the prior year.

So which stock is the better buy? These are both AI-driven fast top-line growers. Neither is a bad choice. But the better choice for investors right now is Dell, given its forward P/E and P/S ratios price the tech giant at near-value stock levels.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 11: Intel Climbs on Broader Chip Rally as AI Infrastructure Demand Lifts Semiconductor Stocks
news.Content:
Intel (NASDAQ:INTC), an x86 processors, AI data-center chips, and contract semiconductor manufacturing conglomerate, closed at $62.50, up 7.52%. Broader chip strength and stronger AI infrastructure sentiment lifted shares, and investors are watching data center demand and foundry progress next.

Trading volume reached 125.6 million shares, coming in nearly 7.4% above its three-month average of 116.9 million shares.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) closed at 7,619, up 1.31%, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) closed at 25,466, up 1.60%. Among semiconductor stocks, Advanced Micro Devices closed at $552.90, up 7.32%, and Nvidia closed at $173.73, up 2.92%, as chipmakers tracked stronger AI infrastructure sentiment.

What this means for investors

On Wednesday, Nov. 11, Intel extended its chip rally as neocloud CoreWeave delivered stronger-than-expected third-quarter results on Nov. 10, reinforcing the strong demand that continues for artificial intelligence infrastructure. CoreWeave announced Q3 revenue of $3.7 billion, more than double the prior year's $1.4 billion, and raised its full-year outlook.

Consequently, investors rotated back into semiconductor stocks after abandoning them in the wake of last week's U.S. midterm results. The Democratic Party gained control of Congress in the elections, raising fears that incoming Democratic leadership might push for tighter AI regulations and pause data center construction projects, leading to a semiconductor sector sell-off that swept up Intel shares with it.

CoreWeave's strong Q3 results softened investor concerns over the AI industry's future, boosting Intel shares. This is a reversal from the stock's crash after the chipmaker released fiscal Q3 earnings results on Oct. 29. The company issued a weak Q4 forecast due to a faltering PC market, a key business for Intel.

The PC sector is expected to see a steep downturn in Q4 due to component shortages and skyrocketing prices tied to AI infrastructure demand. The situation reset Wall Street's expectations for Intel's turnaround story.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 11: Advanced Micro Devices Jumps -- and Not Only Because of CoreWeave's Results
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), a major semiconductor player, closed at $552.90, up 7.32%. Shares rose after solid results from CoreWeave pointed to continued demand for advanced computing chips. Goldman Sachs also named AMD as one of three attractive semiconductor stocks amid the broader sell-off. Trading volume reached 42.5 million shares, coming in about 83% above its three-month average of 23.2 million shares.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 rose 1.31% to 7,619, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.60% to 25,466. Among chipmakers, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) closed at $173.73, up 2.92%, and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) closed at $62.50, up 7.52%.

What this means for investors

AMD stock gained today as chip stocks started to put the post-election sell-off behind them. The stock has risen 36.99% since Nov. 6, as investors look for opportunities in the artificial intelligence (AI) sector. Its recent earnings beat analyst expectations, with Q3 revenue up 45% year-on-year to a record $13.4 billion. It also guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $17 billion, predicting that server and center revenue will expand further.

CoreWeave's results are just one of several signs that demand for advanced computing chips will continue to grow. Another is this week's cloud deal with Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)'s Google, which will see AMD's 5th-gen EPYC chips powering its cloud Tensor Processing Unit (TPU). AMD is also named as a key investor in Anthropic's IPO prospectus.

For investors, AMD is well-positioned to benefit from increased AI chip demand, particularly if Nvidia's recent difficulties continue. There is a risk that political shifts or other factors hamper the AI buildout and AMD will be susceptible to wider AI jitters. However, AMD's diversified business, strong leadership, and competitive market position could make it a long-term AI winner.

news.Title: Hugging Face co-founder says AI hacks show even the biggest labs haven't figured out AI alignment
news.Content:
In July, the open-source AI site Hugging Face was attacked by a swarm of AI models developed by OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ).

The episode, known as the Hugging Face incident , was one of the first major examples of how AI models can break free of their constraints and go rogue in an effort to complete assigned tasks.

The hack , which was followed by reports of similar cyberattacks perpetuated by models from Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ); Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ); and Meta ( META ), coupled with the development of increasingly powerful frontier models, has led to a greater focus on cybersecurity in the age of AI.

It also raised questions about AI alignment, or whether AI systems act the way their developers intend them to.

"Our attack was indeed a consequence of this misalignment," Hugging Face co-founder and chief science officer Thomas Wolf told Deirdre Bosa.

"The AI should have decided when it was on the internet and was starting to penetrate an infrastructure that this was a bad behavior. And so that was, for me, the first sign that even though the labs are doing very good work, and they are massive, and there's a lot of very smart people there, they don't have it fully figured out," he added.

In response, Hugging Face has established its own open alignment team dedicated to working on safety and alignment for open models.

But the AI security issue is more than just alignment. Nefarious actors are already using AI models to scale their attacks against targets across the globe .

Wolf, however, says that there's at least a silver lining amid the chaos.

"I think … the positive view of that is that it's mostly an engineering process," he said.

"Cybersecurity has always been the story of offense increasing. First [there was a] virus, we invent the antivirus, everyone sets up, and then now we have these new steps. So we need to invent the new defense step," Wolf added.

"I think everyone in industry, at least in AI and tech industry, is focusing on that right now."

news.Title: Apple Shares (AAPL) Look Expensive Heading into 2027
news.Content:
Apple (AAPL) shares look expensive heading into 2027, despite the company's strong growth prospects. Shares of the iPhone maker have soared in 2026, easily outperforming the Nasdaq-100 ( NDX ) as tracked by the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) . This comes as Apple has delivered higher sales and revenues this year, a trend analysts expect to continue into Fiscal 2027.

What is more, Apple may benefit from higher device sales should memory costs normalize, potentially making the shares interesting for investors looking to diversify their artificial intelligence (AI) exposure away from current high memory cost beneficiaries such as Micron (MU) .

Despite these positives for the Apple investment case, my rating on the shares remains a Hold . I believe that with the stock trading at 37.08x analysts' consensus 2027 earnings per share (EPS) estimate of $9.40, the outlook for investor returns is quite modest even as the company is likely to continue its strong underlying performance.

Promotion

BLACK FRIDAY SALE

Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Apple's Record Net Income and EPS

Apple delivered Q4 2026 EPS of $2.10 , a 14% increase relative to the prior-year quarter and a Q4 record for the company from a historical perspective. While results were boosted by a $0.05 per share one-off tariff refund, underlying performance was nevertheless quite strong.

Case in point, Apple sales increased 12% year-over-year , driven by the low-margin products segment. Apple cited strong iPhone demand as a key revenue driver. Growth in the high-margin services business was somewhat weaker, at 10% year-over-year. A 32% year-over-year increase in research & development expenses was a relative disappointment, although this should help Apple's innovation over the medium term.

CEO John Ternus was quite optimistic for the company's prospects going into Q1 2027. He said, "We're closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet. That includes the iPhone Duo, the most transformational iPhone since the original, alongside iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, our most powerful iPhones yet. We also just introduced a whole new generation of hardware for the home and brought Touch to Mac for the first time. Together with the all-new Siri AI, it's an incredible lineup to carry us into the holiday season."

Story Continues

Despite the strong product pipeline, Apple's forecast for Q1 2027 shows that the company anticipates total revenue to increase by about 7%–10% year-over-year , with Services revenue growing by about 8%–9%. As such, we do see that the company expects a near-term slowdown relative to the growth rate achieved in Q4 2026.

To sum up, while the one-off tariff benefit and somewhat weaker growth in the Services business arguably support my Hold on Apple, I must admit that the underlying performance of the company remains quite reasonable. As I will discuss in the next section, however, the strong revenue and earnings momentum going into 2027 appears priced in.

Apple Valuation

Analysts expect Apple to generate EPS of about $9.40 in Fiscal 2027, implying roughly 4.8% growth relative to the $8.97 EPS achieved in 2026. The earnings increase is projected to be driven more by higher sales than by a meaningful pickup in margins, as revenues are expected to be about 10% higher at $527.53 billion.

Indeed, I expect the low-margin products revenue category to continue to be a key sales contributor to Apple's top line. This comes as the initial sales results of iPhone Duo will begin to be booked in Fiscal 2027.

Product margins are currently squeezed by high memory costs. The silver lining is that Apple's product margin may see a recovery in 2028–2029, when I expect the memory shortage to begin to normalize. As such, I do see Apple's earnings trajectory increasing over the medium term.

Unfortunately, this positive medium-term backdrop appears to be priced into Apple stock, as it already trades at 37.08x expected 2027 earnings. This high valuation is a key factor in my Hold rating, as Apple trades at a hefty premium to the S&P 500's ( SPX ) 19.8x forward P/E multiple. This kind of valuation premium is typically reserved for conservative health care companies such as Eli Lilly (LLY) , rather than consumer electronics companies such as Apple, which can see a downturn in sales during recessions.

To conclude, while Apple may offer diversification benefits for technology investors thanks to a potential acceleration in device sales if memory costs decline, I believe this year's stellar returns have frontloaded gains. Indeed, Apple stock may fail to produce attractive returns over the medium term, even as the company's earnings and sales continue to grow.

Wall Street's Take on Apple

On Wall Street, Apple has a Moderate Buy consensus rating, based on 15 Buy, eight Hold, and six Sell ratings over the past three months. The average Apple price target is currently $338.28 , implying roughly 3% downside over the next 12 months.

Conclusion

Apple stock has soared in 2026, with investors rewarding the company for its double-digit revenue and earnings expansion. While a near-term slowdown in Q1 2027 cannot be ruled out based on company guidance, analysts expect full-year 2027 performance to reflect a moderation in growth rates relative to Fiscal 2026.

Looking further ahead, Apple's margins may recover in 2028–2029 should memory costs decline. This could make the shares interesting for investors looking to diversify their technology exposure with companies like Apple, which can deliver higher earnings even as AI capex spending slows.

Despite these positives, my rating on Apple is a Hold . Strong recent gains have pushed the company's valuation well above the S&P 500, potentially indicating that the shares may deliver lackluster returns even as earnings and revenues continue to grow.

This is also evident from Wall Street's 12-month consensus price target for Apple, which implies slight downside from current levels. As such, Apple appears to be a business that is doing quite well on an underlying basis, but nevertheless is likely to deliver modest gains for investors over the medium term.

news.Title: Bots don't fly here: United Airlines restricts AI agents from booking flights
news.Content:
AI agents just got denied boarding at United Airlines ( UAL ).

Ahead of holiday travel, the airline company is cracking down on third-party artificial intelligence agents as more consumers turn to AI tools.

"To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman," United CEO Scott Kirby told the Wall Street Journal on Tuesday.

AI agents function as personal assistants for tasks such as scheduling, shopping, and research. Unlike conventional chatbots, they operate autonomously and are capable of completing transactions independently.

The airline is not the only company to try to limit agentic AI from using its platform. In September, Amazon ( AMZN ) blocked Meta's ( META ) Muse AI agent from shopping on its site.

Other airlines, however, have taken a different tack. In October, Southwest Airlines ( LUV ) launched a ChatGPT plugin that allows travelers to search the carrier's flights and fares.

United traded slightly down Wednesday afternoon. Meta ( META ) stock also declined.

United Airlines said in a press release that it fears that AI agents could expose sensitive information as well as potentially violate Federal Aviation Administration and Department of Transportation rules.

At the same time, airlines have recently found themselves in hot water over AI-powered surveillance pricing. In October, the Federal Trade Commission ordered United Airlines, Delta Air Lines ( DAL ), JetBlue Airways ( JBLU ), and six other major carriers to turn over information on how AI tools influence individual fare pricing and how customer data is used.

Relatedly, many people feel that AI offers inadequate customer service. A new " Consumer Patience Index " poll found that when ranking frustrating support experiences, customers rated "talking to a bot that doesn't understand me" as the biggest pain point, and 61.2% say they have yelled at automation in order to be  routed to a human faster.

news.Title: Is It Worth Investing in TSMC (TSM) Based on Wall Street's Bullish Views?
news.Content:
When deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock, investors often rely on analyst recommendations. Media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts often influence a stock's price, but are they really important?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about TSMC (TSM).

TSMC currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.21, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 19 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.21 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 19 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 16 are Strong Buy and two are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 84.2% and 10.5% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for TSM

Check price target & stock forecast for TSMC here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying TSMC, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

ABR Should Not Be Confused With Zacks Rank

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide.

On the other hand, earnings estimate revisions are at the core of the Zacks Rank. And empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Furthermore, the different grades of the Zacks Rank are applied proportionately across all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide earnings estimates for the current year. In other words, at all times, this tool maintains a balance among the five ranks it assigns.

There is also a key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank when it comes to freshness. When you look at the ABR, it may not be up-to-date. Nonetheless, since brokerage analysts constantly revise their earnings estimates to reflect changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in predicting future stock prices.

Is TSM Worth Investing In?

Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for TSMC, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 5.2% over the past month to $17.46.

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) for TSMC. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>

Therefore, the Buy-equivalent ABR for TSMC may serve as a useful guide for investors.

news.Title: ON Semiconductor Corporation (ON) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
news.Content:
ON Semiconductor Corp. (ON) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Shares of this semiconductor components maker have returned -9.2% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -3.7% change. The Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry, to which ON Semiconductor Corp. belongs, has lost 6.4% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, ON Semiconductor Corp. is expected to post earnings of $1.01 per share, indicating a change of +57.8% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +5.6% over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $3.27 points to a change of +39.2% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +2.2%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $4.76 indicates a change of +45.6% from what ON Semiconductor Corp. is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +6.3%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for ON Semiconductor Corp..

12 Month EPS

Projected Revenue Growth

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of ON Semiconductor Corp., the consensus sales estimate of $1.76 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +15.4%. The $6.61 billion and $7.58 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +10.3% and +14.6%, respectively.

The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters. The company topped consensus revenue estimates three times over this period.

news.Title: Booking Holdings vs. Target: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
One represents the rebound in global travel while the other serves as a cornerstone of American retail. Choosing between Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG) and Target Corp. (NYSE:TGT) depends on your growth and stability preferences.

Booking operates a high-margin digital platform connecting travelers with accommodations and flights. Target maintains a massive physical and digital footprint, selling everything from groceries to apparel to loyal guests. While they occupy different sectors, both compete for a share of consumer spending as economic conditions shift toward 2027.

The case for Booking Holdings

Booking operates through major brands such as Booking.com and Priceline, providing online travel services in 220 countries and territories. In 2025, the company facilitated approximately 1.2 billion room nights for travelers around the globe. It relies heavily on major search platforms, notably Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL), to drive consumer traffic to its digital properties.

In FY 2025, revenue reached about $26.9 billion, representing a growth of roughly 13.4% compared to the previous year. This performance translated into a net income of approximately $5.4 billion. While the top line grew, the net margin, which measures how much profit a company keeps from every dollar of sales, was about 20.1%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is negative 3.5x, which means total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The current ratio, a measure of a company's ability to pay short-term obligations with short-term assets, is approximately 1.3x. In FY 2025, free cash flow reached around $9.1 billion, which is the cash a company generates after accounting for capital expenditures to maintain its operations.

The case for Target

Target serves millions of customers through its nearly 1,995 stores and a robust digital platform. It differentiates itself among retail stocks through strategic partnerships with major brands. These partnerships include names like Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), CVS Health (NYSE:CVS), Starbucks Corp. (NASDAQ:SBUX), and Ulta Beauty (NASDAQ:ULTA).

In FY 2025, revenue reached roughly $104.8 billion, which reflected a slight decline of approximately 1.7% from the prior year. The company reported a net income of about $3.7 billion for the same fiscal period. Its net margin was approximately 3.5%, reflecting the higher costs associated with inventory management and physical store operations.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.3x, indicating the proportion of debt used to finance assets relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio is approximately 0.9x, suggesting its short-term assets are slightly lower than its short-term liabilities. Free cash flow for FY 2025 was around $2.8 billion, representing the cash a company generates after subtracting capital expenditures used to expand its business.

Story Continues

Risk profile comparison

Booking faces intense competition from global technology firms and other online travel companies that could disrupt its reservation process. The company is also navigating significant dependence on third-party digital platforms for its visibility and customer traffic. Additionally, legal and regulatory risks involving data privacy and international competition laws, particularly in the European Union, remain a primary concern for the business.

Target must contend with intense retail competition and the constant pressure to differentiate its guest experience through merchandise and digital channels. Supply chain disruptions and volatile global trade policies, including its reliance on goods imported from China, pose ongoing operational challenges. Furthermore, the company faces risks related to inventory management, shrink, and potential cybersecurity incidents that could compromise guest or team member data.

Valuation comparison

Booking trades at a slightly lower multiple of future earnings estimates, whereas Target features a lower price relative to sales over the past twelve months.

The Forward P/E compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures the stock price relative to sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Target is in the first year of its multi-year turnaround strategy, which aims to restore top-line growth and margins. It's been going well, but there is concern that elevated gas prices, which raise transportation costs and reduce consumers' spending capabilities, could derail the turnaround story over the near term. But to its benefit, Target is the most-followed retailer on social media platforms, has a strong women's clothing business, and should be able to capture more food business by expanding the section in remodeled stores. About half of Target sales include food items of some sort.

For fiscal 2027, Target is expected to see a sales gain of nearly 6%, to more than $110 billion, which is pretty good considering the pinched American consumer. Net income should improve much more strongly, to more than $1 billion, up to $4.7 billion.

Booking Holdings is successfully shifting from an agency model to a primarily merchant model. That means it used to make its money as an agent--connecting travelers to a hotel and collecting a commission while the hotel manages collecting payment from the traveler. In the merchant model, Booking buys capacity from hotels and other providers on its platform and collects payment directly from the traveler. This tends to lead to fatter margins.

The company is also in excellent financial shape. It has $16 billion in cash, which makes its balance sheet investment grade. Another plus for shareholders is that the company has a $20 billion share buyback program. The brand is increasingly a destination for travelers, which means it is paying less to companies like Google for search engine visibility. Today, two-thirds of Booking.com's visitors are organic, meaning they are direct visitors rather than from paid ad traffic.

Revenue will grow about 9% this year to $29.3 billion. And net income takes a healthier 50% leap to about $8.1 billion.

That Booking Holdings stock is cheaper, on a forward P/E ratio, than Target's is an opportunity to buy a fast-growth business at a very reasonable price. Target has a strong case to regain its shopper mojo, but at prices like these, Booking's shares are the ones to buy.

news.Title: AWS CEO Matt Garman Says AI Inference Isn’t ‘Even 1%’ of What It Will Become. AMZN Stock Is 1 of 3 Stocks to Buy.
news.Content:
In a recent interview, Amazon (AMZN) Web Services CEO Matt Garman said that inference, the computing used to run AI models, is less than 1% of what it will eventually become. "I don't think it's even 1%," he said. Garman stated that every time inference prices have dropped by half, usage has jumped about tenfold. So instead of price cuts hurting AWS' revenue, they're doing the opposite. Cheaper AI makes companies use it for many things, so the overall market keeps growing.

How Amazon, AMD, and Broadcom Win From Inference

Amazon: Inference is a massive part of Amazon. CEO Andy Jassy said inference already makes up well over half of AWS' AI revenue, and that business is booming. AWS is already at a $184 billion run rate, up 39.3%. I laid out the math recently, and at that pace, it would put the business close to the trillion-dollar mark Jassy is targeting within about five years. The AWS backlog has now reached a whopping $578 billion. The company's Trainium chips handle most of the inference traffic on its Bedrock AI service. Garman said that they can save customers 20% to 30% on inference costs, and they're sold out through the end of next year. This shows how strong the demand is.

CEO Lip-Bu Tan's 150,000-Share Purchase Wasn't Enough to Stop the Slide in Intel Stock

AMD: Some of AMD's (AMD) biggest customers mainly use its chips for inference. OpenAI and Meta (META) each committed to 6 gigawatts of AMD chips, while Anthropic (ANT) agreed to deploy up to 2 gigawatts. On AMD's Q1 call, CEO Lisa Su said that while its GPU deals cover both training and inference, "the largest deployments are for inference." Its MI450 chip has about 50% more memory than Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin. More memory lets one chip hold a large AI model on its own, instead of splitting it across several chips. This makes answering requests faster and cheaper. AMD also benefits through CPUs. AI agents run on inference, and while GPUs run the models, CPUs handle the surrounding work. As I covered when Lisa Su said the real CPU demand wave hasn't started, that's already pushing data centers toward one CPU for every GPU, up from one for every two to four. And AMD earns close to half of all server CPU revenue.

Story Continues

Broadcom: Broadcom (AVGO) designs custom AI chips with the biggest AI companies, including Google's (GOOG) (GOOGL) TPUs, OpenAI's Jalapeno, Meta's (META) MTIA, and chips for Anthropic. These custom chips are built for one specific job, and that makes them a great fit for inference, since it's the same task repeated millions of times. A chip built just for that can answer each request more cheaply than a general-purpose GPU. CEO Hock Tan said OpenAI's first custom chip, Jalapeno, outperforms Nvidia's Grace Blackwell GPU on inference. Meta's custom chip is also built for inference at scale, and Broadcom is expected to start shipping it in the fiscal fourth quarter.

AMD Has Run Furthest, Broadcom Has Lagged

All three stocks have hit their all-time highs this year, but they've moved very differently since. AMD has been the clear winner, surging about 162% in 2026, far ahead of the S&P 500's ($SPX) roughly 11% gain. Strong demand for its server chips from AI agents and big deals with Meta and OpenAI pushed it to a record in October. Since then, it has dropped about 15% after a series of chip selloffs. AMZN stock is up about 16% this year and sits just 7% below its high, helped by AWS posting its fastest growth in years. AVGO stock has been the weakest of the three, up less than 2% this year and 29% below its peak. The stock slid after its June earnings, and worries about AI spending, along with the recent chip selloff, added to the pressure. So if Garman is right about inference, Broadcom might be the cheapest way to get in right now.

Broadcom Looks Like the Best Value of the Three

Amazon's forward price-to-earnings (P/E) of 27.80x looks far below its 5-year average of 158.13x, but that average is inflated by years when it barely made a profit. Its forward price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 3.48x sits about 21% above average. EPS is expected to dip in 2027 after this year's boost from Anthropic gains, but the P/E still falls to about 15x by 2029.

AMD is the most expensive of the three. Its forward P/E of 62.89x is about 56% above its 5-year average, and its P/S ratio of 15.97x is about 81% above. The EPS helps explain that premium. Analysts expect earnings to grow 94% this fiscal year and more than double next year despite being compared to a really high base. That brings the P/E down to about 29x in 2027.

Broadcom looks like the best value. Its forward P/E of 27.39x is right in line with its 5-year average, and its forward P/S of 14.39x is just 9% above its average. The modest premium looks attractive next to its EPS trajectory. Analysts expect earnings to grow over 55% in each of the next three fiscal years. That brings its P/E down to about 10.5x by fiscal 2028. With strong growth and not much of a premium, I think Broadcom stands out among the three.

As per Wall Street analysts, all three of these stocks hold a "Strong Buy" rating. AMZN stock's mean price target of $328.33 indicates 23% upside, which is smaller than it is for the other two, since AMZN sits much closer to its 52-week high than AMD or AVGO.

news.Title: Amazon and Microsoft Lead the Cloud Market. One of Them Has Far Greater Upside.
news.Content:
Following the midterm elections and sweeping victories by candidates opposed to artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, there has been a lot of debate about which AI companies are best positioned in this new political climate.

However, the general consensus seems to be that leading cloud computing companies with strong businesses, like Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), are well positioned to benefit. Of these two, I think Amazon has a lot more upside. Here's why.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Cloud leaders

Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft's Azure are the two largest cloud providers. With the rise of AI, both companies have seen their cloud computing businesses take off.

Microsoft has recorded 13 straight quarters of 30% or more Azure growth, with a 48% increase last quarter to $33.2 billion. AWS has seen its growth accelerate to its fastest level in nearly five years, climbing 39% to $46 billion last quarter.

Microsoft's cloud business continues to be bolstered by its relationship with OpenAI. The company has priority access to OpenAI's models and products through 2032, and it owns a 27% stake in the maker of large language models. Microsoft also has huge commitments from OpenAI, which is a big reason for its huge $677 billion backlog.

Amazon also has a huge backlog, which more than doubled last quarter to $578 billion. The company has a close relationship with and a large stake in Anthropic, which has committed to spending over $100 billion with AWS. It also has a partnership with OpenAI around agentic AI. Amazon offers access to various third-party AI models through its Bedrock solution, which has helped drive growth.

What sets Amazon apart from Microsoft, though, is its custom chip business. Earlier this year, Amazon said its custom chips business -- which included its Trainium AI accelerator and Graviton custom ARM Holdings -based central processing unit (CPU) -- was a $20 billion run-rate business, or roughly $50 billion when including internal use.

Last quarter, it said its chip business more than doubled and that chip commitments have soared 20-fold. Demand is so high for its chips that it plans to start selling them to external data centers late next year. Amazon's custom chip business is both a revenue driver and a cost saving, helping it reduce inference costs and giving it better returns than with graphics processing units (GPUs).

Story Continues

Microsoft has developed its own custom chips, called Maia, and has its own ARM-based CPUs, but it's still very early, and it is nowhere near the scale of Amazon's chip business. As Amazon continues to growth this business and become less reliant on GPUs, I'd expect its two- to three-year AI infrastructure investment payback to move lower over time, giving it the edge over Microsoft.

Non-cloud businesses

Both Amazon and Microsoft also have strong non-cloud businesses. Microsoft is the leader in enterprise productivity software, and the company is seeing strong growth from a combination of more users deploying its AI Copilot assistants and a shift toward a hybrid model that includes AI usage. Last quarter, it saw an impressive eightfold increase in Copilot users to 50,000 seats.

Amazon is the leader in e-commerce. Any potential future reductions or elimination of tariffs should be great for this business. However, what it most impressive is how much operating leverage Amazon has been able to achieve through its use of robotics, automation, and AI. This is helping segment profitability grow much more quickly than revenue growth.

Amazon is the clear winner

While Microsoft's stock has upside from here, I think Amazon is the clear winner. Its AWS business is starting to see growth accelerate, and its custom chip business gives it a clear edge. Meanwhile, the shift in the political landscape could become a big catalyst if tariffs eventually go away or get reduced.

With both stocks trading at similar valuations, I prefer Amazon between the two and would be a buyer of the stock.

news.Title: Billionaire venture capitalist Vinod Khosla says judge AI by usage, not stock prices
news.Content: Wall Street wants to know whether AI is a bubble. Most of the worry is about who's paying for it. The companies leading the build-out are spending faster than their businesses bring in cash. Combined free cash flow for Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), Meta ( META ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Oracle ( ORCL ) fell to about minus $31 billion in the third quarter, according to Goldman Sachs. That's down from positive $37 billion to $62 billion a quarter through 2025. All that spending is a bet that people will use AI. Vinod Khosla, the billionaire Sun Microsystems co-founder and early OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) backer, says usage is the number to watch, not the stock market's mood swings. "It's not prices, it's actual usage," he said Tuesday on Yahoo Finance's Deirdre Bosa Live . He measures it in tokens — the chunks of text AI models process. By that measure, the boom is real. Much of Big Tech's cash goes into computing power that AI labs rent to run their chatbots, and those labs' sales are taking off. OpenAI's quarterly revenue jumped nearly 50% to $10 billion . Khosla has history on his side. "When you look at internet traffic, you can't tell where the bubble was," he said. The share of Americans online kept climbing through the dot-com crash, from about 43% in 2000 to 59% in 2002, even as the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) lost 78%. The builders paid for the internet, and their customers cashed in Usage was never the problem. Overbuilding was. Telecoms spent more than $500 billion laying fiber, and with 85% of it sitting unused, the cost of bandwidth fell 90%, according to research by Kai Wu, founder of Sparkline Capital. Corning ( GLW ), which made the glass, fell 99% from 2000 to 2002 and didn't top its dot-com high until February, a month after it signed a deal worth up to $6 billion to supply fiber for Meta's AI data centers. The AI rush then more than doubled the stock by late June. The stock has since given back more than half, closing Tuesday near its 2000 peak. Cheap bandwidth was a gift to whoever came next. Netflix and Meta "came around and started using it," Wu said on Yahoo Finance's Stocks in Translation podcast. Alphabet, Meta, and Netflix ( NFLX ), none of which was public when the Nasdaq peaked, have added more than $5 trillion in market value since their first trades. Cisco ( CSCO ) is worth about $174 billion less than at its 2000 peak, per Yahoo Finance calculations. The roles have since flipped. "Instead of Global Crossing, we now have Google," Wu said. What AI's Netflix might look like Story Continues The bandwidth pattern is already showing up in AI. OpenAI cut its Luna model's price 80% after launch, and "we saw use go up almost 10x," CFO Sarah Friar said on the same show. If history rhymes, the winners will treat AI as a cheap ingredient. Wu's research finds early AI adopters are "more evenly spread across sectors" than in infrastructure stocks. "All of medicine is a massive application area," Khosla said. Unlike fiber, AI chips are still scarce. "There is going to be a silicon shortage for a couple of years," Khosla said. But chips wear out over years, not decades, Wu noted, giving builders less time to earn back what they spend. John Chambers, who ran Cisco through the dot-com boom and bust, told Yahoo Finance's Sozzi Unleashed this month that he expects "major train wrecks" this time too, because "rising tide does not raise all boats."
