news.Title: AI Sell-Off: Buy ANET, TSM & MU to Make Up for NVIDIA Losses
news.Content:
The artificial intelligence (AI) trade is facing one of its toughest tests yet. After driving Wall Street's rally for much of 2026, technology and semiconductor stocks have come under intense selling pressure as investors question lofty valuations, the sustainability of hyperscaler capital expenditures and the time required to monetize massive AI investments. Rising inflation, higher Treasury yields and uncertainty surrounding data-center construction have added to the pressure.

The weakness is also evident in AI-focused ETFs. Over the past 30 days, the Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) has declined 11.4%, while the iShares Future AI & Tech ETF (ARTY) has plunged 17.1%, entering correction territory. ARTY's steeper decline indicates the extent of selling pressure across companies positioned to benefit from future AI adoption.

The Nov. 5 sell-off was particularly severe. The iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX plunged 12.1%. The pressure escalated on Nov. 8 following a corporate governance controversy involving NVIDIA NVDA. NVIDIA shares fell 4.27% on Nov. 9 as concerns over leadership continuity, board oversight and potential national-security implications weighed on investor sentiment. The sell-off deepened on Nov. 10, with NVIDIA losing another 6.5% and the Nasdaq Composite declining 1%. Broader concerns over AI infrastructure spending, complications surrounding a major Ohio data-center project and hotter-than-expected inflation further undermined technology stocks.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

However, does this correction signal the end of the AI investment opportunity, or is it creating an attractive entry point in fundamentally strong companies? Let's find out.

Here, we have picked three AI stocks — Arista Networks ANET, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM or TSMC and Micron Technology MU — all carrying favorable Zacks Rank and having strong fundamentals, making them attractive alternatives to NVIDIA for investors seeking AI exposure beyond the market leader amid the current volatility.

Why Quality AI Stocks Beyond NVIDIA Are Attractive Now

Despite the correction, long-term AI infrastructure demand remains strong. According to IDC's Nov. 6 report, global AI infrastructure spending reached $121.4 billion in the second quarter, up 53.3% year over year. IDC raised its 2026 spending forecast to $521 billion from $497 billion previously and expects the market to reach $1.17 trillion by 2029.

Notably, non-accelerated, CPU-based infrastructure spending grew 61.1%, outpacing the 52.2% growth in accelerated systems, highlighting expanding investment opportunities beyond GPU suppliers.

Story Continues

Meanwhile, J.P. Morgan projected AI capital expenditure of approximately $900 billion in 2026, although financing, electricity availability and semiconductor supply remain constraints.

This spending creates opportunities beyond NVIDIA across AI networking, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, high-bandwidth memory and computing processors. Investors should focus on companies translating AI demand into measurable revenue growth and stronger earnings rather than speculative AI exposure.

3 Quality AI Stocks to Consider

Arista : It is benefiting from increasing demand for high-speed Ethernet networking in AI data centers. Its third-quarter 2026 revenues surged 58.5% year over year, while non-GAAP EPS increased to $1.20 from 77 cents a year earlier. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 49.1%. Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $3.9-$4 billion. ANET's networking exposure makes it an attractive means to participate in AI infrastructure expansion beyond chip manufacturing.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings indicates growth of 45.6% on current-year sales growth of 47.9%. Over the past seven days, 2026 earnings estimates for ANET have been revised upward by 4.3% to $4.36 per share. The stock sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Taiwan Semiconductor : TSMC's advanced manufacturing capabilities make it indispensable to the AI semiconductor ecosystem. Its October 2026 revenues jumped 59.7% year over year. Its January-October 2026 revenues increased 43.3% to NT$4.49 trillion. TSMC offers exposure to AI demand across multiple chip designers, rather than relying on a single GPU manufacturer.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings suggests 63.9% growth, while sales are expected to increase 40.9%. Over the past seven days, 2026 earnings estimates for TSM have been revised upward by 2.3% to $17.46 per share. The stock sports a Zacks Rank #1.

Micron : The AI expansion is increasing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced DRAM, positioning Micron favorably. The company reported strong fiscal fourth quarter 2026 revenues of $54.23 billion, compared with $11.32 billion a year earlier. Micron has also commenced high-volume shipments of HBM4.

The consensus estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings suggests growth of 133.1%. Sales are expected to surge 110%. Over the past 60 days, fiscal 2027 earnings estimates for MU have been revised upward by 11.5% to $176.04 per share. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

news.Title: The Only 3 Tech Stocks I'd Buy With $5,000 and Never Sell
news.Content:
There are only three tech stocks I'd buy with $5,000 and never sell, and you've heard of all of them. Each company has a gargantuan customer base that would find switching to a competitor expensive, painful, or both.

Each also has a long record of investing in new technology and returning cash to shareholders when those bets pay off.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

1. Apple

Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) has a wide economic moat that starts with hardware people love and ends with subscription bills they keep paying indefinitely. As of January, its installed base had topped 2.5 billion active devices, and each one of those devices is an opportunity for the company to up-sell, cross-sell, and market new services.

Each device is a storefront for apps, subscriptions, and payments that generate recurring revenue without the company incurring large expenses at the same time. Because Apple takes a cut of App Store sales and retains its own subscription revenue, its services segment had a 76.2% gross margin in its fiscal 2026, which ended Sept. 26.

Upgrade cycles and accessory sales also enable Apple to grow by making incremental improvements to the products that it already knows how to sell on a recurring basis. With its fiscal 2026 net income of $132.2 billion, and a 10-year compound annual growth rate of 11.2% for those earnings, I have no problem holding Apple stock for a very long time.

2. Microsoft

While Apple rules consumer hardware, Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) is a powerhouse in the enterprise software and cloud infrastructure realms. Its Azure cloud platform grew revenue 48% year over year in its fiscal 2027 first quarter, which ended Sept. 30.

Even more compelling is Microsoft's commercial remaining performance obligation, meaning contracted revenue not yet recognized, which jumped 73% to $677 billion. Few other cloud computing stocks can point to that much contracted demand waiting in the wings.

Microsoft's "agents and infrastructure" segment, which is home to both Azure and Microsoft 365, brought in $76.8 billion during the quarter, up 25%. A company running its email, documents, log-ins, and cloud computing on Microsoft would face a long and expensive migration if it wanted to leave its ecosystem. And while that stickiness could prove frustrating to a customer that's trying to switch providers, for investors, it's one more reason to expect the company will be able to retain its competitive position.

Story Continues

3. Nvidia

Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) sells crucial hardware to the largest cloud infrastructure builders, including Microsoft.

Its data center sales were $89 billion in its fiscal 2027 second quarter, or 92.5% of its total revenue. Management also returned about $26 billion to shareholders via stock repurchases in the same quarter, which is hard to beat in terms of the absolute size of the buyback.

Aside from the huge scale of its chip manufacturing capabilities, another part of the business' economic moat is its software, with more than 7.5 million developers using its CUDA platform. In order to run CUDA-based AI code on a rival's chips, developers have to rewrite much of it, which means that in practice, developers and their employers are largely locked into Nvidia's hardware.

The main risks for the company are the high levels of concentration among both its suppliers and customers. Just five direct customers make up the majority of Nvidia's accounts receivable balance, and it relies on a mix of hardware suppliers and distributors. Still, I'd buy the stock with $5,000 today anyway, because that situation is not new for the company, and the other stakeholders involved -- both buyers and suppliers -- are all highly reliant on it for their own survival.

news.Title: Prediction: 2 Stocks That Will Be Worth More Than Amazon 5 Years From Now
news.Content:
Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) is worth about $2.9 trillion as of this writing. That is a hard number to pass, and Amazon is not standing still. It is pouring money into data centers, custom chips, and robotics at a pace few companies can match.

That spending has to go somewhere, though. Every dollar Amazon spends on AI hardware flows to a supplier, and two of those suppliers sit in a position Amazon can't replicate. They collect from Amazon, and from every one of Amazon's rivals, at the same time. Those suppliers are Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO), and I think both will pass Amazon in market value by 2031. Here's why.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Taiwan Semiconductor builds the chips everyone else designs

Taiwan Semiconductor, or TSMC, is a foundry. It doesn't design chips. It manufactures them for companies that do, which means it gets paid whether Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) wins, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) wins, or Amazon's in-house Trainium chip wins. Amazon designs Trainium to lower its reliance on Nvidia, and then it sends that design to TSMC to be built . The customer and the competitor end up at the same factory door.

TSMC is worth around $1.8 trillion today, so the gap between it and Amazon is the smaller of the two. What closes it, to me, is the Arizona project. TSMC has raised its planned U.S. investment from $12 billion in 2020 to $265 billion, and in July it said it intends to add more fabs for 2-nanometer and smaller chips plus more advanced packaging plants. The second Arizona fab is aiming for volume production in the second half of 2027, and the third is slated for the company's N2 and A16 processes before the decade ends.

Why does that matter beyond the headline? Advanced packaging, the step where chips get stacked and connected, is the bottleneck in AI hardware right now. Owning that step on U.S. soil, next to the customers who need it, turns TSMC from an overseas supplier into local infrastructure.

Broadcom is the stock that has to grow the most

Broadcom sits at around $1.56 trillion, which means it needs to gain about 70% on Amazon over five years, before accounting for Amazon's own growth. That is the harder call, and it is the one I feel better about.

Broadcom builds custom AI accelerators, which it calls XPUs, for the companies that want an alternative to buying Nvidia chips off the shelf. On Oct. 26, Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Blackstone (NYSE: BX), Citi (NYSE: C), and Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) announced a $63 billion financing structure to buy Broadcom accelerators and networking gear and lease them to Anthropic, with deliveries starting in 2027. Four of the largest financial firms in the world built a vehicle to finance one customer's purchases of one chipmaker's hardware. Broadcom is backing part of the deal with residual value support, which tells you how confident it is that the gear holds its worth.

Story Continues

That same month, Broadcom rolled out new networking products at the OCP Global Summit. Networking is the quieter half of its story. When thousands of accelerators run as one system, the switches connecting them matter as much as the chips, and Broadcom is one of a few companies that sells both.

What investors should take from this

Passing Amazon is not the point of owning either stock. The point is understanding where AI money goes once it leaves the companies building data centers. Amazon has to win its own race. TSMC and Broadcom get paid no matter who wins, as long as the race keeps running. That said, the AI race has hit some turbulence, especially in the last couple of months.

Look at Nvidia this week for proof. On Thursday last week, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had its worst day since April 2025, the Nasdaq Composite closed in correction territory, and Nvidia shed more than 9% on fears that a new Congress could slow the data center build-out.

Then, on Sunday, Nvidia's board announced an independent review into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The stock opened down about 8% on Monday, erasing about $350 billion in value before clawing some of it back. None of that had anything to do with chip demand. It was politics one day, and a governance headline the next. The most valuable company in the world still moved like a small-cap.

That is what a market finding its footing looks like. The AI trade is real, but it is not yet steady, and anyone buying TSMC or Broadcom on this thesis should expect more weeks like this one.

news.Title: History Says This Is What Will Happen to Sandisk Stock After Its 8-for-1 Split
news.Content:
Since separating from Western Digital in February 2025, Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) has benefited from soaring demand for data storage, particularly from artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

However, the company's latest announcement has introduced an interesting twist. On Oct. 29, Sandisk announced an 8-for-1 stock split , scheduled to take effect after the market closes on Nov. 19.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Normally, stock splits generate excitement among investors. But Sandisk stock has actually plunged since the announcement. Between Oct. 29 and Nov. 9, Sandisk fell from $1,330 to $886, a 33% decline.

Let's examine how stock splits work, what happened with other semiconductor companies that split their stock in recent years, and whether Sandisk is worth buying before its upcoming split.

Why Sandisk is splitting its stock

A stock split increases the number of outstanding shares while proportionately reducing their price. For example, an investor holding one Sandisk share worth $800 before the split would subsequently own eight shares worth approximately $100 apiece post-split. The investment would still be worth $800.

As investors can see, stock splits don't create shareholder value, change a company's earnings, or alter its market capitalization. So, why do companies pursue them?

One reason is accessibility. Lower share prices in terms of absolute dollars can make stocks more appealing to retail investors who prefer purchasing whole shares rather than fractional shares. That's precisely what Sandisk wants to accomplish. Management explained that its stock price has appreciated substantially since the Western Digital spinoff, making a split attractive for a broader base of investors and employees participating in the company's stock purchase program.

The announcement accompanied impressive financial results. During its fiscal first quarter of 2027, Sandisk generated $11 billion in revenue, increasing 378% year over year and 23% sequentially. Adjusted earnings per share reached $49.51 per share compared with just $1.22 during the same period last year.

These results reflect robust demand for NAND flash memory, particularly as data centers require more storage capacity. However, Sandisk's post-earnings sell-off suggests investors are becoming more concerned about valuation and the sustainability of memory pricing.

Story Continues

Image source: The Motley Fool.

What Nvidia and Broadcom reveal about semiconductor stock splits

In June 2024, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) completed a 10-for-1 split after its shares surged alongside demand for its GPUs. Nvidia subsequently experienced prolonged volatility, including a sharp pullback during the summer of 2024. Nevertheless, its shares eventually reached higher levels as revenue and earnings continued expanding.

Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) followed with its own 10-for-1 split in July 2024. Similar to Nvidia, Broadcom benefited from growing AI infrastructure spending, particularly demand for custom accelerators and networking technology. Its stock also experienced fleeting fluctuations after the split before benefiting from continued acceleration in its AI semiconductor business.

NVDA data by YCharts

What will happen to Sandisk stock after the split?

I wouldn't be surprised to see Sandisk experience a short-term rebound once its shares begin trading at a lower nominal price. Using the Nov. 9 closing price of $886, the theoretical post-split share price would be around $111, assuming no additional price movement. That's considerably more accessible than a stock trading near $900.

The lower price could attract more investors who previously considered Sandisk too expensive to purchase in whole-share increments. However, increased interest from retail investors doesn't necessarily translate into sustainable stock price appreciation.

Here's where I'd exercise caution: Sandisk's recent financial results have been historic, but the memory industry is also cyclical. Demand for data center storage is growing rapidly, while supply constraints are contributing to higher average selling prices. Those conditions support Sandisk's margins and profitability... for now.

Investors need to understand the difference between a stock becoming cheaper per share and becoming cheaper based on valuation. An 8-for-1 split doesn't reduce Sandisk's price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio. If investors bid up shares after the split, they could ironically end up paying an even higher valuation for a business whose profits are sensitive to memory pricing cycles.

Sandisk could enjoy a brief rally around the time of its split, especially after the recent sell-off. However, given what happened with Nvidia and Broadcom, history suggests the momentum will not be sustainable without continued earnings growth.

Nvidia and Broadcom ultimately rewarded shareholders because their underlying businesses grew, not because dividing their shares magically created value. Sandisk could follow a similar path if demand for its NAND flash storage remains strong. For now, though, I think patience is the more prudent strategy.

news.Title: What Valens Semiconductor (VLN) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Valens Semiconductor, Ltd.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Q3 results beat guidance: Revenue rose 27% year over year to $21.9 million, led by automotive sales climbing to $7.9 million. The GAAP net loss narrowed to $5.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss of $2.7 million was better than forecast.

Valens is broadening its growth strategy: It plans to embed connectivity technology in more audio-video equipment and sell finished products such as dongles and active cables. Its collaboration with onsemi aims to make lower-cost automotive cameras, with production from four A-PHY design wins expected to start in 2027.

2026 outlook reaffirmed: Valens expects revenue of $78 million to $81 million, with results trending toward the upper end, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $12.9 million to $14.9 million. It ended the quarter with $74.7 million in cash and no debt.

Be Cautious of Valens Semiconductor Analyst Estimates

Valens Semiconductor (NYSE:VLN) reported third-quarter revenue above its guidance as automotive sales rose sharply, and outlined a strategy to expand beyond premium connectivity applications into higher-volume audio-video and automotive markets.

Revenue rose to $21.9 million from $17.3 million a year earlier, exceeding the company's forecast of $21.3 million to $21.7 million. The GAAP net loss narrowed to $5.5 million, or $0.05 per share, from $7.3 million, or $0.07 per share, in the prior-year quarter.

→ Wall Street May Be Making a Big Mistake With monday.com Stock

Valens Semiconductor Stock is an Under the Radar Chip Play

Chief Executive Officer Yoram Salinger said the company plans to embed its connectivity technology in more types of video conferencing equipment and sell finished connectivity products, rather than relying solely on chipset sales. In automotive, Valens is working with onsemi on a lower-cost camera solution using the MIPI A-PHY connectivity standard.

Automotive Growth Drives Revenue Increase

Automotive revenue reached $7.9 million, up from $4.1 million a year earlier and $5 million in the second quarter. The cross-industry business, which includes audio-video, contributed $14 million, compared with $13.2 million a year earlier.

→ Atlassian Tanks After Huge Run as Guidance Disappoints, But Strength Remains

Chief Financial Officer Karine Pinto-Flomenboim said Valens technology is used across Mercedes-Benz passenger vehicle models, making its automotive revenue dependent on demand for those vehicles. She said the company expects revenue at the recent level to continue, subject to Mercedes-Benz demand, while noting seasonal variation between quarters.

Story Continues

GAAP gross margin was 62.2%, above the company's 60% to 62% guidance range but below 63% a year earlier. Automotive gross margin increased to 53.9% from 41.5% in the second quarter, primarily because of lower testing facility expenses and a change in product mix. Cross-industry gross margin fell to 66.8% from 69.2% sequentially, which Pinto-Flomenboim attributed mainly to product mix.

→ America's Rare Earth Clock Is Running Out, But the Bottleneck Isn't Where You Think

Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $2.7 million, better than the company's forecast for a loss of $3.4 million to $2.8 million. The loss improved from $4.3 million a year earlier, mainly because of higher revenue, partly offset by chip tape-out costs.

Expansion Beyond Premium Audio-Video Products

Salinger said Valens' new VS6310 chipset is designed for lower bandwidth, shorter distances and lower power consumption than its premium solutions. The company intends to work with equipment manufacturers to embed the technology in products such as cameras, video bars and touch controllers.

Valens also plans to sell system-level products, including dongles, extender boxes, active cables and adapters, to distributors and, in some cases, installers and integrators. Salinger said the company is drawing on capabilities acquired through its 2024 purchase of Acroname, including its BrainStem technology and product engineering expertise.

Asked about the potential effect on margins, Salinger said he did not expect the two audio-video growth initiatives to affect gross margin in 2027. He added that Valens believes it can maintain margins on products such as active cables and dongles, with any overall impact unlikely to be substantial.

Salinger also pointed to recent customer product launches, including Jabra's Reach, which uses Valens' HDBaseT technology to connect a laptop to meeting-room equipment through a single USB-C cable.

Onsemi Collaboration Targets Mainstream Cameras

Valens and onsemi are developing a solution that integrates A-PHY connectivity into a three-megapixel image sensor, eliminating the need for a separate serializer chip. Salinger said the approach is intended to reduce component count, simplify camera designs and lower costs for applications such as surround view, side and rear driver-assistance systems, and electronic mirrors.

The resulting chip will be an onsemi product manufactured using onsemi's facilities and marketed by both companies, Salinger said. He described the collaboration as a way to offer automakers a second source for A-PHY technology and help address barriers to broader adoption.

Valens has secured four A-PHY design wins, with production expected to begin in 2027, according to Salinger. He said the company's existing VA7000 technology addresses higher-end applications, including eight-megapixel front-facing driver-assistance cameras.

Full-Year Outlook Reaffirmed

Valens reaffirmed its 2026 revenue forecast of $78 million to $81 million and said it expects results toward the upper end of that range. It forecast a full-year adjusted EBITDA loss of $12.9 million to $14.9 million.

The company ended the quarter with $74.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term bank deposits, down from $83.4 million at the end of June, and no debt. Pinto-Flomenboim said the decline primarily reflected the timing of collections on revenue recognized toward the end of the quarter.

She also said Valens expects more significant tape-out costs after completing development of its VC500 product, with those costs to be included in next year's guidance. The CFO cautioned that future supply-management expenses are difficult to forecast and could affect segment margins.

About Valens Semiconductor (NYSE:VLN)

Valens Semiconductor Ltd. is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Hod Hasharon, Israel. Founded in 2006, the company develops high-speed connectivity solutions for the audio-video and automotive markets, with an emphasis on transmitting data reliably over longer distances and through challenging environments. Valens is best known for its HDBaseT technology, which enables the distribution of high-definition video, audio, power and control signals over standard cabling. Its products serve professional audio-video applications such as conference rooms, classrooms, digital signage and residential entertainment systems.

news.Title: Here’s Why Truist and Evercore Slashed Their Price Targets on Microchip (MCHP)
news.Content:
We just published a list of the Analysts Just Slashed Their Price Targets on These 10 Stocks and Microchip Technology (NASDAQ:MCHP) ranked 7th on this list.

Wall Street had its worst day in 19 months last Thursday, with chip stocks leading the selloff. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315.00, its biggest one-day drop since the April 2025 tariff announcement. The S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, erasing about $3 trillion in market value and marking its worst day since that same tariff crash. The Dow lost 3.44%.

The Nasdaq is now in a correction, more than 10% below the record close it set last month. Volume was heavy: 26.9 billion shares changed hands, against a 20-session average of 17.7 billion.

Photo by Arturo Añez on Unsplash

Fear of Tighter AI Rules Hit Chip Stocks

The trigger was politics. Investors worried about tighter AI regulation after Democrats won control of Congress, including in states where opposition to new data centers has been growing. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index fell more than 12% in one session, its worst day since March 2020. Candidates in both parties had campaigned against AI data centers, Yahoo Finance 's Jared Blikre reported.

Melissa Brown, global head of investment decision research at SimCorp, said some newly elected members of Congress and governors want to slow the pace of AI infrastructure development, and that any slowdown would raise concerns. We covered the group's earlier pullback in our list of oversold AI stocks that Wall Street analysts saw 50%+ upside in , published before the selloff.

A Partial Rebound, With Rate Hikes Still in View

Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, called Thursday "the capitulation phase for the data center capex beneficiary stocks" and said the size of the moves looked excessive. Chip stocks did bounce on Friday: the semiconductor index rose 4.2% and the Nasdaq gained 1.1% to 24,579.43, and the S&P 500 rose 0.32% to 7,376.86, while the Dow slipped 0.46% to 51,285.73. But the Nasdaq still posted its fourth straight weekly decline, down 3.4% for the week, while the S&P 500 fell 2.7%, its worst week since June, and the Dow fell 0.9%.

Readers weighing how far the technology sector has fallen can also look at our roundup of technology stocks trading near 52-week lows that analysts favor . Through Thursday's close, the S&P 500 was still up 7.4% for 2026 and the Nasdaq up 4.6%. Friday's jobs report showed employers added 165,000 jobs in October, against 59,000 expected, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%. Traders expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates next month, following a hike in September.

Story Continues

Microchip made it to our list because it has an average upside potential of 45%. Truist maintained a Hold on Microchip Technology on November 6 and cut its price target to $62 from $90. The same day, Evercore ISI analyst Mark Lipacis lowered his target to $75 from $117. The notes point to the same two problems: supply limits and a reset in expectations after the quarter.

Those calls followed the company's latest report. Sales grew 42.2% from a year earlier and beat the company's own guidance, but guidance for the December quarter was $1.573 billion to $1.638 billion, and the stock fell about 10% the next day. CEO Steve Sanghi said AI customers have absorbed foundry and packaging capacity, so lead times on standard parts now run as long as 32 weeks, against a normal four to eight. About $53 million of that quarter's sales came from one-time items, which explains part of the step-down in guidance.

Microchip makes microcontrollers for cars, factory equipment and appliances, and data centers are a minority of its sales. Its Hailo acquisition and edge AI push are covered in our look at why it is buying edge AI on the cheap .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MCHP as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: AXTI's AI Data Center Boom: Can Substrate Demand Sustain Growth?
news.Content:
AXT, Inc. AXTI is seeing accelerating demand for its indium phosphide (InP) substrates as hyperscalers expand AI data centers and deploy increasingly GPU-dense computing systems. These facilities require faster optical links to move growing volumes of data, making InP-based lasers and photodetectors increasingly important.

The transition to 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers is a major catalyst. AXT's InP revenues reached $54.3 million in third-quarter 2026, primarily driven by data center applications. Total revenues surged 162% year over year and 54% sequentially to a record $73.4 million. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 56.1% from 45% in the preceding quarter, benefiting from higher volumes, favorable product mix and increasing InP prices.

Demand extends across geographies. Management believes AXT's materials are deployed at multiple U.S. hyperscalers, while China's growing AI investments have accelerated demand for InP-based lasers. The company's backlog exceeded $500 million, with customers on allocation as demand outstripped available supply. AXT surpassed its 2026 goal of doubling InP capacity and plans further expansion in 2027.

The shift toward higher-value 4-inch wafers, emerging 6-inch capabilities and future co-packaged optics could add to this momentum. Although scaling production remains critical, surging optical connectivity requirements and a substantial backlog suggest AI data center expansion can sustain AXT's substrate-driven revenue growth.

Rivals Benefiting From the Trend

Coherent COHR is benefiting from growing demand for InP-based lasers, photodiodes and 1.6T optical transceivers. Coherent reported Datacenter & Communications revenues of $1.95 billion in first-quarter fiscal 2027, up 79% year over year. With advanced 6-inch InP fabrication capabilities, Coherent is expanding its optical manufacturing footprint. However, its substrate supply agreement with AXT also makes it an important customer rather than solely a competitor.

Lumentum LITE is capitalizing on AI data center investments through its InP lasers, optical circuit switches and cloud networking solutions. Lumentum reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $1.26 billion, up 136.5% year over year, driven by strong optical infrastructure demand. Lumentum is also expanding domestic InP manufacturing capacity while maintaining a long-term substrate supply agreement with AXT, reinforcing their complementary positions in the optical connectivity ecosystem.

news.Title: Amazon Wants to Put an Autonomous Flying Robot in Your Living Room
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ) shares gained approximately 1.5% Tuesday after its Ring division unveiled AI-powered security robots capable of patrolling homes and businesses autonomously. The launch expands Amazon's ambitions beyond traditional security cameras into robotics, potentially opening new hardware and subscription revenue opportunities as competition intensifies across the smart-home market. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with AMZN. Is AMZN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Amazon's Ring business sells video doorbells, security cameras, alarms and connected home-monitoring services. Its products generate hardware sales and recurring subscription revenue, while integrating customers into Amazon's broader technology ecosystem. On November 10, Ring introduced Ring Robotics, featuring two products: the Ring Drone Cam for residential customers and Ring Rover Cam for businesses. The Drone Cam, priced at $249.99, flies preset indoor routes and can automatically investigate disturbances when connected Ring alarms or sensors activate. Its approximately eight-minute flight time limits continuous monitoring, but automated docking and recharging allow repeated patrols. The Rover Cam, starting at $999.99, uses wheels to navigate commercial spaces and includes a siren, warning lights and two-way communication. Both devices use Ring's AI Pilot technology, combining cameras, sensors and cloud processing to navigate obstacles. Ring founder Jamie Siminoff described the initiative as the beginning of a future where proactive, autonomous protection is something every home and every business can have. The company already benefits from substantial market penetration. According to SmartHome.org, approximately 61% of U.S. households have security cameras, while Ring accounts for 43% of primary security systems identified by surveyed users. However, Amazon has not disclosed expected sales volumes or revenue contributions from the products. Investors Takeaway The Rover Cam begins shipping December 16, followed by the Drone Cam on January 27, subject to regulatory clearance. Investors should monitor initial sales, customer reviews, subscription adoption and whether robotics encourages existing Ring customers to purchase additional products. Privacy concerns, device reliability and regulatory requirements could complicate broader adoption. Competition from Alphabet's Google Nest and other security providers also remains significant. For Amazon shareholders, the opportunity is less about immediate earnings growth and more about building another recurring-revenue business. Strong customer adoption could strengthen Ring's ecosystem, while disappointing demand would limit the financial significance of its robotics expansion. news.Title: Amkor's Communications Business Weakens: Can a Recovery Take Hold?
news.Content:
Amkor Technology AMKR is grappling with a sharp contraction in its Communications business, as smartphone-related production disruptions and material constraints weigh on sales. Communications revenues declined 28% year over year and 8% sequentially in third-quarter 2026. The end market accounted for 37% of total revenues, down from 51% a year earlier, limiting consolidated revenue growth to just 0.2%.

The weakness primarily reflects the strategic migration of system-in-package (SiP) programs from Korea to Vietnam and associated preproduction activities. Memory supply constraints, higher component costs and changes in smartphone build patterns have added pressure. Management expects these headwinds to persist into the fourth quarter, with Communications revenues projected to decline a high-single-digit percentage sequentially. Both iOS- and Android-related business is expected to weaken, while lower-tier Android devices face greater difficulty absorbing higher memory prices.

Nevertheless, the transfer could improve Amkor's longer-term operating model. Management sees a meaningful SiP pipeline and expects business to rebound as Vietnamese production scales. The move also frees Korean cleanroom capacity for higher-value advanced packaging. Meanwhile, Computing and Automotive and Industrial revenues each rose 37% year over year in the third quarter, cushioning the Communications decline and supporting gross-margin expansion to 18.3% from 14.3% a year earlier.

A Communications recovery therefore appears possible, but not imminent. Its pace depends on completing the SiP transition, easing supply constraints and stronger smartphone demand; for now, growth elsewhere offers the clearer offset.

AMKR Faces Stiff Competition in Advanced Chip Packaging

GlobalFoundries GFS poses competition to Amkor through advanced packaging solutions for mobile connectivity chips. GlobalFoundries has qualified its SLATE wafer-bonding technology for compact 5G radio-frequency components, potentially improving semiconductor integration and efficiency. Although primarily a foundry rather than a traditional outsourced assembly-and-test provider, GlobalFoundries offers integrated manufacturing and packaging capabilities that could intensify competition for selected communications-related semiconductor programs.

Intel INTC competes with Amkor through advanced packaging technologies, including Foveros 3D stacking and EMIB interconnect solutions. Intel is strengthening its position in heterogeneous integration and chiplet-based architectures, targeting AI and high-performance computing applications. Intel's extensive manufacturing infrastructure and advanced packaging expertise could intensify competition for high-value semiconductor projects, although Amkor maintains a stronger focus on outsourced packaging and smartphone-related SiP services.

news.Title: MP Materials Clears GM Magnet Milestone, Targets Apple as Next Customer
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in MP Materials Corp.? Here are five stocks we like better.

MP Materials qualified its rare earth magnets for General Motors and is ramping production at its Independence facility. CEO Jim Litinsky said Apple is expected to come online as a customer next year; Apple has agreed to buy at least $500 million of magnets.

The company is advancing its planned 10X magnet project under a Department of War agreement, with the Pentagon contracted for all planned output. MP says the deal is binding and it expects bipartisan support.

Litinsky sees robotics and defense as potential sources of future demand, but said widespread humanoid-robot production may be three to five years away. He identified NdPr—not heavy rare earths—as the more significant supply constraint.

America's Rare Earth Clock Is Running Out, But the Bottleneck Isn't Where You Think

MP Materials (NYSE:MP) has qualified rare earth magnets for General Motors and is ramping production, CEO and Chairman Jim Litinsky said at an investor conference, marking a milestone in the company's expansion beyond mining and refining.

Litinsky said the company plans to bring Apple online as a customer next year and is focused on increasing production at its Independence facility and completing its planned 10X magnet manufacturing project with the Department of War. He said MP has more than 300 employees in its magnetics business.

→ Wall Street May Be Making a Big Mistake With monday.com Stock

China Still Dominates Rare Earths—These 3 U.S. Companies Could Benefit

The CEO also outlined potential demand from robotics and defense applications, while cautioning that large-scale humanoid robotics demand could take years to develop.

Domestic supply chain and Pentagon agreement

Litinsky said rare earth magnets are used in products ranging from electric vehicles and consumer electronics to drones and defense systems. He described the current U.S.-China trade situation as an "uneasy détente," saying Chinese export licensing continues to restrict access for some applications.

→ Atlassian Tanks After Huge Run as Guidance Disappoints, But Strength Remains

First Citizens BancShares vs MP Materials: A Tale of 2 Regulation Bets

He said MP was selected for its Department of War agreement because it can conduct mining, refining, metal making and magnet manufacturing within the United States. Litinsky said the Pentagon wanted to expand the company's capabilities tenfold.

Asked whether a Democratic-controlled Congress could affect the agreement, Litinsky said the company has a binding contract and expects continued bipartisan support for critical minerals. He said MP has "almost no concern" about changes to its deal.

Story Continues

→ America's Rare Earth Clock Is Running Out, But the Bottleneck Isn't Where You Think

The Pentagon has contracted for 100% of the planned 10X production, Litinsky said, adding that MP can allocate that output to customers as long as it supplies American industry.

Mining and magnet production

Litinsky said MP's rare earth oxide production run rate is above 50,000 tons and is moving toward 60,000 tons. He said the company's refining operation is running at a substantially normalized level and highlighted planned projects including chlor-alkali production and recycling for Apple.

The CEO said MP has reduced the heavy rare earth content in magnets meeting automotive specifications by approximately 50% to 60% over the past two years. He said the company expects to satisfy many uses, including some robotics and defense applications, without heavy rare earths when 10X comes online.

Instead, Litinsky argued that neodymium-praseodymium, or NdPr, is the more significant supply constraint. He cited MP and Lynas as the principal existing sources of NdPr production outside China, saying much of Lynas' output is committed to Japan.

Robotics demand and expansion plans

Litinsky estimated that a humanoid robot could require roughly three to five kilograms of magnets, although he noted that designs and estimates vary. He said a manufacturer producing 1 million humanoid robots annually could use approximately 40% to 70% of MP's planned 10X capacity.

MP is already receiving requests for quotations related to robotics that exceed planned 10X production, he said. But he added that large-scale demand is unlikely to be a 2026 or 2027 event and could develop over the next three to five years.

Asked about the risk of customers substituting other technologies for rare earth magnets, Litinsky said alternatives exist for electric vehicles but can involve higher material costs or reduced efficiency. He said substitution would be more challenging in robotics, where compact components and torque density are important.

Litinsky said MP expects its magnetics business to become materially larger over time but intends to expand methodically rather than speculate on capacity. He noted that Apple has agreed to purchase a minimum of $500 million of magnets from the Independence facility and is the foundational customer for MP's recycling business.

For now, he said, the company's priorities are to continue ramping Independence and complete 10X. He also said MP could look to acquire other assets if opportunities emerge at attractive prices.

About MP Materials (NYSE:MP)

MP Materials operates the Mountain Pass rare earth mine and processing facility in California. The site is a major North American source of rare earth materials, which are used in products such as electric vehicles, wind turbines, electronics and defense systems. The company mines and processes rare earth ore into concentrate and separated products, including neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr), a key input for high-strength permanent magnets. MP Materials is also developing domestic magnet manufacturing capabilities to extend its business further along the supply chain.

news.Title: Tesla Clears Major Hurdle in European Self-Driving Push
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) has secured approval to introduce its supervised driver-assistance technology in Finland, marking another step toward a broader European rollout. The decision could eventually unlock additional software revenue for the electric vehicle maker, although a crucial European Union regulatory vote remains unresolved.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 7 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Finland's Transport and Communications Agency, Traficom, announced Wednesday that it had recognized provisional approval previously granted by Dutch regulators, allowing Tesla to immediately offer its Assisted Driving system to Finnish customers.

The technology, previously called Full Self-Driving (Supervised), can steer, accelerate and brake automatically, but drivers must remain attentive and responsible for operating their vehicles.

Tesla also made changes to satisfy regulators, including removing self-driving references from the product's name and tightening speed-control settings that previously allowed excessive speeding.

The Netherlands became the first European country to grant provisional approval in April, with Belgium, Estonia and Croatia among the countries subsequently permitting the technology.

Nearly a dozen European countries have now granted provisional authorizations, but Tesla has yet to secure support from the EU's largest member states.

That distinction matters because Europe-wide approval requires backing from a qualified majority of member countries.

Finland's approval is relatively modest commercially, with approximately 8,000 to 9,000 compatible Tesla vehicles operating in the country.

However, the regulatory precedent could prove more valuable than immediate software sales.

A successful European rollout would expand Tesla's opportunity to monetize software subscriptions beyond vehicle purchases, potentially improving its revenue mix and margins.

Investors Takeaway

The next major catalyst is a potential EU regulatory vote in December, although final approval could slip into the winter.

Investors should monitor whether larger European markets support the system and whether additional technical modifications are required.

Adoption rates, subscription pricing and software revenue will determine the financial benefits of a wider rollout.

Finland's harsh winter conditions also present an operational test, particularly when snow and slush obscure vehicle cameras.

Importantly, a rejection at the EU level could invalidate existing national approvals.

For Tesla shareholders, broad regulatory acceptance and sustained customer adoption would be more significant than Finland's limited near-term revenue opportunity.

news.Title: Something happened in October that changes the TSMC stock debate
news.Content:
If you opened your brokerage app on Nov. 5, you probably wanted to close it again. Plenty of investors seemed sure the AI bubble had finally burst, and chip stocks led the losses.

Five days later, the world's largest contract chipmaker posted a month for the record books.

On Nov. 10, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) said October revenue reached about NT$586.89 billion ($17.88 billion), according to CNBC . Sales jumped 59.7% from October 2025, according to TSMC's monthly report .

TSMC has never reported a bigger month, according to its monthly revenue filings .

TSMC released the number with no outlook and no comment. It didn't need to, because October's total changes what investors are arguing about.

The debate is shifting from whether chip demand is cracking to whether politics will let the buildout keep its pace.

Also read: TSMC's $46.7 billion quarter leaves 1 question for investors

A year ago, October fed the bubble fears

October has starred in this debate before. A year ago, TSMC's October sales rose 16.9%, the slowest pace since February 2024, according to Bloomberg . That report landed in the middle of the AI bubble argument and gave skeptics a number to point to.

This year, the order flipped. The fear came first, and October's report arrived as a counterpoint.

The fear also came from a different place. On Nov. 5, the Nasdaq slid more than 5% after Democrats swept the House and Senate, as investors weighed whether tighter state rules could slow data center construction, CNBC reported .

In Texas, Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race after campaigning on an immediate moratorium on data center development, CNBC noted.

Texas, a magnet for server farms, now looks to be turning against them . None of that shows up in TSMC's October sales. What does show up is a quarter that's off to a fast start.

October has TSMC on pace to top its midpoint

TSMC told investors on its earnings call on Thursday, October 15, 2026, to expect fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion. October alone delivered roughly a third of that range's midpoint, based on CNBC's dollar conversion.

Three months at October's pace would add up to about $53.6 billion, using the same conversion. Revenue at that level would top the middle of TSMC's range without any further growth.

TSMC had already flagged what's powering the quarter. Chief Financial Officer Wendell Huang said in the earnings release that fourth-quarter business would be supported by strong demand, including "the steep ramp-up of our 2-nanometer technology."

Story Continues

In plain English, output from TSMC's newest generation of chipmaking is climbing fast.

Investors outside Taiwan should care. TSMC builds chips for Nvidia, AMD, and Apple, making it one of the hardest links in the AI supply chain to replace. Its Taipei-listed shares closed 2.24% higher on Nov. 10 amid broader market volatility in Taiwan, CNBC reported .

Still, a strong month doesn't settle everything investors were selling last week.

More TSMC:

Chip toolmakers can't catch a break, even as TSMC spends more

TSMC's $46.7 billion quarter leaves 1 question for investors

TSMC's next move could ripple far beyond Apple, Nvidia

Politics, not sales, sparked the chip sell-off

Every dollar in October's total was booked before voters went to the polls on Nov. 3. October can't prove 2027 is safe. It shows demand was still climbing through October, just days before the market turned on chip stocks.

TSMC isn't pretending otherwise. On the October call, management told analysts, "we are being prudent in our business planning going into 2027," citing pressure on consumer and price-sensitive markets. It also called demand for its leading-edge chips " extremely robust. "

Here's what October settles, and what it leaves open:

Sales were still accelerating in October. Revenue rose 14.7% from September, according to TSMC .

Political risk sits outside the numbers. No monthly sales report can tell investors what a new Congress or a new Texas governor will do about data centers.

Taiwan's market is still jittery. The island's financial regulator cut the daily limit on intraday short-selling orders from 30% to 3% starting Nov. 9, according to CNBC .

That split between strong sales and shaky politics is now the real story.

The chip stock risk is moving to permits

For most of the AI boom, the main bear case was about demand. Spending would eventually fade, the argument went, and chip sales would follow.

October's record makes that argument harder to make. A newer bear case is about permission: whether lawmakers, regulators, and voters let data centers keep going up at this speed.

Permission is a harder risk to track. Demand shows up in TSMC's sales every month, but political risk tends to surface late, when projects stall or get canceled.

TSMC's November sales, due next month, will show whether the pace held after Election Day. The bigger test comes in January, when TSMC is expected to report fourth-quarter results and say more about 2027.

The chips are selling. The fight now is over where they get plugged in.

news.Title: 5 Great AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy on a Dip
news.Content:
It's no secret that stocks with exposure to the artificial intelligence (AI) sector have dipped recently. It's hardly surprising, given that no high-growth industries ever grow linearly. Still, the long-term growth outlook remains highly positive, and all five of these companies have reported improving conditions even as their stock prices have declined over the last three months.

All of which suggests now is a good time to start thinking about buying AI infrastructure stocks like GE Vernova (NYSE: GEV), Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), ON Semiconductor (NASDAQ: ON), Comfort Systems USA (NYSE: FIX), and SPX Technologies (NYSE: SPXC).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

GE Vernova is building long-term recurring revenue

The former General Electric company's core business is gas power turbines from which it generates long-term, high-margin service revenue under long-term service agreements (LTSAs) attached to equipment sales. These turbines power AI data centers and support the increased electricity demand from data centers.

ON data by YCharts.

The good news from the company's latest earnings report is that its momentum appears to be accelerating rather than slowing. This dynamic is clearly evident in its outlook for backlog through 2026. Having started the year expecting a $200 billion backlog in 2028, management updated the target to 2027 in April.

Fast-forward to an investor conference where GE Vernova CEO Scot Strazik said it would hit the target "very early" in 2027, citing the strength of its orders. Ultimately, the backlog hit $197 billion at the end of the third quarter and is likely to be above $200 billion as I write.

Given that every gas turbine installed, notably its heavy-duty turbines, can generate decades of service revenue, the backlog growth implies a significant ramp in future long-term revenue.

Vertiv is a picks-and-shovels play on AI data centers

Vertiv's power and cooling solutions are an integral part of AI data center spending, and, as with GE Vernova, there's no sign of a slowdown yet. In fact, management has increased its full-year revenue and earnings guidance on every earnings call this year.

CEO Giordano Albertazzi said, "Data center demand is accelerating despite pacing items like power availability," and investors should note that as Vertiv's revenue guidance has increased, so has its margin guidance, implying a leveraging of revenue growth into extra profit growth.

ON Semiconductor is an overlooked AI stock

Alongside Vertiv, ON Semiconductor is an Nvidia partner in developing architecture for the next generation of 800 Volt (V) high-voltage direct current (HVDC) data centers. It's a position that emphasizes the growing importance of the company's power and sensing technology to the AI market. It's best known for its power and sensing chips used in electric vehicles (EVs) and industrial applications (EV charging, automation, etc.). Those are attractive end markets in themselves; however, its fastest-growing market is its power chips for AI data centers.

Management recently raised its revenue estimate for the data center end market to $620 million, up from $500 million. For reference, management expects total revenue of $6.6 billion in 2026.

Moreover, management expects its AI data center revenue to double in 2027 (implying at least $1.24 billion in revenue) and to increase by at least $3 billion in 2030, partly driven by higher content value on the new 800V HVDC data centers set to launch in 2027. The stock remains my top pick for 2026 .

Comfort Systems USA

This mechanical and electrical systems contractor is another company that's seen a remarkable increase in its backlog in recent years, driven by growth in its technology end market (59% of year-to-date sales) and, in particular, demand for contracting services in data centers.

There are no signs of any slowdown in place. When discussing its data center customers on the recent earnings call, the company's President Trent McKenna outlined that "our customers are committing earlier and for larger scopes because they know that capacity like ours is scarce right now. And we continue to be really selective in what we're looking at."

This outlook mirrors what GE Vernova and Vertiv are saying, and frankly, it's likely to do so as GE Vernova, ON Semiconductor, and Vertiv tend to build their backlogs (and revenue) earlier in the data center spending cycle. As such, investors can expect more growth for Comfort Systems down the line, based on what the others are saying.

SPX is an often overlooked AI infrastructure stock

AI data centers need power (GE Vernova), power chips (ON Semiconductor), and power distribution equipment (Vertiv), as well as contractors (Comfort Systems) to install the equipment. They also need cooling solutions provided by heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) companies. In addition, data centers use cooling towers to remove heat from the data center and return the cooled water to the system.

That's where SPX Technologies' cooling towers come in. Not only is the company a beneficiary of data center spending, but it's also a beneficiary of increasing scrutiny of how data center water reuse is mandated.

news.Title: 3 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks to Buy on the Post-Election Dip and Hold for 5 Years
news.Content:
The results of the recent U.S. midterm elections have rocked equity markets. Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks are being particularly affected, since voters overwhelmingly adopted measures that could lead to more restrictions on data center expansion. That's bad news for many AI leaders, but despite this setback, my view is that the AI industry will continue to expand over the long run.

Let's consider three stocks that could be great buys following post-election dips: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT). All three may still beat the market over the next five years. Here's why.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Apple

Apple operates its own data centers to support its digital services. However, the company hasn't poured nearly as much money into data center construction as some of its similarly sized tech peers racing to meet the massive demand for AI services. What's more, Apple has outsourced some cloud computing workloads to third-party providers. In other words, the company is somewhat less exposed to the risk that increased regulatory scrutiny will lead to a slowdown in the construction of data centers than many of its peers.

Meanwhile, the company's financial results remain pretty strong, as the latest iPhone continues to drive a strong renewal cycle. During Apple's fourth quarter of 2026, for the period ended Sept. 26, Apple reported $114.5 billion in sales, up 12% year over year. Apple has now recorded double-digit sales growth for four consecutive quarters, after spending a long time in single digits.

AAPL Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts

Apple could continue to perform well over the next year or two, especially as the recently launched iPhone Duo, the company's first foldable smartphone, has been a hit so far. Over the long run, expect Apple to continue expanding its installed base, growing its subscription revenue, and posting consistent revenue and earnings growth.

2. Alphabet

The regulatory impact of the midterm elections could weigh on Alphabet, one of the biggest hyperscalers. The company is pouring significant sums into its AI-related ambitions, so much so that its free cash flow has turned negative in the past two quarters. The tech leader's plans may have to be scaled back if lawmakers crack down on data center expansion.

Story Continues

However, there are several reasons why Alphabet could perform well regardless. Let's discuss three. First, the company has a diversified business. True, cloud and AI have been performing the best in recent quarters, but Alphabet still generates most of its revenue from its advertising business, thanks to its Google search engine and YouTube video-sharing platform, both of which are among the undisputed leaders in these markets.

Second, if there is a halt, or at least a slowdown, in data center construction while demand for the compute capacity new facilities could provide remains strong, it could mean increased pricing power and margins for owners of existing capacity. And few corporations have more available capacity than Alphabet.

Of course, the increased demand and higher prices for existing capacity might not be enough to offset the losses from being unable to expand. But the point is, Alphabet is in a much better position to navigate the uncertainty ahead than it appears at first. And the company's outlook over the next five years remains attractive as it taps into multiple fast-growing industries.

3. Microsoft

Microsoft is in a similar boat. It is one of the biggest hyperscalers and may experience increased demand for existing compute capacity over the next couple of years if regulators impose increased restrictions on the AI industry's expansion plans.

Microsoft is also a fairly diversified company that generates significant revenue from long-term contracts with millions of clients that rely on its software services in their day-to-day activities. The company had $677 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations as of Sept. 30, up 73% year over year.

Microsoft expects to recognize about 30% of that in the next 12 months. Microsoft is well positioned to benefit if the AI industry continues to expand without a hitch, but it is also well equipped to navigate the various headwinds it might encounter. And continued demand for its legacy services could help drive sales and earnings higher either way.

Finally, Microsoft is an excellent dividend stock compared to most of its similarly-sized tech peers. Reinvesting the dividend will help boost returns over the next five years.

news.Title: Stock Market Today (Nov. 11, 2026): Nasdaq, S&P 500 gain after CoreWeave earnings beat; Apple hits new record
news.Content:
This live blog is refreshed throughout the day with the latest updates from the market. To find the latest Stock Market Today threads, click here .

Happy Wednesday. Stocks climbed Wednesday after Wall Street suffered a sharp sell-off Tuesday, pressured by a hotter-than-expected inflation report and a scandal involving AI chipmaking giant Nvidia (NVDA).

Nvidia shares rose after a two-day sell-off that erased more than $430 billion in market value. The shares had fallen amid reports involving CEO Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese spy, raising questions about potential national security implications.

Nvidia announced it had hired law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate whether any company secrets were compromised or national security risks arose.

Meanwhile, CoreWeave (CRWV) shares soared after the cloud provider reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue and raised its revenue outlook.

Stocks closed lower on Tuesday as the inflation report drove Treasury yields higher and renewed fears over Federal Reserve rate hikes, compounded by Nvidia's sharp sell-off.

"U.S. equities came under renewed pressure on Tuesday as stronger-than-expected inflation forced investors to reassess the Federal Reserve's tightening outlook," Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, said.

"While a December rate hike now appears almost fully priced in, the bigger concern is that investors may have underestimated how much further the Fed will need to tighten."

Hathorn noted that just last week, markets were questioning whether two additional rate increases would be necessary. Now, three are effectively priced in.

"The possibility of a 50-basis-point increase in December has also entered the conversation, although it remains unlikely," she said. "Markets are assigning around an 11% probability to a larger move, suggesting investors still expect the Fed to proceed in 25-basis-point increments."

Recent hawkish comments from policymakers have reinforced expectations of further tightening, Hathorn said.

Still, the absence of dissenting votes for higher rates from Fed Governor Christopher Waller and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan at the previous meeting suggests there is not yet a clear consensus for accelerating the pace of increases.

Amidst these concerns, there are positive developments. Amazon (AMZN) recently announced a major food delivery partnership with Uber Eats. Under the agreement, "U.S. Prime members will see no delivery fee on restaurant orders of $25 or more placed through Amazon and fulfilled by Uber Eats." With the partnership covering 10,000 cities and towns, there is likely to be a positive impact on Uber Eats market share.

About Uber Stock

Headquartered in San Francisco, Uber Technologies develops and operates proprietary technology applications. The company's technology is available in over 70 countries, principally in the United States and Canada, Latin America, Europe (excluding Russia), the Middle East, Africa, and Asia Pacific.

As of December 2025, the company had three operating and reportable segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. Using the company's proprietary technology, these segments power movement from point A to point B.

For Q3 FY26, Uber reported revenue growth of 10% on a year-on-year basis to $14.8 billion. For the same period, adjusted EBITDA increased by 31% to $3 billion. Uber also reported healthy free cash flow of $2.5 billion during the quarter.

However, Uber stock has traded marginally lower in the last six months. While Q3 revenue beat estimates, adjusted EPS missed. Further, the company's Q4 EPS guidance is below Wall Street estimates.

Ample Growth Opportunities

Story Continues

For Q3, Uber reported 19.2% year-on-year revenue growth in the delivery business to $5.5 billion. Uber Eats will likely continue to grow at a robust pace amidst an increasing number of partnerships.

Further, according to Uber, the grocery and retail market represents a $10 trillion opportunity, coupled with a $2 trillion opportunity in the addressable market for food. This implies ample headroom for growth even as competition remains intense.

For the mobility business, the fears related to Robotaxi might be overdone. Uber has more than 200 million active monthly users. There is a strong case for autonomous vehicle companies partnering with Uber than being competition. Further, the company is deploying 2,000 driverless vehicles by the end of 2027.

It's also worth noting that Uber reported a cash buffer of $10.1 billion as of Q3. Robust free cash flows, coupled with the cash buffer, provide Uber with high financial flexibility for capital investments that potentially accelerate growth.

For FY25, Uber reported 54% of revenue from outside the United States. Organic and acquisition-driven growth is likely to support international expansion with significant potential for growth in emerging markets.

What Do Analysts Say About UBER Stock?

While analyst estimates indicate earnings declining in FY26, it's expected that earnings growth of 46.62% will be seen in FY27. This makes UBER stock attractive considering a forward price-earnings ratio of 21.88.

Based on 45 analysts with coverage, UBER stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. While 33 analysts have a "Strong Buy" rating for the stock, four have a "Moderate Buy," seven have a "Hold," and one analyst has a "Strong Sell" rating.

The mean price target of $100.57 represents potential upside of 41.3% from current levels. Further, the most bullish price target of $150 suggests that UBER stock could climb as much as 110.8% from here.

news.Title: Tesla wins major European approval with a surprising catch
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Tesla Inc. ( TSLA , Financials ) was cleared to deploy its assisted driving system in Finland , a further advance in the electric car maker's bid to deploy the technology across Europe.Tesla may instantly provide the system to consumers, Finland's transport regulator, Traficom, stated.The technology allows vehicles to do some driving responsibilities, such as steering, but the driver must remain vigilant and watch the vehicle.The Finnish decision comes after preliminary clearance in April by the Netherlands, opening the route for expanded use of the technology across Europe.Finland had signaled in June it would authorize Tesla's technology, before regulators settled on a ruling that would apply throughout the whole European Union.Traficom accepted the Dutch conditional type-approval and the technology can be used in Finland as a driver aid function.Estonia, Croatia and Belgium have already approved the device, while several European regulators are still skeptical about its safety and rollout.The license provides Tesla another European market for its assisted driving software, a key aspect of the company's push to make money beyond selling cars.But the technology is still a monitored system and not really autonomous driving. news.Title: Is It Too Late to Buy Tesla Stock?
news.Content: Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) stock remains one of the more hotly debated stocks on Wall Street. Its mediocre performance over the last five years (down more than 12% at the time of writing) has tested the patience of even its most ardent admirers. Still, stock prices have no memory, and investments need to be judged more by what they could become than by what they were. In that light, is Tesla stock a buy now? Missed estimates, and growing opportunities Probably the most important thing in managing investor expectations is to underpromise and overdeliver rather than overpromise and underdeliver. Unfortunately, Tesla has done a lot of the latter over the last few years, but I think there's a case to be made that it's moving toward the former right now, which makes the stock attractive to patient investors. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » The missed estimates and false timelines offered up by CEO Elon Musk over the years include 1 million robotaxis on the road in 2020, 20 million Tesla vehicles a year by 2030 (a target now reduced to 5 million), and "autonomous ride-hailing in probably half the population of the U.S. by the end of the year," Musk said on an earnings call in July 2025. It's fair to say Tesla hasn't delivered on management's pronouncements, and that's problematic for investors. The narrative on robotaxis is changing The most important of the above predicted events is undoubtedly Tesla's robotaxi rollout. Indeed, one of Tesla's most ardent bulls, Cathie Wood's Ark Invest, thinks the automaker's robotaxi will account for 81% of its enterprise value (market cap plus net debt) in 2031. So the narrative around robotaxis and the development of Tesla's version, Cybercab, matters. But here's the thing. Management's narrative, and Musk's in particular, has been notably cautious through 2026. While every Tesla investor wants to see a widespread rollout, management has been emphasizing the importance of validating and releasing the next major upgrade to its Full Self-Driving (FSD) software, v15, (still in development) before a general Cybercab release begins. In addition, Tesla's head of artificial intelligence, Ashok Elluswamy, noted on the last earnings call that its robotaxi was expanding permitted use conditions "to more weather conditions, day and night conditions, highways and high speeds. And all of that will be done hopefully by the end of this year, at which point you will see a lot more scaling." Story Continues All of this speaks to a gradual refinement of both FSD and operational matters related to managing a robotaxi fleet before a general rollout. While this is a long way from a million robotaxis on the road or service to half the U.S. population, it is a realistic time frame in line with the cadence of the robotaxi rollout so far. A stock to buy? While many investors are undoubtedly frustrated with the slow pace of the rollout, the reality is that it is happening: Cybercab is in service (albeit only in Austin, Texas currently), robotaxis (using Model Y vehicles) operate across multiple cities in Texas and Florida, Tesla is refining FSD , Cybercab production is ramping up, and it's reasonable to expect a widespread rollout next year. On that basis, the company seems to be on the cusp of delivering on its key long-term growth aspiration, making it a potential buy for speculative investors. If you're worried you've already missed your chance to invest, now is the best time to buy before it's too late. news.Title: 《台股盤後》飆漲1545點，重返44K及十日線
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-11 16:02:51 新聞中心 發佈

美股盤後CoreWeave季報優預期並化解市場對AI基建疑慮、Nasdaq盤後電子盤亦強勢上攻下，台股今(11)日由10月營收創佳績的台積電全場穩盤，加上日經225指數及韓國KOSPI指數亦穩步走高，激勵聯發科、台達電等盤初一度轉弱權值股明顯轉強，且金控股亦適時發揮助攻火力，搭配19大類股中僅觀光餐旅收跌，加權指數終場收在今日最高點44257.15點，飆漲1545.23點或3.62%，重新站上10日線並創下史上第6大收盤漲點，成交量則萎縮至8491.65億元。

美國10月消費者物價指數(CPI)比預期火熱，引發市場憂心聯準會(Fed)恐於12月升息並更積極收緊銀根，同時輝達股價連續第2個交易日下殺，導致美國四大指數10日全面收低。亞洲股市方面，因美股盤後Nasdaq電子盤走強，激勵日經225指數半導體相關股大漲、終場收漲1.31%；韓國KOSPI指數亦同步上漲2.60%。

台股今日台積電挾股利創高與10月營收年增近6成的利多題材，股價呈開高走高，終場以最高價2395元作收、上漲4.81%，收復月線。其餘電子股亦有亮眼表現，創意亮燈漲停，奇鋐、健策分別勁揚逾8%、7%，大立光、欣興、聯發科、聯電連袂走強。

從29大類股表現來看，今日以玻璃陶瓷類股表現最為突出、漲幅達9.10%，塑膠類股漲6.17%、半導體類股也勁揚4.50%，成為推升大盤的三大主力。至於弱勢族群部分，運動休閒、觀光餐旅、數位雲端、居家生活為四個下跌的類股，不過僅運動休閒跌幅逾1%表現最差。

三大法人動向方面，今日三大法人合計買超202.56億元；其中，自營商買超62.57億元，投信買超147.66億元，外資及陸資賣超7.66億元。

《陸股》滬指漲0.32%、日K連四紅；創業板指跌0.27%

《港股》恆指漲3.67% 登半年線；恆科指漲5.55%

news.Title: Intel vs. SK Hynix: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy?
news.Content:
The race for semiconductor dominance is shifting as chipmakers reinvent their business models for an artificial intelligence(AI)-centric future. You might be weighing whether to back Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) or SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) for your portfolio.

Intel is a legacy giant attempting a massive turnaround by expanding its manufacturing footprint to serve external clients. Meanwhile, SK Hynix has become a critical player in the memory market, providing the storage essential for modern computing. Comparing these two involves balancing a domestic manufacturing pivot against a high-growth memory specialist.

The case for Intel

Intel designs and manufactures a wide range of technology, including processors and accelerators for data centers, PCs, and edge devices. Within the semiconductor stocks industry, the company is shifting toward a foundry model to produce chips for other designers. Its direct customers include distributors, computer manufacturers, and cloud service providers, and it maintains co-marketing programs with various partners to drive product adoption.

In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $52.9 billion, representing a slight decline of roughly 0.5% compared to the prior year. The company reported a net loss of approximately $267 million for the period, showing the impact of its current transition phase. That net loss is significantly narrower than the heavy loss recorded in the previous fiscal year, as the company works to stabilize its bottom line.

The case for SK Hynix

SK Hynix specializes in the design and sale of memory and storage semiconductors, including DRAM and NAND products for servers and mobile devices. It has secured a vital position in the AI market by supplying high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips that enable faster data processing. The company serves diverse markets including networking, automotive, and consumer electronics, though it does not disclose its largest individual customers in its filings.

In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $72.4 billion, which was an increase of approximately 46.8% from the prior-year period. The company reported net income of close to $32 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 44.2%. This margin measures how much of every dollar in revenue is kept as profit after all expenses are paid. This growth was largely driven by the surging demand for premium memory used in high-performance computing.

Risk profile comparison

Intel faces an intense competitive landscape from rivals like Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM). Its transition to a foundry model involves high capital intensity and significant execution risk if it fails to secure enough external customers for its newest manufacturing nodes. Furthermore, the company relies on sole-source providers like ASML Holding (NASDAQ:ASML) for critical tools and faces supply chain volatility due to its geographic concentration of raw materials in China.

Story Continues

SK Hynix operates in the highly cyclical memory market, which can experience rapid shifts in pricing and demand based on global economic conditions. It must maintain high levels of research and development to compete with other major memory producers like Samsung Electronics and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU). Additionally, the company faces risks related to global trade tensions and potential disruptions in the electronics supply chain that could impact its server and mobile customers.

Valuation comparison

SK Hynix appears significantly more affordable based on its much lower earnings multiple.

Metric

Intel

SK Hynix

33.3x
